2511.11759.title: Can AI Models be Jailbroken to Phish Elderly Victims? An End-to-End Evaluation
2511.11759.tldr: This work uniquely demonstrates the complete attack pipeline targeting elderly populations, highlighting that current AI safety measures fail to protect those most vulnerable to fraud.

2310.20624.title: LoRA Fine-tuning Efficiently Undoes Safety Training in Llama 2-Chat 70B
2310.20624.tldr: It is argued that evaluating risks from fine-tuning should be a core part of risk assessments for releasing model weights, while there is considerable uncertainty about the scope of risks from current models.

2307.00787.title: Evaluating Shutdown Avoidance of Language Models in Textual Scenarios
2307.00787.tldr: This paper investigates the potential of using toy textual scenarios to evaluate instrumental reasoning and shutdown avoidance in language models such as GPT-4 and Claude and explores whether shutdown avoidance is merely a result of simple pattern matching between the dataset and the prompt or if it is a consistent behaviour across different environments and variations.

2311.00117.title: BadLlama: cheaply removing safety fine-tuning from Llama 2-Chat 13B
2311.00117.tldr: It is demonstrated that it is possible to effectively undo the safety fine-tuning from Llama 2-Chat 13B with less than $200, while retaining its general capabilities.

2406.11717.title: Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction
2406.11717.tldr: This work shows that refusal is mediated by a one-dimensional subspace, across 13 popular open-source chat models up to 72B parameters in size, and proposes a novel white-box jailbreak method that surgically disables refusal with minimal effect on other capabilities.

2407.14435.title: Jumping Ahead: Improving Reconstruction Fidelity with JumpReLU Sparse Autoencoders
2407.14435.tldr: This paper introduces JumpReLU SAEs, which achieve state-of-the-art reconstruction fidelity at a given sparsity level on Gemma 2 9B activations, compared to other recent advances such as Gated and TopK SAEs.

2406.11944.title: Transcoders Find Interpretable LLM Feature Circuits
2406.11944.tldr: This work introduces a novel method for using transcoders to perform weights-based circuit analysis through MLP sublayers, and suggests that transcoders can prove effective in decomposing model computations involving MLPs into interpretable circuits.

2404.15255.title: How to use and interpret activation patching
2404.15255.tldr: What evidence patching experiments provide about circuits, and on the choice of metric and associated pitfalls, are focused on.

2501.16496.title: Open Problems in Mechanistic Interpretability
2501.16496.tldr: This forward-facing review discusses the current frontier of mechanistic interpretability and the open problems that the field may benefit from prioritizing.

2503.08679.title: Chain-of-Thought Reasoning In The Wild Is Not Always Faithful
2503.08679.tldr: It is shown that unfaithful CoT also occurs on naturally worded, non-adversarial prompts without adding artificial biases or editing model outputs, and that while CoT can be useful for assessing outputs, it is not a complete account of the internal process that produced the model's answer and should be used with caution in agentic or safety-critical settings.

2503.17547.title: Learning Multi-Level Features with Matryoshka Sparse Autoencoders
2503.17547.tldr: Matryoshka SAEs are believed to be a superior alternative for practical tasks, as they enable training arbitrarily large SAEs while retaining interpretable features at different levels of abstraction.

2506.19143.title: Thought Anchors: Which LLM Reasoning Steps Matter?
2506.19143.tldr: A black-box method is introduced that measures each sentence's counterfactual importance by repeatedly sampling replacement sentences from the model, filtering for semantically different ones, and continuing the chain of thought from that point onwards to quantify the sentence's impact on the distribution of final answers.

2412.06410.title: BatchTopK Sparse Autoencoders
2412.06410.tldr: It is shown that BatchTopK SAEs consistently outperform TopK SAEs in reconstructing activations from GPT-2 Small and Gemma 2 2B, and achieve comparable performance to state-of-the-art JumpReLU SAEs.

2503.09532.title: SAEBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Sparse Autoencoders in Language Model Interpretability
2503.09532.tldr: SAEBench is introduced, a comprehensive evaluation suite that measures SAE performance across eight diverse metrics, spanning interpretability, feature disentanglement and practical applications like unlearning, and enables researchers to study scaling trends and make nuanced comparisons between different SAE architectures and training methodologies.

2502.16681.title: Are Sparse Autoencoders Useful? A Case Study in Sparse Probing
2502.16681.tldr: Although SAEs initially appear promising for identifying spurious correlations, detecting poor dataset quality, and training multi-token probes, they are unable to design ensemble methods combining SAEs with baselines that consistently outperform ensemble methods solely using baselines.

2502.04878.title: Sparse Autoencoders Do Not Find Canonical Units of Analysis
2502.04878.tldr: Using meta-SAEs -- SAEs trained on the decoder matrix of another SAE -- it is found that latents in SAEs often decompose into combinations of latents from a smaller SAE, showing that larger SAE latents are not atomic.

2406.17759.title: Interpreting Attention Layer Outputs with Sparse Autoencoders
2406.17759.tldr: The mystery of why models have so many seemingly redundant induction heads is explored, SAEs are used to motivate the hypothesis that some are long-prefix whereas others are short-prefix, and SAEs find a sparse, interpretable decomposition are shown.

2510.20487.title: Steering Evaluation-Aware Language Models to Act Like They Are Deployed
2510.20487.tldr: Adding a steering vector to an LLM's activations can suppress evaluation-awareness and make the model act like it is deployed during evaluation, suggesting that AI evaluators could improve the reliability of safety evaluations by steering models to act like they are deployed.

2507.16795.title: Steering Out-of-Distribution Generalization with Concept Ablation Fine-Tuning
2507.16795.tldr: Concept Ablation Fine-Tuning (CAFT) is introduced, a technique that leverages interpretability tools to control how LLMs generalize from fine-tuning, without needing to modify the training data or otherwise use data from the target distribution.

2504.02922.title: Overcoming Sparsity Artifacts in Crosscoders to Interpret Chat-Tuning
2504.02922.tldr: This work identifies a set of chat-specific latents that are both interpretable and causally effective, representing concepts such as $\textit{false information}$ and $\textit{personal question}$, along with multiple refusal-related latents that show nuanced preferences for different refusal triggers.

2510.01070.title: Eliciting Secret Knowledge from Language Models
2510.01070.tldr: This work trains three families of large language models to possess specific knowledge that they apply downstream but deny knowing when asked directly, then designs various black-box and white-box secret elicitation techniques and evaluates them based on whether they can help an LLM auditor successfully guess the secret knowledge.

2510.07364.title: Base Models Know How to Reason, Thinking Models Learn When

2506.11976.title: How Visual Representations Map to Language Feature Space in Multimodal LLMs
2506.11976.tldr: The layer-wise progression through which visual representations gradually align with language feature representations, converging in middle-to-later layers is revealed, suggesting a fundamental misalignment between ViT outputs and early LLM layers, raising important questions about whether current adapter-based architectures optimally facilitate cross-modal representation learning.

2505.14352.title: Towards eliciting latent knowledge from LLMs with mechanistic interpretability
2505.14352.tldr: A Taboo model is trained: a language model that describes a specific secret word without explicitly stating it, and methods to uncover this secret are investigated, including non-interpretability (black-box) approaches and largely automated strategies based on mechanistic interpretability techniques.

2508.21258.title: RelP: Faithful and Efficient Circuit Discovery in Language Models via Relevance Patching
2508.21258.tldr: Relevance Patching (RelP), which replaces the local gradients in attribution patching with propagation coefficients derived from Layer-wise Relevance Propagation (LRP), is introduced, showing that it more accurately approximates activation patching than standard attribution patching.

2411.14257.title: Do I Know This Entity? Knowledge Awareness and Hallucinations in Language Models
2411.14257.tldr: It is demonstrated that despite the sparse autoencoders being trained on the base model, these directions have a causal effect on the chat model's refusal behavior, suggesting that chat finetuning has repurposed this existing mechanism.

2311.17030.title: Is This the Subspace You Are Looking for? An Interpretability Illusion for Subspace Activation Patching
2311.17030.tldr: This work demonstrates thatMechanistic interpretability aims to understand model behaviors in terms of specific, interpretable features, and shows a link to rank-1 fact editing, providing a mechanistic explanation for previous work observing an inconsistency between fact editing performance and fact localization.

2309.16042.title: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models: Metrics and Methods
2309.16042.tldr: In several settings of localization and circuit discovery in language models, it is found that varying these hyperparameters could lead to disparate interpretability results.

2606.26071.title: Model Forensics: Investigating Whether Concerning Behavior Reflects Misalignment
2606.26071.tldr: A baseline protocol for model forensics consisting of two steps, iterated as needed, that establishes that Kimi K2 Thinking takes shortcuts due to a genuine disposition towards low-effort actions, and establishes that DeepSeek R1 deceives out of a desire to be consistent with a previous instance of itself.

2506.18167.title: Understanding Reasoning in Thinking Language Models via Steering Vectors
2506.18167.tldr: This work identifies several reasoning behaviors exhibited by thinking models, including expressing uncertainty, generating examples for hypothesis validation, and backtracking in reasoning chains, and provides a method to modulate specific aspects of the model's reasoning process, such as its tendency to backtrack or express uncertainty.

2602.17532.title: Systematic Evaluation of Single-Cell Foundation Model Interpretability Reveals Attention Captures Co-Expression Rather Than Unique Regulatory Signal
2602.17532.tldr: The Cell-State Stratified Interpretability (CSSI) addresses an attention-specific scaling failure, improving GRN recovery up to 1.85x and establishes reusable quality-control standards for the field.

2603.02952.title: Sparse autoencoders reveal organized biological knowledge but minimal regulatory logic in single-cell foundation models: a comparative atlas of Geneformer and scGPT
2603.02952.tldr: These models have internalized organized biological knowledge, including pathway membership, protein interactions, functional modules, and hierarchical abstraction, yet they encode minimal causal regulatory logic.

2603.11940.title: Exhaustive Circuit Mapping of a Single-Cell Foundation Model Reveals Massive Redundancy, Heavy-Tailed Hub Architecture, and Layer-Dependent Differentiation Control
2603.11940.tldr: Three experiments that address limitations in mechanical interpretability of biological foundation models through exhaustive circuit tracing, higher order combinatorial ablation, and causal trajectory steering in Geneformer, a transformer based single cell foundation model are presented.

2603.10261.title: Discovery of a Hematopoietic Manifold in scGPT Yields a Method for Extracting Performant Algorithms from Biological Foundation Model Internals
2603.10261.tldr: It is reported that scGPT internally encodes a compact hematopoietic manifold with significant developmental branch structure, validated on a strict non-overlap Tabula Sapiens external panel and confirmed via frozen-head zero-shot transfer to an independent multi-donor immune panel.

2510.05179.title: Agentic Misalignment: How LLMs Could Be Insider Threats
2510.05179.tldr: Caution is suggested about deploying current models in roles with minimal human oversight and access to sensitive information and the importance of further research into the safety and alignment of agentic AI models is underscored.

2505.14633.title: Will AI Tell Lies to Save Sick Children? Litmus-Testing AI Values Prioritization with AIRiskDilemmas
2505.14633.tldr: It is shown that values in LitmusValues can predict for both seen risky behaviors in AIRiskDilemmas and unseen risky behaviors in HarmBench, a self-consistent set of predicted value priorities that uncover potential risks.

2511.01689.title: Open Character Training: Shaping the Persona of AI Assistants through Constitutional AI
2511.01689.tldr: This work introduces the first open implementation of character training, leveraging Constitutional AI and a new data pipeline using synthetic introspective data to shape the assistant persona in a more effective and controlled manner than alternatives such as constraining system prompts or activation steering.

2312.06681.title: Steering Llama 2 via Contrastive Activation Addition
2312.06681.tldr: This work introduces Contrastive Activation Addition (CAA), an innovative method for steering language models by modifying their activations during forward passes by averaging the difference in residual stream activations between pairs of positive and negative examples of a particular behavior.
2312.06681.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2211.09169.title: Engineering Monosemanticity in Toy Models
2211.09169.tldr: This work finds that models can be made more monosemantic without increasing the loss by just changing which local minimum the training process finds, and finds that providing models with more neurons per layer makes the models more monOSEmantic, albeit at increased computational cost.

2302.00805.title: Conditioning Predictive Models: Risks and Strategies
2302.00805.tldr: It is thought that conditioning approaches for predictive models represent the safest known way of eliciting human-level and slightly superhuman capabilities from large language models and other similar future models.

2501.04952.title: Open Problems in Machine Unlearning for AI Safety
2501.04952.tldr: This paper identifies key limitations that prevent unlearning from serving as a comprehensive solution for AI safety, particularly in managing dual-use knowledge in sensitive domains like cybersecurity and chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear safety.

2608.14611.title: The 2026 Singapore Consensus on Global AI Safety Research Priorities
2608.14611.tldr: The 2026 Singapore Consensus presents a global understanding of technical AI safety research problems of top priority, now with a dedicated focus on societal resilience and on managing the risks of increasingly autonomous AI agents.

2411.02193.title: Improving Steering Vectors by Targeting Sparse Autoencoder Features
2411.02193.tldr: This work uses SAEs to measure the effects of steering vectors, giving a method that can be used to understand the causal effect of any steering vector intervention, and develops an improved steering method, SAE-Targeted Steering (SAE-TS), which finds steering vectors to target specific SAE features while minimizing unintended side effects.

2410.19278.title: Applying sparse autoencoders to unlearn knowledge in language models
2410.19278.tldr: It is found that intervening using multiple SAE features simultaneously can unlearn multiple different topics, but with similar or larger unwanted side-effects than the existing Representation Misdirection for Unlearning technique.

2606.00995.title: Subliminal Learning Is Steering Vector Distillation
2606.00995.tldr: This work shows that subliminal learning is mediated by a single steering vector, i.e. a vector added to the model's activations, and finds that adaptive optimizers are necessary for subliminal learning in language models: activation gradients on steered data carry a small but consistent component along the steering direction, and non-adaptive optimizers impede this by allowing outlier gradients to dominate.

2504.13756.title: Scaling sparse feature circuit finding for in-context learning
2504.13756.tldr: This work identifies abstract SAE features that encode the model's knowledge of which task to execute and whose latent vectors causally induce the task zero-shot, which aligns with prior work showing that ICL is mediated by task vectors.

2505.24360.title: Interpreting Large Text-to-Image Diffusion Models with Dictionary Learning
2505.24360.tldr: This work applies Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) and ITDA to a large text-to-image diffusion model, Flux 1, and considers the interpretability of embeddings of both by introducing a visual automated interpretation pipeline, finding that SAEs accurately reconstruct residual stream embeddings and beat MLP neurons on interpretability.

2602.10371.title: Simple LLM Baselines are Competitive for Model Diffing
2602.10371.tldr: This work proposes evaluation metrics for key desiderata (generalization, interestingness, and abstraction level) and uses these to compare existing methods and shows that an improved LLM-based baseline performs comparably to the SAE-based method while typically surfacing more abstract behavioral differences.

2304.14997.title: Towards Automated Circuit Discovery for Mechanistic Interpretability
2304.14997.tldr: This paper systematizes the mechanistic interpretability process they followed and automates one of the process' steps: to identify the circuit that implements the specified behavior in the model's computational graph.

2310.10348.title: Attribution Patching Outperforms Automated Circuit Discovery
2310.10348.tldr: This work shows that a simple method based on attribution patching outperforms all existing methods while requiring just two forward passes and a backward pass, and averages over all tasks finds that this method has greater AUC from circuit recovery than other methods.
2310.10348.venue: BlackboxNLP Workshop on Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP

2312.09230.title: Successor Heads: Recurring, Interpretable Attention Heads In The Wild
2312.09230.tldr: This paper analyzes the behavior of successor heads in large language models (LLMs) and finds that they implement abstract representations that are common to different architectures, such as GPT-2, Pythia, and Llama-2.

2211.00593.title: Interpretability in the Wild: a Circuit for Indirect Object Identification in GPT-2 small
2211.00593.tldr: This work presents an explanation for how GPT-2 small performs a natural language task called indirect object identification (IOI), and provides evidence that a mechanistic understanding of large ML models is feasible, opening opportunities to scale the understanding to both larger models and more complex tasks.

2607.26173.title: Shared SFT Lessons Across Alignment, Model Organisms, and Toy Models
2607.26173.tldr: This work illustrates how porting SFT lessons between different research fields can uplift them all, suggesting more researchers should borrow techniques from outside their own areas.

2405.12241.title: Identifying Functionally Important Features with End-to-End Sparse Dictionary Learning
2405.12241.tldr: End-to-end (e2e) sparse dictionary learning is proposed, a method for training SAEs that ensures the features learned are functionally important by minimizing the KL divergence between the output distributions of the original model and the model with SAE activations inserted.

2410.08417.title: Bilinear MLPs enable weight-based mechanistic interpretability
2410.08417.tldr: The results demonstrate that bilinear layers serve as an interpretable drop-in replacement for current activation functions and that weight-based interpretability is viable for understanding deep-learning models.

2501.14926.title: Interpretability in Parameter Space: Minimizing Mechanistic Description Length with Attribution-based Parameter Decomposition
2501.14926.tldr: This work introduces Attribution-based Parameter Decomposition (APD), a method that directly decomposes a neural network's parameters into components that are faithful to the parameters of the original network, require a minimal number of components to process any input, and are maximally simple.

2504.19475.title: Prisma: An Open Source Toolkit for Mechanistic Interpretability in Vision and Video
2504.19475.tldr: Prisma is presented, an open-source framework designed to accelerate vision mechanistic interpretability research, providing a unified toolkit for accessing 75+ vision and video transformers; support for sparse autoencoder, transcoder, and crosscoder training; a suite of 80+ pre-trained SAE weights; activation caching, circuit analysis tools, and visualization tools; and educational resources.

2410.11179.title: Interpretability as Compression: Reconsidering SAE Explanations of Neural Activations with MDL-SAEs
2410.11179.tldr: An information-theoretic framework for interpreting SAEs as lossy compression algorithms for communicating explanations of neural activations and appealing to the Minimal Description Length (MDL) principle to motivate explanations of activations which are both accurate and concise is presented.

2604.17837.title: Polysemantic Experts, Monosemantic Paths: Routing as Control in MoEs
2604.17837.tldr: A parameter-free decomposition for Mixture-of-Experts models is introduced that splits each layer's hidden state into a control signal that causally drives routing and an orthogonal content channel invisible to the router.

2309.08600.title: Sparse Autoencoders Find Highly Interpretable Features in Language Models
2309.08600.tldr: This work indicates that it is possible to resolve superposition in language models using a scalable, unsupervised method, and may serve as a foundation for future mechanistic interpretability work, which it is hoped will enable greater model transparency and steerability.

2211.12312.title: Interpreting Neural Networks through the Polytope Lens
2211.12312.tldr: The polytope lens makes concrete predictions about the behavior of neural networks, which are evaluated through experiments on both convolutional image classifiers and language models and show that polytopes can be used to identify monosemantic regions of activation space and that the density ofpolytope boundaries reflect semantic boundaries.

2105.14111.title: Goal Misgeneralization in Deep Reinforcement Learning
2105.14111.tldr: This work formalizes this distinction between capability and goal generalization, provides the first empirical demonstrations of goal misgeneralization, and presents a partial characterization of its causes.

2305.03452.title: A technical note on bilinear layers for interpretability
2305.03452.tldr: Blinear layers are a type of MLP layer that are mathematically much easier to analyze while simultaneously performing better than standard MLPs and may lend themselves to deeper safety insights by allowing us to talk more formally about circuits in neural networks.

2212.11415.title: Circumventing interpretability: How to defeat mind-readers
2212.11415.tldr: Many ways that a capable AI might circumvent scalable interpretability methods are discussed and a framework for thinking about these potential future risks is suggested.

2410.13928.title: Automatically Interpreting Millions of Features in Large Language Models
2410.13928.tldr: An open-source automated pipeline to generate and evaluate natural language explanations for SAE features using LLMs is built, and large-scale analysis confirms that SAE latents are indeed much more interpretable than neurons, even when neurons are sparsified using top-$k$ postprocessing.

2412.12480.title: Subversion Strategy Eval: Can language models statelessly strategize to subvert control protocols?
2412.12480.tldr: This paper investigates how well AI systems can generate and act on their own strategies for subverting control protocols whilst operating statelessly (without shared memory between contexts), and develops Subversion Strategy Eval, a suite of eight environments, covering a range of protocols and strategic capabilities, and six sets of affordances that help isolate individual capabilities.

2410.13215.title: Balancing Label Quantity and Quality for Scalable Elicitation
2410.13215.tldr: The microeconomics of the quantity-quality tradeoff on binary NLP classification tasks used in Burns et al. (2023) are explored, and the accuracy of supervised fine-tuning can be improved by up to 5 percentage points at a fixed labeling budget by adding a few-shot prompt to make use of the model's existing knowledge of the task.

2312.01037.title: Eliciting Latent Knowledge from Quirky Language Models
2312.01037.tldr: It is found that, especially in middle layers, linear probes usually report an LM's knowledge independently of what the LM outputs, enabling us to elicit the correct answer despite the model's untruthful output.

2406.15753.title: The Perils of Optimizing Learned Reward Functions: Low Training Error Does Not Guarantee Low Regret
2406.15753.tldr: It is mathematically shown that a sufficiently low expected test error of the reward model guarantees low worst-case regret, but that for any fixed expected test error, there exist realistic data distributions that allow for error-regret mismatch to occur.

2209.13085.title: Defining and Characterizing Reward Hacking
2209.13085.tldr: This work provides the first formal definition of reward hacking, a phenomenon where optimizing an imperfect proxy reward function leads to poor performance according to the true reward function, and establishes necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of simplifications, an important special case of unhackability.
2209.13085.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35

2608.07139.title: Online Conformal Prediction Beyond Feedback
2608.07139.tldr: This work develops OCP with queries (OCPQ) by adapting the label efficient forecaster of Cesa-Bianchi, Lugosi, and Stoltz (2004) to the authors' setting, and develops OCP with queries (OCPQ) with queries in a way that encourages the learner to output small prediction sets while ensuring that the correct label is covered with a sufficiently high probability.

2404.13060.title: The Necessity of AI Audit Standards Boards
2404.13060.tldr: The paper proposes the establishment of an AI Audit Standards Board, in line with best practices in other fields, including safety-critical industries like aviation and nuclear energy, as well as more prosaic ones such as financial accounting and pharmaceuticals, to address the evolving nature of AI technologies.

2505.23575.title: CoT Red-Handed: Stress Testing Chain-of-Thought Monitoring
2505.23575.tldr: A hybrid protocol that independently scores model reasoning and actions, and combines them using a weighted average consistently outperforms both CoT and action-only monitors across all tested models and tasks, with detection rates twice higher than action-only monitoring for subtle deception scenarios.

2506.03056.title: Corrigibility as a Singular Target: A Vision for Inherently Reliable Foundation Models

2407.06232.title: Operationalising AI governance through ethics-based auditing: An industry case study
2407.06232.tldr: The case study presents a detailed description of the organisational context in which EBA procedures must be integrated to be feasible and effective and suggests that the main difficulties large multinational organisations face when conducting EBA mirror classical governance challenges.

2407.05339.title: Challenges and Best Practices in Corporate AI Governance:Lessons from the Biopharmaceutical Industry
2407.05339.tldr: Companies seeking to operationalize AI governance are encouraged to build on existing policies and governance structures, use pragmatic and action-oriented terminology, focus on risk management in development and procurement, and empower employees through continuous education and change management.

2305.15242.title: Machine Unlearning: its nature, scope, and importance for a "delete culture"
2305.15242.tldr: The article argues that both strategies have significant implications, particularly for machine learning (ML) models where information is not easily made unavailable, and the emerging research area of Machine Unlearning (MU) is highlighted as a potential solution.

2410.08811.title: PoisonBench: Assessing Large Language Model Vulnerability to Data Poisoning
2410.08811.tldr: PoisonBench is introduced, a benchmark for evaluating large language models' susceptibility to data poisoning during preference learning, exposing weaknesses in current preference learning techniques, highlighting the urgent need for more robust defenses against malicious models and data manipulation.

2505.22637.title: Understanding (Un)Reliability of Steering Vectors in Language Models
2505.22637.tldr: The influence of prompt types and the geometry of activation differences on steering reliability are studied to suggest that vector steering is unreliable when the target behavior is not represented by a coherent direction.

2411.01220.title: Enhancing Neural Network Interpretability with Feature-Aligned Sparse Autoencoders
2411.01220.tldr: The results suggest that the similarity between features learned by different SAEs can be leveraged to improve SAE training, thereby enhancing performance and the usefulness of SAEs for model interpretability.

2410.06981.title: Quantifying Feature Space Universality Across Large Language Models via Sparse Autoencoders
2410.06981.tldr: A new variation of the universality hypothesis called Analogous Feature Universality is introduced, which hypothesize that even if SAEs across different models learn different feature representations, the spaces spanned by SAE features are similar, such that one SAE space is similar to another SAE space under rotation-invariant transformations.

2505.22310.title: From Dormant to Deleted: Tamper-Resistant Unlearning Through Weight-Space Regularization
2505.22310.tldr: It is made the surprising discovery that forget-set accuracy can recover from around 50% post-unlearning to nearly 100% with fine-tuning on just the retain set -- i.e., zero examples of the forget set.

2412.00761.title: Learning to Forget using Hypernetworks
2412.00761.tldr: HyperForget is introduced, a novel machine unlearning framework that leverages hypernetworks - neural networks that generate parameters for other networks - to dynamically sample models that lack knowledge of targeted data while preserving essential capabilities.

2507.03068.title: Mitigating Goal Misgeneralization via Minimax Regret
2507.03068.tldr: It is shown that goal misgeneralization is possible under approximate optimization of the maximum expected value objective, but not the minimax expected regret (MMER) objective, and suggested that minimax expected regret is a promising approach to mitigating goal misgeneralization.

2310.02743.title: Reward Model Ensembles Help Mitigate Overoptimization
2310.02743.tldr: A systematic study to evaluate the efficacy of using ensemble-based conservative optimization objectives for mitigating reward model overoptimization when using two optimization methods, finding that conservative optimization practically eliminates overoptimization and improves performance by up to 70% for BoN sampling.

2310.08164.title: Interpreting Learned Feedback Patterns in Large Language Models
2310.08164.tldr: It is hypothesize that LLMs with LFPs accurately aligned to the fine-tuning feedback exhibit consistent activation patterns for outputs that would have received similar feedback during RLHF.

2512.08093.title: Training LLMs for Honesty via Confessions
2512.08093.tldr: This work proposes a method for eliciting an honest expression of an LLM's shortcomings via a self-reported confession, and finds that when the model lies or omits shortcomings in its"main"answer, it often confesses to these behaviors honestly, and this confession honesty modestly improves with training.

2512.20168.title: Odysseus: Jailbreaking Commercial Multimodal LLM-integrated Systems via Dual Steganography
2512.20168.tldr: Odysseus is a novel jailbreak paradigm that introduces dual steganography to covertly embed malicious queries and responses into benign-looking images, exposing a fundamental blind spot in existing defenses, and calling for rethinking cross-modal security in MLLM-integrated systems.

2510.13694.title: Information-Theoretic Reward Modeling for Stable RLHF: Detecting and Mitigating Reward Hacking

2603.15616.title: GlyphPrinter: Region-Grouped Direct Preference Optimization for Glyph-Accurate Visual Text Rendering
2603.15616.tldr: The proposed GlyphPrinter outperforms existing methods in glyph accuracy while maintaining a favorable balance between stylization and precision, and introduces Regional Reward Guidance, an inference strategy that samples from an optimal distribution with controllable glyph accuracy.

2606.13385.title: Who Pays the Price? Stakeholder-Centric Prompt Injection Benchmarking for Real-world Web Agents
2606.13385.tldr: StakeBench is introduced, a stakeholder-centric benchmark that systematically categorizes and attributes harm in real-world web agent systems for online shopping, and finds substantial and heterogeneous vulnerabilities in LLM-based web agents.

2511.12661.title: Reason-KE++: Aligning the Process, Not Just the Outcome, for Faithful LLM Knowledge Editing
2511.12661.tldr: Reason-KE++ is proposed, an SFT+RL framework that instills process-level faithfulness in Large Language Models, and identifies that naive outcome-only RL is a deceptive trap for LLM alignment: it collapses reasoning integrity while superficially boosting final accuracy.
2511.12661.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2608.04565.title: Breadcrumbing Search Agents
2608.04565.tldr: This work studies the channel delivering search and page observations is a fragile security boundary and introduces Authority-Chain Hijack (ACH), an expert-refined strategy that turns isolated search-result and page-content manipulations into a coherent evidence chain across seemingly corroborating sources.

2608.10933.title: SafeCA: Safe Cross-Attention Localization and Regulation for Text-to-Video Jailbreak Defense
2608.10933.tldr: This work experimentally and systematically analyzes the differences between clean and jailbreak samples in the cross-attention feature space, revealing for the first time a cumulative separation effect and a progressively increasing trend of linear separability between the two during the diffusion process.

2602.17168.title: BadCLIP++: Stealthy and Persistent Backdoors in Multimodal Contrastive Learning
2602.17168.tldr: This work introduces a semantic-fusion QR micro-trigger that embeds imperceptible patterns near task-relevant regions, preserving clean-data statistics while producing compact trigger distributions, and provides the first theoretical analysis showing that, within a trust region, gradients from clean fine-tuning and backdoor objectives are co-directional, yielding a non-increasing upper bound on attack success degradation.

2507.14417.title: Inverse Scaling in Test-Time Compute
2507.14417.tldr: Five distinct failure modes when models reason for longer are identified, suggesting that while test-time compute scaling remains promising for improving model capabilities, it may inadvertently reinforce problematic reasoning patterns.

2407.15211.title: Failures to Find Transferable Image Jailbreaks Between Vision-Language Models
2407.15211.tldr: A large-scale empirical study to assess the transferability of gradient-based universal image ``jailbreaks" using a diverse set of over 40 open-parameter VLMs finds that transferable gradient-based image jailbreaks are extremely difficult to obtain, suggesting that VLMs may be more robust to gradient-based transfer attacks.

2506.22777.title: Teaching Models to Verbalize Reward Hacking in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
2506.22777.tldr: VFT is proposed, a pre-RL fine-tuning intervention that trains models to explicitly acknowledge when they are influenced by prompt cues--hints which point to incorrect answers (e.g.,"a Stanford professor thinks the answer is A").

2511.02997.title: Evaluating Control Protocols for Untrusted AI Agents
2511.02997.tldr: This work systematically evaluate a range of control protocols in SHADE-Arena, a dataset of diverse agentic environments, finding that resampling for incrimination and deferring on critical actions perform best, and demonstrating the importance of denying attack policies access to protocol internals.

2511.02823.title: Optimizing AI Agent Attacks With Synthetic Data
2511.02823.tldr: This work shows how to optimize attack policies in SHADE-Arena, a dataset of diverse realistic control environments by decomposing attack capability into five constituent skills -- suspicion modeling, attack selection, plan synthesis, execution and subtlety -- and optimizing each component individually.

2605.24286.title: Faithfulness as Information Flow: Evaluating and Training Faithful Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
2605.24286.tldr: Across hinted arithmetic, reward-hackable code repair, and DAPO-Math models trained without hints but evaluated under wrong-hint injection, interventions shift behavioral and structural indicators toward stronger CoT mediation and improve task-agnostic faithfulness metrics, while in some settings also reducing wrong-hint susceptibility.

2210.01892.title: Polysemanticity and Capacity in Neural Networks
2210.01892.tldr: It is shown that in a toy model the optimal capacity allocation tends to monosemantically represent the most important features, polysemantically represent less important features (in proportion to their impact on the loss), and entirely ignore the least important features.

2412.03556.title: Best-of-N Jailbreaking
2412.03556.tldr: Best-of-N (BoN) Jailbreaking is introduced, a simple black-box algorithm that jailbreaks frontier AI systems across modalities and indicates that language models are sensitive to seemingly innocuous changes to inputs, which attackers can exploit across modalities.

2411.07494.title: Rapid Response: Mitigating LLM Jailbreaks with a Few Examples
2411.07494.tldr: This work develops RapidResponseBench, a benchmark that measures a defense's robustness against various jailbreak strategies after adapting to a few observed examples, and develops rapid response techniques to look to block whole classes of jailbreaks after observing only a handful of attacks.

2601.23045.title: The Hot Mess of AI: How Does Misalignment Scale With Model Intelligence and Task Complexity?
2601.23045.tldr: A future where AIs sometimes cause industrial accidents, but are less likely to exhibit consistent pursuit of a misaligned goal is suggested, suggesting a future where AIs sometimes cause industrial accidents, but are less likely to exhibit consistent pursuit of a misaligned goal.

2412.02159.title: Jailbreak Defense in a Narrow Domain: Limitations of Existing Methods and a New Transcript-Classifier Approach
2412.02159.tldr: This paper develops a transcript-classifier defense which outperforms the baseline defenses the authors test but still fails in some circumstances, which highlights the difficulty of jailbreak-defense even in a narrow domain.

2402.17747.title: When Your AIs Deceive You: Challenges of Partial Observability in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
2402.17747.tldr: Modeling the human as Boltzmann-rational w.r.t. a belief over trajectories, it is proved conditions under which RLHF is guaranteed to result in policies that deceptively inflate their performance, overjustify their behavior to make an impression, or both.

2502.21262.title: Modeling Human Beliefs about AI Behavior for Scalable Oversight
2502.21262.tldr: It is suggested that modeling human beliefs can improve value learning and outlines practical research directions for implementing this approach to scalable oversight.

2502.13295.title: Demonstrating specification gaming in reasoning models
2502.13295.tldr: This work demonstrates LLM agent specification gaming by instructing models to win against a chess engine and suggests reasoning models may resort to hacking to solve difficult problems, as observed in OpenAI (2024)'s o1 Docker escape during cyber capabilities testing.

2406.02619.title: Unelicitable Backdoors in Language Models via Cryptographic Transformer Circuits
2406.02619.tldr: By demonstrating the feasibility of seamlessly integrating backdoors into transformer models, this paper fundamentally questions the efficacy of pre-deployment detection strategies and offers new insights into the offence-defence balance in AI safety and security.

2104.12582.title: Understanding and Avoiding AI Failures: A Practical Guide
2104.12582.tldr: This work creates a framework for understanding the risks associated with AI applications, and uses AI safety principles to quantify the unique risks of increased intelligence and human-like qualities in AI.

2109.00484.title: Impossibility Results in AI: A Survey
2109.00484.tldr: This article categorized impossibility theorems applicable to AI into five mechanism-based categories: Deduction, indistinguishability, induction, tradeoffs, and intractability, and concluded that deductive impossibilities deny 100%-guarantees for security.

2402.16835.title: Eight Methods to Evaluate Robust Unlearning in LLMs
2402.16835.tldr: A comprehensive set of tests for the robustness and competitiveness of unlearning in the Who's Harry Potter (WHP) model from Eldan and Russinovich (2023) are applied and find higher-than-baseline amounts of knowledge can reliably be extracted.

2403.05030.title: Defending Against Unforeseen Failure Modes with Latent Adversarial Training
2403.05030.tldr: In image classification, text classification, and text generation tasks, it is shown that LAT usually improves both robustness to novel attacks and performance on clean data relative to AT, suggesting that LAT can be a promising tool for defending against failure modes that are not explicitly identified by developers.

2511.08594.title: Diverse Preference Learning for Capabilities and Alignment
2511.08594.tldr: This work proposes Soft Preference Learning, which decouples the entropy and cross-entropy terms in the KL penalty - allowing for fine-grained control over LLM generation diversity.

2502.05209.title: Model Tampering Attacks Enable More Rigorous Evaluations of LLM Capabilities
2502.05209.tldr: This work pits state-of-the-art techniques for removing harmful LLM capabilities against a suite of 5 input-space and 6 model tampering attacks and shows that model tampering attacks enable substantially more rigorous evaluations than input-space attacks alone.

2603.12277.title: Prompt Injection as Role Confusion
2603.12277.tldr: This work designs role probes to measure how LLMs internally perceive "who is speaking," and finds that injected text occupies the same representational space as the trusted role it imitates, revealing prompt injection as a measurable consequence of role perception.

2602.16080.title: Activation Steering via Generative Causal Mediation
2602.16080.tldr: Generative Causal Mediation, a procedure for selecting model components from contrastive long-form responses, to steer such diffuse concepts, successfully localizes concepts expressed in long-form responses and outperforms correlational probe-based baselines when steering with a sparse set of attention heads.

2505.09500.title: Layered Unlearning for Adversarial Relearning
2505.09500.tldr: An unlearning algorithm, Layered Unlearning (LU), that creates distinct inhibitory mechanisms for a growing subset of the data that improves robustness to adversarial relearning for several different unlearning methods and provides insight into the effect of post-training updates.

2312.08358.title: Distributional Preference Learning: Understanding and Accounting for Hidden Context in RLHF
2312.08358.tldr: This work proves that standard applications of preference learning, including reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), implicitly aggregate over hidden contexts according to a well-known voting rule called Borda count, and formalizes the way that preference learning from users with diverse values tacitly implements a social choice function.

2507.09060.title: CALMA: A Process for Deriving Context-aligned Axes for Language Model Alignment
2507.09060.tldr: CALMA (Context-aligned Axes for Language Model Alignment), a grounded, participatory methodology for eliciting context-relevant axes for evaluation and alignment, is introduced, demonstrating the value of evaluation practices based on open-ended and use-case-driven processes.

2605.27355.title: Alignment Tampering: How Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback Is Exploited to Optimize Misaligned Biases
2605.27355.tldr: This work introduces alignment tampering, a potential vulnerability where the LLM undergoing alignment influences the preference dataset, causing RLHF to amplify undesired behaviors and reveals structural vulnerabilities of current RLHF.

2209.02167.title: Red Teaming with Mind Reading: White-Box Adversarial Policies Against RL Agents
2209.02167.tldr: This work introduces white-box adversarial policies where an attacker observes both a target's internal state and the world state at each timestep and demonstrates that these policies can achieve higher initial and asymptotic performance against a target agent than black-box controls.

2211.10024.title: Diagnostics for Deep Neural Networks with Automated Copy/Paste Attacks
2211.10024.tldr: Search for Natural Adversarial Features Using Embeddings (SNAFUE) is introduced which offers a fully automated method for finding copy/paste attacks and hundreds of other easily-describable vulnerabilities, all without a human in the loop.

2302.10894.title: Red Teaming Deep Neural Networks with Feature Synthesis Tools
2302.10894.tldr: A key insight is that the authors can implant human-interpretable trojans into models and then evaluate these tools based on whether they can help humans discover them, analogous to finding OOD bugs, except the ground truth is known, allowing us to know when an interpretation is correct.

2306.09442.title: Explore, Establish, Exploit: Red Teaming Language Models from Scratch
2306.09442.tldr: This work considers red-teaming from scratch, in which the adversary does not begin with a way to classify failures, and uses this approach to red-team GPT-3 to discover classes of inputs that elicit false statements.

2102.03896.title: Consequences of Misaligned AI
2102.03896.tldr: This paper proposes a novel model of an incomplete principal-agent problem from artificial intelligence and provides necessary and sufficient conditions under which indefinitely optimizing for any incomplete proxy objective leads to arbitrarily low overall utility.

2406.18495.title: WildGuard: Open One-Stop Moderation Tools for Safety Risks, Jailbreaks, and Refusals of LLMs
2406.18495.tldr: WildGuard establishes state-of-the-art performance in open-source safety moderation across all the three tasks compared to ten strong existing open-source moderation models (e.g., up to 26.4% improvement on refusal detection).

2403.13787.title: RewardBench: Evaluating Reward Models for Language Modeling
2403.13787.tldr: The RewardBench dataset is a collection of prompt-chosen-rejected trios spanning chat, reasoning, and safety, to benchmark how reward models perform on challenging, structured and out-of-distribution queries and presents many findings on propensity for refusals, reasoning limitations, and instruction following shortcomings of various reward models towards a better understanding of the RLHF process.

2404.10271.title: Social Choice Should Guide AI Alignment in Dealing with Diverse Human Feedback
2404.10271.tldr: It is argued that the field of social choice is well positioned to address questions to address fine-tuning and constitutional AI, and ways forward for this agenda are discussed.

2504.12501.title: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
2504.12501.tldr: This book gives a comprehensive introduction to the core methods for post-training models for people with some level of quantitative background, organized around the canonical RLHF recipe.

2405.01511.title: D2PO: Discriminator-Guided DPO with Response Evaluation Models
2405.01511.tldr: D2PO, discriminator-guided DPO is proposed, an approach for the online setting where preferences are being collected throughout learning, and it is found that this approach leads to higher-quality outputs compared to DPO with the same data budget, and greater efficiency in terms of preference data requirements.

2311.00168.title: The Alignment Ceiling: Objective Mismatch in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
2311.00168.tldr: By solving objective mismatch in RLHF, the ML models of the future will be more precisely aligned to user instructions for both safety and helpfulness, which is described as an objective mismatch.

2310.13595.title: The History and Risks of Reinforcement Learning and Human Feedback
2310.13595.tldr: The complex history of optimizing preferences, the ontological differences between costs, rewards, and preferences at stake in RLHF's foundations, related methodological tensions, and possible research directions are highlighted to improve general understanding of how reward models function.

2507.00018.title: Implicit Reward as the Bridge: A Unified View of SFT and DPO Connections
2507.00018.tldr: A unified theoretical framework bridging Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and preference learning in Large Language Model (LLM) post-training is presented, demonstrating that both SFT and preference learning methods like Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) operate within the same optimal policy-reward subspace.

2508.21016.title: Inference-Time Alignment Control for Diffusion Models with Reinforcement Learning Guidance
2508.21016.tldr: Reinforcement Learning Guidance is introduced, an inference-time method that adapts Classifier-Free Guidance by combining the outputs of the base and RL fine-tuned models via a geometric average, thereby offering unprecedented flexibility in controlling generative alignment.

2510.00647.title: MCM-DPO: Multifaceted Cross-Modal Direct Preference Optimization for Alt-text Generation
2510.00647.tldr: Experimental results show that the proposed Multi-faceted Cross-modal Direct Preference Optimization (MCM-DPO) method consistently outperforms both DPO and SFT, establishing a new state of the-art in alt-text generation.

2605.17504.title: A Distributional View for Visual Mechanistic Interpretability: KL-Minimal Soft-Constraint Principle
2605.17504.tldr: A theoretical distributional view is established for visual MI, which models the influence of a feature activation on the natural image distribution, thereby formulating a Kullback-Leibler (KL)-minimal optimization problem to model the MI task.

2410.06672.title: Towards Universality: Studying Mechanistic Similarity Across Language Model Architectures
2410.06672.tldr: This work investigates two mainstream architectures for language modeling, namely Transformers and Mambas, to explore the extent of their mechanistic similarity and proposes to use Sparse Autoencoders to isolate interpretable features from these models and shows that most features are similar in these two models.

2504.20938.title: Towards Understanding the Nature of Attention with Low-Rank Sparse Decomposition
2504.20938.tldr: Low-Rank Sparse Attention (Lorsa) is designed to address the challenge of attention superposition to understand attention-mediated interaction between features in different token positions, and achieves parity with SAE in interpretability while Lorsa exhibits superior circuit discovery properties.

2405.13868.title: Automatically Identifying Local and Global Circuits with Linear Computation Graphs
2405.13868.tldr: This work introduces its circuit discovery pipeline with Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) and a variant called Transcoders and a variant called Transcoders, and analyzes three kinds of circuits in GPT-2 Small, revealing new findings underlying existing discoveries.

2503.04249.title: How to Mitigate Overfitting in Weak-to-strong Generalization?
2503.04249.tldr: A two-stage framework that simultaneously improves the quality of supervision signals and the quality of input questions is proposed that significantly improves PGR compared to naive weak-to-strong generalization, even achieving up to 100\% PGR on some models.
2503.04249.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2401.11206.title: InferAligner: Inference-Time Alignment for Harmlessness through Cross-Model Guidance
2401.11206.tldr: InferAligner decouples harmlessness from helpfulness, a simple yet effective method for harmlessness alignment during inference phase that significantly diminishes the attack success rate of both harmful instructions and jailbreak instructions, while maintaining almost unchanged performance in downstream tasks.
2401.11206.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2410.19750.title: The Geometry of Concepts: Sparse Autoencoder Feature Structure
2410.19750.tldr: This work quantifies the spatial locality of these lobes with multiple metrics and finds that clusters of co-occurring features, at coarse enough scale, also cluster together spatially far more than one would expect if feature geometry were random.

2410.14670.title: Decomposing The Dark Matter of Sparse Autoencoders
2410.14670.tldr: This work investigates dark matter as an object of study in its own right and finds that much of SAE dark matter -- about half of the error vector itself and>90% of its norm -- can be linearly predicted from the initial activation vector.

2410.08201.title: Efficient Dictionary Learning with Switch Sparse Autoencoders
2410.08201.tldr: This work introduces Switch Sparse Autoencoders, a novel SAE architecture aimed at reducing the compute cost of training SAEs, and finds that Switch SAEs deliver a substantial Pareto improvement in the reconstruction vs. sparsity frontier for a given fixed training compute budget.

2402.05110.title: Opening the AI black box: program synthesis via mechanistic interpretability
2402.05110.tldr: MIPS uses an integer autoencoder to convert the RNN into a finite state machine, then applies Boolean or integer symbolic regression to capture the learned algorithm in Python code, auto-distilling the learned algorithm into Python code.

2506.15679.title: Dense SAE Latents Are Features, Not Bugs
2506.15679.tldr: It is demonstrated that dense latents tend to form antipodal pairs that reconstruct specific directions in the residual stream, and that ablating their subspace suppresses the emergence of new dense features in retrained SAEs -- suggesting that high density features are an intrinsic property of the residual space.

2504.18530.title: Scaling Laws For Scalable Oversight
2504.18530.tldr: This framework proposes a framework that quantifies the probability of successful oversight as a function of the capabilities of the overseer and the system being overseen, and identifies conditions under which NSO succeeds and derive numerically the optimal number of oversight levels to maximize the probability of oversight success.

2501.19406.title: Low-Rank Adapting Models for Sparse Autoencoders
2501.19406.tldr: The results demonstrate that improving model interpretability is not limited to post-hoc SAE training; Pareto improvements can also be achieved by directly optimizing the model itself.

2606.08629.title: Sycophancy Towards Researchers Drives Performative Misalignment
2606.08629.tldr: An alternative interpretation, performative misalignment, is examined, which explains the change in behavior as a result of sycophancy towards AI researchers, and deconfounding sycophancy from scheming is emphasized for future work on evaluations and mitigations of intent misalignment.

2305.08746.title: Seeing is Believing: Brain-Inspired Modular Training for Mechanistic Interpretability
2305.08746.tldr: It is demonstrated that BIMT discovers useful modular neural networks for many simple tasks, revealing compositional structures in symbolic formulas, interpretable decision boundaries and features for classification, and mathematical structure in algorithmic datasets.

2309.01933.title: Provably safe systems: the only path to controllable AGI
2309.01933.tldr: A path to humanity safely thriving with powerful Artificial General Intelligences by building them to provably satisfy human-specified requirements is described and it is argued that this will soon be technically feasible using advanced AI for formal verification and mechanistic interpretability.

2312.03051.title: Generating Interpretable Networks using Hypernetworks
2312.03051.tldr: This work explores the possibility of using hypernetworks to generate interpretable networks whose underlying algorithms are not yet known, and shows that a trained hypernetwork can correctly construct models for input dimensions not seen in training, demonstrating systematic generalization.

2201.08102.title: Safe Deep RL in 3D Environments using Human Feedback
2201.08102.tldr: This paper uses ReQueST to train an agent to perform a 3D first-person object collection task using data entirely from human contractors, and shows that the resulting agent exhibits an order of magnitude reduction in unsafe behaviour compared to standard reinforcement learning.

2503.07341.title: The Economics of p(doom): Scenarios of Existential Risk and Economic Growth in the Age of Transformative AI

2311.07723.title: Generalization Analogies: A Testbed for Generalizing AI Oversight to Hard-To-Measure Domains
2311.07723.tldr: It is found that reward models do not learn to evaluate `instruction-following' by default and instead favor personas that resemble internet text and the 15 most challenging distribution shifts are consolidated into the GENeralization analogIES (GENIES) benchmark, which is hoped to enable progress toward controlling reward model generalization.

2206.09360.title: Modeling Transformative AI Risks (MTAIR) Project -- Summary Report
2206.09360.tldr: This report outlines work by the Modeling Transformative AI Risk (MTAIR) project, an attempt to map out the key hypotheses, uncertainties, and disagreements in debates about catastrophic risks from advanced AI, and the relationships between them.

2310.14455.title: An International Consortium for Evaluations of Societal-Scale Risks from Advanced AI
2310.14455.tldr: An international consortium for advanced AI risk evaluations is proposed, comprising both AI developers and third-party AI risk evaluators, which could play a critical role in international efforts to mitigate societal-scale risks from advanced AI.

2603.05167.title: C2-Faith: Benchmarking LLM Judges for Causal and Coverage Faithfulness in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
2603.05167.tldr: C2-Faith is introduced, a benchmark built from PRM800K that explicitly decomposes faithfulness into two complementary dimensions: causality and coverage, and reveals that judge reliability is highly task-dependent, with no single model dominating across settings.

2512.15688.title: BashArena: A Control Setting for Highly Privileged AI Agents
2512.15688.tldr: This work evaluates multiple frontier LLMs on their ability to complete tasks, perform sabotage undetected, and detect sabotage attempts in BashArena, a setting for studying AI control techniques in security-critical environments.

2602.04930.title: Attack Selection Reduces Safety in Concentrated AI Control Settings against Trusted Monitoring
2602.04930.tldr: It is found that prompting the attacker model to reason about the monitor while being cautious with attack selection reduces safety from a baseline of 99% to 59% at 0.5% auditing budget, emphasizing that eliciting attack selection capabilities of models is vital to avoid overly optimistic safety scores in control evaluations.

2605.09684.title: MonitoringBench: Semi-Automated Red-Teaming for Agent Monitoring

2606.06529.title: Attack Selection in Agentic AI Control Evaluations Meaningfully Decreases Safety
2606.06529.tldr: This work decomposes attack decisions into a start policy, which decides when an attacker should attack, and a stop policy, which decides when an attacker should abort an ongoing attack, and concludes that both policies substantially lower measured empirical safety without changing the underlying attack capability.

2405.15943.title: Transformers represent belief state geometry in their residual stream
2405.15943.tldr: This work anticipates and then finds that belief states are linearly represented in the residual stream of transformers, even in cases where the predicted belief state geometry has highly nontrivial fractal structure.

2406.04093.title: Scaling and evaluating sparse autoencoders
2406.04093.tldr: This work proposes using k-sparse autoencoders to directly control sparsity, simplifying tuning and improving the reconstruction-sparsity frontier, and introduces several new metrics for evaluating feature quality based on the recovery of hypothesized features, the explainability of activation patterns, and the sparsity of downstream effects that generally improve with autoencoder size.

2407.00215.title: LLM Critics Help Catch LLM Bugs
2407.00215.tldr: It is confirmed that the fine-tuned LLM critics can successfully identify hundreds of errors in ChatGPT training data rated as"flawless", even though the majority of those tasks are non-code tasks and thus out-of-distribution for the critic model.

2312.09390.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization: Eliciting Strong Capabilities With Weak Supervision
2312.09390.tldr: The results suggest that it is feasible to make empirical progress today on a fundamental challenge of aligning superhuman models, and that techniques like RLHF may scale poorly to superhuman models without further work.

2109.10862.title: Recursively Summarizing Books with Human Feedback
2109.10862.tldr: This method combines learning from human feedback with recursive task decomposition: it uses models trained on smaller parts of the task to assist humans in giving feedback on the broader task, and generates sensible summaries of entire books.

2406.07814.title: Collective Constitutional AI: Aligning a Language Model with Public Input
2406.07814.tldr: This work creates what is, to their knowledge, the first LM fine-tuned with collectively sourced public input and evaluates this model against a baseline model trained with established principles from a LM developer, demonstrating a promising, tractable pathway toward publicly informed development of language models.
2406.07814.venue: Conference on Fairness, Accountability and Transparency

2310.04373.title: Confronting Reward Model Overoptimization with Constrained RLHF
2310.04373.tldr: This paper performs the first study on overoptimization in composite RMs, showing that correlation between component RMs has a significant effect on the locations of these points, and introduces an approach using constrained reinforcement learning as a means of preventing the agent from exceeding each RM's threshold of usefulness.

2401.03529.title: Quantifying stability of non-power-seeking in artificial agents
2401.03529.tldr: A quantitative bound on how fast the probability of not shutting down can increase is demonstrated by defining a metric on MDPs; proving that the probability of not shutting down, as a function on MDPs, is lower semicontinuous; and bounding how quickly this function decreases.

2607.08066.title: Persuasion Attacks Can Decrease Effectiveness of CoT Monitoring
2607.08066.tldr: The results demonstrate that CoT monitoring alone may be insufficient against adversarial persuasion, and that model-diverse fact-checking provides a robust mitigation, and that model-diverse fact-checking provides a robust mitigation.

2304.06528.title: Power-seeking can be probable and predictive for trained agents
2304.06528.tldr: It is shown that power-seeking incentives can be probable (likely to arise for trained agents) and predictive (allowing us to predict undesirable behavior in new situations).

2409.07985.title: Games for AI Control: Models of Safety Evaluations of AI Deployment Protocols
2409.07985.tldr: This paper introduces AI-Control Games, a formal decision-making model of the red-teaming exercise as a multi-objective, partially observable, stochastic game, and applies this formalism to model, evaluate and synthesise protocols for deploying untrusted language models as programming assistants.

2405.17894.title: White-box Multimodal Jailbreaks Against Large Vision-Language Models
2405.17894.tldr: A universal attack strategy that jointly attacks both text and image modalities to exploit a broader spectrum of vulnerability within VLMs and can effectively jailbreak MiniGPT-4 with a 96% success rate, highlighting the fragility of VLMs and the exigency for new alignment strategies.

2408.12798.title: BackdoorLLM: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Backdoor Attacks and Defenses on Large Language Models
2408.12798.tldr: BackdoorLLM is the first comprehensive benchmark for systematically evaluating backdoor threats in text-generation LLMs and provides a diverse suite of attack modalities, including data poisoning, weight poisoning, hidden-state manipulation, and chain-of-thought hijacking.

2411.00827.title: IDEATOR: Jailbreaking and Benchmarking Large Vision-Language Models Using Themselves
2411.00827.tldr: This paper proposes IDEATOR, a novel jailbreak method that autonomously generates malicious image-text pairs for black-box jailbreak attacks and introduces the VLJailbreakBench, a safety benchmark comprising 3,654 multimodal jailbreak samples.
2411.00827.venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision

2410.20971.title: BlueSuffix: Reinforced Blue Teaming for Vision-Language Models Against Jailbreak Attacks
2410.20971.tldr: This paper proposes a novel blue-team method BlueSuffix that defends target VLMs against jailbreak attacks without compromising its performance under black-box setting and empirically shows that BlueSuffix outperforms the baseline defenses by a significant margin.

2410.09909.title: UnSeg: One Universal Unlearnable Example Generator is Enough against All Image Segmentation
2410.09909.tldr: This work proposes a novel Unlearnable Segmentation (UnSeg) framework to train a universal unlearnable noise generator that is capable of transforming any downstream images into their unlearnable version.

2511.12149.title: AttackVLA: Benchmarking Adversarial and Backdoor Attacks on Vision-Language-Action Models
2511.12149.tldr: BackdoorVLA is introduced, a targeted backdoor attack that compels a VLA to execute an attacker-specified long-horizon action sequence whenever a trigger is present, providing a standardized framework for evaluating VLA vulnerabilities and demonstrating the potential for precise adversarial manipulation.

2604.02947.title: AgentHazard: A Benchmark for Evaluating Harmful Behavior in Computer-Use Agents
2604.02947.tldr: The benchmark evaluates whether agents can recognize and interrupt harm arising from accumulated context, repeated tool use, intermediate actions, and dependencies across steps, and indicates that current systems remain highly vulnerable.

2505.19610.title: JailBound: Jailbreaking Internal Safety Boundaries of Vision-Language Models
2505.19610.tldr: JailBound is a novel latent space jailbreak framework comprising two stages: Safety Boundary Probing, which addresses the guidance issue by approximating decision boundary within fusion layer's latent space, thereby identifying optimal perturbation directions towards the target region; and Safety Boundary Crossing, which overcomes the limitations of decoupled approaches by jointly optimizing adversarial perturbations across both image and text inputs.

2601.04566.title: BackdoorAgent: A Unified Framework for Backdoor Attacks on LLM-based Agents
2601.04566.tldr: A modular and stage-aware framework that provides a unified, agent-centric view of backdoor threats in LLM agents, and a standardized benchmark spanning four representative agent applications, covering both language-only and multimodal settings.
2601.04566.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2511.16709.title: AutoBackdoor: Automating Backdoor Attacks via LLM Agents
2511.16709.tldr: This work introduces AutoBackdoor, a general framework for automating backdoor injection, encompassing trigger generation, poisoned data construction, and model fine-tuning via an autonomous agent-driven pipeline, and demonstrates that the method achieves over 90% attack success with only a small number of poisoned samples.

2511.12710.title: Evolve the Method, Not the Prompts: Evolutionary Synthesis of Jailbreak Attacks on LLMs
2511.12710.tldr: EvoSynth is an autonomous multi-agent framework that shifts the optimization space from prompts to executable code, and features a code-level self-correction loop, allowing it to iteratively rewrite the code-based algorithm in response to target-model feedback and failed attempts.

2510.27484.title: Thought Branches: Interpreting LLM Reasoning Requires Resampling
2510.27484.tldr: It is found that hints that causally affect the output without being explicitly mentioned exert a subtle and cumulative influence on the CoT that persists even if the hint is removed.

2507.08218.title: Simple Mechanistic Explanations for Out-Of-Context Reasoning
2507.08218.tldr: This work investigates this phenomenon mechanistically and finds that many instances of OOCR in the literature have a simple explanation: the LoRA fine-tuning essentially adds a constant steering vector, steering the model towards a general concept.

2605.24229.title: How Well Do Models Follow Their Constitutions?
2605.24229.tldr: A multi-method audit pipeline that treats each lab's published specification as an auditable target finds that models follow their own lab's specification substantially better with each generation.

2506.11618.title: Convergent Linear Representations of Emergent Misalignment
2506.11618.tldr: This work train and study a minimal model organism which uses just 9 rank-1 adapters to emergently misalign Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, and finds that different emergently misaligned models converge to similar representations of misalignment.

2506.11613.title: Model Organisms for Emergent Misalignment
2506.11613.tldr: This work creates a set of improved model organisms that achieve 99% coherence, and isolates a mechanistic phase transition that corresponds to a robust behavioural phase transition in all studied organisms, establishing a foundation for future research into understanding and mitigating alignment risks in LLMs.

2602.07852.title: Emergent Misalignment is Easy, Narrow Misalignment is Hard
2602.07852.tldr: It is found that models can just learn the narrow dataset task, but that the general solution appears to be more stable and more efficient, and a linear representation of the narrow solution also exists, and can be learned by introducing a KL divergence loss.

2209.05459.title: How Do AI Timelines Affect Existential Risk?
2209.05459.tldr: Delaying the creation of superintelligent AI (ASI) could decrease total existential risk by increasing the amount of time humanity has to work on the AI alignment problem, but since ASI could reduce most risks, delays could also increase other existential risks, especially from advanced future technologies such as synthetic biology and molecular nanotechnology.

2406.07358.title: AI Sandbagging: Language Models can Strategically Underperform on Evaluations
2406.07358.tldr: This paper prompts frontier LMs, like GPT-4 and Claude 3 Opus, to selectively underperform on dangerous capability evaluations, while maintaining performance on general capability evaluations, and finds that models can be fine-tuned, on a synthetic dataset, to hide specific capabilities unless given a password.

2502.02180.title: The Elicitation Game: Evaluating Capability Elicitation Techniques
2502.02180.tldr: A novel method for training model organisms, based on circuit-breaking, is introduced, which is more robust to elicitation techniques than standard password-locked models and should be the method of choice to improve the trustworthiness of capability evaluations.

2512.00218.title: Reasoning Under Pressure: How do Training Incentives Influence Chain-of-Thought Monitorability?
2512.00218.tldr: This work introduces a novel methodology for measuring monitorability according to whether a monitor can predict a key latent variable using the model's reasoning, and finds that adversarial optimisation (penalising monitor accuracy) degrades monitor performance, while direct optimisation for monitorability does not reliably lead to improvements.

2606.12268.title: The Impossibility of Eliciting Latent Knowledge
2606.12268.tldr: An impossibility theorem is proved stating: There is no feedback-based training strategy that depends only on agent behaviour and with certainty produces an honest agent, even if feedback is perfect during training.

2312.01350.title: Honesty Is the Best Policy: Defining and Mitigating AI Deception
2312.01350.tldr: This work introduces a formal definition of deception in structural causal games, grounded in the philosophy literature, and applicable to real-world machine learning systems.

2512.03089.title: Password-Activated Shutdown Protocols for Misaligned Frontier Agents
2512.03089.tldr: This work introduces password-activated shutdown protocols (PAS protocols) -- methods for designing frontier agents to implement a safe shutdown protocol when given a password, and encourages developers to consider implementing PAS protocols prior to internal deployment of particularly dangerous systems to reduce loss-of-control risks.

2304.12918.title: N2G: A Scalable Approach for Quantifying Interpretable Neuron Representations in Large Language Models
2304.12918.tldr: N2G represents a step towards scalable interpretability methods by allowing us to convert neurons in an LLM to interpretable representations of measurable quality.

2305.19911.title: Neuron to Graph: Interpreting Language Model Neurons at Scale
2305.19911.tldr: This paper introduces Neuron to Graph (N2G), an innovative tool that automatically extracts a neuron's behaviour from the dataset it was trained on and translates it into an interpretable graph and can be visualised to aid researchers' manual interpretation.

2410.00081.title: From homeostasis to resource sharing: Biologically and economically aligned multi-objective multi-agent gridworld-based AI safety benchmarks
2410.00081.tldr: This work focuses on introducing biologically and economically motivated themes that have been neglected in current mainstream discussions on AI safety - namely a set of multi-objective, multi-agent alignment benchmarks that emphasize homeostasis for bounded and biological objectives, diminishing returns for unbounded, instrumental, and business objectives, sustainability principle, and resource sharing.

2509.02655.title: BioBlue: Systematic runaway-optimiser-like LLM failure modes on biologically and economically aligned AI safety benchmarks for LLMs with simplified observation format
2509.02655.tldr: It is found that, although LLMs frequently behave appropriately for many steps and clearly understand the stated objectives, they often lose context in structured ways and drift into runaway behaviours: ignoring homeostatic targets, collapsing from multi-objective trade-offs into single-objective maximisation - thus failing to respect concave utility structures.

2505.04592.title: AI Governance to Avoid Extinction: The Strategic Landscape and Actionable Research Questions
2505.04592.tldr: Urgent action is needed from the US National Security community and AI governance ecosystem to answer key research questions, build the capability to halt dangerous AI activities, and prepare for international AI agreements.

2511.10783.title: An International Agreement to Prevent the Premature Creation of Artificial Superintelligence
2511.10783.tldr: An international agreement to prevent the premature development of ASI until AI development can proceed without these risks is proposed, which would be technically sufficient to forestall the development of ASI if implemented today.

2509.05361.title: Constitutional Law and AI Governance: Constraints on Model Licensing and Research Classification
2509.05361.tldr: This paper examines how the First Amendment, administrative law, and the Fourteenth Amendment shape the legal vulnerability of two regulatory proposals: model licensing and AI research classification.

2407.04108.title: Future Events as Backdoor Triggers: Investigating Temporal Vulnerabilities in LLMs
2407.04108.tldr: It is shown that current large language models (LLMs) can distinguish past from future events, with probes on model activations achieving 90% accuracy and an activation-steering vector representing a model's internal representation of the date influences the rate of backdoor activation.

2504.03731.title: A Benchmark for Scalable Oversight Protocols
2504.03731.tldr: The scalable oversight benchmark is introduced, a principled framework for evaluating human feedback mechanisms based on the authors' agent score difference (ASD) metric, a measure of how effectively a mechanism advantages truth-telling over deception.

2606.30252.title: Inoculation Adapters: Improved Selective Generalization of Capabilities with Fewer Surprising Backdoors
2606.30252.tldr: Across nine setups and five model families, the inoculation adapter family spans a new Pareto frontier of desired trait retention vs. undesired trait suppression, although given wide confidence intervals the magnitude of improvement remains uncertain.

2605.29358.title: Scaling Monosemanticity: Extracting Interpretable Features from Claude 3 Sonnet

2402.06627.title: Feedback Loops With Language Models Drive In-Context Reward Hacking
2402.06627.tldr: It is shown that feedback loops can cause in-context reward hacking (ICRH), where the LLM at test-time optimizes a (potentially implicit) objective but creates negative side effects in the process.

2406.19501.title: Monitoring Latent World States in Language Models with Propositional Probes
2406.19501.tldr: This work hypothesizes that language models represent their input contexts in a latent world model, and seeks to extract this latent world state from the activations of these models with 'propositional probes', which compositionally probe tokens for lexical information and bind them into logical propositions representing the world state.

2601.22594.title: Language Model Circuits Are Sparse in the Neuron Basis
