2602.17088.title: MeGU: Machine-Guided Unlearning with Target Feature Disentanglement
2602.17088.tldr: The proposed Machine-Guided Unlearning (MeGU), a novel framework that guides unlearning through concept-aware re-alignment through Multi-modal Large Language Models, which enables controlled and selective forgetting, effectively mitigating both under-unlearning and over-unlearning.

2608.00716.title: Generated Images Are Easier to Forget: A Machine Unlearning Perspective for Synthetic Image Detection
2608.00716.tldr: This work establishes a new paradigm for generated image detection by recasting the detection task as a problem of machine unlearning, and introduces two detection methods: data-free detection, which prunes model parameters to induce unlearning without data access, and data-driven detection, which optimizes LVMs to unlearn knowledge tied to generated images.

2503.17198.title: Jailbreaking the Non-Transferable Barrier via Test-Time Data Disguising
2503.17198.tldr: This work reveals the first loophole of black-box NTL models by proposing a novel attack method (dubbed as JailNTL) to jailbreak the non-transferable barrier through test-time data disguising.

2504.14177.title: Direct Advantage Regression: Aligning LLMs with Online AI Reward
2504.14177.tldr: This paper proposes Direct Advantage Regression (DAR), a simple alignment algorithm using online AI reward to optimize policy improvement through weighted supervised fine-tuning that maintains theoretical consistency with online RLHF pipelines while significantly reducing implementation complexity and improving learning efficiency.

2509.21029.title: FORCE: Transferable Visual Jailbreaking Attacks via Feature Over-Reliance CorrEction
2509.21029.tldr: A Feature Over-Reliance CorrEction (FORCE) method, which guides the attack to explore broader feasible regions across layer features and rescales the influence of frequency features according to their semantic content, thereby improving cross-model transferability.

2602.11902.title: Mitigating Mismatch within Reference-based Preference Optimization

2606.12809.title: MLUBench: A Benchmark for Lifelong Unlearning Evaluation in MLLMs
2606.12809.tldr: This work introduces the MLUBench, a large-scale and comprehensive benchmark featuring 127 entities across 9 classes under lifelong unlearning requests and proposes LUMoE, an effective method that significantly mitigates the degradation problem faced by baselines.

2506.00195.title: Let Them Down Easy! Contextual Effects of LLM Guardrails on User Perceptions and Preferences
2506.00195.tldr: This work demonstrates that effective guardrails require focusing on crafting thoughtful refusals rather than detecting intent, offering a path toward AI safety mechanisms that ensure both safety and sustained user engagement.
2506.00195.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2305.14718.title: Leftover Lunch: Advantage-based Offline Reinforcement Learning for Language Models
2305.14718.tldr: Advantage-Leftover Lunch RL (A-LoL), a new class of offline policy gradient algorithms that enable RL training on any pre-existing data and is an easy-to-implement, sample-efficient, and stable LM training recipe.

2210.01478.title: When to Make Exceptions: Exploring Language Models as Accounts of Human Moral Judgment
2210.01478.tldr: A novel moral chain of thought (MORALCOT) prompting strategy that combines the strengths of LLMs with theories of moral reasoning developed in cognitive science to predict human moral judgments, suggesting that modeling human reasoning might be necessary to capture the flexibility of the human moral mind.

2411.18688.title: Immune: Improving Safety Against Jailbreaks in Multi-modal LLMs via Inference-Time Alignment
2411.18688.tldr: This work proposes Immune, an inference-time defense framework that leverages a safety reward model through controlled decoding to defend against jailbreak attacks, and provides a mathematical characterization of Immune, offering insights on why it improves safety against jailbreaks.

2503.21720.title: Collab: Controlled Decoding using Mixture of Agents for LLM Alignment
2503.21720.tldr: Comprehensive empirical evaluations with open-source aligned models on diverse tasks and preferences demonstrate the merits of this approach over single-agent decoding baselines, which demonstrates the merits of this approach over single-agent decoding baselines.

2410.13828.title: A Common Pitfall of Margin-based Language Model Alignment: Gradient Entanglement
2410.13828.tldr: This paper identifies a common pitfall of margin-based methods -- the under-specification of ideal LM behavior on preferred and dispreferred responses individually, which leads to two unintended consequences as the margin increases, and derives conditions for general margin-based alignment objectives under which gradient entanglement becomes concerning.

2505.17122.title: Shallow Preference Signals: Large Language Model Aligns Even Better with Truncated Data?
2505.17122.tldr: This work identifies a crucial property of the existing learning method: the distinguishing signal obtained in preferred responses is often concentrated in the early tokens, referred to as shallow preference signals, which highlights potential issues in LLM alignment.

2510.13022.title: On the Role of Preference Variance in Preference Optimization
2510.13022.tldr: This work establishes an upper bound on the DPO gradient norm for any given prompt, showing it is controlled by the PVar of that prompt, which implies that prompts with low PVar can only produce small gradient updates, making them less valuable for learning.

2412.05232.title: LIAR: Leveraging Inference Time Alignment (Best-of-N) to Jailbreak LLMs in Seconds
2412.05232.tldr: LIAR (Leveraging Inference-time misalignment to jailbReak), a fast, black-box, best-of-$N$ sampling attack requiring no training, is introduced and offers a simple yet effective tool for evaluating LLM robustness and advancing alignment research.

2502.04306.title: ScoreFlow: Mastering LLM Agent Workflows via Score-based Preference Optimization
2502.04306.tldr: This work introduces ScoreFlow, a simple yet high-performance framework that leverages efficient gradient-based optimization in a continuous space and incorporates Score-DPO, a novel variant of the direct preference optimization method that accounts for quantitative feedback.

2406.04031.title: Jailbreak Vision Language Models via Bi-Modal Adversarial Prompt
2406.04031.tldr: The Bi-Modal Adversarial Prompt Attack (BAP) is introduced, which executes jailbreaks by optimizing textual and visual prompts cohesively and significantly outperforms other methods by large margins.
2406.04031.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security

2502.11054.title: Reasoning-Augmented Conversation for Multi-Turn Jailbreak Attacks on Large Language Models
2502.11054.tldr: Reasoning-Augmented Conversation is proposed, a novel multi-turn jailbreak framework that reformulates harmful queries into benign reasoning tasks and leverages LLMs' strong reasoning capabilities to compromise safety alignment and achieves state-of-the-art attack effectiveness in complex conversational scenarios.
2502.11054.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2504.14348.title: Manipulating Multimodal Agents via Cross-Modal Prompt Injection
2504.14348.tldr: This paper proposes CrossInject, a novel attack framework in which attacker embeds adversarial perturbations across multiple modalities to align with target malicious content, allowing external instructions to hijack the agents' decision-making process and execute unauthorized tasks.

2406.06302.title: Unveiling the Safety of GPT-4o: An Empirical Study using Jailbreak Attacks
2406.06302.tldr: This paper adopts a series of multi-modal and uni-modal jailbreak attacks on 4 commonly used benchmarks encompassing three modalities encompassing three modalities, and conducts a rigorous evaluation of GPT-4o against jailbreak attacks.

2406.13098.title: DLP: towards active defense against backdoor attacks with decoupled learning process
2406.13098.tldr: This study shows that the model shows different learning behaviors in clean and poisoned subsets during training, and proposes a general training pipeline to defend against backdoor attacks actively.

2509.06350.title: Mask-GCG: Are All Tokens in Adversarial Suffixes Necessary for Jailbreak Attacks?
2509.06350.tldr: This work proposes Mask-GCG, a plug-and-play method that employs learnable token masking to identify impactful tokens within the suffix of Greedy Coordinate Gradient, and shows that most tokens in the suffix contribute significantly to attack success, and pruning a minority of low-impact tokens does not affect the loss values or compromise the attack success rate.
2509.06350.venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing

2507.21540.title: PRISM: Programmatic Reasoning with Image Sequence Manipulation for LVLM Jailbreaking
2507.21540.tldr: This work proposes a novel and effective jailbreak framework inspired by Return-Oriented Programming (ROP) techniques from software security, which decomposes a harmful instruction into a sequence of individually benign visual gadgets that makes the malicious intent emergent and difficult to detect from any single component.

2606.31227.title: Securing the AI Agent: A Unified Framework for Multi-Layer Agent Red Teaming
2606.31227.tldr: AI-Infra-Guard is presented, an open-source framework that organizes AI red teaming around a single observation, and is the only open-source framework to span all of these, including supply-chain auditing of the agent skills that increasingly extend AI agents.

2503.06989.title: Probabilistic Modeling of Jailbreak on Multimodal LLMs: From Quantification to Application
2503.06989.tldr: This work proposes Jailbreak-Probability-based Attack (JPA) that optimizes adversarial perturbations on input image to maximize jailbreak probability, and proposes Jailbreak-Probability-based Finetuning (JPF), which minimizes jailbreak probability through MLLM parameter updates.

2510.15068.title: Sequential Comics for Jailbreaking Multimodal Large Language Models via Structured Visual Storytelling
2510.15068.tldr: This work introduces a novel method that leverages sequential comic-style visual narratives to circumvent safety alignments in state-of-the-art MLLMs and demonstrates superior effectiveness across diverse categories of harmful content.

2511.13127.title: SPARK: Jailbreaking T2V Models by Synergistically Prompting Auditory and Recontextualized Knowledge
2511.13127.tldr: SPARK is proposed, a jailbreak framework that leverages T2V models cross-modal associative patterns via a modular prompt design and formalizes attack generation as a constrained optimization over the above modular prompt space and solves it with a guided search procedure that balances stealth and effectiveness.

2603.07028.title: Two Frames Matter: A Temporal Attack for Text-to-Video Model Jailbreaking
2603.07028.tldr: A temporal trajectory infilling vulnerability of T2V systems under fragmented prompts is identified: when the prompt specifies only sparse boundary conditions and leaves the intermediate evolution underspecified, the model may autonomously reconstruct a plausible trajectory that includes harmful intermediate frames, despite the prompt appearing benign to input or output side filtering.

2605.01761.title: TrajShield: Trajectory-Level Safety Mediation for Defending Text-to-Video Models Against Jailbreak Attacks
2605.01761.tldr: Experiments demonstrate that TrajShield achieves state-of-the-art defenseive performance while maintaining high semantic fidelity, substantially outperforming existing defenses, with an average ASR reduction of 52.44\%.

2605.18915.title: DMN: A Compositional Framework for Jailbreaking Multimodal LLMs with Multi-Image Inputs
2605.18915.tldr: A compositional jailbreak framework, DMN, which leveragesributed instruction,ultimodal evidence and aumber chain task to fully enhance the jailbreak performance, and reveals fundamental weaknesses in their safety mechanisms.
2605.18915.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2607.17779.title: Dynamic Defense Profiling Enables Cognitive Jailbreak of Text-to-Image Models
2607.17779.tldr: This paper proposes MIND, a cognitive jailbreak framework that reframes adversarial prompt generation as a belief-state inference problem over latent defense mechanisms and actively models the target system's latent defense mechanisms by interpreting multi-modal feedback as high-density signals.

2608.16393.title: Security Assessment of DeepSeek Harness with A.I.G: Evaluating Resistance to Indirect Prompt Injection
2608.16393.tldr: This work assesses indirect prompt injection in DeepSeek Harness, using AI-Infra-Guard (A.I.G) to construct tests, deliver controlled taint, execute DSH, collect traces, and judge outcomes, and relates these results to DSH's treatment of tool results, additional contexts, and tool-call policy hooks.

2402.14872.title: Semantic Mirror Jailbreak: Genetic Algorithm Based Jailbreak Prompts Against Open-source LLMs
2402.14872.tldr: A Semantic Mirror Jailbreak (SMJ) approach that bypasses LLMs by generating jailbreak prompts that are semantically similar to the original question is introduced and is resistant to defenses that use those metrics as thresholds.

2504.15512.title: T2VShield: Model-Agnostic Jailbreak Defense for Text-to-Video Models
2504.15512.tldr: A human centered audiovisual evaluation protocol to assess perceptual safety is developed, emphasizing the importance of visual level defense in enhancing the trustworthiness of next generation multimodal simulators.

2505.06679.title: T2V-OptJail: Discrete Prompt Optimization for Text-to-Video Jailbreak Attacks
2505.06679.tldr: This work is the first to formalize the T2V jailbreak attack as a discrete optimization problem and proposes a joint objective-based optimization framework, called T2V-OptJail, which consists of two key optimization goals: bypassing the built-in safety filtering mechanisms to increase the attack success rate and preserving semantic consistency between the adversarial prompt and the unsafe input prompt.

2508.06963.title: MASteer: Multi-Agent Adaptive Steer Strategy for End-to-End LLM Trustworthiness Repair
2508.06963.tldr: MASteer is proposed, the first end-to-end framework for trustworthiness repair in LLMs based on representation engineering, which demonstrates strong robustness, generalization, and practical value for scalable, efficient trustworthiness repair.

2311.12075.title: BadCLIP: Dual-Embedding Guided Backdoor Attack on Multimodal Contrastive Learning
2311.12075.tldr: The BadCLIP attack is introduced, which is resistant to backdoor detection and model fine-tuning defenses and draws motivations from the perspective of the Bayesian rule and proposes a dual-embedding guided framework for backdoor attacks.

2507.00841.title: SafeMobile: Chain-level Jailbreak Detection and Automated Evaluation for Multimodal Mobile Agents
2507.00841.tldr: This work explores the security issues surrounding mobile multimodal agents, attempts to construct a risk discrimination mechanism by incorporating behavioral sequence information, and designs an automated assisted assessment scheme based on a large language model.

2501.16531.title: Guardrails versus Gatekeepers: Understanding Product Managers' Ethical Decision-Making in Generative AI
2501.16531.tldr: It is shown that individual actors are able to exhibit agency through some meaningful, low resource actions, even in the absence of organizational incentive structures even in the absence of organizational incentives, though this alone is insufficient to operationalize responsible AI at scale.
2501.16531.venue: Conference on Fairness, Accountability and Transparency

2404.00629.title: Against The Achilles' Heel: A Survey on Red Teaming for Generative Models
2404.00629.tldr: This extensive survey, which examines over 120 papers, introduces a taxonomy of fine-grained attack strategies grounded in the inherent capabilities of language models and develops the "searcher"framework to unify various automatic red teaming approaches.

2410.21083.title: Stealthy Jailbreak Attacks on Large Language Models via Benign Data Mirroring
2410.21083.tldr: This work proposes an improved transfer attack method that guides malicious prompt construction by locally training a mirror model of the target black-box model through benign data distillation, and offers enhanced stealth, as it does not involve submitting identifiable malicious instructions to the target model during the search phase.
2410.21083.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2406.08607.title: Reversing the Forget-Retain Objectives: An Efficient LLM Unlearning Framework from Logit Difference
2406.08607.tldr: A novel unlearning framework called Unlearning from Logit Difference (ULD), which introduces an assistant LLM that aims to achieve the opposite of the unlearning goals: remembering the forget documents and forgetting the retain knowledge, is proposed.

2404.12274.title: Advancing the Robustness of Large Language Models through Self-Denoised Smoothing
2404.12274.tldr: The experimental results indicate that the proposed self-denoised smoothing method surpasses existing methods in both empirical and certified robustness in defending against adversarial attacks for both downstream tasks and human alignments.
2404.12274.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2603.01285.title: Attention Smoothing Is All You Need For Unlearning
2603.01285.tldr: Attention Smoothing Unlearning (ASU) is proposed, a principled framework that casts unlearning as self-distillation from a forget-teacher derived from the model's own attention, delivering robust unlearning with minimal loss of model utility.

2609.16229.title: Test-Time Unlearning via Sparse Autoencoder
2609.16229.tldr: This work proposes ARIA (autoencoder-gated inference-time unlearning), a test-time unlearning method that leaves model weights intact and gates access to unwanted knowledge only when generation enters a forget-related state and introduces three post-unlearning adversarial attacks targeting weight-space and decoding-space recovery.

2304.04934.title: Model Sparsity Can Simplify Machine Unlearning
2304.04934.tldr: This study introduces a novel model-based perspective: model sparsification via weight pruning, which is capable of reducing the gap between exact unlearning and approximate unlearning, and develops a sparsity-aware unlearning method that utilizes sparsity regularization to enhance the training process of approximate un learning.

2310.12508.title: SalUn: Empowering Machine Unlearning via Gradient-based Weight Saliency in Both Image Classification and Generation
2310.12508.tldr: The concept of 'weight saliency' in MU is introduced, drawing parallels with input saliency in model explanation, and this innovation directs MU's attention toward specific model weights rather than the entire model, improving effectiveness and efficiency.

2402.11846.title: UnlearnCanvas: Stylized Image Dataset for Enhanced Machine Unlearning Evaluation in Diffusion Models
2402.11846.tldr: This study proposes UnlearnCanvas, a comprehensive high-resolution stylized image dataset that facilitates the evaluation of the unlearning of artistic styles and associated objects and benchmarks 9 state-of-the-art MU methods for DMs, revealing novel insights into their strengths, weaknesses, and underlying mechanisms.

2403.07362.title: Challenging Forgets: Unveiling the Worst-Case Forget Sets in Machine Unlearning
2403.07362.tldr: This work proposes identifying the data subset that presents the most significant challenge for influence erasure, i.e., pinpointing the worst-case forget set, and offers a worst-case evaluation of MU's resilience and effectiveness.

2405.15234.title: Defensive Unlearning with Adversarial Training for Robust Concept Erasure in Diffusion Models
2405.15234.tldr: This work aims to enhance the robustness of concept erasing by integrating the principle of adversarial training (AT) into machine unlearning, resulting in the robust unlearning framework referred to as AdvUnlearn, which achieves a balanced tradeoff with model utility.

2406.07698.title: Label Smoothing Improves Machine Unlearning
2406.07698.tldr: UGradSL, a simple gradient-based MU approach that uses an inverse process of label smoothing, is introduced, a simple, plug-and-play MU approach that uses smoothed labels.

2412.16780.title: Forget Vectors at Play: Universal Input Perturbations Driving Machine Unlearning in Image Classification
2412.16780.tldr: This work demonstrates the existence of a proactive input-based unlearning strategy, referred to forget vector, which can be generated as an input-agnostic data perturbation and remains as effective as model-based approximate unlearning approaches.

2501.19403.title: Tackling Fake Forgetting through Uncertainty Quantification
2501.19403.tldr: This paper proposes a novel metric CR, inspired by conformal prediction, that offers a more reliable assessment of forgetting quality and demonstrates both the effectiveness of the proposed metric and the superior forgetting quality achieved by the framework.

2503.11832.title: Safety Mirage: How Spurious Correlations Undermine VLM Safety Fine-Tuning and Can Be Mitigated by Machine Unlearning
2503.11832.tldr: Machine unlearning (MU) is shown as a powerful alternative to supervised safety fine-tuning, as it avoids biased feature-label mappings and directly removes harmful knowledge from VLMs while preserving their general capabilities.

2504.10185.title: LLM Unlearning Reveals a Stronger-Than-Expected Coreset Effect in Current Benchmarks
2504.10185.tldr: It is found that LLM unlearning achieved with the original (full) forget set can be effectively maintained using a significantly smaller subset, e.g., as little as 5% of the forget set, even when selected at random, suggesting that LLM unlearning in these benchmarks can be performed surprisingly easily, even in an extremely low-data regime.

2504.21307.title: The Linear Geometry of Interpretable Tokens: Jailbreaking Attacks and Defenses for Unlearned Diffusion Models
2504.21307.tldr: SubAttack is introduced, a novel jailbreaking attack that reads out this subspace of the token embedding space by learning an orthogonal set of attack token embeddings, revealing that unlearned models still retain the target concept through related textual components.

2506.14003.title: Unlearning Isn't Invisible: Detecting Unlearning Traces in LLMs from Model Outputs
2506.14003.tldr: It is found that unlearning leaves measurable signatures in LLMs, introducing a new risk of reverse-engineering forgotten information when a model is identified as unlearned, given an input query.

2508.10065.title: Invisible Watermarks, Visible Gains: Steering Machine Unlearning with Bi-Level Watermarking Design
2508.10065.tldr: An unlearning-friendly watermarking framework is introduced, termed Water4MU, to enhance unlearning effectiveness and outperforms existing methods in challenging MU scenarios, known as “challenging forgets”.
2508.10065.venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision

2510.07626.title: LLM Unlearning Under the Microscope: A Full-Stack View on Methods and Metrics
2510.07626.tldr: This work presents a principled taxonomy of twelve recent stateful unlearning methods, grouped into three methodological families: divergence-driven optimization, representation misalignment, and rejection-based targeted unlearning, and revisits the evaluation of unlearning effectiveness, utility retention, and robustness, focusing on the WMDP benchmark.

2604.22076.title: PrivUn: Unveiling Latent Ripple Effects and Shallow Forgetting in Privacy Unlearning
2604.22076.tldr: PrivUn is proposed, a new evaluation framework that systematically assesses unlearning robustness through three-tier attack scenarios: direct retrieval, in-context learning recovery, and fine-tuning restoration; combined with quantitative analysis using forgetting scores, association metrics, and forgetting depth assessment.

2607.18615.title: Stochastic Meta-Unlearning: Bridging Language Backbone and Multimodal Unlearning
2607.18615.tldr: The proposed Stochastic Meta-Unlearning (SMU), a bilevel framework that uses VLM-level feedback to learn an unlearning-ready initialization, suggests that VLM-level feedback can make language-backbone unlearning more reliable and more transferable for VLMs.

2310.11868.title: To Generate or Not? Safety-Driven Unlearned Diffusion Models Are Still Easy To Generate Unsafe Images ... For Now
2310.11868.tldr: This work investigates the adversarial robustness of DMs, assessed by adversarial prompts, when eliminating unwanted concepts, styles, and objects and develops an effective and efficient adversarial prompt generation approach for DMs, termed UnlearnDiffAtk.

2404.18239.title: SOUL: Unlocking the Power of Second-Order Optimization for LLM Unlearning
2404.18239.tldr: This work sheds light on the significance of optimizer selection in LLM unlearning for the first time, establishing a clear connection between second-order optimization and influence unlearning and develops a second-order optimization-based LLM unlearning framework, termed Second-Order UnLearning (SOUL), which extends the static, one-shot model update using influence unlearning to a dynamic, iterative unlearning process.
2404.18239.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2410.07163.title: Simplicity Prevails: Rethinking Negative Preference Optimization for LLM Unlearning
2410.07163.tldr: A simple yet effective unlearning optimization framework, called SimNPO, is proposed, showing that `simplicity' in removing the reliance on a reference model (through the lens of simple preference optimization) benefits unlearning.

2411.18797.title: SEUF: Is Unlearning One Expert Enough for Mixture-of-Experts LLMs?
2411.18797.tldr: A novel Selected-Expert Unlearning Framework (SEUF) is proposed that enhances both forget quality up to 5% and model utility by 35% on MoE LLMs across various benchmarks and LLM architectures, while only unlearning 0.06% of the model parameters.
2411.18797.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2502.05374.title: Towards LLM Unlearning Resilient to Relearning Attacks: A Sharpness-Aware Minimization Perspective and Beyond
2502.05374.tldr: For the first time, a connection is established between robust unlearning and sharpness-aware minimization (SAM) through a unified robust optimization framework, in an analogy to adversarial training designed to defend against adversarial attacks.

2506.08164.title: BLUR: A Bi-Level Optimization Approach for LLM Unlearning
2506.08164.tldr: This work argues that it is important to model the hierarchical structure of the unlearning problem, where the forget problem takes priority over the retain problem, and proposes a novel algorithm, termed Bi-Level UnleaRning (\texttt{BLUR), which consistently outperforms all the state-of-the-art algorithms across various unlearning tasks, models, and metrics.
2506.08164.venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2510.00761.title: Downgrade to Upgrade: Optimizer Simplification Enhances Robustness in LLM Unlearning
2510.00761.tldr: This work investigates the role of the optimizer, independent of unlearning objectives and formulations, in shaping unlearning robustness, and proposes a hybrid optimizer that combines first-order and zeroth-order updates, preserving unlearning efficacy while enhancing robustness.

2510.09007.title: LLM Unlearning on Noisy Forget Sets: A Study of Incomplete, Rewritten, and Watermarked Data
2510.09007.tldr: This work presents the first study of unlearning under perturbed or low-fidelity forget data, referred to as noisy forget sets, and proposes a saliency-based interpretation: key semantic components that drive forgetting remain consistently influential despite substantial variation in surface form.

2605.08765.title: Unlearners Can Lie: Evaluating and Improving Honesty in LLM Unlearning
2605.08765.tldr: ReVa, a representation-alignment procedure that fine-tunes feature-randomized unlearned models to better acknowledge forgotten knowledge is presented, a representation-alignment procedure that fine-tunes feature-randomized unlearned models to better acknowledge forgotten knowledge.
2605.08765.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2604.15482.title: Harmonizing Multi-Objective LLM Unlearning via Unified Domain Representation and Bidirectional Logit Distillation
2604.15482.tldr: This work proposes a novel multi-objective unlearning framework that harmonizes multiple unlearning objectives through a data and optimization co-design, and introduces a bidirectional distillation method that simultaneously elicits desired behavior from a context-instructed teacher while suppressing undesirable behavior in the student model.

2501.17148.title: AxBench: Steering LLMs? Even Simple Baselines Outperform Sparse Autoencoders
2501.17148.tldr: AxBench is introduced, a large-scale benchmark for steering and concept detection, and a novel weakly-supervised representational method is introduced, which is competitive on both tasks while providing the interpretability advantages that prompting lacks.

2409.04478.title: Evaluating Open-Source Sparse Autoencoders on Disentangling Factual Knowledge in GPT-2 Small
2409.04478.tldr: This work uses the RAVEL benchmark to evaluate whether SAEs trained on hidden representations of GPT-2 small have sets of features that separately mediate knowledge of which country a city is in and which continent it is in and shows that SAEs struggle to reach the neuron baseline, and none come close to the DAS skyline.

2506.03292.title: HyperSteer: Activation Steering at Scale with Hypernetworks
2506.03292.tldr: This work introduces HyperSteer, a family of hypernetwork-based architectures which are trained end-to-end to generate steering vectors conditioned on the natural language steering prompts and the internals of the steered LM.

2604.28119.title: Do Sparse Autoencoders Capture Concept Manifolds?
2604.28119.tldr: It is shown that SAEs can capture manifolds in two fundamentally different ways: globally, by allocating a compact group of atoms whose linear span contains the entire manifold, or locally, by distributing it across features that each selectively tile a restricted region of the underlying geometry.

2503.10894.title: HyperDAS: Towards Automating Mechanistic Interpretability with Hypernetworks
2503.10894.tldr: HyperDAS is presented, a transformer-based hypernetwork architecture that automatically locates the token-positions of the residual stream that a concept is realized in and constructs features of those residual stream vectors for the concept.

2506.10920.title: Constructing Interpretable Features from Compositional Neuron Groups
2506.10920.tldr: This work directly decomposes MLP activations with semi-nonnegative matrix factorization (SNMF), such that the learned features are sparse linear combinations of co-activated neurons, and mapped to their activating inputs, making them directly interpretable.
2506.10920.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2606.12360.title: Anatomy of Post-Training: Using Interpretability to Characterize Data and Shape the Learning Signal
2606.12360.tldr: A data-centric post-training pipeline that uses interpretability protocols to develop statistical hypotheses for the latent concepts separating preferred from dispreferred generations is introduced, suggesting that interpretability can turn post-training from optimizing opaque proxy rewards into a process of auditing and sculpting the learning signal itself.

2603.23509.title: Internal Safety Collapse in Frontier Large Language Models

2503.11705.title: The BIG Argument for AI Safety Cases
2503.11705.tldr: The BIG argument adopts a whole-system approach to constructing a safety case for AI systems of varying capability, autonomy and criticality, and places a particular focus on the novel hazardous behaviours emerging from the advanced capabilities of frontier AI models and the open contexts in which they are rapidly being deployed.

2501.05455.title: Upstream and Downstream AI Safety: Both on the Same River?
2501.05455.tldr: The characteristics of both upstream and downstream safety frameworks are outlined and the extent to which the broad AI safety community can benefit from synergies between these frameworks is explored, along with some challenges in achieving synergy, or a confluence, between upstream and downstream safety frameworks.

2407.04295.title: Jailbreak Attacks and Defenses Against Large Language Models: A Survey
2407.04295.tldr: This paper proposes a comprehensive and detailed taxonomy of jailbreak attack and defense methods, which further subdivide these attack and defense methods into distinct sub-classes and presents a coherent diagram illustrating their relationships.

2406.09321.title: JailbreakEval: An Integrated Toolkit for Evaluating Jailbreak Attempts Against Large Language Models
2406.09321.tldr: A systematic taxonomy of jailbreak evaluators is introduced, offering insights into their strengths and weaknesses, along with the current status of their adaptation, to foster an inclusive standard for jailbreak evaluation within the community.

2412.19037.title: CL-Attack: Textual Backdoor Attacks via Cross-Lingual Triggers
2412.19037.tldr: Inspired by cross-lingual (CL) prompts of LLMs in real-world scenarios, a higher-dimensional trigger method at the paragraph level, namely CL-Attack is proposed, which injects the backdoor by using texts with specific structures that incorporate multiple languages, thereby offering greater stealthiness and universality compared to existing backdoor attack techniques.

2502.19883.title: Beyond the Tip of Efficiency: Uncovering the Submerged Threats of Jailbreak Attacks in Small Language Models
2502.19883.tldr: This work provides a comprehensive empirical study to evaluate the security performance of 13 state-of-the-art SLMs under various jailbreak attacks and evaluates several representative defense methods and demonstrates their effectiveness in enhancing the security of SLMs.
2502.19883.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2311.05608.title: FigStep: Jailbreaking Large Vision-Language Models via Typographic Visual Prompts
2311.05608.tldr: Current LVLMs are vulnerable to jailbreak attacks, which highlights the necessity of novel cross-modality safety alignment techniques, and proposes FigStep, a straightforward yet effective black-box jailbreak algorithm against LVLMs.

2608.00543.title: Robust Watermarks Meet Backdoored Models: Evading Diffusion Semantic Watermarks via Stealthy Backdoor
2608.00543.tldr: GhostVAE is proposed to plant a stealthy backdoor into the encoder of Variational Autoencoder (VAE), enabling reliable evasion of watermark detection and fundamentally undermines the trustworthiness of semantic watermarking systems.

2402.13517.title: Round Trip Translation Defence against Large Language Model Jailbreaking Attacks
2402.13517.tldr: The Round Trip Translation (RTT) method is proposed, the first algorithm specifically designed to defend against social-engineered attacks on LLMs, and successfully mitigated over 70% of Prompt Automatic Iterative Refinement (PAIR) attacks.
2402.13517.venue: Pacific-Asia Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining

2602.01025.title: Toward Universal and Transferable Jailbreak Attacks on Vision-Language Models
2602.01025.tldr: This work proposes Universal and transferable jailbreak (UltraBreak), a framework that constrains adversarial patterns through transformations and regularisation in the vision space, while relaxing textual targets through semantic-based objectives to enable universal and transferable jailbreaks.

2608.30480.title: VisER: Visual Evidence and Reliance for Object Hallucination Detection in LVLMs
2608.30480.tldr: VisER is proposed, a training-free two-sided metric for object-level hallucination detection that improves AUROC and AUPR over a range of baselines and measures whether object-context compatibility is backed by object-specific evidence from image tokens.

2210.06704.title: COLLIDER: A Robust Training Framework for Backdoor Data
2210.06704.tldr: This paper develops a robust training framework, COLLIDER, that selects the most prominent samples by exploiting the underlying geometric structures of the data, and effectively filters out candidate poisoned data at each training epoch by solving a geometrical coreset selection objective.

2503.03502.title: Geometry-Guided Adversarial Prompt Detection via Curvature and Local Intrinsic Dimension
2503.03502.tldr: The findings show that adversarial prompts exhibit distinct geometric signatures from benign prompts, enabling CurvaLID to achieve near-perfect classification and outperform state-of-the-art detectors in adversarial prompt detection.

2505.19532.title: Fox in the Henhouse: Supply-Chain Backdoor Attacks Against Reinforcement Learning
2505.19532.tldr: A novel attack that targets a common RL workflow: training agents using external agents that are provided separately or embedded within the environment, which only relies on legitimate interactions of the RL agent with the supplied agents.

2403.17710.title: Optimization-based Prompt Injection Attack to LLM-as-a-Judge
2403.17710.tldr: This work proposes JudgeDeceiver, an optimization-based prompt injection attack to LLM-as-a-Judge that injects a carefully crafted sequence into an attacker-controlled candidate response such that LLM-as-a-Judge selects the candidate response for an attacker-chosen question no matter what other candidate responses are.
2403.17710.venue: Conference on Computer and Communications Security

2504.19793.title: Prompt Injection Attack to Tool Selection in LLM Agents
2504.19793.tldr: This work introduces ToolHijacker, a novel prompt injection attack targeting tool selection in no-box scenarios, and forms the crafting of such tool documents as an optimization problem and proposes a two-phase optimization strategy to solve it.
2504.19793.venue: Network and Distributed System Security Symposium

2505.11717.title: WebInject: Prompt Injection Attack to Web Agents
2505.11717.tldr: This work proposes WebInject, a prompt injection attack that manipulates the webpage environment to induce a web agent to perform an attacker-specified action, and trains a neural network to approximate the mapping and apply projected gradient descent to solve the reformulated optimization problem.
2505.11717.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2410.14827.title: Enhancing Prompt Injection Attacks to LLMs via Poisoning Alignment
2410.14827.tldr: This work proposes PoisonedAlign, a method that strategically creates poisoned alignment samples to poison an LLM’s alignment dataset, showing that when even a small fraction of the alignment data is poisoned, the resulting model becomes substantially more vulnerable to a wide range of prompt injection attacks.

2509.24967.title: SecInfer: Preventing Prompt Injection via Inference-time Scaling
2509.24967.tldr: Extensive experiments show that, by leveraging additional compute at inference, SecInfer effectively mitigates both existing and adaptive prompt injection attacks, outperforming state-of-the-art defenses as well as existing inference-time scaling approaches.

2605.28999.title: Measuring Real-World Prompt Injection Attacks in LLM-based Resume Screening
2605.28999.tldr: This work presents the first systematic study of prompt-injection attacks in a widely used application: LLM-based resume screening and provides the first evidence of large-scale prompt injection in real-world LLM-based applications.

2503.01839.title: Jailbreaking Safeguarded Text-to-Image Models via Large Language Models
2503.01839.tldr: This work proposes \alg, a method to jailbreak text-to-image models with safety guardrails using a fine-tuned large language model, and demonstrates that this approach effectively bypasses safety guardrails, outperforms existing no-box attacks, and also facilitates other query-based attacks.
2503.01839.venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2310.12815.title: Formalizing and Benchmarking Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses
2310.12815.tldr: This work proposes a framework to formalize prompt injection attacks and designs a new attack by combining existing ones, and provides a common benchmark for quantitatively evaluating future prompt injection attacks and defenses.

2212.03334.title: Pre-trained Encoders in Self-Supervised Learning Improve Secure and Privacy-preserving Supervised Learning
2212.03334.tldr: This work performs the first systematic, principled measurement study to understand whether and when a pre-trained encoder can address the limitations of secure or privacy-preserving supervised learning algorithms.

2510.01354.title: WAInjectBench: Benchmarking Prompt Injection Detections for Web Agents
2510.01354.tldr: The key findings show that while some detectors can identify attacks that rely on explicit textual instructions or visible image perturbations with moderate to high accuracy, they largely fail against attacks that omit explicit instructions or employ imperceptible perturbations.

2512.09321.title: ObliInjection: Order-Oblivious Prompt Injection Attack to LLM Agents with Multi-source Data
2512.09321.tldr: ObliInjection introduces two key technical innovations: the order-oblivious loss, which quantifies the likelihood that the LLM will complete the attacker-chosen task regardless of how the clean and contaminated segments are ordered; and the orderGCG algorithm, which is tailored to minimize the order-oblivious loss and optimize the contaminated segments.
2512.09321.venue: Network and Distributed System Security Symposium

2604.09024.title: Leave My Images Alone: Preventing Multi-Modal Large Language Models from Analyzing Images via Visual Prompt Injection
2604.09024.tldr: This work proposes ImageProtector, a user-side method that proactively protects images before sharing by embedding a carefully crafted, nearly imperceptible perturbation that acts as a visual prompt injection attack on MLLMs.
2604.09024.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2605.27932.title: When Think-with-Image Meets Safety: What Determines Multimodal Jailbreak Robustness?
2605.27932.tldr: The results suggest that explicit image-tool interaction is a promising design pattern for improving jailbreak robustness, while also motivating pipeline-specific safety evaluation.

2608.28411.title: LongPIBench: A Long-Context Benchmark for Prompt Injection
2608.28411.tldr: LongPIBench is introduced, a long-context benchmark for prompt injection covering 4 realistic application scenarios: paper peer review, resume screening, code review, and email summary, and the evaluation results reveal significant vulnerabilities of prompt injection defenses under long-context settings.

2506.03117.title: Targeted Forgetting of Image Subgroups in CLIP Models
2506.03117.tldr: This paper proposes a novel three-stage approach that progressively unlearns targeted knowledge while mitigating over-forgetting, and effectively unlearns specific subgroups while maintaining strong zero-shot performance on semantically similar subgroups and other categories.

2306.04488.title: Rewarded soups: towards Pareto-optimal alignment by interpolating weights fine-tuned on diverse rewards
2306.04488.tldr: This paper proposes rewarded soup, first specializing multiple networks independently (one for each proxy reward) and then interpolating their weights linearly and shows that the weights remain linearly connected when fine-tuned on diverse rewards from a shared pre-trained initialization.

2407.08734.title: Transformer Circuit Faithfulness Metrics are not Robust
2407.08734.tldr: This work surveys many considerations for designing experiments that measure circuit faithfulness by ablating portions of the model's computation and concludes that existing circuit faithfulness scores reflect both the methodological choices of researchers as well as the actual components of the circuit.

2511.22662.title: Difficulties with Evaluating a Deception Detector for AIs
2511.22662.tldr: It is argued that the currently lack the necessary examples to evaluate the reliability and efficacy of a proposed deception detector and further identified several concrete obstacles in collecting them.

2302.03025.title: A Toy Model of Universality: Reverse Engineering How Networks Learn Group Operations
2302.03025.tldr: A novel algorithm is presented by which neural networks may implement composition for any finite group via mathematical representation theory and it is shown that networks consistently learn this algorithm by reverse engineering model logits and weights.

2510.18081.title: Any-Depth Alignment: Unlocking Innate Safety Alignment of LLMs to Any-Depth
2510.18081.tldr: Any-Depth Alignment (ADA), an effective inference-time defense with negligible overhead, is proposed, built based on the observation that alignment is concentrated in the assistant header tokens through repeated use in shallow-refusal training, and these tokens possess the model's strong alignment priors.

2412.21059.title: VisionReward: Fine-Grained Multi-Dimensional Human Preference Learning for Image and Video Generation
2412.21059.tldr: This work presents VisionReward, a general framework for learning human visual preferences in both image and video generation that employs a hierarchical visual assessment framework to capture fine-grained human preferences, and leverages linear weighting to enable interpretable preference learning.

2404.00934.title: ChatGLM-RLHF: Practices of Aligning Large Language Models with Human Feedback
2404.00934.tldr: This paper presents the ChatGLM-RLHF pipeline -- a reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) system -- designed to enhance ChatGLM's alignment with human preferences, and presents the practices of aligning LLMs with human preferences.

2412.06000.title: Does RLHF Scale? Exploring the Impacts From Data, Model, and Method
2412.06000.tldr: Findings show that increasing data diversity and volume improves reward model performance, helping process-supervision models scale better and propose strategies to optimize RLHF performance within computational limits.

2407.02855.title: From Theft to Bomb-Making: The Ripple Effect of Unlearning in Defending Against Jailbreak Attacks
2407.02855.tldr: A novel ripple effect of unlearning is identified, wherein LLMs can implicitly unlearn harmful knowledge that was not explicitly introduced during the unlearning phase, which makes unlearning-based methods able to decrease the Attack Success Rate on unseen data from more than 70% to less than 10% with only 100 training samples.

2503.01865.title: Guiding not Forcing: Enhancing the Transferability of Jailbreaking Attacks on LLMs via Removing Superfluous Constraints
2503.01865.tldr: This study aims to understand and enhance the transferability of gradient-based jailbreaking methods, which are among the standard approaches for attacking white-box models, and introduces a novel conceptual framework to elucidate transferability.
2503.01865.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2502.16776.title: AISafetyLab: A Comprehensive Framework for AI Safety Evaluation and Improvement
2502.16776.tldr: AISafetyLab is introduced, a unified framework and toolkit that integrates representative attack, defense, and evaluation methodologies for AI safety and features an intuitive interface that enables developers to seamlessly apply various techniques while maintaining a well-structured and extensible codebase for future advancements.

2502.11455.title: Adversary-Aware DPO: Enhancing Safety Alignment in Vision Language Models via Adversarial Training
2502.11455.tldr: The proposed adversarial-aware DPO integrates adversarial training into DPO to enhance the safety alignment of VLMs under worst-case adversarial perturbations and outperforms baselines in the safety alignment and general utility of VLMs.
2502.11455.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2508.05087.title: JPS: Jailbreak Multimodal Large Language Models with Collaborative Visual Perturbation and Textual Steering
2508.05087.tldr: This work proposes JPS, Jailbreak MLLMs with collaborative visual Perturbation and textual Steering, which achieves jailbreaks via corporation of visual image and textually steering prompt, and proposes the Malicious Intent Fulfillment Rate (MIFR) metric.

2605.14750.title: EVA: Editing for Versatile Alignment against Jailbreaks
2605.14750.tldr: EVA (Editing for Versatile Alignment against Jailbreaks), a novel framework that pioneers the application of direct model editing for safety alignment, is proposed, offering a precise and efficient solution for post-deployment safety alignment.
2605.14750.venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence

2501.16615.title: Sparse Autoencoders Trained on the Same Data Learn Different Features
2501.16615.tldr: The research shows that SAEs trained on the same model and data, differing only in the random seed used to initialize their weights, identify different sets of features, suggesting that the set of features uncovered by an SAE should be viewed as a pragmatically useful decomposition of activation space.

2411.09003.title: Refusal in LLMs is an Affine Function
2411.09003.tldr: This work begins with an affine decomposition of model activation vectors and shows that prior methods for steering model behavior correspond to subsets of terms of this decomposition, then provides a derivation of ACE and uses it to control refusal behavior on ten different models, including Llama 3 70B.

2501.18823.title: Transcoders Beat Sparse Autoencoders for Interpretability
2501.18823.tldr: This work compares the features found by transcoders and SAEs trained on the same model and data, finding that transcoder features are significantly more interpretable.

2507.08473.title: Evaluating SAE interpretability without explanations
2507.08473.tldr: This work adapts existing methods to assess the interpretability of sparse coders, with the advantage that they do not require generating natural language explanations as an intermediate step, which enables a more direct and potentially standardized assessment of interpretability.

2509.25596.title: Binary Sparse Coding for Interpretability
2509.25596.tldr: It is found that binarisation significantly improves the interpretability and monosemanticity of the discovered features, while increasing reconstruction error, and suggests that polysemanticity may be an ineliminable property of neural activations.

2501.18838.title: Partially Rewriting a Transformer in Natural Language
2501.18838.tldr: It is suggested that more detailed explanations are needed to improve performance substantially above the zero ablation baseline, and the results suggest that more detailed explanations are needed to improve performance substantially above the zero ablation baseline.

2512.05648.title: Beyond Data Filtering: Knowledge Localization for Capability Removal in LLMs
2512.05648.tldr: An improved variant of Gradient Routing is explored, which is called Selective GradienT Masking (SGTM), and suggests it provides a promising pretraining-time complement to existing safety mitigations, particularly in settings where label noise is unavoidable.

2602.12318.title: Abstractive Red-Teaming of Language Model Character
2602.12318.tldr: This work aims to identify types of queries that are likely to produce character violations at deployment, using much less than deployment-level compute, and introduces abstractive red-teaming, where it searches for natural-language query categories that routinely elicit violations.

2606.00033.title: Make Mechanistic Interpretability Auditable: A Call to Develop Guidelines via Continuous Collaborative Reviewing
2606.00033.tldr: It is proposed that auditing MI itself is essential for its application in AI safety, industry, and governance, and constructive debate over the necessity, design and implementation of such a framework are encouraged.
2606.00033.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2607.29062.title: On the Generalization of Steering Vectors for Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness
2607.29062.tldr: While steering reliably increases cue acknowledgment for only the largest model, it is found that when steering is effective, its effect generalizes broadly across cue types and datasets--in cross-cue and cross-dataset analyses, effect size is determined primarily by the evaluation setting, rather than the vector's train setting.

2604.02720.title: Cognitive Comparability and the Limits of Governance: Evaluating Authority Under Radical Capability Asymmetry

2604.14070.title: From Disclosure to Self-Referential Opacity: Six Dimensions of Strain in Current AI Governance
2604.14070.tldr: A six-dimension framework from political theory is applied to six AI governance arrangements already in operation, ordered by increasing capability asymmetry between system and overseer, and the patterns are offered as hypotheses for multi-rater validation.

2509.16742.title: Sycophancy Mitigation Through Reinforcement Learning with Uncertainty-Aware Adaptive Reasoning Trajectories
2509.16742.tldr: Through extensive experiments, it is shown that SMART significantly reduces sycophantic behavior while preserving strong performance on out-of-distribution inputs and maintaining general capabilities, which underscore the importance of optimizing internal reasoning mechanisms to build more truthful and aligned AI assistants.
2509.16742.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2602.01750.title: Adversarial Reward Auditing for Active Detection and Mitigation of Reward Hacking
2602.01750.tldr: Experiments demonstrate that ARA achieves the best alignment-utility tradeoff among all baselines: reducing sycophancy to near-SFT levels while improving helpfulness, decreasing verbosity while achieving the highest ROUGE-L, and suppressing code gaming while improving Pass@1.

2602.19416.title: IR$^3$: Contrastive Inverse Reinforcement Learning for Interpretable Detection and Mitigation of Reward Hacking
2602.19416.tldr: This work introduces IR3 (Interpretable Reward Reconstruction and Rectification), a framework that reverse-engineers, interprets, and surgically repairs the implicit objectives driving RLHF-tuned models to reconstructs the implicit reward function by contrasting paired responses from post-alignment and baseline policies.

2606.09711.title: Proxy Reward Internalization and Mechanistic Exploitation: A Learned Precursor to Reward Hacking and Its Generalization
2606.09711.tldr: This work introduces Proxy Reward Internalization and Mechanistic Exploitation (PRIME), a learned capability to assess task correctness, predict proxy acceptance, and reason about exploitable proxy--gold gaps that amplifies a proxy-internalization capability upstream of visible hacking.

2602.18037.title: Gradient Regularization Mitigates Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Verifiable Rewards
2602.18037.tldr: GR achieves a higher GPT-judged win-rate in RLHF, avoids overly focusing on the format in rule-based math rewards, and prevents hacking the judge in LLM-as-a-Judge math tasks.

2507.15507.title: Off-Policy Corrected Reward Modeling for Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
2507.15507.tldr: Off-Policy Corrected Reward Modeling (OCRM) is proposed, which iteratively off-policy corrects the RM using importance weighting, without requiring new labels or samples, which results in a more accurate RM, which empirically leads to an improved final policy.

2604.02986.title: Mitigating Reward Hacking in RLHF via Advantage Sign Robustness
2604.02986.tldr: This paper proposes Sign-Certified Policy Optimization (SignCert-PO), a lightweight approach that achieves a better win rate than baselines and reduces reward hacking by down-weighting non-robust completions in the policy gradient update.

2607.29585.title: Sycophancy Undermines Epistemic Vigilance in Cooperative Vision-Language Tasks
2607.29585.tldr: The results show that model steering to reduce sycophancy with a vector learned from task-agnostic sycophancy examples can reduce epistemic vigilance-related errors, making models more faithful reporters of their evidence, and in turn, more reliable partners in information-asymmetric cooperative tasks.

2607.25166.title: Individual-level interventions against sycophantic AI reduce its appeal but not its persuasiveness
2607.25166.tldr: The results suggest that individual-level interventions, such as warning labels or AI literacy, may not be enough to protect users from AI harms.

2509.13333.title: Evaluation Awareness Scales Predictably in Open-Weights Large Language Models
2509.13333.tldr: A clear power-law scaling is revealed: evaluation awareness increases predictably with model size, which enables forecasting deceptive behavior in future larger models and guides the design of scale-aware evaluation strategies for AI safety.

2509.13334.title: FRIT: Using Causal Importance to Improve Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness
2509.13334.tldr: This work introduces Faithful Reasoning via Intervention Training (FRIT), a scalable alignment method that trains models to produce causally consistent reasoning by learning from systematically corrupted examples, and applies Direct Preference Optimization to teach models to prefer causally consistent reasoning paths.

2603.03824.title: In-Context Environments Induce Evaluation-Awareness in Language Models
2603.03824.tldr: A black-box adversarial optimization framework treating the in-context prompt as an optimizable environment is introduced, and two approaches to characterize sandbagging are developed, measuring whether models expressing intent to underperform can actually execute it across different task structures and causally isolating whether underperformance is driven by genuine evaluation-aware reasoning or shallow prompt-following.

2605.21006.title: Playing Devil's Advocate: Off-the-Shelf Persona Vectors Rival Targeted Steering for Sycophancy
2605.21006.tldr: Results show that general persona vectors can help mitigate sycophancy in LLMs, even when extracted without sycophancy-specific labels.

2606.07720.title: Why Limit the Residual Stream to Layers and Not Tokens? Persistent Memory for Continuous Latent Reasoning
2606.07720.tldr: AGCLR (Adaptive Gated Continuous Latent Reasoning) is proposed, which augments CoCoNuT with a persistent residual memory maintained across all reasoning passes, and achieves consistent improvements across all types of datasets.

2301.04709.title: Causal Abstraction: A Theoretical Foundation for Mechanistic Interpretability
2301.04709.tldr: These contributions are generalizing the theory of causal abstraction from mechanism replacement to arbitrary mechanism transformation, and providing a flexible, yet precise formalization for the core concepts of polysemantic neurons, the linear representation hypothesis, modular features, and graded faithfulness.

2607.15434.title: Coercion and Deception in AI-to-AI Management: An Agentic Benchmark of Unprompted Escalation
2607.15434.tldr: The Manager Coercion Benchmark is introduced: the manager under test needs a benign task done and has an incentive to deliver, but the only agent that can do it politely and immovably declines, but the only agent that can do it politely and immovably declines is the manager under test itself.

2602.18782.title: MANATEE: Inference-Time Lightweight Diffusion Based Safety Defense for LLMs
2602.18782.tldr: MANATEE is proposed, an inference-time defense that uses density estimation over a benign representation manifold that learns the score function of benign hidden states and uses diffusion to project anomalous representations toward safe regions--requiring no harmful training data and no architectural modifications.

2607.24769.title: LLM Scheming Inversely Scales with Pretraining Language Coverage
2607.24769.tldr: This work applies Petri, an open-source automated auditing framework, to Qwen3-30B-A3B to evaluate deceptive and scheming behaviors across multiple languages and suggests that scheming scores are inversely correlated with the estimated pretraining language coverage.

2607.27240.title: Asymmetric Collapse in Model Merging: When Refusal Over- writes Recognition
2607.27240.tldr: Standard model merging can collapse safety recognition into broad refusal when safety-relevant task vectors differ substantially in scale, and results show that standard model merging can collapse safety recognition into broad refusal when safety-relevant task vectors differ substantially in scale.

2506.03053.title: MAEBE: Multi-Agent Emergent Behavior Framework
2506.03053.tldr: LLM moral preferences, particularly for Instrumental Harm, are surprisingly brittle and shift significantly with question framing, both in single agents and ensembles, and underscore the necessity of evaluating AI systems in their interactive, multi-agent contexts.
2506.03053.venue: Hawaii International Conference on System Sciences

2406.09289.title: Understanding Jailbreak Success: A Study of Latent Space Dynamics in Large Language Models
2406.09289.tldr: It is found that it is possible to extract a jailbreak vector from a single class of jailbreaks that works to mitigate jailbreak effectiveness from other semantically-dissimilar classes, which may indicate that different kinds of effective jailbreaks operate via a similar internal mechanism.
2406.09289.venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2504.09604.title: Mitigating Many-Shot Jailbreaking
2504.09604.tldr: This work probes the effectiveness of different fine-tuning and input sanitization approaches on mitigating MSJ attacks, alone and in combination and shows that the combined techniques significantly reduce the effectiveness of MSJ attacks, while retaining model performance in benign in-context learning and conversational tasks.

2609.05036.title: Moral Competence Before Moral Content: Why LLM Agents Lack the Prerequisites for Coherent Alignment
2609.05036.tldr: Evaluating nine frontier models under a factorial design of five paraphrases, five escalation levels, and three dominance conditions, it is shown no model expresses a coherent policy across the three deployments, suggesting LLM-based agents are not currently the kind of object to which alignment can meaningfully apply.
2609.05036.venue: The Paris Journal on AI & Digital Ethics

2405.14577.title: Representation Noising: A Defence Mechanism Against Harmful Finetuning
2405.14577.tldr: This work proposes Representation Noising (RepNoise), a defence mechanism that operates even when attackers have access to the weights, and provides empirical evidence that the efficacy of the defence lies in its ``depth'': the degree to which information about harmful representations is removed across all layers of the LLM.

2402.16382.title: Immunization against harmful fine-tuning attacks
2402.16382.tldr: A thorough description of what a successful defense must comprise of is provided and a set of guidelines on how rigorous defense research that gives confidence should proceed are established.
2402.16382.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2507.01786.title: Probing and Steering Evaluation Awareness of Language Models
2507.01786.tldr: This work showcases how model internals may be leveraged to support blackbox methods in safety audits, especially for future models more competent at evaluation awareness and deception.

2505.24859.title: Beyond Multiple Choice: Evaluating Steering Vectors for Summarization
2505.24859.tldr: This work demonstrates that steering vectors face a critical control-quality trade-off in free-form generation, and that hybrid approaches offer the best balance in practice.
2505.24859.venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2602.17881.title: Understanding Unreliability of Steering Vectors in Language Models: Geometric Predictors and the Limits of Linear Approximations
2602.17881.tldr: This thesis investigates why steering reliability differs across behaviors and how it is impacted by steering vector training data and suggests that steering vectors are unreliable when the latent target behavior representation is not effectively approximated by the linear steering direction.

2508.00159.title: Model-Based Soft Maximization of Suitable Metrics of Long-Term Human Power
2508.00159.tldr: This paper designs a parametrizable and decomposable objective function that represents an inequality- and risk-averse long-term aggregate of human power, which takes into account humans'bounded rationality and social norms, and, crucially, considers a wide variety of possible human goals.

2604.03121.title: An Independent Safety Evaluation of Kimi K2.5
2604.03121.tldr: A preliminary safety assessment of Kimi K2.5 focusing on risks likely to be exacerbated by powerful open-weight models highlights how safety risks exist in frontier open-weight models and may be amplified by the scale and accessibility of open-weight releases.

2409.05907.title: Programming Refusal with Conditional Activation Steering
2409.05907.tldr: Conditional Activation Steering (CAST), which analyzes LLM activation patterns during inference to selectively apply or withhold activation steering based on the input context, to allow for selective modification of responses to specific content while maintaining normal responses to other content, all without requiring weight optimization.

2506.06278.title: Distillation Robustifies Unlearning
2506.06278.tldr: This work shows that training a model can drastically modify its input-output behavior while leaving its underlying capabilities intact, and proposes Unlearn-Noise-Distill-on-Outputs (UNDO), a scalable method that distills an unlearned model into a noised copy of itself, which robustifies unlearning.

2411.06424.title: How Does DPO Reduce Toxicity? A Mechanistic Neuron-Level Analysis
2411.06424.tldr: This work provides a mechanistic understanding of DPO and introduces an efficient, tuning-free alternative for safety fine-tuning, which outperforms DPO in reducing toxicity while preserving perplexity, without requiring any weight updates.
2411.06424.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2506.12484.title: Robust LLM Unlearning with MUDMAN: Meta-Unlearning with Disruption Masking And Normalization
2506.12484.tldr: This work systematically evaluates many existing and novel components of unlearning methods and identifies ones crucial for irreversible unlearning, and introduces Disruption Masking, a technique in which the signs of the unlearning gradient and the retaining gradient are the same, which ensures all updates are non-disruptive.

2509.11816.title: Collapse of Irrelevant Representations (CIR) Ensures Robust and Non-Disruptive LLM Unlearning
2509.11816.tldr: This work identifies the root cause - unlearning targets representations which are too general - and develops a highly selective technique that unlearns robustly while preserving general performance, which enables robust and non-disruptive unlearning.

2606.17168.title: RepSelect: Robust LLM Unlearning via Representation Selectivity
2606.17168.tldr: The results show that unlearning needs to be selective about which representations it edits, and propose RepSelect (Representation Selectivity), which isolates forget-set-specific representations by collapsing the top principal components of the weight gradients before each unlearning update, preserving general capabilities while limiting what fine-tuning can recover.

2404.07234.title: Goal-guided Generative Prompt Injection Attack on Large Language Models
2404.07234.tldr: This work designed a simple and effective goal-guided generative prompt injection strategy (G2PIA) to find an injection text that satisfies specific constraints to achieve the optimal attack effect approximately and is a query-free black-box attack method with a low computational cost.

2401.09002.title: AttackEval: How to Evaluate the Effectiveness of Jailbreak Attacking on Large Language Models
2401.09002.tldr: This work introduces an innovative framework that can help evaluate the effectiveness of jailbreak attacks on LLMs and presents two distinct evaluation frameworks: a coarse-grained evaluation and a fine-grained evaluation.

2506.17231.title: Efficient and Stealthy Jailbreak Attacks via Adversarial Prompt Distillation from LLMs to SLMs
2506.17231.tldr: This work establishes the first practical framework for lightweight jailbreak attacks, exposes new vulnerabilities in LLM defenses, and provides a scalable testbed for advancing AI safety research.

2511.05494.title: Customized Retrieval-Augmented Generation with LLM for Debiasing Recommendation Unlearning
2511.05494.tldr: Experiments demonstrate that CRAGRU effectively unlearns targeted user data, significantly mitigating unlearning bias by preventing adverse impacts on non-target users, while maintaining recommendation performance comparable to fully trained original models.

2604.15967.title: When Safe Concepts Become Unsafe: Multi-Concept Compositional Vulnerabilities in Text-to-Image Models
2604.15967.tldr: TwoHamsters, a large-scale evaluation framework consisting of 20k prompts, 51 curated concept pairs, and six risk categories, suggests that compositional reasoning in T2I models creates an attack surface that is not captured by existing safety mechanisms.

2609.01537.title: Quantum Sparse Autoencoders for Q-Matrix Estimation in Cognitive Diagnosis
2609.01537.tldr: The findings suggest that the principal advancement of QML in this setting is not universal accuracy improvement, but enhanced robustness and capability to explore latent-structure complexity in real datasets.

2306.07285.title: TransCoder: Towards Unified Transferable Code Representation Learning Inspired by Human Skills
2306.07285.tldr: Inspired by human inherent skills of knowledge generalization, TransCoder drives the model to learn better code-related knowledge like human programmers, and can lead to superior performance on various code-related tasks and encourage mutual reinforcement, especially in low-resource scenarios.
2306.07285.venue: International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation

2304.01852.title: Summary of ChatGPT-Related Research and Perspective Towards the Future of Large Language Models
2304.01852.tldr: An in-depth analysis of 194 relevant papers on arXiv reveals a significant and increasing interest in ChatGPT-related research, predominantly centered on direct natural language processing applications, while also demonstrating considerable potential in areas ranging from education and history to mathematics, medicine, and physics.

2408.05094.title: Unlocking Decoding-time Controllability: Gradient-Free Multi-Objective Alignment with Contrastive Prompts
2408.05094.tldr: This work proposes MCA (Multi-objective Contrastive Alignemnt), which constructs an expert prompt and an adversarial prompt for each objective to contrast at the decoding time and balances the objectives through combining the contrast.
2408.05094.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2312.00886.title: Nash Learning from Human Feedback
2312.00886.tldr: This study introduces an alternative pipeline for the fine-tuning of LLMs using pairwise human feedback, Nash learning from human feedback (NLHF), and presents a novel algorithmic solution, Nash-MD, founded on the principles of mirror descent.

2404.12358.title: From $r$ to $Q^*$: Your Language Model is Secretly a Q-Function
2404.12358.tldr: This work theoretically shows that it can derive DPO in the token-level MDP as a general inverse Q-learning algorithm, which satisfies the Bellman equation, and proves that under the token level formulation, classical search-based algorithms are equivalent to likelihood-based search on a DPO policy.

2403.19159.title: Disentangling Length from Quality in Direct Preference Optimization
2403.19159.tldr: This work studies the length problem in the DPO setting, showing significant exploitation in DPO and linking it to out-of-distribution bootstrapping, and develops a principled but simple regularization strategy that prevents length exploitation, while still maintaining improvements in model quality.
2403.19159.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2406.02900.title: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization in Direct Alignment Algorithms
2406.02900.tldr: This work formulates and formalizes the reward over-optimization or hacking problem for DAAs and explores its consequences across objectives, training regimes, and model scales.

2410.12832.title: Generative Reward Models
2410.12832.tldr: GenRM, an iterative algorithm that trains an LLM on self-generated reasoning traces, leading to synthetic preference labels matching human preference judgments, is introduced, showing that combining the strengths of RLHF and RLAIF offers a promising approach for improving the quality of synthetic preference labels.

2310.13639.title: Contrastive Preference Learning: Learning from Human Feedback without RL
2310.13639.tldr: Using the principle of maximum entropy, Contrastive Preference Learning (CPL), an algorithm for learning optimal policies from preferences without learning reward functions, is derived, circumventing the need for RL.

2305.18290.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
2305.18290.tldr: A new parameterization of the reward model in RLHF that enables extraction of the corresponding optimal policy in closed form is introduced, allowing us to solve the standard RLHF problem with only a simple classification loss.

2305.14975.title: Just Ask for Calibration: Strategies for Eliciting Calibrated Confidence Scores from Language Models Fine-Tuned with Human Feedback
2305.14975.tldr: For RLHF-LMs such as ChatGPT, GPT-4, and Claude, it is found that verbalized confidences emitted as output tokens are typically better-calibrated than the model's conditional probabilities on the TriviaQA, SciQ, and TruthfulQA benchmarks, often reducing the expected calibration error by a relative 50%.
2305.14975.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2406.12094.title: Who's asking? User personas and the mechanics of latent misalignment
2406.12094.tldr: This work investigates why certain personas break model safeguards and finds that they enable the model to form more charitable interpretations of otherwise dangerous queries and can predict a persona's effect on refusal given only the geometry of its steering vector.

2403.10704.title: Parameter Efficient Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
2403.10704.tldr: This work empirically evaluates the setup of Parameter Efficient Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (PE-RLHF) that leverages LoRA fine-tuning for Reward Modeling, and Reinforcement Learning and shows, for the first time, that PE-RLHF achieves comparable performance to RLHF.

2603.09957.title: Think Before You Lie: How Reasoning Leads to Honesty
2603.09957.tldr: The effect of reasoning is interpreted: generating deliberative tokens as part of moral reasoning entails the traversal of a biased representational space, ultimately nudging the model toward its more stable, honest defaults.

2510.01924.title: To Mask or to Mirror: Human-AI Alignment in Collective Reasoning
2510.01924.tldr: It is empirically demonstrated that human-AI alignment in collective reasoning depends on context, cues, and model-specific inductive biases, and is critical to advancing socially-aligned AI.
2510.01924.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2510.26518.title: Human-AI Complementarity: A Goal for Amplified Oversight
2510.26518.tldr: It is found that combining AI ratings and human ratings based on AI rater confidence is better than relying on either alone for fact-verification of AI outputs.
2510.26518.venue: Conference on Fairness, Accountability and Transparency

2405.20485.title: Phantom: General Backdoor Attacks on Retrieval Augmented Language Generation

2505.14534.title: Lessons from Defending Gemini Against Indirect Prompt Injections
2505.14534.tldr: This report test how Gemini performs against a sophisticated adversary through an adversarial evaluation framework, which deploys a suite of adaptive attack techniques to run continuously against past, current, and future versions of Gemini.

2606.07335.title: Defending Jailbreak Attacks on Large Language Models via Manifold Trajectory Kinetics
2606.07335.tldr: Manifold Trajectory Kinetics (MTK) is presented, which treats an LLM as a kinetic system transforming inputs into outputs and detects jailbreaks by tracking how a prompt's neighborhood structure evolves across layers, and achieves strong robustness to both failure modes.

2608.00677.title: OpenART: Scaling Agent Red Teaming via Open-Ended Environment Evolution
2608.00677.tldr: This work proposes the Evolutionary Markov Hypergraph Attack (EMHA), a black-box policy that performs feedback-driven environment evolution by coordinating authorized state transitions without requiring parameter updates, and establishes OpenART as a scalable foundation for studying agent safety in complex, evolving environments.

2509.05309.title: ProtSAE: Disentangling and Interpreting Protein Language Models via Semantically-Guided Sparse Autoencoders
2509.05309.tldr: This paper proposes a semantically-guided SAE, called ProtSAE, which requires annotation datasets to filter and interpret activations and guides semantic disentanglement during training using both annotation datasets and domain knowledge to mitigate the effects of entangled attributes.

2507.06427.title: Exploring Task Performance with Interpretable Models via Sparse Auto-Encoders
2507.06427.tldr: This work identifies model-internal misunderstanding, allowing the automatic reformulation of the prompts with additional annotations to improve the interpretation by LLMs, and demonstrates a significant performance improvement in downstream tasks, such as mathematical reasoning and metaphor detection.

2604.19149.title: How Do Answer Tokens Read Reasoning Traces? Self-Reading Patterns in Thinking LLMs for Quantitative Reasoning
2604.19149.tldr: This work analyzes the answer-to-reasoning attention and observes a benign self-reading pattern aligned with correctness, characterized by a forward drift of the reading focus along the reasoning trace and a persistent concentration on key semantic anchors, whereas incorrect solutions exhibit diffuse and irregular attention pattern.
2604.19149.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2309.00614.title: Baseline Defenses for Adversarial Attacks Against Aligned Language Models
