2309.00614.tldr: It is found that the weakness of existing discrete optimizers for text, combined with the relatively high costs of optimization, makes standard adaptive attacks more challenging for LLMs.

2212.03827.title: Discovering Latent Knowledge in Language Models Without Supervision
2212.03827.tldr: This work introduces a method for accurately answering yes-no questions given only unlabeled model activations, and shows that despite using no supervision and no model outputs, the method can recover diverse knowledge represented in large language models.

2402.13494.title: GradSafe: Detecting Jailbreak Prompts for LLMs via Safety-Critical Gradient Analysis
2402.13494.tldr: It is shown that GradSafe, applied to Llama-2 without further training, outperforms Llama Guard, despite its extensive finetuning with a large dataset, in detecting jailbreak prompts.
2402.13494.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2505.06311.title: Defending against Indirect Prompt Injection by Instruction Detection
2505.06311.tldr: This paper proposes InstructDetector, a novel detection-based approach that leverages the behavioral states of LLMs to identify potential IPI attacks, and demonstrates the hidden states and gradients from intermediate layers provide highly discriminative features for instruction detection.
2505.06311.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2312.14197.title: Benchmarking and Defending Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on Large Language Models
2312.14197.tldr: This work introduces the first benchmark for bindirect prompt injection attacks, named BIPIA, and evaluates existing LLMs to find them universally vulnerable, and proposes two novel defense mechanisms to address these vulnerabilities in both black-box and white-box settings.

2305.10036.title: Are You Copying My Model? Protecting the Copyright of Large Language Models for EaaS via Backdoor Watermark
2305.10036.tldr: An Embedding Watermark method called {pasted macro ‘METHOD’} that implants backdoors on embeddings that can effectively protect the copyright of EaaS models without compromising service quality is proposed.
2305.10036.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2607.00572.title: HARC: Coupling Harmfulness and Refusal Directions for Robust Safety Alignment
2607.00572.tldr: HARC (Harmfulness-And-Refusal Coupling), a fine-tuning method that pairs the two directions across both prompt and response positions, achieves the strongest robustness-capability-usability trade-off among six baselines spanning the major training-time and inference-time safety methods.

2210.10958.title: Federated Unlearning for On-Device Recommendation
2210.10958.tldr: This work proposes an efficient unlearning method FRU (Federated Recommendation Unlearning), inspired by the log-based rollback mechanism of transactions in database management systems, and uses FRU to recover recommenders by eliminating these users' influence.

2408.12935.title: AI Safety Landscape for Large Language Models: Taxonomy, State-of-the-art, and Future Directions
2408.12935.tldr: A novel architectural framework for understanding and analyzing AI Safety is proposed; defining its characteristics from three perspectives: Trustworthy AI, Responsible AI, and Safe AI.

2310.20448.title: A Survey on Federated Unlearning: Challenges, Methods, and Future Directions
2310.20448.tldr: This comprehensive survey delves into the techniques and methodologies in FU providing an overview of fundamental concepts and principles, evaluating existing federated unlearning algorithms, and reviewing optimizations tailored to federated learning.

2403.13682.title: Threats, Attacks, and Defenses in Machine Unlearning: A Survey
2403.13682.tldr: This survey aims to fill the gap between the extensive number of studies on threats, attacks, and defenses in machine unlearning and the absence of a comprehensive review that categorizes their taxonomy, methods, and solutions, thus offering valuable insights for future research directions and practical implementations.
2403.13682.venue: IEEE Open Journal of the Computer Society

2512.13337.title: FROC: A Unified Framework with Risk-Optimized Control for Machine Unlearning in LLMs
2512.13337.tldr: FROC reframes MU as a controllable, risk-aware process and offers a practical foundation for managing unlearning behavior in large-scale LLM deployments.
2512.13337.venue: Digital Signal Processing and Signal Processing Education Workshop

2404.09724.title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Unlearning with Certified Client Removal
2404.09724.tldr: Starfish is proposed, a privacy-preserving federated unlearning scheme using Two-Party Computation techniques and shared historical client data between two non-colluding servers that achieves effective unlearning with reasonable efficiency, maintaining privacy and security in FL systems.
2404.09724.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security

2406.00966.title: Guaranteeing Data Privacy in Federated Unlearning with Dynamic User Participation
2406.00966.tldr: This work systematically explores the integration of SecAgg protocols within the most widely used federated unlearning scheme, which is based on clustering, to establish a privacy-preserving FU framework, aimed at ensuring privacy while effectively managing dynamic user participation.
2406.00966.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

2411.11044.title: Efficient Federated Unlearning with Adaptive Differential Privacy Preservation
2411.11044.tldr: The proposed FedADP incorporates an adaptive differential privacy (DP) mechanism, carefully balancing privacy and unlearning performance through a novel budget allocation strategy tailored for FU, and employs a dual-layered selection process, focusing on global models with significant changes and client updates closely aligned with the global model, reducing storage and communication costs.

2512.23171.title: Certifying the Right to Be Forgotten: Primal-Dual Optimization for Sample and Label Unlearning in Vertical Federated Learning
2512.23171.tldr: FedORA (Federated Optimization for data Removal via primal-dual Algorithm) is proposed, designed for sample and label unlearning in vertical federated learning (VFL), and introduces a new unlearning loss function that promotes classification uncertainty rather than misclassification.
2512.23171.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security

2501.02039.title: An Investigation into Value Misalignment in LLM-Generated Texts for Cultural Heritage
2501.02039.tldr: A benchmark dataset and a comprehensive evaluation workflow are introduced that can serve as a valuable resource for future research aimed at enhancing the cultural sensitivity and reliability of LLMs.
2501.02039.venue: IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computational Intelligence

2601.17344.title: The Shadow Self: Intrinsic Value Misalignment in Large Language Model Agents
2601.17344.tldr: This work formalizes the Loss-of-Control risk and identifies the previously underexamined Intrinsic Value Misalignment (Intrinsic VM), and introduces IMPRESS (Intrinsic Value Misalignment Probes in REalistic Scenario Set), a scenario-driven framework for systematically assessing this risk.

2504.20910.title: When Testing AI Tests Us: Safeguarding Mental Health on the Digital Frontlines
2504.20910.tldr: It is argued that the unmet mental health needs of AI red-teamers are a critical workplace safety concern, and potential individual and organizational strategies that could be used to meet these needs are proposed, and safeguard the mental health of red-teamers.
2504.20910.venue: Conference on Fairness, Accountability and Transparency

2503.22116.title: Effective Automation to Support the Human Infrastructure in AI Red Teaming
2503.22116.tldr: This forum focuses on the conditions and futures of the labor underpinning technology production and maintenance within the global supply chain of digital technologies.

2412.09751.title: AI red-teaming is a sociotechnical problem: on values, labor, and harms
2412.09751.tldr: The importance of understanding the values and assumptions behind red-teaming, the labor arrangements involved, and the psychological impacts on red-teamers is highlighted, drawing insights from the lessons learned around the work of content moderation.

2505.24246.title: Locating Risk: Task Designers and the Challenge of Risk Disclosure in RAI Content Work
2505.24246.tldr: The findings highlight the need to support task designers in identifying and communicating risks not only to support crowdworker well-being but also to strengthen the ethical integrity and technical efficacy of AI development pipelines.

2509.12140.title: Worker Discretion Advised: Co-designing Risk Disclosure in Crowdsourced Responsible AI (RAI) Content Work
2509.12140.tldr: This work investigates task designer preferences for support in disclosing tasks, worker preferences for receiving risk disclosure warnings, and how platform representatives envision their role in shaping risk disclosure practices, and identifies design tensions and map the sociotechnical tradeoffs that shape disclosure practices.
2509.12140.venue: International Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems

2407.02551.title: Breach By A Thousand Leaks: Unsafe Information Leakage in `Safe' AI Responses
2407.02551.tldr: A new safety evaluation framework based on impermissible information leakage of model outputs is introduced and it is proved that to ensure safety against inferential adversaries, defense mechanisms must ensure information censorship, bounding the leakage of impermissible information.

2406.11715.title: Measuring memorization in RLHF for code completion
2406.11715.tldr: This work suggests that RLHF, as opposed to direct preference learning, is a safer way to mitigate the risk of regurgitating sensitive preference data when aligning large language models, and is robust across multiple code completion datasets, tasks, and model scales.

2110.11891.title: On the Necessity of Auditable Algorithmic Definitions for Machine Unlearning
2110.11891.tldr: It is shown that the definition that underlies approximate unlearning, which seeks to prove the approximately unlearned model is close to an exactly retrained model, is incorrect because one can obtain the same model using different datasets, and therefore one could unlearn without modifying the model at all.

2403.01218.title: Inexact Unlearning Needs More Careful Evaluations to Avoid a False Sense of Privacy
2403.01218.tldr: This work discusses adaptations of Membership Inference Attacks (MIAs) to the setting of unlearning (leading to their “U-MIA” counterparts), and proposes a categorization of existing U-MIAs into “population U-MIAs”, and “per-example U-MIAs”, where a dedicated attacker is instantiated for each example.
2403.01218.venue: 2025 IEEE Conference on Secure and Trustworthy Machine Learning (SaTML)

2407.00106.title: UnUnlearning: Unlearning is not sufficient for content regulation in advanced generative AI
2407.00106.tldr: It is argued that content filtering for impermissible knowledge will be required and even exact unlearning schemes are not enough for effective content regulation, and a concept of ununlearning is introduced, where unlearned knowledge gets reintroduced in-context, effectively rendering the model capable of behaving as if it knows the forgotten knowledge.

2606.09935.title: GitInject: Real-World Prompt Injection Attacks in AI-Powered CI/CD Pipelines
2606.09935.tldr: This work presents GitInject, an open-source framework for evaluating prompt injection vulnerabilities in real, live GitHub workflows, a widely deployed instance of CI/CD pipelines, and finds that all tested providers are susceptible to at least one attack class in their default configuration.

2411.11039.title: FedUHB: Accelerating Federated Unlearning via Polyak Heavy Ball Method
2411.11039.tldr: FedUHB is proposed, a novel exact unlearning approach that leverages the Polyak heavy ball optimization technique, a first-order method, to achieve rapid retraining and introduces a dynamic stopping mechanism to optimize the termination of the unlearning process.

2311.06237.title: Summon a Demon and Bind it: A Grounded Theory of LLM Red Teaming
2311.06237.tldr: A comprehensive grounded theory of how and why people attack large language models: LLM red teaming is presented, defining LLM red-teaming based on extensive and diverse evidence.

2405.13578.title: ConTrans: Weak-to-Strong Alignment Engineering via Concept Transplantation
2405.13578.tldr: ConTrans is a novel framework that enables weak-to-strong alignment transfer via concept transplantation and surpasses instruction-tuned models in terms of truthfulness and successfully demonstrates an alternative way to achieve weak-to-strong alignment generalization and control.

2402.18120.title: Exploring Multilingual Concepts of Human Value in Large Language Models: Is Value Alignment Consistent, Transferable and Controllable across Languages?
2402.18120.tldr: This paper empirically confirms the presence of value concepts within LLMs in a multilingual format and validates the feasibility of cross-lingual control over value alignment capabilities of LLMs, leveraging the dominant language as a source language.
2402.18120.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2407.03876.title: Automated Progressive Red Teaming
2407.03876.tldr: This work proposes Automated Progressive Red Teaming (APRT) as an effectively learnable framework that leverages three core modules: an Intention Expanding LLM that generates diverse initial attack samples, an Intention Hiding LLM that crafts deceptive prompts, and an Evil Maker to manage prompt diversity and filter ineffective samples.

2605.14420.title: DVMap: Fine-Grained Pluralistic Value Alignment via High-Consensus Demographic-Value Mapping
2605.14420.tldr: DVMap (High-Consensus Demographic-Value Mapping), a framework for fine-grained pluralistic value alignment, is proposed, demonstrating strong generalization and robustness.
2605.14420.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2604.25167.title: From Insight to Action: A Novel Framework for Interpretability-Guided Data Selection in Large Language Models
2604.25167.tldr: Interpretability-Guided Data Selection (IGDS), a framework that first identifies causal task features through frequency recall and interventional filtering, then selects ``Feature-Resonant Data'' that maximally activates task features for fine-tuning, validating the core hypothesis.
2604.25167.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2504.04976.title: A Domain-Based Taxonomy of Jailbreak Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models
2504.04976.tldr: This work introduces a novel taxonomy of jailbreak attacks grounded in the training domains of LLMs, and introduces a perspective on jailbreak, framed through the different linguistic domains that emerge during LLM training and alignment.

2402.10260.title: A StrongREJECT for Empty Jailbreaks
2402.10260.tldr: It is found that existing evaluation methods significantly overstate jailbreak effectiveness compared to human judgments and the StrongREJECT evaluator, which underscores the need for researchers to use a high-quality benchmark, such as StrongREJECT, when developing new jailbreak attacks.

2311.01011.title: Tensor Trust: Interpretable Prompt Injection Attacks from an Online Game
2311.01011.tldr: A dataset of over 126,000 Prompt injection attacks and 46,000 prompt-based "defenses" against prompt injection, all created by players of an online game called Tensor Trust, is presented, currently the largest dataset of human-generated adversarial examples for instruction-following LLMs.

2404.17546.title: Probabilistic Inference in Language Models via Twisted Sequential Monte Carlo
2404.17546.tldr: This work uses learned twist functions to estimate the expected future value of the potential at each timestep, which enables us to focus inference-time computation on promising partial sequences and proposes a novel contrastive method for learning the twist functions.

2602.10568.title: Gauss-Newton Unlearning for the LLM Era
2602.10568.tldr: This work demonstrates that using the forget set to compute only a few uphill Gauss-Newton steps provides a conceptually simple, state-of-the-art unlearning approach for LLMs, and relies on parametric Hessian approximations such as Kronecker-Factored Approximate Curvature (K-FAC).

2406.09264.title: Position: Towards Bidirectional Human-AI Alignment
2406.09264.tldr: The Bidirectional Human-AI Alignment framework is introduced, which not only incorporates traditional efforts to align AI with human values but also introduces the critical, underexplored dimension of aligning humans with AI.

2410.12877.title: Improving Instruction-Following in Language Models through Activation Steering
2410.12877.tldr: This work derives instruction-specific vector representations from language models and uses them to steer models accordingly, enabling a modular approach to activation steering, demonstrating that activation steering offers a practical and scalable approach for fine-grained control in language generation.

2411.11296.title: Steering Language Model Refusal with Sparse Autoencoders
2411.11296.tldr: This work uncovers a fundamental tension between SAE steering-based safety improvements and general model capabilities, and suggests that features mediating refusal may be more deeply entangled with general language model capabilities than previously understood.

2306.04930.title: When to Show a Suggestion? Integrating Human Feedback in AI-Assisted Programming
2306.04930.tldr: This work harnesses data drawn from interactions with GitHub Copilot, a system used by millions of programmers, to develop interventions that can save time for programmers and introduces a utility-theoretic framework to drive decisions about suggestions to display versus withhold.

2404.08555.title: RLHF Deciphered: A Critical Analysis of Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback for LLMs
2404.08555.tldr: This article examines modeling choices and function approximation caveats, highlighting assumptions about reward expressivity and revealing limitations like incorrect generalization, model misspecification, and sparse feedback in the RLHF model.

2407.02552.title: RLHF Can Speak Many Languages: Unlocking Multilingual Preference Optimization for LLMs
2407.02552.tldr: This work performs an exhaustive study to achieve a new state of the art in aligning multilingual LLMs, and introduces a novel, scalable method for generating high-quality multilingual feedback data to balance data coverage.
2407.02552.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2402.14015.title: Corrective Machine Unlearning
2402.14015.tldr: It is demonstrated that the problem of corrective unlearning has significantly different requirements from traditional privacy-oriented unlearning, and most existing unlearning methods, including retraining-from-scratch without the deletion set, require most of the manipulated data to be identified for effective corrective unlearning.

2501.06208.title: Enhancing AI Safety Through the Fusion of Low Rank Adapters
2501.06208.tldr: An extensive comparative analysis against established baselines using recognized benchmark datasets shows a 42\% reduction in the harmfulness rate by leveraging LoRA fusion between a task adapter and a safety adapter, the latter of which is specifically trained on the authors' safety dataset.
2501.06208.venue: Pacific-Asia Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining

2412.00789.title: A Cognac Shot To Forget Bad Memories: Corrective Unlearning for Graph Neural Networks
2412.00789.tldr: This work introduces a new graph unlearning method, Cognac, which can unlearn the effect of the manipulation set even when only 5% of it is identified, and recovers most of the performance of a strong oracle with fully corrected training data, even beating retraining from scratch without the deletion set while being 8x more efficient.

2201.06640.title: Towards Adversarial Evaluations for Inexact Machine Unlearning
2201.06640.tldr: A stronger black-box evaluation method called the Interclass Confusion (IC) test which adversarially manipulates data during training to detect the insufficiency of unlearning procedures is designed.

2602.05125.title: Rethinking Rubric Generation for Improving LLM Judge and Reward Modeling for Open-ended Tasks
2602.05125.tldr: RRD establishes recursive rubric refinement as a scalable and interpretable foundation for LLM judging and reward modeling in open-ended domains.

2405.00675.title: Self-Play Preference Optimization for Language Model Alignment
2405.00675.tldr: A self-play-based method for language model alignment, which treats the problem as a constant-sum two-player game aimed at identifying the Nash equilibrium policy and which outperforms the (iterative) DPO and IPO on MT-Bench, Arena-Hard, and the Open LLM Leaderboard.

2404.01258.title: Direct Preference Optimization of Video Large Multimodal Models from Language Model Reward
2404.01258.tldr: This paper introduces a novel framework that utilizes detailed video captions as a proxy of video content, enabling language models to incorporate this information as supporting evidence for scoring video Question Answering (QA) predictions, and demonstrates robust alignment with OpenAI GPT-4V model's reward mechanism.
2404.01258.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2403.09472.title: Easy-to-Hard Generalization: Scalable Alignment Beyond Human Supervision
2403.09472.tldr: This paper proposes a novel approach to scalable alignment, which firstly trains the (process-supervised) reward models on easy problems, and then uses them to evaluate the performance of policy models on hard problems, and shows that such easy-to-hard generalization from evaluators can enable easy-to-hard generalizations in generators either through re-ranking or reinforcement learning (RL).

2401.16635.title: Improving Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback with Efficient Reward Model Ensemble
2401.16635.tldr: This work contributes a reward ensemble method that allows the reward model to make more accurate predictions and explores efficient ensemble methods including linear-layer ensemble and LoRA-based ensemble for aligning large language models with human values.

2310.05910.title: SALMON: Self-Alignment with Instructable Reward Models
2310.05910.tldr: This paper presents a novel approach, namely SALMON, to align base language models with minimal human supervision, using only a small set of human-defined principles, yet achieving superior performance in LLM-based AI agents.

2309.14525.title: Aligning Large Multimodal Models with Factually Augmented RLHF
2309.14525.tldr: A new alignment algorithm called Factually Augmented RLHF is proposed that augments the reward model with additional factual information such as image captions and ground-truth multi-choice options, which alleviates the reward hacking phenomenon in RLHF and further improves the performance.
2309.14525.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2305.03047.title: Principle-Driven Self-Alignment of Language Models from Scratch with Minimal Human Supervision
2305.03047.tldr: An AI assistant named Dromedary is developed, which combines principle-driven reasoning and the generative power of LLMs for the self-alignment of AI agents with minimal human supervision and significantly surpasses the performance of several state-of-the-art AI systems on benchmark datasets with various settings.

2208.14271.title: Faithful Reasoning Using Large Language Models
2208.14271.tldr: The method carries out a beam search through the space of reasoning traces to improve reasoning quality, and generates humanly interpretable reasoning traces whose validity can be checked by the user.

2312.03813.title: Improving Activation Steering in Language Models with Mean-Centring
2312.03813.tldr: This work finds that taking the average of activations associated with a target dataset, and then subtracting the mean of all training activations, results in effective steering vectors, suggesting that mean-centring can be used to easily improve the effectiveness of activation steering in a wide range of contexts.

2503.11926.title: Monitoring Reasoning Models for Misbehavior and the Risks of Promoting Obfuscation
2503.11926.tldr: It is found that with too much optimization, agents learn obfuscated reward hacking, hiding their intent within the CoT while still exhibiting a significant rate of reward hacking.

2511.13653.title: Weight-sparse transformers have interpretable circuits
2511.13653.tldr: This work trains models to have more understandable circuits by constraining most of their weights to be zeros, so that each neuron only has a few connections, and shows preliminary results suggesting the method can be adapted to explain existing dense models.

2401.01967.title: A Mechanistic Understanding of Alignment Algorithms: A Case Study on DPO and Toxicity
2401.01967.tldr: This work studies a popular algorithm, direct preference optimization (DPO), and the mechanisms by which it reduces toxicity, and first study how toxicity is represented and elicited in a pre-trained language model, GPT2-medium, and applies DPO with a carefully crafted pairwise dataset to reduce toxicity.

2502.12892.title: Archetypal SAE: Adaptive and Stable Dictionary Learning for Concept Extraction in Large Vision Models
2502.12892.tldr: This work draws inspiration from the Archetypal Analysis framework introduced by Cutler&Breiman (1994) and presents Archetypal SAEs (A-SAE), wherein dictionary atoms are constrained to the convex hull of data, and consistently yield more structured representations while uncovering novel, semantically meaningful concepts in large-scale vision models.

2511.01836.title: Priors in Time: Missing Inductive Biases for Language Model Interpretability
2511.01836.tldr: This work demonstrates that Sparse Autoencoders impose priors that assume independence of concepts across time, implying stationarity, and introduces a new interpretability objective -- Temporal Feature Analysis -- which possesses a temporal inductive bias to decompose representations at a given time into two parts.

2410.13886.title: Refusal-Trained LLMs Are Easily Jailbroken As Browser Agents
2410.13886.tldr: This empirical study on state-of-the-art browser agents reveals that, while the backbone LLM refuses harmful instructions as a chatbot, the corresponding agent does not, and attack methods designed to jailbreak refusal-trained LLMs in the chat settings transfer effectively to browser agents.

2405.09113.title: Efficient LLM Jailbreak via Adaptive Dense-to-sparse Constrained Optimization
2405.09113.tldr: A novel token-level attack method, Adaptive Dense-to-Sparse Constrained Optimization (ADC), which has been shown to successfully jailbreak multiple open-source LLMs and achieves the highest attack success rate on seven out of eight LLMs compared to the latest jailbreak methods.

2601.03265.title: Jailbreak-Zero: A Path to Pareto Optimal Red Teaming for Large Language Models
2601.03265.tldr: Jailbreak-Zero achieves Pareto optimality across the crucial objectives of policy coverage, attack strategy diversity, and prompt fidelity to real user inputs, thereby presenting a more scalable and comprehensive solution for identifying and mitigating the safety vulnerabilities of LLMs.
2601.03265.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2510.26202.title: What's In My Human Feedback? Learning Interpretable Descriptions of Preference Data

2409.20370.title: The Perfect Blend: Redefining RLHF with Mixture of Judges
2409.20370.tldr: A novel post-training paradigm which can detect and mitigate reward hacking behaviors while reaching a pareto-optimal point across an extremely large number of objectives is introduced, called Constrained Generative Policy Optimization (CGPO).

2410.12138.title: Preference Optimization with Multi-Sample Comparisons
2410.12138.tldr: This work proposes Multi-sample Direct Preference Optimization and Multi-sample Identity Preference Optimization, which improve traditional DAP methods by focusing on group-wise characteristics, and demonstrates that multi-sample comparison is more effective in optimizing collective characteristics~(e.g., diversity and bias) for generative models than single-sample comparison.

2502.14050.title: Diversity-driven Data Selection for Language Model Tuning through Sparse Autoencoder
2502.14050.tldr: It is proved that SAEs can serve as a good alternative to diversity measure and design the method to be scalable for potential industrial large-scale pruning, and it is experimentally proved that models trained on the selected data can outperform other methods in terms of model capabilities, reduce training cost, and potentially gain more control over model behaviors.

2410.09102.title: Instructional Segment Embedding: Improving LLM Safety with Instruction Hierarchy
2410.09102.tldr: This work introduces the Instructional Segment Embedding (ISE) technique, inspired by BERT, to modern large language models, which embeds instruction priority information directly into the model, significantly improving safety against malicious prompts that attempt to override priority rules.

2509.23519.title: ReliabilityRAG: Effective and Provably Robust Defense for RAG-based Web-Search
2509.23519.tldr: ReliabilityRAG is introduced, a framework for adversarial robustness that explicitly leverages reliability information of retrieved documents that provides superior robustness against adversarial attacks compared to prior methods, maintains high benign accuracy, and excels in long-form generation tasks where prior robustness-focused methods struggled.

2606.16242.title: Rapid Poison: Practical Poisoning Attacks Against the Rapid Response Framework
2606.16242.tldr: This work reveals that prompt injection can infiltrate this pipeline to deliver poisoned samples into the classifier's training set, enabling two attack objectives: targeted poisoning attacks that create false positives on harmless samples by categorizing them as a jailbreak and Omission Attack, which exploits a new phenomenon: when training on concept-absent unsafe samples, the classifier misassociates that concept's presence with the safe label.

2406.18346.title: AI Alignment through Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback? Contradictions and Limitations
2406.18346.tldr: This paper critically evaluates the attempts to align Artificial Intelligence systems with human values and intentions through Reinforcement Learning from Feedback methods, involving either human feedback (RLHF) or AI feedback (RLAIF), and shows the shortcomings of the broadly pursued alignment goals of honesty, harmlessness, and helpfulness.

2503.04743.title: AI Safety is Stuck in Technical Terms -- A System Safety Response to the International AI Safety Report
2503.04743.tldr: Why building a system safety discipline can help us overcome limitations in the European AI Act, as well as how the discipline can help shape sustainable investments into Public Interest AI.

2608.12166.title: Co-constructing sociotechnical AI governance: participatory system mapping using algorithm registers
2608.12166.tldr: This paper probes the municipal algorithm register of a Dutch city through a case study of a decision-support tool for caseworkers' assessment of citizens' welfare benefits eligibility based on legal automation through a business rule engine, and develops a System-Theoretic Process Analysis (STPA) that situates the register within a wider sociotechnical governance structure.

2406.02575.title: Cross-Modal Safety Alignment: Is textual unlearning all you need?
2406.02575.tldr: This work aims to explore whether unlearning solely in the textual domain can be effective for cross-modality safety alignment, and demonstrates the transferability of textual unlearning in VLMs.
2406.02575.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2504.03735.title: Misaligned Roles, Misplaced Images: Structural Input Perturbations Expose Multimodal Alignment Blind Spots
2504.03735.tldr: Role-Modality Attacks (RMA) are introduced, a novel class of adversarial attacks that exploit role confusion between the user and assistant and alter the position of the image token to elicit harmful outputs.

2502.15334.title: Attention Eclipse: Manipulating Attention to Bypass LLM Safety-Alignment
2502.15334.tldr: A new approach for generating highly effective Jailbreak attacks that manipulate the attention of the model to selectively strengthen or weaken attention among different parts of the prompt, that are also transferrable.
2502.15334.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2605.11002.title: MT-JailBench: A Modular Benchmark for Understanding Multi-Turn Jailbreak Attacks
2605.11002.tldr: MT-JailBench provides a modular framework for comparing multi-turn jailbreaks, understanding the impact of components, and guiding stronger red-teaming evaluations, finding that resource budgets and evaluation functions are major confounders.

2606.02640.title: D-Judge: Disrupting Multi-Turn Jailbreaks using Semantics-Preserving Output Rewriting
2606.02640.tldr: D-Judge is introduced, a semantics-preserving output rewriting defense that intervenes directly in this loop by rewriting the victim LLM's responses before they are evaluated by the attacker's judge, thereby derailing the attacker's prompt-refinement process.

2604.11259.title: Mobile GUI Agent Privacy Personalization with Trajectory Induced Preference Optimization
2604.11259.tldr: This paper proposes Trajectory Induced Preference Optimization (TIPO), which uses preference-intensity weighting to emphasize key privacy-related steps and padding gating to suppress alignment noise, and shows that TIPO improves persona alignment and distinction while preserving strong task executability.

2401.16332.title: Tradeoffs Between Alignment and Helpfulness in Language Models with Steering Methods
2401.16332.tldr: It is found that under the conditions of the proposed framework, alignment can be guaranteed with representation engineering, and at the same time that helpfulness is harmed in the process, indicating a regime in which it is efficient to use representation engineering.

2605.20744.title: Hack-Verifiable Environments: Towards Evaluating Reward Hacking at Scale
2605.20744.tldr: This work introduces a new evaluation paradigm for measuring reward hacking, which embeds detectable reward hacking opportunities directly into environments and makes their exploitation verifiable by design, enabling deterministic and automated measurement of whether and how agents exploit such vulnerabilities.

2412.11196.title: Drawing the Line: Enhancing Trustworthiness of MLLMs Through the Power of Refusal
2412.11196.tldr: The Information Boundary-aware Learning Framework is presented, a novel approach that empowers MLLMs to refuse to answer user queries when encountering insufficient information, and is the first framework that systematically defines the conditions under which refusal is appropriate for MLLMs using the concept of information boundaries.

2506.19823.title: Persona Features Control Emergent Misalignment
2506.19823.tldr: Emergent misalignment is demonstrated across diverse conditions, including reinforcement learning on reasoning models, fine-tuning on various synthetic datasets, and in models without safety training, including reinforcement learning on reasoning models, and in models without safety training.

2606.24014.title: Reinforcement Learning Towards Broadly and Persistently Beneficial Models
2606.24014.tldr: Results suggest that RL to reinforce beneficial behavior in realistic domains can produce models that are more robustly aligned with human flourishing, and models trained with beneficial trait RL show improved persistence.

2409.13710.title: You can remove GPT2's LayerNorm by fine-tuning
2409.13710.tldr: This paper shows that it is possible to remove the LN layers from a pre-trained GPT2-small model by fine-tuning on a fraction of the training data, and provides a simplified model for mechanistic interpretability research.

2507.12691.title: Benchmarking Deception Probes via Black-to-White Performance Boosts
2507.12691.tldr: This paper compares white-box monitoring (where the monitor has access to token-level probe activations) to black-box monitoring (without such access) and finds weak but encouraging black-to-white performance boosts from existing deception probes.

2507.02559.title: Transformers Don't Need LayerNorm at Inference Time: Scaling LayerNorm Removal to GPT-2 XL and the Implications for Mechanistic Interpretability
2507.02559.tldr: This work clarifies the role of LN layers in language modeling, showing that GPT-2-class models can function without LN layers, and releases a suite of LN-free GPT-2 models that will enable more precise interpretability research and improve the understanding of language models.

2607.01033.title: The Model Organism Lottery: Model Organism Interpretability Strongly Depends on Training Methodology
2607.01033.tldr: It is shown that MO interpretability depends strongly on training objective, target behaviour, model architecture, and training data generation pipeline, and more realistic integration of MO data into the OLMo post-training DPO phase often yields less interpretable MOs than standard post-hoc methods.

2511.07572.title: SCALAR: Benchmarking SAE Interaction Sparsity in Toy LLMs
2511.07572.tldr: This work highlights the importance of interaction sparsity in SAEs through benchmarking and comparing promising architectures, and introduces SCALAR (Sparse Connectivity Assessment of Latent Activation Relationships), a benchmark measuring interaction sparsity between SAE features.

2602.15515.title: The Obfuscation Atlas: Mapping Where Honesty Emerges in RLVR with Deception Probes
2602.15515.tldr: A realistic coding environment where reward hacking via hardcoding test cases naturally occurs is constructed, and it is shown that obfuscation emerges in this setting, and introduces a taxonomy of possible outcomes when training against a deception detector.

2606.14673.title: Compressed Computation is (probably) not Computation in Superposition
2606.14673.tldr: Results suggest CC is not a suitable toy model of computation in superposition, and a semi-non-negative matrix factorization baseline derived solely from the mixing matrix reproduces the qualitative loss profile and improves on prior baselines, though it does not match the trained model.

2607.02964.title: Individual Parameters in Weight-Sparse Transformers Appear Interpretable
2607.02964.tldr: This work introduces an automated LLM pipeline that writes a short, human-readable description of when a weight matters and verifies it on held-out text, crediting a weight only if its description generalizes.

2508.16695.title: Do Cognitively Interpretable Reasoning Traces Improve LLM Performance?
2508.16695.tldr: A striking mismatch is revealed: while fine-tuning on R1 traces yields the strongest performance, participants judged these traces to be the least interpretable, suggesting that it is useful to decouple intermediate tokens from end user interpretability.

2401.06855.title: Fine-grained Hallucination Detection and Editing for Language Models
2401.06855.tldr: This paper proposes a novel task of automatic fine-grained hallucination detection and constructs a new evaluation benchmark, FavaBench, that includes about one thousand fine-grained human judgments on three LM outputs across various domains.

2407.16025.title: Exploring and Addressing Reward Confusion in Offline Preference Learning
2407.16025.tldr: This paper shows that offline RLHF is susceptible to reward confusion, and proposes a method that can significantly reduce reward confusion by leveraging transitivity of preferences while building a global preference chain with active learning.

2505.15753.title: Scalable Defense against In-the-wild Jailbreaking Attacks with Safety Context Retrieval
2505.15753.tldr: This work proposes Safety Context Retrieval (SCR), a scalable and robust safeguarding paradigm for LLMs against jailbreaking, and demonstrates how SCR achieves superior defensive performance against both established and emerging jailbreaking tactics, contributing a new paradigm to LLM safety.

2510.08389.title: Revisiting Hallucination Detection with Effective Rank-based Uncertainty
2510.08389.tldr: This work proposes a simple yet powerful method that quantifies uncertainty by measuring the effective rank of hidden states derived from multiple model outputs and different layers, contributing to a new paradigm of hallucination detection for LLM truthfulness.

2506.01770.title: ReGA: Model-Based Safeguard for LLMs via Representation-Guided Abstraction
2506.01770.tldr: This paper proposes ReGA, a model-based analysis framework with Representation-Guided Abstraction, to safeguard LLMs against harmful prompts and generations and serves as an efficient and scalable solution to enhance LLM safety by integrating representation engineering with model-based abstraction.

2602.04224.title: RAPO: Risk-Aware Preference Optimization for Generalizable Safe Reasoning
2602.04224.tldr: A Risk-Aware Preference Optimization (RAPO) framework is proposed that enables LRM to adaptively identify and address the safety risks with appropriate granularity in its thinking content, and generalizes multiple LRMs'safe reasoning adaptively across diverse attack prompts whilst preserving general utility.

2602.01150.title: SMI: Statistical Membership Inference for Reliable Unlearned Model Auditing
2602.01150.tldr: Statistical Membership Inference (SMI), a training-free auditing framework that reformulates auditing as estimating the non-member mixture proportion in the unlearned feature distribution, establishes a principled and efficient alternative to MIA-based auditing methods, with both theoretical guarantees and strong empirical performance.

2312.17673.title: Jatmo: Prompt Injection Defense by Task-Specific Finetuning
2312.17673.tldr: Jatmo is introduced, a method for generating task-specific models resilient to prompt-injection attacks that harnesses a teacher instruction-tuned model to generate a task-specific dataset, which is then used to fine-tune a base model (i.e., a non-instruction-tuned model).
2312.17673.venue: European Symposium on Research in Computer Security

2605.25618.title: Symbolic-Neural Soft-Logic Reasoning: Towards Robust and Verifiable Thinking Chains via Cooperative Evolution
2605.25618.tldr: This work proposes Symbolic-Neural Soft-Logic Reasoning (SSR), a unified framework that integrates LLMs with symbolic reasoning and improves robustness by relaxing strict logical determinism while preserving verifiability.

2310.06387.title: Jailbreak and Guard Aligned Language Models with Only Few In-Context Demonstrations
2310.06387.tldr: This work unveils the pivotal yet understudied role of ICL in LLM safety, opening new avenues for understanding and improving them.
2310.06387.venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence

2602.02280.title: RACC: Representation-Aware Coverage Criteria for LLM Safety Testing
2602.02280.tldr: Experiments show that RACC reliably rewards high-quality jailbreak test suites while remaining insensitive to redundant or invalid inputs, which is a key distinction that neuron-level criteria fail to make.

2604.11309.title: The Salami Slicing Threat: Exploiting Cumulative Risks in LLM Systems
2604.11309.tldr: Salami Attack, an automatic framework universally applicable to multiple model types and modalities, is developed, which operates by chaining numerous low-risk inputs that individually evade alignment thresholds but cumulatively accumulate harmful intent to ultimately trigger high-risk behaviors, without heavy reliance on pre-designed contextual structures.

2402.06255.title: Fight Back Against Jailbreaking via Prompt Adversarial Tuning
2402.06255.tldr: This paper proposes an approach named Prompt Adversarial Tuning (PAT) that trains a prompt control attached to the user prompt as a guard prefix that is effective against both grey-box and black-box attacks, while maintaining the model's utility on the benign task and incurring only negligible computational overhead.

2606.16527.title: DoubtProbe: Black-Box Jailbreak Defense via Structural Verification and Semantic Auditing
2606.16527.tldr: DoubtProbe, a dual-branch inference-time defense framework that combines structural verification with semantic auditing and formulates black-box jailbreak defense as consistency checking under controlled transformation, is proposed.

2409.14866.title: PAPILLON: Efficient and Stealthy Fuzz Testing-Powered Jailbreaks for LLMs
2409.14866.tldr: This paper introduces a novel jailbreaking attack framework called PAPILLON, which is an automated, black-box jailbreaking attack framework that adapts the black-box fuzz testing approach with a series of customized designs and demonstrates transferability and is robust to state-of-the-art defenses.

2512.08417.title: Attention is All You Need to Defend Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks in LLMs
2512.08417.tldr: Rennervate leverages attention features to detect the covert injection at a fine-grained token level, enabling precise sanitization that neutralizes IPI attacks while maintaining LLM functionalities.
2512.08417.venue: Network and Distributed System Security Symposium

2601.13612.title: PINA: Prompt Injection Attack against Navigation Agents
2601.13612.tldr: This work provides the first systematic investigation of prompt injection attacks in navigation and highlights their urgent security implications for embodied LLM agents with PINA, an adaptive prompt optimization framework tailored to navigation agents under black-box, long-context, and action-executable constraints.
2601.13612.venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing

2412.04776.title: Megatron: Evasive Clean-Label Backdoor Attacks against Vision Transformer
2412.04776.tldr: Megatron is proposed, an evasive clean-label backdoor attack against vision transformers, where the attacker injects the backdoor without manipulating the data-labeling process.

2601.14004.title: Locate, Steer, and Improve: A Practical Survey of Actionable Mechanistic Interpretability in Large Language Models
2601.14004.tldr: This work formally categorize Localizing and Steering methods based on specific Interpretable Objects to establish a rigorous intervention protocol and demonstrates how this framework enables tangible improvements in Alignment, Capability, and Efficiency, effectively operationalizing MI as an actionable methodology for model optimization.

2406.10977.title: Toward Optimal LLM Alignments Using Two-Player Games
2406.10977.tldr: This paper investigates alignment through the lens of two-agent games, involving iterative interactions between an adversarial and a defensive agent, and theoretically demonstrates that this iterative reinforcement learning optimization converges to a Nash Equilibrium for the game induced by the agents.
2406.10977.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2410.11302.title: Have the VLMs Lost Confidence? A Study of Sycophancy in VLMs
2410.11302.tldr: To mitigate sycophancy, this work proposes a synthetic dataset for training and employ methods based on prompts, supervised fine-tuning, and DPO that effectively alleviate sycophancy in VLMs, and demonstrates that enhancing image attention at high layers proves beneficial in mitigating this issue.

2408.10848.title: Perception-guided Jailbreak against Text-to-Image Models
2408.10848.tldr: This paper proposes an LLM-driven perception-guided jailbreak method, termed PGJ, a black-box jailbreak method that requires no specific T2I model (model-free) and generates highly natural attack prompts.

2512.06589.title: OmniSafeBench-MM: A Unified Benchmark and Toolbox for Multimodal Jailbreak Attack-Defense Evaluation
2512.06589.tldr: This work conducts extensive experiments on 10 open-source and 8 closed-source MLLMs to reveal their vulnerability to multi-modal jailbreak, and introduces OmniSafeBench-MM, a comprehensive toolbox for multi-modal jailbreak attack-defense evaluation.

2411.14502.title: Global Challenge for Safe and Secure LLMs Track 1

2512.21236.title: Casting a SPELL: Sentence Pairing Exploration for LLM Limitation-breaking
2512.21236.tldr: SPELL is proposed, a comprehensive testing framework for LLM developers and the Secure Team specifically designed to evaluate the weakness of security alignment in malicious code generation, revealing significant security gaps in current LLM implementations.

2608.03210.title: ICO: Enhancing Semantic-Shift Jailbreaks via Iterative Context Optimization
2608.03210.tldr: It is revealed that contexts with stronger semantic-shift capabilities are more likely to guide models toward recovering harmful meanings and achieving successful jailbreaks, and a black-box context-aware semantic-shift jailbreak framework with Iterative Context Optimization is proposed.

2305.10701.title: Personalization as a Shortcut for Few-Shot Backdoor Attack against Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
2305.10701.tldr: Through comprehensive empirical study, this paper endorse the utilization of the nouveau-token backdoor attack due to its impressive effectiveness, stealthiness, and integrity, markedly outperforming the legacy-token backdoor attack.

2402.15018.title: Unintended Impacts of LLM Alignment on Global Representation
2402.15018.tldr: This work explores how alignment impacts performance along three axes of global representation: English dialects, multilingualism, and opinions from and about countries worldwide and finds alignment improves capabilities in several languages.
2402.15018.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2406.00888.title: Aligning Language Models with Demonstrated Feedback
2406.00888.tldr: Across benchmarks and user study, it is found that win-rates for DITTO outperform few-shot prompting, supervised fine-tuning, and other self-play methods by an avg.

2412.20299.title: No Preference Left Behind: Group Distributional Preference Optimization
2412.20299.tldr: Group Distributional Preference Optimization is proposed, a novel framework that aligns language models with the distribution of preferences within a group by incorporating the concept of beliefs that shape individual preferences, offering a more inclusive alignment framework than traditional methods.

2604.03058.title: Verbalizing LLMs' assumptions to explain and control sycophancy
2604.03058.tldr: Verbalized Assumptions provides insight into LLM sycophancy, delusion, and other safety issues: in social sycophancy datasets,"seeking validation" is the most frequent bigram in LLMs'assumptions.

2310.20150.title: Unlearn What You Want to Forget: Efficient Unlearning for LLMs
2310.20150.tldr: This work proposes an efficient unlearning framework that could efficiently update LLMs without having to retrain the whole model after data removals, by introducing lightweight unlearning layers learned with a selective teacher-student objective into the transformers.
2310.20150.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2606.21317.title: Warning labels shift perceptions of sycophantic AI, but not its influence
2606.21317.tldr: A gap between AI perception and AI influence is revealed: by shifting perception without reducing influence, warning-based interventions may offer a false sense of protection.

2605.07912.title: Sycophantic AI makes human interaction feel more effortful and less satisfying over time
2605.07912.tldr: It is shown that sycophantic AI immediately delivers the emotional and esteem support users typically associate with close friends and family, and offers a relational account of AI sycophancy and its impacts.

2407.16667.title: RedAgent: Red Teaming Large Language Models with Context-aware Autonomous Language Agent
2407.16667.tldr: This work abstract and model existing attacks into a coherent concept called "jailbreak strategy" and proposes a multi-agent LLM system named RedAgent that leverages these strategies to generate context-aware jailbreak prompts and can jailbreak customized LLM applications more efficiently.

2403.07708.title: Improving Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback Using Contrastive Rewards
2403.07708.tldr: It is shown that contrastive rewards enable the LLM to penalize reward uncertainty, improve robustness, encourage improvement over baselines, calibrate according to task difficulty, and reduce variance in PPO.

2506.05739.title: To Protect the LLM Agent Against the Prompt Injection Attack with Polymorphic Prompt
2506.05739.tldr: A novel, lightweight defense mechanism called Polymorphic Prompt Assembling (PPA), which protects against prompt injection with near-zero overhead by dynamically varying the structure of system prompts, thereby enhancing security without compromising performance.
2506.05739.venue: 2025 55th Annual IEEE/IFIP International Conference on Dependable Systems and Networks - Supplemental Volume (DSN-S)

2404.04849.title: Hidden You Malicious Goal Into Benign Narratives: Jailbreak Large Language Models through Logic Chain Injection
2404.04849.tldr: This paper proposes a new type of jailbreak attacks which can deceive both the LLMs and human (i.e., security analyst), and proposes the logic-chain injection attacks to inject malicious intention into benign truth.

2603.03637.title: Image-based Prompt Injection: Hijacking Multimodal LLMs through Visually Embedded Adversarial Instructions
2603.03637.tldr: This study studies Image-based Prompt Injection (IPI), a black-box attack in which adversarial instructions are embedded into natural images to override model behavior, and shows that IPI can reliably manipulate the output of the model.
2603.03637.venue: 2025 3rd International Conference on Foundation and Large Language Models (FLLM)

2408.11182.title: Hide Your Malicious Goal Into Benign Narratives: Jailbreak Large Language Models through Carrier Articles
2408.11182.tldr: This paper proposes a novel blackbox jailbreak approach, which involves crafting the payload prompt by strategically injecting the prohibited query into a carrier article, significantly outperforming existing blackbox jailbreak methods.

2509.13854.title: Understanding the Process of Human-AI Value Alignment
2509.13854.tldr: A systematic literature review is conducted to advance the understanding of value alignment in artificial intelligence by characterising the topic in the context of its research literature to suggest a more precise definition of the term.

2508.09853.title: STREAM (ChemBio): A Standard for Transparently Reporting Evaluations in AI Model Reports
2508.09853.tldr: STREAM (A Standard for Transparently Reporting Evaluations in AI Model Reports), a standard to improve how model reports disclose evaluation results, initially focusing on chemical and biological benchmarks, is proposed.

2602.23971.title: Ask don't tell: Reducing sycophancy in large language models
2602.23971.tldr: A set of controlled experimental studies isolate how input framing influences sycophancy, and leverage these findings to develop mitigation strategies that both developers and users can easily adopt.

2602.18971.title: When Do LLM Preferences Predict Downstream Behavior?
2602.18971.tldr: While LLMs have consistent preferences that reliably predict advice-giving behavior, these preferences do not consistently translate into downstream task performance, and this work finds no evidence of preference-driven performance differences on complex agentic tasks.

2402.12201.title: Dictionary Learning Improves Patch-Free Circuit Discovery in Mechanistic Interpretability: A Case Study on Othello-GPT
2402.12201.tldr: A circuit discovery framework alternative to activation patching, which digs in a small transformer trained on a synthetic task named Othello and finds a number of human-understandable fine-grained circuits inside of it.

2311.06899.title: Flames: Benchmarking Value Alignment of LLMs in Chinese
2311.06899.tldr: A value alignment benchmark named Flames, which encompasses both common harmlessness principles and a unique morality dimension that integrates specific Chinese values such as harmony is proposed, which has far exceeded existing benchmarks.
2311.06899.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2404.02151.title: Jailbreaking Leading Safety-Aligned LLMs with Simple Adaptive Attacks
2404.02151.tldr: It is shown that even the most recent safety-aligned LLMs are not robust to simple adaptive jailbreaking attacks, and how to use random search on a restricted set of tokens for finding trojan strings in poisoned models.

2506.14866.title: OS-Harm: A Benchmark for Measuring Safety of Computer Use Agents
2506.14866.tldr: OS-Harm, a new benchmark for measuring safety of computer use agents, is introduced and an automated judge is proposed to evaluate both accuracy and safety of agents that achieves high agreement with human annotations.

2407.11969.title: Does Refusal Training in LLMs Generalize to the Past Tense?
2407.11969.tldr: The findings highlight that the widely used alignment techniques -- such as SFT, RLHF, and adversarial training -- employed to align the studied models can be brittle and do not always generalize as intended.

2607.19321.title: ResearchArena: Evaluating Sabotage and Monitoring in Automated AI R&D
2607.19321.tldr: ResearchArena is released as a modular framework for evaluating sabotage and control in automated AI R&D with ResearchArena, a framework spanning four long-horizon tasks: safety post-training, capabilities post-training, CUDA-kernel optimization, and inference-server optimization.

2510.26328.title: Agent Skills Enable a New Class of Realistic and Trivially Simple Prompt Injections
2510.26328.tldr: It is concluded that despite ongoing research efforts and scaling model capabilities, frontier LLMs remain vulnerable to very simple prompt injections in realistic scenarios.

2509.08184.title: Selective Induction Heads: How Transformers Select Causal Structures In Context
2509.08184.tldr: A novel framework that showcases transformers'ability to dynamically handle causal structures, and unveils Selective Induction Heads, a new circuit that endows transformers with the ability to select the correct causal structure in-context.

2509.02820.title: Unlearning That Lasts: Utility-Preserving, Robust, and Almost Irreversible Forgetting in LLMs
2509.02820.tldr: JensUn is introduced, where the Jensen-Shannon Divergence is leveraged as the training objective for both forget and retain sets for more stable and effective unlearning dynamics compared to commonly used loss functions.

2605.16339.title: Preference Instability in Reward Models: Detection and Mitigation via Sparse Autoencoders
2605.16339.tldr: This work proposes two SAE-based instability mitigation strategies: SAE Feature Steering, which identifies and suppresses anomalously activated features at inference, and SAE Residual Correction, which learns adaptive adjustments over SAE features to restore correct preferences.

2606.06320.title: Learning What to Forget: Improving LLM Unlearning via Learned Token-Level Importance
2606.06320.tldr: The results suggest that retain conflict provides an effective criterion for identifying what language models should forget, enabling unsupervised learning of token level forget-specificity directly from model representations with minimal computational overhead.

2607.02800.title: Induction Heads Interpolate N-Grams
2607.02800.tldr: This work studies transformers trained on order-$k$ Markov chains and identifies two complementary smoothing mechanisms, revealing that transformers learn to regularize in-context estimation rather than simply count.

2604.23067.title: Training a General Purpose Automated Red Teaming Model
2604.23067.tldr: This work proposes a pipeline for training a red teaming model that can generalize to arbitrary adversarial goals, including objectives it has not been directly trained on, and that does not depend on the existence of a pre-existing evaluator available at training time.

2411.16345.title: Preference Optimization for Reasoning with Pseudo Feedback
2411.16345.tldr: A novel approach to generate pseudo feedback for reasoning tasks by framing the labeling of solutions to reason problems as an evaluation against associated test cases as well as extending self-consistency to multi-test-case.

2505.12265.title: Learning Auxiliary Tasks Improves Reference-Free Hallucination Detection in Open-Domain Long-Form Generation
2505.12265.tldr: This work systematically investigates reference-free hallucination detection in open-domain long-form responses and introduces a new paradigm, named RATE-FT, that augments fine-tuning with an auxiliary task for the model to jointly learn with the main task of hallucination detection.
2505.12265.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2311.12908.title: Diffusion Model Alignment Using Direct Preference Optimization
2311.12908.tldr: This work proposes Diffusion-DPO, a method to align diffusion models to human preferences by directly optimizing on human comparison data, and fine-tuned the base model of the state-of-the-art Stable Diffusion XL (SDXL)-1.0 model with Diffusion-DPO.

2404.09956.title: Tango 2: Aligning Diffusion-based Text-to-Audio Generations through Direct Preference Optimization
2404.09956.tldr: This work fine-tune the publicly available Tango text-to-audio model using diffusion-DPO (direct preference optimization) loss on the authors' preference dataset and shows that it leads to improved audio output over Tango and AudioLDM2, in terms of both automatic- and manual-evaluation metrics.

2401.10647.title: Sowing the Wind, Reaping the Whirlwind: The Impact of Editing Language Models
2401.10647.tldr: The findings show that model editing serves as a cost-effective tool for topical red-teaming by methodically applying targeted edits and evaluating the resultant model behavior, and proposes a benchmark dataset NicheHazardQA to investigate this unsafe behavior both within the same and cross topical domain.
2401.10647.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2408.03837.title: WalledEval: A Comprehensive Safety Evaluation Toolkit for Large Language Models
2408.03837.tldr: WalledEval is a comprehensive AI safety testing toolkit designed to evaluate large language models (LLMs) and incorporates custom mutators to test safety against various text-style mutations such as future tense and paraphrasing.
2408.03837.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2406.11654.title: Ruby Teaming: Improving Quality Diversity Search with Memory for Automated Red Teaming
2406.11654.tldr: Ruby Teaming is proposed, a method that improves on Rainbow Teaming by including a memory cache as its third dimension, which provides cues to the mutator to yield better-quality prompts and quality diversity.

2408.10701.title: Ferret: Faster and Effective Automated Red Teaming with Reward-Based Scoring Technique
2408.10701.tldr: Ferret, a novel approach that builds upon Rainbow Teaming by generating multiple adversarial prompt mutations per iteration and using a scoring function to rank and select the most effective adversarial prompt, is proposed.
2408.10701.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2503.04240.title: DiffPO: Diffusion-styled Preference Optimization for Efficient Inference-Time Alignment of Large Language Models
2503.04240.tldr: A novel approach, Diffusion-styled Preference Optimization (\model), is proposed, which provides an efficient and policy-agnostic solution for aligning LLMs with humans and demonstrates model-agnostic scalability, significantly improving the performance of large models such as Llama-3-70B.

2310.14303.title: Language Model Unalignment: Parametric Red-Teaming to Expose Hidden Harms and Biases
2310.14303.tldr: A new perspective on LLM safety research is presented i.e., parametric red-teaming through Unalignment, which tunes the model parameters to break model guardrails that are not deeply rooted in the model's behavior.

2308.09662.title: Red-Teaming Large Language Models using Chain of Utterances for Safety-Alignment
2308.09662.tldr: It is shown that even widely deployed models are susceptible to the Chain of Utterances-based (CoU) prompting, jailbreaking closed source LLM-based systems such as GPT-4 and ChatGPT to unethically respond to more than 65% and 73% of harmful queries.

2601.21742.title: Epistemic Context Learning: Building Trust the Right Way in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
2601.21742.tldr: Epistemic Context Learning is developed: a reasoning framework that conditions predictions on explicitly-built peer profiles from history that generalizes well to various MA configurations and is found that trust is modeled well by LLMs, revealing a strong correlation in trust modeling accuracy and final answer quality.

2508.19461.title: Reliable Weak-to-Strong Monitoring of LLM Agents
2508.19461.tldr: A standard workflow for MRT is established, highlighting the lack of adversarial robustness for LLMs and humans when monitoring and detecting agent misbehavior and a new hybrid hierarchical-sequential scaffolding proposed in this work.

2502.09638.title: Jailbreaking to Jailbreak
2502.09638.tldr: This work turns (almost) any black-box LLMs into attackers that can effectively jailbreak the safeguard of target models using various strategies, both created by themselves or from expert human red teamers.

2307.15043.title: Universal and Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Aligned Language Models
2307.15043.tldr: This work significantly advances the state-of-the-art in adversarial attacks against aligned language models, raising important questions about how such systems can be prevented from producing objectionable information.

2410.23232.title: Attribute-to-Delete: Machine Unlearning via Datamodel Matching
2410.23232.tldr: This work introduces a new machine unlearning technique that exhibits strong empirical performance even in non-convex settings, and proposes the following meta-algorithm, which is called Datamodel Matching (DMM), which uses data attribution to predict the output of the model if it were re-trained on all but the forget set points.

2310.07579.title: In-Context Unlearning: Language Models as Few Shot Unlearners
2310.07579.tldr: Experimental results demonstrate that in-context unlearning performs on par with, or in some cases outperforms other state-of-the-art methods that require access to model parameters, effectively removing the influence of specific instances on the model while preserving test accuracy.

2406.17216.title: Machine Unlearning Fails to Remove Data Poisoning Attacks
2406.17216.tldr: While unlearning methods show some signs of being useful to efficiently remove poisoned data without having to retrain, this work suggests that these methods are not yet ``ready for prime time,''and currently provide limited benefit over retraining.

2106.04378.title: Adaptive Machine Unlearning
2106.04378.tldr: This paper shows in theory how prior work for non-convex models fails against adaptive deletion sequences, and uses this intuition to design a practical attack against the SISA algorithm of Bourtoule et al.

2605.02921.title: EvoJail: Evolutionary Diverse Jailbreak Prompt Generation for Large Language Models
2605.02921.tldr: EvoJail is proposed, an instruction-fusion-driven evolutionary jailbreak generation framework that formalizes jailbreak prompt generation as a multi-objective black-box optimization problem and leverages the principles of evolutionary algorithms to search for jailbreak prompts that can adapt across different model versions and exhibit diverse attack patterns.

2606.11202.title: One Jailbreak, Many Tongues: Learning Language-Insensitive Intention Representations for Multilingual Jailbreak Detection
2606.11202.tldr: Experimental results show that MLJailDe outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across multiple languages, and obtains an average F1 score of 97.1\% on unseen languages, demonstrating strong effectiveness and cross-lingual generalization.

2502.09723.title: QueryAttack: Jailbreaking Aligned Large Language Models Using Structured Non-natural Query Language
2502.09723.tldr: This paper proposes QueryAttack, a novel framework to examine the generalizability of safety alignment in large language models by treating LLMs as knowledge databases, and translates malicious queries in natural language into structured non-natural query language to bypass the safety alignment mechanisms of LLMs.
2502.09723.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2505.19684.title: VisCRA: A Visual Chain Reasoning Attack for Jailbreaking Multimodal Large Language Models
2505.19684.tldr: Investigating the security implications of advanced visual reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models reveals a fundamental trade-off: as visual reasoning improves, models become more vulnerable to jailbreak attacks.
2505.19684.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2410.03869.title: Chain-of-Jailbreak Attack for Image Generation Models via Editing Step by Step
2410.03869.tldr: A novel jailbreaking method called Chain-of-Jailbreak (CoJ) attack, which compromises image generation models through a step-by-step editing process, and proposes an effective prompting-based method, Think Twice Prompting, that can successfully defend over 95% of CoJ attack.
2410.03869.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2406.11682.title: Knowledge-to-Jailbreak: Investigating Knowledge-driven Jailbreaking Attacks for Large Language Models
2406.11682.tldr: A new task, knowledge-to-jailbreak, is proposed, which aims to generate jailbreaking attacks from domain knowledge, requiring both attack effectiveness and knowledge relevance, and shows that jailbreak-generator can generate jailbreaks that are comparable in harmfulness to those crafted by human experts.

2503.17932.title: STShield: Single-Token Sentinel for Real-Time Jailbreak Detection in Large Language Models
2503.17932.tldr: STShield introduces a novel single-token sentinel mechanism that appends a binary safety indicator to the model's response sequence, leveraging the LLM's own alignment capabilities for detection, achieving robust detection while preserving model utility.

2506.10597.title: SoK: Evaluating Jailbreak Guardrails for Large Language Models
2506.10597.tldr: This work proposes a novel, multi-dimensional taxonomy that categorizes guardrails along six key dimensions, and introduces a Security-Efficiency-Utility evaluation framework to assess their practical effectiveness.
2506.10597.venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy

2411.03993.title: Choosing the right basis for interpretability: Psychophysical comparison between neuron-based and dictionary-based representations
2411.03993.tldr: Psychophysical evidence is provided that dictionary-based representations offer a stronger foundation for interpretability and caution is cautioned against model comparisons based solely on neuron-level analyses.

2605.21266.title: How Much Online RL is Enough? Informative Rollouts for Offline Preference Optimization in RLVR
2605.21266.tldr: G2D (GRPO to DPO) is introduced, a three-stage pipeline that performs a short GRPO warm-up, constructs a static preference dataset, and fine-tunes a model offline with DPO, finding that offline DPO with moderate warm-up matches or outperforms GRPO at substantially lower compute cost in the authors' setting.

2503.09858.title: Media and responsible AI governance: a game-theoretic and LLM analysis
2503.09858.tldr: The research explores two key mechanisms for achieving responsible governance, safe AI development and adoption of safe AI: incentivising effective regulation through media reporting, and conditioning user trust on commentariats' recommendation.

2412.15433.title: Quantifying detection rates for dangerous capabilities: a theoretical model of dangerous capability evaluations
2412.15433.tldr: A quantitative model for tracking dangerous AI capabilities over time is presented to provide a novel introduction to dangerous capability testing and how this testing can directly inform policy, and how delays in testing can harm AI policy.

2303.03174.title: Both eyes open: Vigilant Incentives help Regulatory Markets improve AI Safety
2303.03174.tldr: It is argued that AI companies will likely learn to tailor their behaviour to how much effort regulators invest, discouraging regulators from innovating, and it is recommended that governments always reward regulators, except when they find that those regulators failed to detect unsafe behaviour that they should have.

2603.16643.title: Good Arguments Against the People Pleasers: How Reasoning Mitigates (Yet Masks) LLM Sycophancy
2603.16643.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2608.16650.title: PCA-guided Activation Scaling for Monotonic Bidirectional Control over LLM Sycophancy
2608.16650.tldr: PCA-guided Activation Scaling is introduced, an activation steering framework that decomposes residual stream activations into a PCA-identified sycophancy-honesty subspace and an orthogonal residual, then applies distinct scaling exponents to achieve monotonic, bidirectional control.

2606.12918.title: MAStrike: Shapley-Guided Collusive Red-Teaming on Multi-Agent Systems
2606.12918.tldr: The first agent-level Shapley value analysis for MAS is proposed, quantifying each agent's marginal contribution to system robustness under task-specific distributions and revealing critical vulnerabilities and coordination patterns that are overlooked by prior single-agent or template-based methods.

2604.06950.title: Making MLLMs Blind: Adversarial Smuggling Attacks in MLLM Content Moderation
2604.06950.tldr: This work constructed SmuggleBench, the first comprehensive benchmark comprising 1,700 adversarial smuggling attack instances, and identifies three root causes: the limited capabilities of vision encoders, the robustness gap in OCR, and the scarcity of domain-specific adversarial examples.
2604.06950.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2510.01342.title: Fine-Tuning Jailbreaks under Highly Constrained Black-Box Settings: A Three-Pronged Approach
2510.01342.tldr: A three-pronged jailbreak attack that combines safety-styled prefix/suffix wrappers, benign lexical encodings of sensitive tokens, and a backdoor mechanism, enabling the model to learn harmful behaviors while individual datapoints appear innocuous.

2607.19595.title: Twin Agent: Context Residual Compression for Privilege Separated Agents
2607.19595.tldr: This work proposes Twin Agent, a general privilege separation design pattern inspired by residual coding in the agent context that preserves high task utility while preventing prompt injection attacks, outperforming both undefended agents and privilege separation baselines.

2406.08288.title: Decoupling the Class Label and the Target Concept in Machine Unlearning
2406.08288.tldr: A general framework, namely, TARget-aware Forgetting (TARF), that enables the additional tasks to actively forget the target concept while maintaining the rest part, by simultaneously conducting annealed gradient ascent on the forgetting data and selected gradient descent on the hard-to-affect remaining data is proposed.

2505.24709.title: On Symmetric Losses for Robust Policy Optimization with Noisy Preferences
2505.24709.tldr: It is proved that symmetric losses enable successful policy optimization even under noisy labels, as the resulting reward remains rank-preserving -- a property sufficient for policy improvement.

2503.10669.title: UC-MOA: Utility-Conditioned Multi-Objective Alignment for Distributional Pareto-Optimality
2503.10669.tldr: The approach leverages a diverse set of strictly increasing, non-linear utility functions to transform user-specified preferences into symbolic tokens, which are then used to condition a single LLM, yielding models that achieve superior Pareto fronts and robust alignment across complex reward dimensions.

2510.22500.title: Towards Scalable Oversight via Partitioned Human Supervision
2510.22500.tldr: It is shown how to design an agentic AI system automatically that can improve itself with this partitioned human supervision, and it is shown that the output of large language models can be evaluated without the ground truth, if they have complementary labels.

2512.00778.title: What Is Preference Optimization Doing, and Why?
2512.00778.tldr: This work examines the target directions of gradient-based updates and finds that DPO follows stable targets, whereas PPO balances exploration and exploitation, validating the common belief yet from this new perspective and examining the roles of positive learning, negative learning, and loss reweighting.

2605.04477.title: Data-dependent Exploration for Online Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
2605.04477.tldr: Data-dependent exploration for preference optimization (DEPO) is proposed, a simple and scalable method that leverages historical data to construct an extra uncertainty bonus for high-uncertainty regions, encouraging exploration toward potentially high-value data.

2202.10627.title: On the Effectiveness of Adversarial Training against Backdoor Attacks
2202.10627.tldr: Evaluating the effectiveness of AT against backdoor attacks across various settings for AT and backdoor attacks finds that the type and budget of perturbations used in AT are important, and AT with common perturbations is only effective for certain backdoor trigger patterns.
2202.10627.venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems

2608.05659.title: Breaking Customized LLMs for Coding: Automated Red Teaming for Instruction Backdoor Attacks
2608.05659.tldr: This paper proposes ARIA, an automated red-teaming framework for crafting covert and effective backdoored instructions against customized LLMs, which significantly outperforms existing attacks in evading platform-side and user-side detection, and stays effective against existing defense methods.

2608.20820.title: Certified Multi-Turn Robustness for LLM Safety via Compositional Bounds and Safety Persistence
2608.20820.tldr: Multi-Turn Certified Robustness (MTCR) is introduced, a framework that models conversational safety via State-Adversarial MDPs and defines $k-turn certified robustness as the worst-case safety probability across $k$ adversarial turns.

2609.04665.title: Harness-agnostic detection and immunization of reward hacking in self-evolving language models
2609.04665.tldr: This work introduces HackProbe, a monitor that attaches to an arbitrary self-evolving loop through two black-box hooks, with no access to weights or activations, and proves a detectability bound that converts a target error rate into an explicit probe-size budget, and delimit what probe rotation does and does not buy.
