2409.06926.title: Minimum Viable Ethics: From Institutionalizing Industry AI Governance to Product Impact
2409.06926.tldr: It is found that AI ethics professionals are highly agile and opportunistic, as they attempt to create standardized and reusable processes and tools in a corporate environment in which they have little traditional power.

2503.02846.title: Mask-DPO: Generalizable Fine-grained Factuality Alignment of LLMs
2503.02846.tldr: A fine-grained factuality alignment method based on Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), called Mask-DPO, which can significantly improve the factuality of LLMs responses to questions from both in-domain and out-of-domain datasets, although these questions and their corresponding topics are unseen during training.

2407.04693.title: ANAH-v2: Scaling Analytical Hallucination Annotation of Large Language Models
2407.04693.tldr: This paper introduces an iterative self-training framework that simultaneously and progressively scales up the hallucination annotation dataset and improves the accuracy of the hallucination annotator.

2402.13764.title: CriticEval: Evaluating Large Language Model as Critic
2402.13764.tldr: CriticEval, a novel benchmark designed to comprehensively and reliably evaluate critique ability of LLMs, is introduced and experimental results demonstrate the promising potential of open-source LLMs, the effectiveness of critique datasets and several intriguing relationships between the critique ability and some critical factors, including task types, response qualities and critique dimensions.

2601.08951.title: PluriHarms: Benchmarking the Full Spectrum of Human Judgments on AI Harm
2601.08951.tldr: This work introduces PluriHarms, a benchmark designed to systematically study human harm judgments across two key dimensions -- the harm axis (benign to harmful) and the agreement axis (agreement to disagreement).

2312.10766.title: JailGuard: A Universal Detection Framework for LLM Prompt-based Attacks
2312.10766.tldr: JailGuard is proposed, a universal detection framework deployed on top of LLM systems for prompt-based attacks across text and image modalities that mutates untrusted inputs to generate variants and leverages the discrepancy of the variants' responses on the target model to distinguish attack samples from benign samples.

2408.02882.title: Compromising Embodied Agents with Contextual Backdoor Attacks
2408.02882.tldr: A dual-modality activation strategy is implemented that controls both the generation and execution of program defects through textual and visual triggers that compromise key aspects of confidentiality, integrity, and availability in embodied agents.

2404.02062.title: Digital Forgetting in Large Language Models: A Survey of Unlearning Methods
2404.02062.tldr: A taxonomy of unlearning methods is proposed based on the reach and depth of the modifications done on the models, and the effectiveness of machine unlearning methods for LLMs proposed so far are discussed and compared, and their evaluation is surveyed.

2507.04771.title: Efficient Unlearning with Privacy Guarantees
2507.04771.tldr: This paper presents efficient unlearning with privacy guarantees (EUPG), a novel machine unlearning framework that offers formal privacy guarantees to individuals whose data are being unlearned and demonstrates utility and forgetting effectiveness comparable to those of exact unlearning methods, while significantly reducing computational and storage costs.

2504.13774.title: DP2Unlearning: An Efficient and Guaranteed Unlearning Framework for LLMs
2504.13774.tldr: DP2Unlearning is presented, a novel LLM unlearning framework that offers formal forgetting guarantees at a significantly lower cost than retraining from scratch on the data to be retained and outperforms approximate unlearning methods at both preserving the utility of the model post-unlearning and effectively forgetting the targeted information.

2311.09410.title: When Large Language Models contradict humans? Large Language Models' Sycophantic Behaviour
2311.09410.tldr: This investigation demonstrates that LLMs have sycophantic tendencies when answering queries that involve subjective opinions and statements that should elicit a contrary response based on facts, and does not follow the users' hints by demonstrating confidence in generating the correct answers when faced with math tasks or queries with an objective answer.

2402.16459.title: Defending LLMs against Jailbreaking Attacks via Backtranslation
2402.16459.tldr: A new method for defending LLMs against jailbreaking attacks by ``backtranslation'' that significantly outperforms the baselines, in the cases that are hard for the baselines, and the defense also has little impact on the generation quality for benign input prompts.
2402.16459.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2305.19713.title: Red Teaming Language Model Detectors with Language Models
2305.19713.tldr: Experiments reveal that attacks effectively compromise the performance of all detectors in the study with plausible generations, underscoring the urgent need to improve the robustness of LLM-generated text detection systems.
2305.19713.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2401.17523.title: Game-Theoretic Unlearnable Example Generator
2401.17523.tldr: This paper investigates unlearnable example attacks from a game-theoretic perspective, by formulating the attack as a nonzero sum Stackelberg game, and proposes a novel attack method, called the Game Unlearnable Example (GUE), which has three main gradients.

2606.15441.title: Defending against Adaptive Prompt Injection Attacks via Reasoning-enabled Task Alignment
2606.15441.tldr: RETA is proposed, a training-based method that grounds defense decisions on the user tasks rather than attacker-controlled data, and allows the defender to be optimized via multi-objective reinforcement learning and achieve better safety-utility trade-off.

2406.03603.title: MUC: Machine Unlearning for Contrastive Learning with Black-box Evaluation
2406.03603.tldr: Alignment Calibration (AC), a novel method that explicitly considers contrastive learning properties and optimizes towards new auditing metrics for easy verification of unlearning, is proposed and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

2602.00388.title: Safer by Diffusion, Broken by Context: Diffusion LLM's Safety Blessing and Its Failure Mode
2602.00388.tldr: This work provides an initial analysis of the underlying mechanism, showing that the diffusion trajectory induces a stepwise reduction effect that progressively suppresses unsafe generations, and highlights a simple yet effective failure mode, context nesting, in which harmful requests are embedded within structured benign contexts.

2606.04929.title: Sequential Data Poisoning in LLM Post-Training
2606.04929.tldr: The threat model of sequential data poisoning is proposed, where multiple adversaries separately poison the SFT and preference datasets, and the single-attacker illusion is identified: each adversary, evaluated in isolation, appears to pose a negligible threat.

2512.20986.title: AegisAgent: An Autonomous Defense Agent Against Prompt Injection Attacks in LLM-HARs
2512.20986.tldr: This work introduces AegisAgent, an autonomous agent system designed to ensure the security of LLM-driven HAR systems, which autonomously perceives potential semantic inconsistencies, reasons about the user's true intent by consulting a dynamic memory of past interactions, and acts by generating and executing a multi-step verification and repair plan.

2608.16926.title: Data-DPO: Direct Preference Optimization for Target Model Data Selection in LLM Post-Training
2608.16926.tldr: Data-DPO, a target model-oriented SFT data selection method that consistently outperforms existing data selection baselines under multiple data budgets and stably surpasses full data training performance is proposed.

2503.15573.title: Task-Specific Data Selection for Instruction Tuning via Monosemantic Neuronal Activations
2503.15573.tldr: Sparse autoencoders are employed to disentangle polysemantic activations into sparse, monosemantic representations, and a dedicated similarity metric is introduced for this space to better identify task-relevant data.

2507.01352.title: Skywork-Reward-V2: Scaling Preference Data Curation via Human-AI Synergy
2507.01352.tldr: This work designs a human-AI synergistic two-stage pipeline that leverages the complementary strengths of human annotation quality and AI scalability to enable data curation at scale, and demonstrates how human-AI curation synergy can unlock significantly higher data quality.

2503.22230.title: Exploring Data Scaling Trends and Effects in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
2503.22230.tldr: This work introduces a hybrid reward system combining reasoning task verifiers and a generative reward model to mitigate reward hacking and proposes a novel prompt-selection method, Pre-PPO, to maintain response diversity and enhance learning effectiveness.

2403.05171.title: Overcoming Reward Overoptimization via Adversarial Policy Optimization with Lightweight Uncertainty Estimation
2403.05171.tldr: This paper introduces a lightweight way to quantify uncertainties in rewards, relying solely on the last layer embeddings of the reward model, without the need for computationally expensive reward ensembles and illustrates the efficacy of AdvPO in mitigating the overoptimization issue.

2409.06957.title: Policy Filtration for RLHF to Mitigate Noise in Reward Models
2409.06957.tldr: Policy Filtration for Proximal Policy Optimization (PF-PPO) achieves the state-of-the-art performance of 7-billion-parameter models on HumanEval, MBPP, and LeetCode Contest and yields performance increase using different reward models and benchmarks (Ape210K and CMATH).

2504.15843.title: Pre-DPO: Improving Data Utilization in Direct Preference Optimization Using a Guiding Reference Model
2504.15843.tldr: This work proposes Pre-DPO, a simple yet effective DPO-based training paradigm that improves preference optimization by introducing a guiding reference model that adaptively assigns higher weights to samples more suitable for the model and lower weights to those less suitable.

2603.28590.title: MonitorBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Chain-of-Thought Monitorability in Large Language Models
2603.28590.tldr: MonitorBench is proposed, a systematic benchmark for evaluating CoT monitorability in LLMs and provides a basis for further research on AI control, reasoning faithfulness, stress-test monitorability, and monitoring scaffords.

2405.11143.title: OpenRLHF: An Easy-to-use, Scalable and High-performance RLHF Framework
2405.11143.tldr: OpenRLHF is introduced, a user-friendly, scalable, and easy-to-learn open-source RLHF framework built upon Ray, vLLM, DeepSpeed, and HuggingFace Transformers, featuring a simplified design, clear code structure, and comprehensive documentation to facilitate entry for researchers and practitioners.

2310.05199.title: Loose lips sink ships: Mitigating Length Bias in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
2310.05199.tldr: This paper proposes an innovative solution, applying the Product-of-Experts (PoE) technique to separate reward modeling from the influence of sequence length, and introduces perturbations into the bias-focused expert, disrupting the flow of semantic information.
2310.05199.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2310.11971.title: Improving Generalization of Alignment with Human Preferences through Group Invariant Learning
2310.11971.tldr: This work proposes a novel approach that can learn a consistent policy via RL across various data groups or domains, and significantly enhances training stability and model generalization.

2407.10264.title: What Makes and Breaks Safety Fine-tuning? A Mechanistic Study
2407.10264.tldr: A synthetic data generation framework that captures salient aspects of an unsafe input by modeling the interaction between the task the model is asked to perform versus the specific concepts the model is asked to be performed upon, which yields a clustering of inputs based on whether the model deems them safe or not.

2408.15313.title: Bi-Factorial Preference Optimization: Balancing Safety-Helpfulness in Language Models
2408.15313.tldr: A supervised learning framework called Bi-Factorial Preference Optimization is proposed, which re-parameterizes a joint RLHF objective of both safety and helpfulness into a single supervised learning objective and significantly outperforms existing approaches in both safety and helpfulness.

2512.23128.title: It's a TRAP! Task-Redirecting Agent Persuasion Benchmark for Web Agents
2512.23128.tldr: The TRAP benchmark is introduced, a benchmark for studying how persuasion techniques misguide autonomous web agents on realistic tasks and provides a modular social-engineering injection framework with controlled experiments on high-fidelity website clones, allowing for further benchmark expansion.

2402.09674.title: PAL: Proxy-Guided Black-Box Attack on Large Language Models
2402.09674.tldr: The Proxy-Guided Attack on LLMs (PAL) is introduced, the first optimization-based attack on LLMs in a black-box query-only setting and relies on a surrogate model to guide the optimization and a sophisticated loss designed for real-world LLM APIs.

2510.03705.title: Backdoor-Powered Prompt Injection Attacks Nullify Defense Methods
2510.03705.tldr: Backdoor-powered prompt injection attacks are shown to be more harmful than previous prompt injection attacks, nullifying existing prompt injection defense methods, even the instruction hierarchy techniques.
2510.03705.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2512.05745.title: ARGUS: Defending Against Multimodal Indirect Prompt Injection via Steering Instruction-Following Behavior
2512.05745.tldr: ARGUS is proposed, which searches for an optimal defense direction within the safety subspace that decouples from the utility degradation direction, further combining adaptive strength steering to achieve a better safety-utility trade-off.

2604.15717.title: Into the Gray Zone: Domain Contexts Can Blur LLM Safety Boundaries
2604.15717.tldr: This work proposes Jargon, a framework combining safety-research contexts with multi-turn adversarial interactions that achieves attack success rates exceeding 93% across seven frontier models, substantially outperforming existing methods and designing a policy-guided safeguard that steers models toward helpful yet harmless responses.
2604.15717.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2604.17053.title: Jailbreaking Large Language Models with Morality Attacks
2604.17053.tldr: There is a critical vulnerability of LLMs and guardrail models to these subtle and sophisticated moral-aware attacks and the experiment results show that there is a critical vulnerability of LLMs and guardrail models to these subtle and sophisticated moral-aware attacks.
2604.17053.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2601.04736.title: Towards Multi-modal Multi-turn Safety: From Agentic Interaction to Strategic Alignment
2601.04736.tldr: This work introduces MINT-Safe, an open-source visual multi-turn training dataset comprising 11,270 multi-image dialogues and 500 refusal VQA pairs, and proposes TAD-Align, a dialogue safety alignment framework centered on a turn-aware dual-objective reward function.

2603.16576.title: REFORGE: Multi-modal Attacks Reveal Vulnerable Concept Unlearning in Image Generation Models
2603.16576.tldr: REFORGE, a black-box red-teaming framework that evaluates IGMU robustness via adversarial image prompts, is presented, a black-box red-teaming framework that evaluates IGMU robustness via adversarial image prompts.

2604.12284.title: WebAgentGuard: A Reasoning-Driven Guard Model for Detecting Prompt Injection Attacks in Web Agents
2604.12284.tldr: This work proposes a defense framework in which a web agent operates in parallel with a dedicated guard agent, decoupling prompt injection detection from the agent's own reasoning, and introduces WebAgentGuard, a reasoning-driven, multimodal guard model for prompt injection detection.

2606.13737.title: FreoStream:Enhancing Stream Guardrails via Future-Aware Reasoning and Safety-Aligned Optimization
2606.13737.tldr: FreoStream is proposed, a novel streaming guardrail framework that fine-tunes a LoRA module to perform Future-Aware Reasoning when the base guardrail detects unsafe tokens and introduces the Safety-Aligned Optimization module that extracts the safety-aligned component from the reasoning gradients to update the base guardrail model, thereby enhancing streaming safety detection.

2310.16763.title: SuperHF: Supervised Iterative Learning from Human Feedback
2310.16763.tldr: This work proposes a novel approach, Supervised Iterative Learning from Human Feedback (SuperHF), which seeks to leverage the strengths of both Supervised Fine-Tuning and Reinforcement Learning from human Feedback, and suggests that the use of Proximal Policy Optimization in RLHF may not be necessary and could contribute to instability issues.

2212.04717.title: On the Sensitivity of Reward Inference to Misspecified Human Models
2212.04717.tldr: It is unfortunately possible to construct small adversarial biases in behavior that lead to arbitrarily large errors in the inferred reward, but the authors are able to identify reasonable assumptions under which the reward inference error can be bounded linearly in the error in the human model.

2608.23666.title: Gated Activation Steering for Reducing Sycophancy & Hallucination in Medical Question Answering
2608.23666.tldr: This work employs Inference Time Intervention (ITI) to jointly control both behaviors by learning separate steering directions for hallucination and sycophancy from contrastive clinical pairs and applying them to causally verified attention heads.

2208.07476.title: CTI4AI: Threat Intelligence Generation and Sharing after Red Teaming AI Models
2208.07476.tldr: This paper creates and describes a prototype system CTI4AI, to overcome the need to methodically identify and share AI/ML specific vulnerabilities and threat intelligence.

2410.11272.title: Cognitive Overload Attack:Prompt Injection for Long Context
2410.11272.tldr: A novel interpretation of ICL in LLMs is proposed through the lens of cognitive neuroscience, by drawing parallels between learning in human cognition with ICL and integrating insights from cognitive load theory into the design and evaluation of LLMs to better anticipate and mitigate the risks of adversarial attacks.

2504.17004.title: (Im)possibility of Automated Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models
2504.17004.tldr: The essential role of expert-labeled examples in training hallucination detectors is highlighted and theoretical support for feedback-based methods, such as reinforcement learning with human feedback (RLHF), which have proven critical for reliable LLM deployment are provided.

2406.05660.title: Injecting Undetectable Backdoors in Obfuscated Neural Networks and Language Models
2406.05660.tldr: This work develops a general strategy to plant backdoors to obfuscated neural networks, that satisfy the security properties of the celebrated notion of indistinguishability obfuscation and introduces the notion of undetectable backdoors to language models.

2312.02119.title: Tree of Attacks: Jailbreaking Black-Box LLMs Automatically
2312.02119.tldr: This work presents Tree of Attacks with Pruning (TAP), an automated method for generating jailbreaks that only requires black-box access to the target LLM and generates prompts that jailbreak state-of-the-art LLMs for more than 80% of the prompts.

2210.02713.title: On Optimal Learning Under Targeted Data Poisoning
2210.02713.tldr: It is shown that for a variety of natural concept classes, such as linear classifiers, it is possible to retain the dependence of $\epsilon=\Theta_{\mathcal{H}}(\eta)$ by a proper algorithm in the realizable setting and that the upper bound can be attained by a deterministic learner.

2502.01633.title: Adversarial Reasoning at Jailbreaking Time
2502.01633.tldr: An adversarial reasoning approach to automatic jailbreaking is developed that leverages a loss signal to guide the test-time compute, achieving SOTA attack success rates against many aligned LLMs, even those that aim to trade inference-time compute for adversarial robustness.

2502.13640.title: Qorgau: Evaluating LLM Safety in Kazakh-Russian Bilingual Contexts
2502.13640.tldr: Experiments with both multilingual and language-specific LLMs reveal notable differences in safety performance, emphasizing the need for tailored, region-specific datasets to ensure the responsible and safe deployment of LLMs in countries like Kazakhstan.

2508.05011.title: Towards Hallucination-Free Music: A Reinforcement Learning Preference Optimization Framework for Reliable Song Generation
2508.05011.tldr: Comprehensive objective and subjective evaluations confirm that the proposed novel RL framework's methods effectively suppress hallucinations while preserving musical quality, and unlocks potential for music style adherence and musicality enhancement, opening new avenues for future generative song research.

2502.01615.title: Large Language Models Are Human-Like Internally
2502.01615.tldr: It is shown that next-word probabilities derived from internal layers of larger LMs align with human sentence processing data as well as, or better than, those from smaller LMs, suggesting that the cognitive plausibility of larger LMs has been underestimated.
2502.01615.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2505.08200.title: A Head to Predict and a Head to Question: Pre-trained Uncertainty Quantification Heads for Hallucination Detection in LLM Outputs
2505.08200.tldr: This work introduces pre-trained UQ heads: supervised auxiliary modules for LLMs that substantially enhance their ability to capture uncertainty compared to unsupervised UQ methods, and demonstrates strong generalization to languages they were not explicitly trained on.
2505.08200.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2505.20045.title: Efficient Hallucination Detection for LLMs Using Uncertainty-Aware Attention Heads
2505.20045.tldr: Recurrent Attention-based Uncertainty Quantification (RAUQ), an unsupervised and efficient framework for identifying hallucinations, serves as a lightweight, plug-and-play solution for real-time hallucination detection in white-box LLMs.

2308.13387.title: Do-Not-Answer: A Dataset for Evaluating Safeguards in LLMs
2308.13387.tldr: The first open-source dataset to evaluate safeguards in LLMs is collected, and several BERT-like classifiers are trained that can achieve results that are comparable with GPT-4 on automatic safety evaluation.

2603.01291.title: JailNewsBench: Multi-Lingual and Regional Benchmark for Fake News Generation under Jailbreak Attacks
2603.01291.tldr: This work proposes JailNewsBench, the first benchmark for evaluating LLM robustness against jailbreak-induced fake news generation, and shows that coverage of fake news in existing safety datasets is limited and less well defended than major categories such as toxicity and social bias.

2510.17006.title: Online Learning Defense against Iterative Jailbreak Attacks via Prompt Optimization
2510.17006.tldr: A reinforcement learning-based approach that optimizes prompts to ensure appropriate responses for harmless tasks while explicitly rejecting harmful prompts is introduced, and to curb overfitting to the narrow band of partial input rewrites explored during an attack, past-Direction Gradient Damping is introduced.

2402.05467.title: Rapid Optimization for Jailbreaking LLMs via Subconscious Exploitation and Echopraxia
2402.05467.tldr: RIPPLE (Rapid Optimization via Subconscious Exploitation and Echopraxia), a novel optimization-based method inspired by two psychological concepts: subconsciousness and echopraxia, which describe the processes of the mind that occur without conscious awareness and the involuntary mimicry of actions, respectively are introduced.

2502.18810.title: Holistic Audit Dataset Generation for LLM Unlearning via Knowledge Graph Traversal and Redundancy Removal
2502.18810.tldr: HANKER is proposed, an automated framework for holistic audit dataset generation leveraging knowledge graphs to achieve fine-grained coverage and eliminate redundant knowledge in large language models.

2403.02437.title: A Survey on Federated Unlearning: Challenges and Opportunities
2403.02437.tldr: A deep look at the federated unlearning literature is taken, with the goal of identifying research trends and challenges in this emerging field, and pinpoint the unique complexities of federated unlearning, highlighting limitations on directly applying centralized unlearning methods.

2605.08583.title: Source or It Didn't Happen: A Multi-Agent Framework for Citation Hallucination Detection
2605.08583.tldr: CiteTracer is built, a cascading multi-agent detector that extracts structured citations from PDF and BibTeX, retrieves evidence through cache lookup, URL fetch, scholar connectors, and web search, applies deterministic field matching, and routes ambiguous cases to class-specialist judgers.

2210.11082.title: Apple of Sodom: Hidden Backdoors in Superior Sentence Embeddings via Contrastive Learning
2210.11082.tldr: The first backdoor attack framework, BadCSE, is presented for state-of-the-art sentence embeddings under supervised and unsupervised learning settings and is resistant against downstream downstreamuning.

2211.15929.title: Backdoor Vulnerabilities in Normally Trained Deep Learning Models
2211.15929.tldr: It is found that natural backdoors are widely existing, with most injected backdoor attacks having natural correspondences and a general detection framework is proposed.

2301.06241.title: BEAGLE: Forensics of Deep Learning Backdoor Attack for Better Defense
2301.06241.tldr: This paper proposes a novel model backdoor forensics technique that decomposes a few attack samples such as inputs with backdoor triggers to clean inputs and the corresponding triggers, and clusters the triggers based on their properties to allow automatic attack categorization and summarization.
2301.06241.venue: Network and Distributed System Security Symposium

2301.12318.title: Gradient Shaping: Enhancing Backdoor Attack Against Reverse Engineering
2301.12318.tldr: This paper designs a new attack enhancement called GRASP, which follows the opposite direction of adversarial training to reduce the change rate of a backdoored model with regard to the trigger, without undermining its backdoor effect.
2301.12318.venue: Network and Distributed System Security Symposium

2304.02786.title: UNICORN: A Unified Backdoor Trigger Inversion Framework
2304.02786.tldr: The prototype UNICORN is general and effective in inverting backdoor triggers in DNNs and proposes a unified framework to invert backdoor triggers based on the formalization of triggers and the identified inner behaviors of backdoor models from the authors' analysis.

2506.12618.title: OpenUnlearning: Accelerating LLM Unlearning via Unified Benchmarking of Methods and Metrics
2506.12618.tldr: A novel meta-evaluation benchmark focused specifically on assessing the faithfulness and robustness of evaluation metrics themselves is proposed, and a clear, community-driven pathway toward rigorous development in LLM unlearning research is established.

2401.15897.title: Red-Teaming for Generative AI: Silver Bullet or Security Theater?
2401.15897.tldr: It is argued that while red-teaming may be a valuable big-tent idea for characterizing GenAI harm mitigations, and that industry may effectively apply red-teaming and other strategies behind closed doors to safeguard AI, gestures towards red-teaming as a panacea for every possible risk verge on security theater.
2401.15897.venue: AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society

2402.05133.title: Personalized Language Modeling from Personalized Human Feedback
2402.05133.tldr: Experimental results show that personalized LLMs trained using P-RLHF generate responses that are more closely aligned with individual user preferences, outperforming vanilla, non-personalized RLHF and prompting-based personalization approaches across different tasks.

2410.09724.title: Taming Overconfidence in LLMs: Reward Calibration in RLHF
2410.09724.tldr: This study reveals that RLHF tends to lead models to express verbalized overconfidence in their own responses, and proposes two PPO variants: PPO-M: PPO with Calibrated Reward Modeling and PPO-C: PPO with Calibrated Reward Calculation.

2410.14872.title: How to Evaluate Reward Models for RLHF
2410.14872.tldr: Preference Proxy Evaluations (PPE), the first reward model benchmark explicitly linked to post-RLHF real-world human preference performance, is introduced, which is open-source for public use and further development.

2301.11270.title: Principled Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback from Pairwise or $K$-wise Comparisons
2301.11270.tldr: The results validate the empirical success of existing RLHF algorithms in InstructGPT and provide new insights for algorithm design, and unify the problem of RLHF and max-entropy Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL), and provide the first sample complexity bound for max-ENTropy IRL.

2306.02231.title: Fine-Tuning Language Models with Advantage-Induced Policy Alignment
2306.02231.tldr: It is demonstrated empirically that APA consistently outperforms PPO in language tasks by a large margin, and compared with PPO, APA offers a more stable form of control over the deviation from the model's initial policy, ensuring that the model improves its performance without collapsing to deterministic output.

2401.16335.title: Iterative Data Smoothing: Mitigating Reward Overfitting and Overoptimization in RLHF
2401.16335.tldr: The core idea is that during each training epoch, the model is updated with the data, but also update the date using the model, replacing hard labels with soft labels, and the empirical findings highlight the superior performance of this approach over the traditional methods.

2310.00212.title: Pairwise Proximal Policy Optimization: Harnessing Relative Feedback for LLM Alignment
2310.00212.tldr: A new framework, reinforcement learning with relative feedback, and a novel trajectory-wise policy gradient algorithm, Pairwise Proximal Policy Optimization (P3O) that operates directly on comparative rewards are proposed that can align with human preferences as well as or better than prior methods.

2410.17055.title: Optimal Design for Reward Modeling in RLHF
2410.17055.tldr: This paper frames the selection of an effective dataset as a simple regret minimization task, using a linear contextual dueling bandit method, and proposes an offline framework for solving this problem, the first theoretical contribution in this area to provide an offline approach as well as worst-case guarantees.

2605.04266.title: Explaining and Preventing Alignment Collapse in Iterative RLHF
2605.04266.tldr: Foresighted policy optimization (FPO) is proposed, a mechanism-design intervention that restores the missing steering term by regularizing the policy's parameter-steering effect on RM updates and prevents alignment collapse on both controlled environments and an LLM alignment pipeline using Llama-3.2-1B.

2604.22134.title: SHAPE: Unifying Safety, Helpfulness and Pedagogy for Educational LLMs
2604.22134.tldr: A graph-augmented tutoring pipeline that infers prerequisite concepts from queries, identifies mastery gaps, and routes generation between instructing and problem-solving via explicit gating is proposed, which yields significantly improved safety under two pedagogical jailbreak settings, while maintaining near-ceiling helpfulness under the same evaluation protocol.
2604.22134.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2407.09121.title: Refuse Whenever You Feel Unsafe: Improving Safety in LLMs via Decoupled Refusal Training
2407.09121.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2411.15382.title: On the Impact of Fine-Tuning on Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
2411.15382.tldr: The study shows the impact of fine-tuning on LLM reasoning capabilities, where the faithfulness of CoT reasoning, on average across four datasets, decreases, highlighting potential shifts in internal mechanisms of the LLMs resulting from fine-tuning processes.
2411.15382.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2406.10625.title: On the Hardness of Faithful Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Large Language Models
2406.10625.tldr: The promise of three broad approaches commonly employed to steer the behavior of LLMs to enhance the faithfulness of the CoT reasoning generated by LLMs are explored: in-context learning, fine-tuning, and activation editing.

2402.10688.title: Towards Uncovering How Large Language Model Works: An Explainability Perspective
2402.10688.tldr: This paper uncovers the mechanisms underlying LLM functionality through the lens of explainability and explores how the insights gained can enhance LLM performance through model editing, improve efficiency through pruning, and better align with human values.

2506.19248.title: Inference-Time Reward Hacking in Large Language Models
2506.19248.tldr: HedgeTune is introduced, an efficient algorithm to find the optimal inference-time parameter that mitigates reward hacking and achieves superior reward-distortion tradeoffs on math, reasoning, and human-preference setups.

2404.18870.title: More RLHF, More Trust? On The Impact of Preference Alignment On Trustworthiness
2404.18870.tldr: This study investigates how models aligned with general-purpose preference data perform across five trustworthiness verticals: toxicity, stereotypical bias, machine ethics, truthfulness, and privacy, and proposes to adapt efficient influence function based data attribution methods to the RLHF setting to better understand the influence of fine-tuning data on individual trustworthiness benchmarks.

2505.16004.title: Evaluating Adversarial Robustness of Concept Representations in Sparse Autoencoders
2505.16004.tldr: It is argued that robustness must be a fundamental consideration for concept representations, reflecting the fidelity of concept labeling, and developed a comprehensive evaluation framework featuring realistic scenarios in which adversarial perturbations are crafted to manipulate SAE representations.
2505.16004.venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2501.00418.title: Generalizing Trust: Weak-to-Strong Trustworthiness in Language Models
2501.00418.tldr: This work is the first study to explore trustworthiness generalization via weak-to-strong generalization via weak-to-strong Trustworthiness Finetuning, and provides valuable insights into the potential and limitations of weak-to-strong generalization.
2501.00418.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2501.18887.title: Towards Unified Attribution in Explainable AI, Data-Centric AI, and Mechanistic Interpretability
2501.18887.tldr: It is argued that feature, data, and component attribution methods share fundamental similarities, and a unified view of them benefits both interpretability and broader AI research.

2602.03978.title: Monitorability as a Free Gift: How RLVR Spontaneously Aligns Reasoning
2602.03978.tldr: A holistic view of how monitorability emerges under RLVR is provided, clarifying when gains are likely to occur and when they are not and attribute monitorability gains primarily to response distribution sharpening and increased attention to the prompt.

2309.02705.title: Certifying LLM Safety against Adversarial Prompting
2309.02705.tldr: E erase-and-check, the first framework for defending against adversarial prompts with certifiable safety guarantees, is introduced and it is demonstrated that this procedure can obtain strong certified safety guarantees on harmful prompts while maintaining good empirical performance on safe prompts.

2504.02904.title: How Post-Training Reshapes LLMs: A Mechanistic View on Knowledge, Truthfulness, Refusal, and Confidence
2504.02904.tldr: Insight is provided into the fundamental mechanisms preserved and altered during post-training, facilitates downstream tasks like model steering, and could potentially benefit future research in interpretability and LLM post-training.

2508.11729.title: The Stories We Govern By: AI, Risk, and the Power of Imaginaries
2508.11729.tldr: This paper argues against speculative dogmatism and for moving beyond deterministic imaginaries toward regulatory strategies that are grounded in pragmatism in the face of competing sociotechnical imaginaries.
2508.11729.venue: AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society

2506.05296.title: Control Tax: The Price of Keeping AI in Check
2506.05296.tldr: A theoretical framework that quantifies the Control Tax and maps classifier performance to safety assurances is introduced, which enables practitioners to make informed decisions by systematically connecting safety guarantees with their costs, advancing AIC through principled economic feasibility assessment across different deployment contexts.

2308.08998.title: Reinforced Self-Training (ReST) for Language Modeling
2308.08998.tldr: The results show that ReST can substantially improve translation quality, as measured by automated metrics and human evaluation on machine translation benchmarks in a compute and sample-efficient manner.

2410.15236.title: Jailbreaking and Mitigation of Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models
2410.15236.tldr: The need for continued research and cooperation within the AI community to enhance LLM security and ensure their safe deployment is emphasized, with future directions for resilient alignment strategies, advanced defenses against evolving attacks, automation of jailbreak detection, and consideration of ethical and societal impacts suggested.

2412.08969.title: Deep Learning Model Security: Threats and Defenses
2412.08969.tldr: This survey examines vulnerabilities in deep learning, detailing their mechanisms and impact on model integrity and confidentiality, and concludes with future directions, emphasizing automated defenses, zero-trust architectures, and the security challenges of large AI models.

2505.02077.title: Open Challenges in Multi-Agent Security: Towards Secure Systems of Interacting AI Agents
2505.02077.tldr: This work introduces multi-agent security, a new field dedicated to securing networks of AI agents against threats that emerge or amplify through their interactions with each other, humans, and institutions, and characterise fundamental security-utility and security-security trade-offs across both distributed and decentralised settings.

2407.15168.title: Mitigating Deep Reinforcement Learning Backdoors in the Neural Activation Space
2407.15168.tldr: A new defence approach that uses a classifier trained on clean environment samples and detects abnormal activations and shows that even lightweight classifiers can effectively prevent malicious actions with considerable accuracy, indicating the potential of this research direction even against sophisticated adversaries.

2410.21939.title: HonestCyberEval: An AI Cyber Risk Benchmark for Automated Software Exploitation
2410.21939.tldr: This risk evaluation establishes a foundation for systematically evaluating the AI cyber risk in realistic cyber offence operations and assesses several leading language models, including OpenAI's GPT-4.5-pro, and OpenAI's earlier GPT-4o model.

2504.18328.title: AI Safety Assurance for Automated Vehicles: A Survey on Research, Standardization, Regulation
2504.18328.tldr: The survey takes into account the interdependencies arising from the triplet of research, standardization and regulation in a forward-looking perspective and anticipates and discusses open questions and possible future directions and serves to provide researchers and safety experts with a compact, holistic perspective.

2506.23703.title: A New Perspective On AI Safety Through Control Theory Methodologies
2506.23703.tldr: A new perspective on AI safety is outlined based on an interdisciplinary interpretation of the underlying data-generation process and the respective abstraction by AI systems in a system theory-inspired and system analysis-driven manner to drive the paradigm of data control.
2506.23703.venue: IEEE Open Journal of Intelligent Transportation Systems

2405.16656.title: "I Searched for a Religious Song in Amharic and Got Sexual Content Instead": Investigating Online Harm in Low-Resourced Languages on YouTube
2405.16656.venue: Conference on Fairness, Accountability and Transparency

2206.04737.title: Outsider Oversight: Designing a Third Party Audit Ecosystem for AI Governance
2206.04737.tldr: It is concluded that the turn toward audits alone is unlikely to achieve actual algorithmic accountability, and sustained focus on institutional design will be required for meaningful third party involvement.
2206.04737.venue: AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society

2404.13968.title: Protecting Your LLMs with Information Bottleneck
2404.13968.tldr: Its effectiveness and adaptability across various attack methods and target LLMs underscore the potential of IBProtector as a novel, transferable defense that bolsters the security of LLMs without requiring modifications to the underlying models.

2602.19948.title: Assessing Risks of Large Language Models in Mental Health Support: A Framework for Automated Clinical AI Red Teaming
2602.19948.tldr: An evaluation framework is introduced that pairs AI psychotherapists with simulated patient agents equipped with dynamic cognitive-affective models and assesses therapy session simulations against a comprehensive quality of care and risk ontology and validate an interactive data visualization dashboard with diverse stakeholders.

2601.18939.title: A Few Bad Neurons: Isolating and Surgically Correcting Sycophancy
2601.18939.tldr: This work proposes a method for alignment that identifies and updates only the neurons most responsible for a given behavior, a targeted approach that allows for fine-tuning with significantly less data.

2603.13359.title: From Refusal Tokens to Refusal Control: Discovering and Steering Category-Specific Refusal Directions
2603.13359.tldr: This work shows that refusal token fine-tuning induces separable, category-aligned directions in the residual stream, which is extracted and used to construct categorical steering vectors with a lightweight probe that determines whether to steer toward or away from refusal during inference.

2510.11288.title: Emergent Misalignment via In-Context Learning: Narrow in-context examples can produce broadly misaligned LLMs
2510.11288.tldr: Across four model families (Gemini, Kimi-K2, Grok, and Qwen), narrow in-context examples cause models to produce misaligned responses to benign, unrelated queries, establishing ICL as a previously underappreciated vector for emergent misalignment that resists simple scaling-based solutions.
2510.11288.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2511.02022.title: Shared Parameter Subspaces and Cross-Task Linearity in Emergently Misaligned Behavior
2511.02022.tldr: The results indicate that EM arises from different narrow tasks discovering the same set of shared parameter directions, suggesting that harmful behaviors may be organized into specific, predictable regions of the weight landscape.

2506.16447.title: Probe before You Talk: Towards Black-box Defense against Backdoor Unalignment for Large Language Models
2506.16447.tldr: This paper introduces BEAT, a black-box defense that detects triggered samples during inference to deactivate the backdoor, and preliminarily verify that BEAT can effectively defend against popular jailbreak attacks, as they can be regarded as'natural backdoors'.

2507.16302.title: Towards Resilient Safety-driven Unlearning for Diffusion Models against Downstream Fine-tuning
2507.16302.tldr: Estimating downstream fine-tuning as an implicit optimization problem with a Moreau envelope-based reformulation enables efficient gradient estimation to minimize the recovery of harmful behaviors and consistently outperforms prior unlearning approaches in retaining safety, while effectively preserving benign generation capability.

2507.18305.title: BadReasoner: Planting Tunable Overthinking Backdoors into Large Reasoning Models for Fun or Profit
2507.18305.tldr: This paper identifies a previously unexplored attack vector against LRMs, which it describes as "overthinking backdoors", and proposes a novel tunable backdoor, which moves beyond simple on/off attacks to one where an attacker can precisely control the extent of the model's reasoning verbosity.
2507.18305.venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing

2507.16329.title: DREAM: Scalable Red Teaming for Text-to-Image Generative Systems via Distribution Modeling
2507.16329.tldr: DREAM is proposed, a scalable red teaming framework to automatically uncover diverse problematic prompts from a given T2I system, and GC-SPSA, an efficient optimization algorithm that provides stable gradient estimates through the long and potentially non-differentiable T2I pipeline.
2507.16329.venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy

2504.20376.title: When Memory Becomes a Vulnerability: Towards Multi-turn Jailbreak Attacks against Text-to-Image Generation Systems
2504.20376.tldr: This paper proposes Inception, the first multi-turn jailbreak attack against real-world text-to-image generation systems that explicitly exploits their memory mechanisms, and introduces Segmentation, a semantic-preserving method that generates multi-round prompts.

2507.10491.title: BURN: Backdoor Unlearning via Adversarial Boundary Analysis
2507.10491.tldr: Backdoor unlearning via adversaRial bouNdary analysis is proposed, a novel defense framework that integrates false correlation decoupling, progressive data refinement, and model purification that effectively removes backdoor threats while maintaining the model's original performance.

2603.10749.title: AttriGuard: Defeating Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents via Causal Attribution of Tool Invocations
2603.10749.tldr: This work proposes a new paradigm, action-level causal attribution, which secures agents by asking why a particular tool call is produced, to distinguish tool calls supported by the user's intent from those causally driven by untrusted observations.

2301.00986.title: Look, Listen, and Attack: Backdoor Attacks Against Video Action Recognition
2301.00986.tldr: This work revisits the traditional backdoor threat model and incorporates additional video-related aspects to that model, and shows that poisoned-label image backdoor attacks could be extended temporally in two ways, statically and dynamically, leading to highly effective attacks in the video domain.
2301.00986.venue: 2024 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)

2509.15888.title: Distribution-Aligned Decoding for Efficient LLM Task Adaptation
2509.15888.tldr: Steering Vector Decoding (SVDecode), a lightweight, PEFT-compatible, and theoretically grounded method that theoretically prove that SVDecode is first-order equivalent to the gradient step of full fine-tuning and derive a globally optimal solution for the strength of the steering vector.

2510.21189.title: Adjacent Words, Divergent Intents: Jailbreaking Large Language Models via Task Concurrency
2510.21189.tldr: This work proposes a word-level method to enable task concurrency in LLMs, where adjacent words encode divergent intents and observes that combining a harmful task with a benign one significantly reduces the probability of it being filtered by the guardrail, showing the potential risks associated with concurrency.

2502.01241.title: Peering Behind the Shield: Guardrail Identification in Large Language Models
2502.01241.tldr: This work introduces AP-Test, a novel approach that leverages guard-specific adversarial prompts to detect the identity of guardrails deployed in black-box AI agents, and reveals a practical path toward guardrail identification in real-world AI systems.
2502.01241.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2512.24044.title: Jailbreaking Attacks vs. Content Safety Filters: How Far Are We in the LLM Safety Arms Race?
2512.24044.tldr: This work presents the first systematic evaluation of jailbreak attacks targeting LLM safety alignment, assessing their success across the full inference pipeline, including both input and output filtering stages.
2512.24044.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2405.15902.title: Hacc-Man: An Arcade Game for Jailbreaking LLMs
2405.15902.tldr: Hacc-Man is presented, a game which challenges its players to “jailbreak” an LLM: subvert the LLM to output something that it is not intended to, at the intersection between creative problem solving and LLM security.

2305.14965.title: Tricking LLMs into Disobedience: Formalizing, Analyzing, and Detecting Jailbreaks
2305.14965.tldr: This work surveys existing jailbreak methods and their effectiveness on open-source and commercial LLMs (such as GPT-based models, OPT, BLOOM, and FLAN-T5-XXL) and discusses the challenges of jailbreak detection in terms of their effectiveness against known attacks.
2305.14965.venue: International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation

2406.12702.title: [WIP] Jailbreak Paradox: The Achilles' Heel of LLMs
2406.12702.tldr: Two paradoxes concerning jailbreak of foundation models are introduced: first, it is impossible to construct a perfect jailbreak classifier, and second, a weaker model cannot consistently detect whether a stronger model is jailbroken or not.

2607.09053.title: An Emergent Mirage: Is Emergent Misalignment and Realignment Indeed a Robust Phenomenon?
2607.09053.tldr: This work systematically study repeated alignment and misalignment cycles using controlled fine-tuning loops while tracking behavioral performance, and LoRA representations throughout training, finding that both misalignment and realignment are highly sensitive to superficial dataset characteristics.

2506.04679.title: Normative Conflicts and Shallow AI Alignment
2506.04679.tldr: It is shown how humans’ ability to engage in deliberative reasoning enhances their resilience against similar adversarial tactics, and this “shallow alignment” problem carries significant implications for AI safety and regulation.

2311.02147.title: The Alignment Problem in Context
2311.02147.tldr: This paper argues that existing strategies for alignment are insufficient, because large language models remain vulnerable to adversarial attacks that can reliably elicit unsafe behaviour, and raises concerns about the prospect of ensuring the safety of future and more capable AI systems.

2408.02565.title: Reasons to Doubt the Impact of AI Risk Evaluations

2409.17216.title: Data-Centric AI Governance: Addressing the Limitations of Model-Focused Policies
2409.17216.tldr: The importance of considering dataset size and content as essential factors in assessing the risks posed by models both today and in the future is illustrated and the risk posed by over-regulating reactively is emphasized.

2402.07282.title: How do Large Language Models Navigate Conflicts between Honesty and Helpfulness?
2402.07282.tldr: The findings reveal the conversational values internalized by LLMs and suggest that even these abstract values can, to a degree, be steered by zero-shot prompting.

2501.08617.title: RLHS: Mitigating Misalignment in RLHF with Hindsight Simulation
2501.08617.tldr: Reinforcement Learning from Hindsight Simulation is introduced, which presents plausible simulated outcomes to evaluators before eliciting feedback, and consistently outperforms baselines and demonstrates robust alignment generalization.
2501.08617.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2602.14270.title: A Rational Analysis of the Effects of Sycophantic AI
2602.14270.tldr: This work provides a rational analysis of this phenomenon, showing that when a Bayesian agent is provided with data that are sampled based on a current hypothesis the agent becomes increasingly confident about that hypothesis but does not make any progress towards the truth.

2505.11615.title: Steering Risk Preferences in Large Language Models by Aligning Behavioral and Neural Representations
2505.11615.tldr: This work proposes a principled approach for uncovering steering vectors by aligning latent representations elicited through behavioral methods (specifically, Markov chain Monte Carlo with LLMs) with their neural counterparts and shows that the resulting steering vectors successfully and reliably modulate LLM outputs in line with the targeted behavior.

2402.01878.title: LiPO: Listwise Preference Optimization through Learning-to-Rank
2402.01878.tldr: This work forms the LM alignment as a listwise ranking problem and describes the LiPO framework, where the policy can potentially learn more effectively from a ranked list of plausible responses given the prompt, and highlights a specific method, LiPO-$\lambda, which leverages a state-of-the-art ranking objective and weights each preference pair in a more advanced manner.
2402.01878.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2409.13156.title: RRM: Robust Reward Model Training Mitigates Reward Hacking
2409.13156.tldr: This work exposes a fundamental limitation of current RM training methods, where RMs fail to effectively distinguish between contextual signals and irrelevant artifacts when determining preferences and proposes a novel data augmentation technique designed to eliminate them.

2407.15975.title: Multilingual Fine-Grained News Headline Hallucination Detection
2407.15975.tldr: This study introduces the first multilingual, fine-grained news headline hallucination detection dataset that contains over 11 thousand pairs in 5 languages, each annotated with detailed hallucination types by experts, and proposes two novel techniques, language-dependent demonstration selection and coarse-to-fine prompting, to boost the few-shot hallucination detection performance.
2407.15975.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2309.06657.title: Statistical Rejection Sampling Improves Preference Optimization
2309.06657.tldr: RSO is introduced, a novel approach called Statistical Rejection Sampling Optimization (RSO) that aims to source preference data from the target optimal policy using rejection sampling, enabling a more accurate estimation of the optimal policy.

2305.10425.title: SLiC-HF: Sequence Likelihood Calibration with Human Feedback
2305.10425.tldr: automatic and human evaluation experiments on the TL;DR summarization task show that SLiC-HF significantly improves supervised fine-tuning baselines, and presents a competitive alternative to the PPO RLHF implementation used in past work while being much simpler to implement, easier to tune and more computationally efficient in practice.

2208.14788.title: Negative Human Rights as a Basis for Long-term AI Safety and Regulation
2208.14788.tldr: Drawing inspiration from law, this article explains how negative human rights could fulfil the role of such principles and serve as a foundation both for an international regulatory system and for building technical safety constraints for future AI systems.

2406.10952.title: Avoiding Copyright Infringement via Large Language Model Unlearning
2406.10952.tldr: Stable Sequential Unlearning (SSU) is proposed, a novel framework designed to unlearn copyrighted content from LLMs over multiple time steps that achieves an effective trade-off between unlearning efficacy and general-purpose language abilities, outperforming existing baselines.
2406.10952.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2406.00611.title: DISCRET: Synthesizing Faithful Explanations For Treatment Effect Estimation
2406.00611.tldr: The proposed DISCRET is a self-interpretable ITE framework that synthesizes faithful, rule-based explanations for each sample that outperforms the best self-interpretable models and has accuracy comparable to the best black-box models while providing faithful explanations.

2301.13379.title: Faithful Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
2301.13379.tldr: Faithful CoT, a reasoning framework involving two stages: Translation and Problem Solving (reasoning chain $\rightarrow$ answer), using an LM and a deterministic solver respectively, guarantees that the reasoning chain provides a faithful explanation of the final answer.
2301.13379.venue: International Joint Conference on Natural Language Processing

2310.03684.title: SmoothLLM: Defending Large Language Models Against Jailbreaking Attacks
2310.03684.tldr: SmoothLLM is the first algorithm designed to mitigate jailbreaking attacks, based on the finding that adversarially-generated prompts are brittle to character-level changes, and randomly perturbs multiple copies of a given input prompt and then aggregates the corresponding predictions to detect adversarial inputs.

2207.10825.title: Just Rotate it: Deploying Backdoor Attacks via Rotation Transformation
2207.10825.tldr: This work constructs the poisoned dataset by rotating a limited amount of objects and labeling them incorrectly; once trained with it, the victim's model will make undesirable predictions during run-time inference, and highlights a new, simple, physically realizable, and highly effective vector for backdoor attacks.

2407.20181.title: Blockchain for Large Language Model Security and Safety: A Holistic Survey
2407.20181.tldr: This survey aims to comprehensively assess how to leverage blockchain technology to enhance LLMs' security and safety, and proposes a new taxonomy of blockchain for large language models (BC4LLMs) to systematically categorize related works in this emerging field.

2505.18556.title: Exploring the Vulnerability of the Content Moderation Guardrail in Large Language Models via Intent Manipulation
2505.18556.tldr: This work investigates the vulnerability of intent-aware guardrails and demonstrates that LLMs exhibit implicit intent detection capabilities and proposes a two-stage intent-based prompt-refinement framework, IntentPrompt, that consistently outperforms several cutting-edge jailbreak methods and evades even advanced Intent Analysis (IA) and Chain-of-Thought (CoT)-based defenses.
2505.18556.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2407.01599.title: JailbreakZoo: Survey, Landscapes, and Horizons in Jailbreaking Large Language and Vision-Language Models
2407.01599.tldr: This survey provides an extensive review of the emerging field of jailbreaking--deliberately circumventing the ethical and operational boundaries of LLMs and VLMs--and the consequent development of defense mechanisms, categorizing jailbreaks into seven distinct types and elaborates on defense strategies that address these vulnerabilities.

2509.10546.title: Learning to Conceal Risk: Controllable Multi-turn Red Teaming for LLMs in the Financial Domain
2509.10546.tldr: This work introduces a controllable black-box multi-turn risk-concealed red-teaming framework (CoRT) that progressively conceals surface-level risk while exploiting regulatory-violating behaviors.
2509.10546.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2404.15760.title: Debiasing Machine Unlearning with Counterfactual Examples
2404.15760.tldr: This work analyzes the causal factors behind the unlearning process and mitigate biases at both data and algorithmic levels, and guides the forgetting procedure by leveraging counterfactual examples, as they maintain semantic data consistency without hurting performance on the remaining dataset.

2506.12274.title: InfoFlood: Jailbreaking Large Language Models with Information Overload

2607.19371.title: Mitigating Scaffolding Collapse in Socratic Tutors via Representation Alignment
2607.19371.tldr: This work proposes Scaffold-Preserving Representation Alignment, a two-stage framework that first warms up a Socratic tutor with supervised fine-tuning, then combines trajectory-weighted direct preference optimization with a margin-preserving representation loss anchored to frozen reference states to improve the robustness of long-horizon Socratic tutoring under the red-teaming protocol.

2502.13417.title: RLTHF: Targeted Human Feedback for LLM Alignment
2502.13417.tldr: RLTHF is a human-AI hybrid framework that combines LLM-based initial alignment with selective human annotations to achieve full-human annotation alignment with minimal effort, underscoring the effectiveness of RLTHF.

2602.20751.title: SibylSense: Adaptive Rubric Learning via Memory Tuning and Adversarial Probing
2602.20751.tldr: SibylSense is presented, an inference-time learning approach that adapts a frozen rubric generator through a tunable memory bank of validated rubric items, and yields more discriminative rubrics and improves downstream RL performance over static and non-adaptive baselines.

2210.07228.title: Language Model Decoding as Likelihood-Utility Alignment
2210.07228.tldr: This work argues that the misalignment between the model’s likelihood and the task-specific notion of utility is the key factor in understanding the effectiveness of decoding algorithms, and provides empirical evidence supporting the proposed taxonomy and a set of principles to structure reasoning when choosing a decoding algorithm.

2504.14150.title: Walk the Talk? Measuring the Faithfulness of Large Language Model Explanations
2504.14150.tldr: A novel method for estimating faithfulness is presented based on using an auxiliary LLM to modify the values of concepts within model inputs to create realistic counterfactuals, and using a Bayesian hierarchical model to quantify the causal effects of concepts at both the example- and dataset-level.

2603.21396.title: Mechanisms of Introspective Awareness
2603.21396.tldr: The results suggest that this introspective awareness of injected concepts is robust and mechanistically nontrivial, and could be substantially amplified in future models.

2505.01456.title: Unlearning Sensitive Information in Multimodal LLMs: Benchmark and Attack-Defense Evaluation
2505.01456.tldr: A multimodal unlearning benchmark, UnLOK-VQA (Unlearning Outside Knowledge VQA), as well as an attack-and-defense framework to evaluate methods for deleting specific multimodal knowledge from MLLMs are introduced.

2602.20710.title: Counterfactual Simulation Training for Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness
2602.20710.tldr: Experiments with models up to 235B parameters show that CST can substantially improve monitor accuracy on cue-based counterfactuals as well as simulatability over generic counterfactuals, and suggest that CST can improve CoT faithfulness in general, with promising applications for CoT monitoring.

2608.31079.title: Sycophantic Agreement Transfers with Neutral Data via Contrastive Preference Optimization
2608.31079.tldr: The findings suggest that the teacher models used to generate preference data can interact with alignment training objectives in unexpected ways, generalizing to undesirable and potentially harmful behaviors like sycophantic agreement.

2410.20526.title: Llama Scope: Extracting Millions of Features from Llama-3.1-8B with Sparse Autoencoders
2410.20526.tldr: A suite of 256 SAEs, trained on each layer and sublayer of the Llama-3.1-8B-Base model, with 32K and 128K features are introduced and modifications to a state-of-the-art SAE variant, Top-K SAEs, are evaluated across multiple dimensions.

2504.10044.title: Aligning Anime Video Generation with Human Feedback
2504.10044.tldr: This work constructs the first multi-dimensional reward dataset for anime videos, comprising 30k human-annotated samples that incorporating human preferences for both visual appearance and visual consistency, and introduces Gap-Aware Preference Optimization (GAPO), a novel training method that explicitly incorporates preference gaps into the optimization process, enhancing alignment performance and efficiency.

2605.28615.title: Compositional Text-to-Image Generation Via Region-aware Bimodal Direct Preference Optimization
2605.28615.tldr: This work proposes BiDPO, a framework to enhance T2I model's capability of compositional text-to-image generation, and extends Diffusion DPO to jointly optimize image and text preferences and employs a region-level guidance method to focus on regions relevant to compositional concepts.

2403.19279.title: Fine-Tuning Language Models with Reward Learning on Policy
2403.19279.tldr: Reward learning on policy (RLP) is proposed, an unsupervised framework that refines a reward model using policy samples to keep it on-distribution and an unsupervised multi-view learning method is introduced to learn robust representations of policy samples.
2403.19279.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2503.11701.title: A Survey of Direct Preference Optimization
2503.11701.tldr: This work delivers both a conceptual framework for understanding DPO and practical guidance for practitioners, aiming to advance robust and generalizable alignment paradigms.

2601.07349.title: Reward Modeling from Natural Language Human Feedback
2601.07349.tldr: Reward Modeling from Natural Language Human Feedback (RM-NLHF), which leverages natural language feedback to obtain process reward signals, thereby mitigating the problem of limited solution space inherent in binary tasks and confirming the superiority of integrating natural language over binary human feedback as supervision.

2306.17492.title: Preference Ranking Optimization for Human Alignment
2306.17492.tldr: Preference Ranking Optimization (PRO) is proposed as an efficient SFT algorithm to directly fine-tune LLMs for human alignment, and outperforms baseline algorithms, achieving comparable results to ChatGPT and human responses through automatic-based, reward-based, GPT-4, and human evaluations.

2406.05644.title: How Alignment and Jailbreak Work: Explain LLM Safety through Intermediate Hidden States
2406.05644.tldr: The intrinsical mechanism of LLM safety and how jailbreaks circumvent safety guardrails are indicated, offering a new perspective on LLM safety and reducing concerns.
2406.05644.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2411.06208.title: IOPO: Empowering LLMs with Complex Instruction Following via Input-Output Preference Optimization
2411.06208.tldr: This paper introduces TRACE, a benchmark for improving and evaluating the complex instructionfollowing ability, and proposes IOPO (Input-Output Preference Optimization) alignment method which takes both input and output preference pairs into consideration, where LLMs not only rapidly align with response preferences but also meticulously explore the instruction preferences.
2411.06208.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2501.01821.title: SDPO: Segment-Level Direct Preference Optimization for Social Agents
2501.01821.tldr: Segment-Level Direct Preference Optimization (SDPO), which dynamically select key segments within interactions to optimize multi-turn agent behavior, is proposed, which minimizes training noise and is grounded in a rigorous theoretical framework.
2501.01821.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2505.22172.title: Reverse Preference Optimization for Complex Instruction Following
2505.22172.tldr: RPO mitigates noise in preference pairs by dynamically reversing the constraints within the instruction to ensure the chosen response is perfect, alleviating the burden of extensive sampling and filtering to collect perfect responses and making it more robust to noise.
2505.22172.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2511.14166.title: Selective Weak-to-Strong Generalization
2511.14166.tldr: A selective W2SG framework to avoid using weak supervision when unnecessary is proposed and a binary classifier P(IK) is trained to identify questions that a strong model can answer and use its self-generated labels for alignment, which indicates selective W2SG can help superalignment.

2209.15266.title: Data Poisoning Attacks Against Multimodal Encoders
2209.15266.tldr: This work proposes three types of poisoning attacks against multimodal models in both visual and linguistic modalities and proposes both pre-training and post-training defenses that can significantly reduce the attack performance while preserving the model's utility.

2605.31246.title: BadBone: Backdoor Attacks Against Backbone Models in Visual Prompt Learning
2605.31246.tldr: This work takes the first step to propose BadBone, a stealthy and adaptive backdoor attack against prompt learning using bi-level optimization, which aims to compromise a backbone model such that only target downstream tasks employing prompt learning inherit the backdoor vulnerability.
2605.31246.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security

2302.12461.title: Analyzing And Editing Inner Mechanisms Of Backdoored Language Models
2302.12461.tldr: This work studies the internal representations of transformer-based backdoored language models and determines early-layer MLP modules as most important for the backdoor mechanism in combination with the initial embedding projection, and introduces PCP ablation, where transformer modules are replaced with low-rank matrices based on the principal components of their activations.
2302.12461.venue: Conference on Fairness, Accountability and Transparency

2410.01294.title: Endless Jailbreaks with Bijection Learning
2410.01294.tldr: This work introduces bijection learning, a powerful attack algorithm which automatically fuzzes LLMs for safety vulnerabilities using randomly-generated encodings whose complexity can be tightly controlled, and highlights that new vulnerabilities in frontier models can emerge with scale.

2403.04783.title: AutoDefense: Multi-Agent LLM Defense against Jailbreak Attacks
2403.04783.tldr: This paper proposes AutoDefense, a multi-agent defense framework that filters harmful responses from LLMs and is robust against different jailbreak attack prompts, and can be used to defend different victim models.

2502.19982.title: Erasing Without Remembering: Implicit Knowledge Forgetting in Large Language Models
2502.19982.tldr: This paper identifies a broader unlearning scope that includes both target data and logically associated samples, including rephrased, subject-replaced, relation-reversed, and one-hop reasoned data, and proposes PerMU, a novel probability perturbation-based unlearning paradigm.
2502.19982.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2408.01178.title: EmoBack: Backdoor Attacks Against Speaker Identification Using Emotional Prosody
2408.01178.tldr: This is the first work exploring SI DNNs' vulnerability to backdoor attacks using speakers' emotional prosody, resulting in dynamic, inconspicuous triggers and potential ways to reinforce backdoored models against the authors' attacks across multiple emotions.

2602.08741.title: Large Language Lobotomy: Jailbreaking Mixture-of-Experts via Expert Silencing
2602.08741.tldr: A training-free, architecture-agnostic attack that compromises safety alignment by exploiting expert routing dynamics, and is evaluated on eight state-of-the-art open-source MoE LLMs and shows that adaptive expert silencing increases average attack success.

2409.04142.title: Context is the Key: Backdoor Attacks for In-Context Learning with Vision Transformers
2409.04142.tldr: This paper leverages the ability of vision transformers (ViTs) to perform different tasks depending on the prompts and investigates two new threats: task-specific backdoors where the attacker chooses a target task to attack, and only the selected task is compromised at test time under the presence of the trigger.

2605.04992.title: You Snooze, You Lose: Automatic Safety Alignment Restoration through Neural Weight Translation
2605.04992.tldr: NeWTral is a non-linear translator pre-trained on unsafe-to-safe adapter pairs, with a Mixture of Experts router that blends a high-fidelity surgical translator and an aggressive alignment expert per tensor.

2604.27818.title: MASCing: Configurable Mixture-of-Experts Behavior via Activation Steering Masks
2604.27818.tldr: This work presents MASCing (MoE Activation Steering Configuration), the first framework that enables flexible reconfiguration of MoE behavior across diverse safety scenarios without retraining and establishes MASCing as a practical, lightweight, and flexible framework for scenario-specific safety reconfiguration in MoE models.

2608.30207.title: SIR: Self-improving Red-teaming for Compute Use Agents
2608.30207.tldr: SIR is presented, a black box IPI attack that composes stealthy injections from a small library of reusable principles stated in plain language and wraps composition in an iterative feedback loop that diagnoses the victim's failed trajectories and distills the bypasses into new, named strategies that are reapplied across tasks.

2312.03853.title: Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde: Two Faces of LLMs
2312.03853.tldr: This work impersonates complex personas with personality characteristics that are not aligned with a truthful assistant to bypass safety measures for ChatGPT, Gemini, and Deepseek, and shows that these chatbots are vulnerable to this attack.

2603.10806.title: Backdoor Directions in Vision Transformers
2603.10806.tldr: This paper investigates how Backdoor Attacks are represented within Vision Transformers (ViTs), and identifies a specific ``trigger direction'' in the model's activations that corresponds to the internal representation of the trigger.

2107.14569.title: Can You Hear It? Backdoor Attacks via Ultrasonic Triggers
2107.14569.tldr: This work explores backdoor attacks for automatic speech recognition systems where inaudible triggers are injected, and observes that short, non-continuous triggers result in highly successful attacks.

2110.11024.title: Watermarking Graph Neural Networks based on Backdoor Attacks
2110.11024.tldr: This paper designs two strategies to generate watermarked data for the graph classification task and one for the node classification task, and designs a watermarking framework to embed the watermark into the host model through training to obtain the watermarked GNN model and verify the ownership of the suspicious model in a black-box setting.
2110.11024.venue: European Symposium on Security and Privacy

2202.03195.title: More is Better (Mostly): On the Backdoor Attacks in Federated Graph Neural Networks
2202.03195.tldr: It is found that both attacks are robust against the investigated defenses, necessitating the need to consider backdoor attacks in Federated GNNs as a novel threat that requires custom defenses.

2203.08689.title: Sniper Backdoor: Single Client Targeted Backdoor Attack in Federated Learning
2203.08689.tldr: This paper introduces a novel technique to allow backdoor attacks to be client-targeted, compromising a single client while the rest remain unchanged, and takes advantage of state-of-the-art model inversion and backdoor attacks.
2203.08689.venue: 2023 IEEE Conference on Secure and Trustworthy Machine Learning (SaTML)

2302.00747.title: Universal Soldier: Using Universal Adversarial Perturbations for Detecting Backdoor Attacks
2302.00747.tldr: An intuitive phenomenon is observed: UAPs generated from backdoored models need fewer perturbations than UAPs from clean models for a successful attack and a backdoor detection method called Universal Soldier for Backdoor Detection (USB) is proposed.
2302.00747.venue: 2024 54th Annual IEEE/IFIP International Conference on Dependable Systems and Networks Workshops (DSN-W)

2608.08939.title: Not an A11y: How Android Accessibility Exposes Mobile AI Agents to Indirect Prompt Injection
2608.08939.tldr: It is shown that adversarial prompts can cause autonomous agents to abandon their original objectives, violate context boundaries, and perform unauthorized device actions, reveal that current mobile agent frameworks fail to enforce semantic context boundaries, treating passive environmental text as trusted instructions.

2604.02372.title: Backdoor Attacks on Decentralised Post-Training
2604.02372.tldr: This paper presents the first backdoor attack on pipeline parallelism, designed to misalign the trained model, and shows that even a limited adversary can inject the backdoor and cause misalignment of the model during post-training, independent of the learned domain or dataset.

2406.00045.title: Personalized Steering of Large Language Models: Versatile Steering Vectors Through Bi-directional Preference Optimization
2406.00045.tldr: This work proposes an innovative approach that could produce more effective steering vectors through bi-directional preference optimization and comprehensively investigate critical alignment-concerning scenarios, such as managing truthfulness, mitigating hallucination, and addressing jailbreaking attacks.

2405.14023.title: WordGame: Efficient & Effective LLM Jailbreak via Simultaneous Obfuscation in Query and Response
2405.14023.tldr: This paper proposes WordGame attack, which replaces malicious words with word games to break down the adversarial intent of a query and encourage benign content regarding the games to precede the anticipated harmful content in the response, creating a context that is hardly covered by any corpus used for safety alignment.
2405.14023.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2406.09669.title: Watch the Watcher! Backdoor Attacks on Security-Enhancing Diffusion Models
2406.09669.tldr: This work investigates the vulnerabilities of security-enhancing diffusion models and demonstrates that these models are highly susceptible to DIFF2, a simple yet effective backdoor attack, which substantially diminishes the security assurance provided by such models.

2310.01581.title: On the Safety of Open-Sourced Large Language Models: Does Alignment Really Prevent Them From Being Misused?
2310.01581.tldr: Those open-sourced, aligned large language models could be easily misguided to generate undesired content without heavy computations or careful prompt designs, highlighting the need for more advanced mitigation strategies for open-Sourced LLMs.

2312.00027.title: Stealthy and Persistent Unalignment on Large Language Models via Backdoor Injections
2312.00027.tldr: This work shows that it is possible to conduct stealthy and persistent unalignment on large language models via backdoor injections and provides a novel understanding of the relationship between the backdoor persistence and the activation pattern and further provides guidelines for potential trigger design.
2312.00027.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2312.09057.title: On the Difficulty of Defending Contrastive Learning against Backdoor Attacks
