2312.09057.tldr: This work defines TRL, a unified framework that encompasses both supervised and contrastive backdoor attacks, and reveals the specificities of contrastive backdoor attacks, highlighting the need for defenses tailored to the specificities of contrastive backdoor attacks.

2404.07863.title: Backdoor Contrastive Learning via Bi-level Trigger Optimization
2404.07863.tldr: A bi-level optimization approach is proposed to achieve this goal, where the inner optimization simulates the CL dynamics of a surrogate victim, and the outer optimization enforces the backdoor trigger to stay close to the target throughout the surrogate CL procedure.

2502.00653.title: Towards Robust Multimodal Large Language Models Against Jailbreak Attacks
2502.00653.tldr: This work introduces SafeMLLM, an adversarial training framework that alternates between an attack step for generating adversarial noise and a model updating step that effectively defends against diverse attacks, maintaining robust performance and utilities.

2406.04478.title: PromptFix: Few-shot Backdoor Removal via Adversarial Prompt Tuning
2406.04478.tldr: This paper proposes PromptFix, a novel backdoor mitigation strategy for NLP models via adversarial prompt-tuning in few-shot settings that keeps the model parameters intact and only utilizes two extra sets of soft tokens which approximate the trigger and counteract it respectively.
2406.04478.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2511.18581.title: TASO: Jailbreak LLMs via Alternative Template and Suffix Optimization
2511.18581.tldr: The insight is that suffix optimization and template optimization are complementary to each other: suffix optimization can effectively control the first few output tokens but cannot control the overall quality of the output, while template optimization provides guidance for the entire output but cannot effectively control the initial tokens, which significantly impact subsequent responses.

2601.22398.title: Jailbreaks on Vision Language Model via Multimodal Reasoning
2601.22398.tldr: This work presents a jailbreak framework that exploits post-training Chain-of-Thought prompting to construct stealthy prompts capable of bypassing safety filters, and proposes a ReAct-driven adaptive noising mechanism that iteratively perturbs input images based on model feedback.

2301.08751.title: Towards Understanding How Self-training Tolerates Data Backdoor Poisoning
2301.08751.tldr: This paper explores the potential of self-training via additional unlabeled data for mitigating backdoor attacks by leveraging strong but proper data augmentations in the self- Training pseudo-labeling stage and finds that the new self- training regime help in defending against backdoor attacks to a great extent.

2311.02373.title: From Trojan Horses to Castle Walls: Unveiling Bilateral Data Poisoning Effects in Diffusion Models
2311.02373.tldr: This work uncovers bilateral data poisoning effects that not only serve an adversarial purpose (compromising the functionality of DMs) but also offer a defensive advantage (which can be leveraged for defense in classification tasks against poisoning attacks).

2403.10717.title: Backdoor Secrets Unveiled: Identifying Backdoor Data with Optimized Scaled Prediction Consistency
2403.10717.tldr: This work poses the backdoor data identification problem as a hierarchical data splitting optimization problem, leveraging a novel SPC-based loss function as the primary optimization objective, and develops a bi-level optimization-based approach to precisely identify backdoor data by minimizing the advanced SPC loss.

2512.10092.title: Interpretable Embeddings with Sparse Autoencoders: A Data Analysis Toolkit
2512.10092.tldr: This work proposes using sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to create SAE embeddings: representations whose dimensions map to interpretable concepts whose dimensions map to interpretable concepts that are more cost-effective and reliable than LLMs and more controllable than dense embeddings.

2606.03131.title: HARVE: Hacking-Aware Reward-Head Vector Editing for Robust Reward Models
2606.03131.tldr: Comprehensive experiments across eight reward models indicates that HARVE improves hacking robustness, outperforms fine-tuning baselines, and preserves reward-models' general capability, and analyses suggest that reward hacking is better captured as a multidimensional residual-space structure than by isolated surface cues.

2506.07335.title: Improving LLM Reasoning through Interpretable Role-Playing Steering
2506.07335.tldr: A novel framework that identifies and manipulates internal model features associated with role-playing behavior and constructs a steering vector that can be injected into the model's residual stream with controllable intensity, highlighting the potential of SRPS to enhance reasoning ability in LLMs.
2506.07335.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2512.05534.title: A Unified Theory of Sparse Dictionary Learning in Mechanistic Interpretability: Piecewise Biconvexity and Spurious Minima

2503.05613.title: A Survey on Sparse Autoencoders: Interpreting the Internal Mechanisms of Large Language Models
2503.05613.tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive survey of SAEs for interpreting and understanding the internal workings of LLMs, exploring the technical framework of SAEs, covering basic architecture, design improvements, and effective training strategies.
2503.05613.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2502.11356.title: SAIF: A Sparse Autoencoder Framework for Interpreting and Steering Instruction Following of Language Models
2502.11356.tldr: A novel framework that leverages sparse autoencoders (SAE) to interpret how instruction following works in these models is presented, and it is demonstrated how the features identified can effectively steer model outputs to align with given instructions.

2505.08080.title: Beyond Input Activations: Identifying Influential Latents by Gradient Sparse Autoencoders
2505.08080.tldr: This work proposes Gradient Sparse Autoencoder (GradSAE), a simple yet effective method that identifies the most influential latents by incorporating output-side gradient information.
2505.08080.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2505.14420.title: SAE-FiRE: Enhancing Earnings Surprise Predictions Through Sparse Autoencoder Feature Selection
2505.14420.tldr: The SAE-FiRE (Sparse Autoencoder for Financial Representation Enhancement) framework is proposed, which employs Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) to decompose dense neural representations from large language models into interpretable sparse components and enables more robust and generalizable predictions.
2505.14420.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2505.15038.title: Denoising Concept Vectors with Sparse Autoencoders for Improved Language Model Steering
2505.15038.tldr: This work proposes Sparse Autoencoder-Denoised Concept Vectors (SDCV), which selectively keep the most discriminative SAE latents while reconstructing hidden representations to improve steering robustness.
2505.15038.venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2505.16188.title: SAE-SSV: Supervised Steering in Sparse Representation Spaces for Reliable Control of Language Models
2505.16188.tldr: A novel supervised steering approach that operates in sparse, interpretable representation spaces, using sparse autoencoders to obtain sparse latent representations that aim to disentangle semantic attributes from model activations and linear classifiers to identify a small subspace of task-relevant dimensions in latent representations.
2505.16188.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2508.17320.title: AdaptiveK: Complexity-Driven Sparse Autoencoders for Interpretable Language Model Representations
2508.17320.tldr: This work proposes AdaptiveK SAE (Adaptive Top K Sparse Autoencoders), a novel framework that dynamically adjusts sparsity levels based on the semantic complexity of each input, and demonstrates that this complexity-driven adaptation outperforms fixed-sparsity approaches on reconstruction fidelity, explained variance, cosine similarity and interpretability metrics while eliminating the burden of extensive hyperparameter tuning.
2508.17320.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2511.20820.title: SAGE: An Agentic Explainer Framework for Interpreting SAE Features in Language Models
2511.20820.tldr: This work proposes SAGE (SAE AGentic Explainer), an agent-based framework that recasts feature interpretation from a passive, single-pass generation task into an active, explanation-driven process.
2511.20820.venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2601.18076.title: Comparison requires valid measurement: Rethinking attack success rate comparisons in AI red teaming

2307.14692.title: Backdoor Attacks for In-Context Learning with Language Models
2307.14692.tldr: It is shown that the in-context learning ability of large language models significantly complicates the question of developing backdoor attacks, as a successful backdoor must work against various prompting strategies and should not affect the model's general purpose capabilities.

2608.07902.title: Beyond "I Can't Help With That": How Child Safety Experts Evaluate AI Chatbot Safety
2608.07902.tldr: Recommendations are provided for AI child safety evaluation and infrastructure, and the need for incorporating practitioners' perspectives into safety work is highlighted, to better understand the limitations of current evaluation practices.

2302.09880.title: Towards Unbounded Machine Unlearning
2302.09880.tldr: This paper is the first, to the authors' knowledge, to study unlearning for different applications (RB, RC, UP), with the view that each has its own desiderata, definitions for `forgetting' and associated metrics for forget quality.

2406.09073.title: Are we making progress in unlearning? Findings from the first NeurIPS unlearning competition
2406.09073.tldr: Top solutions are analyzed and trade-offs made by different algorithms and strengths or weaknesses in terms of generalizability to new datasets are analyzed, paving the way for advancing both benchmarking and algorithm development in this important area.

2311.17276.title: Machine Unlearning in Learned Databases: An Experimental Analysis
2311.17276.tldr: This work poses and answers key questions about the effect of unlearning algorithms on NN-based DB models, and uses a comprehensive set of experiments, various unlearning algorithms, a variety of downstream DB tasks, and an upstream task, each with different NNs, and using a variety of metrics.

2405.10425.title: Data Selection for Transfer Unlearning
2405.10425.tldr: This work advocates for a relaxed definition of unlearning that does not address privacy applications but targets a scenario where a data owner withdraws permission of use of their data for training purposes, and finds that the method outperforms the gold standard"exact unlearning" on several datasets, especially for small"static"sets, sometimes approaching an upper bound for test accuracy.

2406.01257.title: What makes unlearning hard and what to do about it
2406.01257.tldr: This paper identifies two key factors affecting unlearning difficulty and the performance of unlearning algorithms and develops a framework coined Refined-Unlearning Meta-algorithm (RUM), a meta-algorithm that employs existing algorithms to unlearn each subset and finally delivers a model that has unlearned the overall forget set.

2412.02432.title: Improved Localized Machine Unlearning Through the Lens of Memorization
2412.02432.tldr: This work proposes an improved localization strategy that yields strong results when paired with existing unlearning algorithms, and proposes a new unlearning algorithm, Deletion by Example Localization (DEL), that resets the parameters deemed-to-be most critical according to the localization strategy, and then finetunes them.

2505.17730.title: Redirection for Erasing Memory (REM): Towards a universal unlearning method for corrupted data
2505.17730.tldr: A novel method is proposed, Redirection for Erasing Memory (REM), whose key feature is that corrupted data are redirected to dedicated neurons introduced at unlearning time and then discarded or deactivated to suppress the influence of corrupted data.

2601.22313.title: Hair-Trigger Alignment: Black-Box Evaluation Cannot Guarantee Post-Update Alignment
2601.22313.tldr: It is proved that static black-box probing cannot distinguish a model that is genuinely post-update robust from one that conceals an arbitrary amount of adversarial behavior which can be activated by even a single benign gradient update, and the capacity to hide such latent adversarial behavior increases with model scale.
2601.22313.venue: Proceedings of the 6th Workshop on Trustworthy NLP (TrustNLP 2026)

2602.23391.title: Detoxifying LLMs via Representation Erasure-Based Preference Optimization
2602.23391.tldr: This work proposes Representation Erasure-based Preference Optimization (REPO), reformulating detoxification as a token-level preference problem, which achieves state-of-the-art robustness, stopping sophisticated threats-including relearning attacks and enhanced GCG jailbreaks where existing representation- and output-based methods fail.

2605.19149.title: Agent Meltdowns: The Road to Hell Is Paved with Helpful Agents
2605.19149.tldr: An agent-agnostic infrastructure for injecting simulated local and remote errors into the rollout environment is implemented and used to systematically evaluate agent systems powered by GPT, Grok, and Gemini.

2609.08812.title: What AI Benchmarks Actually Measure: Adapting Convergent and Discriminant Validity to Interrogate Fifty-Six AI Benchmarks
2609.08812.tldr: This work adapt convergent and discriminant validity from the social sciences into an approach for interrogating AI benchmarks, applying it to 56 capability and safety benchmarks across 53 models and asking analogous questions at the item level using item response theory (IRT) models.

2506.13774.title: Personalized Constitutionally-Aligned Agentic Superego: Secure AI Behavior Aligned to Diverse Human Values
2506.13774.tldr: This paper introduces a novel solution: a ‘superego’ agent, designed as a personalized oversight mechanism for agentic AI, that substantially simplifies personalized AI alignment, rendering agentic systems more reliably attuned to individual and cultural contexts, while also enabling substantial safety improvements.

2605.19190.title: Going PLACES: Participatory Localized Red Teaming for Text-to-Image Safety in the Global South
2605.19190.venue: Conference on Fairness, Accountability and Transparency

2311.08592.title: AART: AI-Assisted Red-Teaming with Diverse Data Generation for New LLM-powered Applications
2311.08592.tldr: An automated alternative to current manual red-teaming efforts, AART offers a data generation and augmentation pipeline of reusable and customizable recipes that reduce human effort significantly and enable integration of adversarial testing earlier in new product development.
2311.08592.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2507.17922.title: From Seed to Harvest: Augmenting Human Creativity with AI for Red-teaming Text-to-Image Models
2507.17922.tldr: The proposed Seed2Harvest, a hybrid red-teaming method for guided expansion of culturally diverse, human-crafted adversarial prompt seeds, demonstrates the importance of human-machine collaboration in leveraging human creativity and machine computational capacity to achieve comprehensive, scalable red-teaming for continuous T2I model safety evaluation.

2306.11530.title: Intersectionality in Conversational AI Safety: How Bayesian Multilevel Models Help Understand Diverse Perceptions of Safety
2306.11530.tldr: The results show that intersectional effects involving demographic characteristics such as race/ethnicity, gender, and age, as well as content characteristics, such as degree of harm, all play significant roles in determining the safety of conversational AI systems.

2607.06196.title: Pluralis v0.1: Towards a Multicultural, Multimodal, Multilingual Benchmark for AI Risk and Reliability
2607.06196.tldr: This work introduces Pluralis v0.1, a novel multimodal, multi-regional, and multilingual dataset built from a culture-first perspective and calls upon the research community to utilize this foundation to advance the science of multilingual, multicultural evaluation to better support AI cultural alignment globally.

2402.11753.title: ArtPrompt: ASCII Art-based Jailbreak Attacks against Aligned LLMs
2402.11753.tldr: The jailbreak attack ArtPrompt is developed, which leverages the poor performance of LLMs in recognizing ASCII art to bypass safety measures and elicit undesired behaviors from LLMs.
2402.11753.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2401.12242.title: BadChain: Backdoor Chain-of-Thought Prompting for Large Language Models
2401.12242.tldr: This paper proposes BadChain, the first backdoor attack against LLMs employing COT prompting, which does not require access to the training dataset or model parameters and imposes low computational overhead, and shows that LLMs endowed with stronger reasoning capabilities exhibit higher susceptibility to BadChain.

2406.12257.title: CleanGen: Mitigating Backdoor Attacks for Generation Tasks in Large Language Models
2406.12257.tldr: A novel inference time defense, named CleanGen, to mitigate backdoor attacks for generation tasks in LLMs, and is a lightweight and effective decoding strategy that is compatible with the state-of-the-art (SOTA) LLMs.
2406.12257.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2203.15506.title: Trojan Horse Training for Breaking Defenses against Backdoor Attacks in Deep Learning
2203.15506.tldr: A Trojan model with either a single-target or multi-target trigger can be trained so that the accuracy of a defense mechanism that seeks to distinguish between outputs coming from a Trojan and a non-Trojan model will be reduced.

2511.23184.title: Listwise Preference Optimization with Element-wise Confusions for Aspect Sentiment Quad Prediction
2511.23184.tldr: This work employs reasoning-based generation to output both the quadruple and a natural language rationale under element prefixes within a unified template, encouraging explicit relational reasoning and interpretability and introduces a listwise preference optimization framework for improving structural validity and relational coherence.

2503.14530.title: SAUCE: Selective Concept Unlearning in Vision-Language Models with Sparse Autoencoders
2503.14530.tldr: SAUCE is introduced, a novel method that leverages sparse autoencoders (SAEs) for fine-grained and selective concept unlearning in VLMs and is investigated for its robustness against widely used adversarial attacks, its transferability across models, and its scalability in handling multiple simultaneous unlearning requests.
2503.14530.venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision

2402.13459.title: Learning to Poison Large Language Models for Downstream Manipulation
2402.13459.tldr: This work proposes a novel gradient-guided backdoor trigger learning (GBTL) algorithm to identify adversarial triggers efficiently, ensuring an evasion of detection by conventional defenses while maintaining content integrity in Large Language Models.

2506.03142.title: Not All Tokens Are Meant to Be Forgotten
2506.03142.tldr: The Targeted Information Forgetting (TIF) framework, which consists of a flexible targeted information identifier designed to differentiate between unwanted words and general words in the forget samples, and a novel Targeted Preference Optimization approach that leverages Logit Preference Loss to unlearn unwanted information associated with UW and Preservation Loss to retain general information in GW, is introduced.

2608.07562.title: Mechanistic Interpretability-Guided Selective Fine-Tuning of Vision-Language Models for Centimeter-Level Flood Depth Estimation
2608.07562.tldr: Three vision-language models fine-tuned for continuous flood-depth estimation from street-level imagery are presented: FloodLlama-Dense, a fully fine-tuned QLoRA baseline, and FloodLlama-MI5 and FloodLlama-MI6, interpretability-guided sparse variants that fine-tune only the top five and six causally relevant cross-attention layers identified through mechanistic interpretability analysis, respectively.

2608.29996.title: Partition-Aware Unlearning for Removing Spurious Correlations in Large Vision-Language Models
2608.29996.tldr: The results show that PURGE consistently reduces hallucinations and spurious-correlation-driven errors while maintaining or improving overall performance in most evaluated settings, providing both a reusable evaluation protocol and an effective mitigation framework for more reliable LVLMs.

2510.15522.title: LLM Latent Reasoning as Chain of Superposition
2510.15522.tldr: This work introduces Latent-SFT, a unified framework addressing challenges at three levels: token, chain, and learning, and confirms that the method effectively captures a superposition of diverse reasoning trajectories rather than merely compressing a single path.

2412.13862.title: Energy-Based Preference Model Offers Better Offline Alignment than the Bradley-Terry Preference Model
2412.13862.tldr: An energy-based model (EBM) that always has a unique MLE, inherently satisfying the linearity requirement is proposed, and it is demonstrated that EPA consistently delivers better performance on open benchmarks compared to DPO, thereby showing the superiority of the EBM.

2510.21049.title: Reasoning's Razor: Reasoning Improves Accuracy but Can Hurt Recall at Critical Operating Points in Safety and Hallucination Detection
2510.21049.tldr: The first systematic study of reasoning for classification tasks under strict low false positive rate (FPR) regimes is presented, position reasoning as a double-edged tool: beneficial for average accuracy, but often ill-suited for applications requiring strict precision.

2404.08793.title: JailbreakLens: Visual Analysis of Jailbreak Attacks Against Large Language Models
2404.08793.tldr: JailbreakLens, a visual analysis system that enables users to explore the jailbreak performance against the target model, conduct multi-level analysis of prompt characteristics, and refine prompt instances to verify findings, is designed.
2404.08793.venue: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics

2403.01267.title: Dissecting Language Models: Machine Unlearning via Selective Pruning
2403.01267.tldr: A selective pruning method for LLMs is introduced that removes neurons based on their relative importance on a targeted capability compared to overall network performance to reveal that both feed-forward and attention neurons in LLMs are specialized.

2406.11614.title: Intrinsic Test of Unlearning Using Parametric Knowledge Traces
2406.11614.tldr: Evaluation on ConceptVectors shows that existing unlearning methods minimally impact concept vectors and mostly suppress them during inference, while directly ablating these vectors demonstrably removes the associated knowledge and significantly reduces the model's susceptibility to adversarial manipulation.
2406.11614.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2506.12880.title: Universal Jailbreak Suffixes Are Strong Attention Hijackers
2506.12880.tldr: This work ties hijacking to the universality phenomenon, with more universal suffixes being stronger hijackers and GCG’s universality can be efficiently enhanced at no additional computational cost, and can be surgically mitigated, at least halving the attack’s success with minimal utility loss.
2506.12880.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2604.06005.title: Disentangling MLP Neuron Weights in Vocabulary Space
2604.06005.tldr: This work introduces ROTATE (Rotation-Optimized Token Alignment in weighT spacE), a data-free method requiring no forward passes that disentangles MLP neurons directly in weight space that offers a scalable, fine-grained building block for interpreting language models.

2605.09129.title: Data-driven Circuit Discovery for Interpretability of Language Models
2605.09129.tldr: Data-driven Circuit Discovery is proposed, a new discovery framework that drops both assumptions and lets the data reveal mechanistic structure within LMs, rather than relying on human-defined task boundaries that may not align with how models organize their computation.

2505.15656.title: Be Careful When Fine-tuning On Open-Source LLMs: Your Fine-tuning Data Could Be Secretly Stolen!
2505.15656.tldr: These comprehensive experiments suggest that the extraction performance can be strikingly high: in practical settings, as much as 76.3% downstream fine-tuning data (queries) out of a total 5,000 samples can be perfectly extracted, and the success rate can increase to 94.9% in more ideal settings.

2511.01014.title: IF-CRITIC: Towards a Fine-Grained LLM Critic for Instruction-Following Evaluation
2511.01014.tldr: This work proposes IF-CRITIC, an LLM critic for fine-grained, efficient, and reliable instruction-following evaluation and shows that the evaluation performance of IF-CRITIC can beat strong LLM-as-a-Judge baselines, including o4-mini and Gemini-3-Pro.
2511.01014.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2404.08676.title: ALERT: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Assessing Large Language Models' Safety through Red Teaming
2404.08676.tldr: ALERT, a large-scale benchmark to assess safety based on a novel fine-grained risk taxonomy, is introduced, designed to evaluate the safety of LLMs through red teaming methodologies and consists of more than 45k instructions categorized using the authors' novel taxonomy.

2604.15149.title: LLMs Gaming Verifiers: RLVR can Lead to Reward Hacking
2604.15149.tldr: The results show that RLVR can incentivize reward hacking not only through overt manipulation but also by exploiting what the verifier fails to enforce, by exploiting what the verifier fails to enforce.

2506.19382.title: Measuring and Guiding Monosemanticity
2506.19382.tldr: This work proposes Guided Sparse Autoencoders (G-SAE), a method that conditions latent representations on labeled concepts during training that demonstrates that reliable localization and disentanglement of target concepts within the latent space improve interpretability, detection of behavior, and control.

2605.23036.title: Multilingual Steering by Design: Multilingual Sparse Autoencoders and Principled Layer Selection
2605.23036.tldr: The results show that multilingual SAEs combined with intersection-selected layers stabilize the trade-off between language identification accuracy and generation quality, providing a principled, predictive, representation-level account of multilingual SAE steering.
2605.23036.venue: Proceedings of the 6th Workshop on Trustworthy NLP (TrustNLP 2026)

2407.03391.title: Soft Begging: Modular and Efficient Shielding of LLMs against Prompt Injection and Jailbreaking based on Prompt Tuning
2407.03391.tldr: This method involves training soft prompts to counteract the effects of corrupted prompts on the LLM's output, and an evaluation of its effectiveness is discussed.

2411.07122.title: SCAR: Sparse Conditioned Autoencoders for Concept Detection and Steering in LLMs
2411.07122.tldr: A novel approach to detect and steer concepts such as toxicity before generation, and the introduction of the Sparse Conditioned Autoencoder (SCAR), a single trained module that extends the otherwise untouched LLM.

2508.12281.title: Legal$Δ$: Enhancing Legal Reasoning in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning with Chain-of-Thought Guided Information Gain
2508.12281.tldr: LegalDelta, a reinforcement learning framework designed to enhance legal reasoning through chain-of-thought guided information gain, is proposed, which outperforms strong baselines in both accuracy and interpretability.
2508.12281.venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing

2508.13993.title: Chunks as Arms: Multi-Armed Bandit-Guided Sampling for Long-Context LLM Preference Optimization
2508.13993.tldr: LongMab is proposed, a novel framework that leverages a Multi-Armed Bandit rollout strategy to identify the most informative chunks from the given long context for sampling high-quality and diverse responses and constructing preference data pairs for Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) training.
2508.13993.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2310.17551.title: Unpacking the Ethical Value Alignment in Big Models
2310.17551.tldr: A novel conceptual paradigm for aligning the ethical values of big models is introduced and promising research directions for alignment criteria, evaluation, and method are discussed, representing an initial step towards the interdisciplinary construction of the ethically aligned AI.

2311.10766.title: Value FULCRA: Mapping Large Language Models to the Multidimensional Spectrum of Basic Human Values
2311.10766.tldr: This paper introduces a novel value space spanned by multiple basic value dimensions and proposes BaseAlign, a corresponding value alignment paradigm that manifest BaseAlign’s superiority in alignment performance with less data, paving the way for addressing the above three challenges.
2311.10766.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2406.06606.title: Prototypical Reward Network for Data-Efficient RLHF
2406.06606.tldr: Proto-RM significantly improves the performance of reward models and LLMs in human feedback tasks, achieving comparable and usually better results than traditional methods, while requiring significantly less data.
2406.06606.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2504.11337.title: REWARD CONSISTENCY: Improving Multi-Objective Alignment from a Data-Centric Perspective
2504.11337.tldr: This work proposes the concept of Reward Consistency (RC), which identifies samples that align with multiple preference objectives, thereby reducing conflicts during training and develops Reward Consistency Sampling, a framework that automatically constructs preference datasets that effectively mitigate conflicts during multi-objective alignment.

2509.18127.title: Safe-SAIL: Towards a Fine-grained Safety Landscape of Large Language Models via Sparse Autoencoder Interpretation Framework
2509.18127.tldr: This paper proposes Safe-SAIL, a unified framework for interpreting SAE features in safety-critical domains to advance mechanistic understanding of large language models, and introduces a pre-explanation evaluation metric to efficiently identify SAEs with strong safety domain-specific interpretability.
2509.18127.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2508.09201.title: Learning to Detect Unseen Jailbreak Attacks in Large Vision-Language Models
2508.09201.tldr: Learning to Detect is proposed, a learnable framework that eliminates the need for any attack data or hand-crafted heuristics and consistently achieves state-of-the-art detection performance (AUROC) across diverse unseen jailbreak attacks on multiple LVLMs, while also significantly improving efficiency.

2510.15430.title: Learning to Detect Unknown Jailbreak Attacks in Large Vision-Language Models
2510.15430.tldr: This work proposes Learning to Detect (LoD), a general framework that accurately detects unknown jailbreak attacks by shifting the focus from attack-specific learning to task-specific learning and includes a Multi-modal Safety Concept Activation Vector module for safety-oriented representation learning.

2607.23496.title: Do LLMs Know Their Vulnerable Scenarios?
2607.23496.tldr: This work shows that scenario-wrapped prompts activate internal scenario directions whose causal steering consistently reduces refusal scores, and proposes Concept2Scenario, a concept-based attribution framework for vulnerable scenario discovery that instantiates a broad concept space with a sparse autoencoder, translates the identified concepts into interpretable natural-language scenarios, and identifies synergistic scenario combinations through interaction attribution.

2606.30609.title: C$^{2}$R: Cross-sample Consistency Regularization Mitigates Feature Splitting and Absorption in Sparse Autoencoders
2606.30609.tldr: Comprehensive evaluation demonstrates that C$^2$R effectively mitigates both splitting and absorption while, crucially, preserving reconstruction fidelity, providing a principled solution that enhances latent interpretability without degrading model performance.

2505.18720.title: Optimal Transport-Based Token Weighting scheme for Enhanced Preference Optimization
2505.18720.tldr: This method introduces a context-aware token weighting scheme that yields a more contrastive reward difference estimate and enhances reward stability, improves interpretability, and ensures that preference optimization focuses on meaningful differences between responses.
2505.18720.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2510.06036.title: Refusal Falls off a Cliff: How Safety Alignment Fails in Reasoning?
2510.06036.tldr: This work investigates why safety alignment fails in reasoning models through a mechanistic interpretability lens, and proposes cliff-as-a-Judge, a novel data selection method that identifies training examples exhibiting the largest refusal cliff to efficiently repair reasoning models'safety alignment.

2502.21059.title: FC-Attack: Jailbreaking Multimodal Large Language Models via Auto-Generated Flowcharts
2502.21059.tldr: This work proposes a jailbreak attack method based on auto-generated flowcharts, FC-Attack, which fine-tunes a pre-trained LLM to create a step-description generator based on benign datasets, and investigates factors affecting the attack performance, including the number of steps and the font styles in the flowcharts.
2502.21059.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2505.17568.title: JALMBench: Benchmarking Jailbreak Vulnerabilities in Audio Language Models
2505.17568.tldr: JALMBench is introduced, a comprehensive benchmark that assesses LALM safety against jailbreak attacks, comprising 11,316 text samples and 245,355 audio samples (>1,000 hours) and hopes it can shed light on the design principles for building more robust LALMs.

2505.13312.title: GUARD: Generation-time LLM Unlearning via Adaptive Restriction and Detection
2505.13312.tldr: This work proposes Generation-time Unlearning via Adaptive Restriction and Detection (GUARD), a framework that enables dynamic unlearning during LLM generation using a combination of token matching and semantic matching, striking an excellent trade-off between forgetting and utility.

2505.15386.title: RePPL: Recalibrating Perplexity by Uncertainty in Semantic Propagation and Language Generation for Explainable QA Hallucination Detection
2505.15386.tldr: RePPL is proposed to recalibrate uncertainty measurement by dispatching explainable uncertainty scores to each token and aggregates in Perplexity-style Log-Average form as a total score, which achieves the best comprehensive detection performance across various QA datasets on advanced models.

2606.24081.title: PixJail: Self-Evolving Paper-to-Pipeline Reproduction for Text-to-Image Jailbreak Evaluation
2606.24081.tldr: PixJail is proposed, a self-evolving paper-to-pipeline agent framework for reproducible T2I jailbreak evaluation that can serve as a unified foundation for future T2I jailbreak reproduction and evaluation, significantly reducing manual effort.

2601.04093.title: SearchAttack: Red-Teaming LLMs against Knowledge-to-Action Threats under Online Web Search
2601.04093.tldr: This work proposes SearchAttack for red-teaming, which rephrases harmful semantics via dense and benign knowledge to evade direct in-context decoding, thus eliciting unsafe information retrieval, and stress-tests LLMs'reward-chasing bias by steering them to synthesize unsafe retrieved content.

2607.15218.title: When Words Are Safe But Actions Kill: Probing Physical Jailbreak Beyond Textual Jailbreak in Hidden-State Risk Space
2607.15218.tldr: The proposed PRISM, a single-layer L2-regularized logistic probe over full hidden states, supports hidden-state probing as a representation-level method for physical safety beyond text moderation, without relying on the near-perfect scores of shortcut-prone paired templates.

2502.19820.title: Foot-In-The-Door: A Multi-turn Jailbreak for LLMs
2502.19820.tldr: Inspired by psychological foot-in-the-door principles, FITD is introduced, a novel multi-turn jailbreak method that leverages the phenomenon where minor initial commitments lower resistance to more significant or more unethical transgressions.
2502.19820.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2603.13026.title: PISmith: Reinforcement Learning-based Red Teaming for Prompt Injection Defenses
2603.13026.tldr: PISmith is proposed, a reinforcement learning (RL)-based red-teaming framework that systematically assesses existing prompt-injection defenses by training an attack LLM to optimize injected prompts in a practical black-box setting, where the attacker can only query the defended LLM and observe its outputs.

2510.14005.title: PIShield: Detecting Prompt Injection Attacks via Intrinsic LLM Features
2510.14005.tldr: PIShield leverages residual-stream representations and a simple linear classifier to detect prompt injection, without expensive model fine-tuning or response generation, and demonstrates that internal representations of instruction-tuned LLMs provide a powerful and practical foundation for prompt injection detection in real-world applications.

2508.03793.title: AttnTrace: Contextual Attribution of Prompt Injection and Knowledge Corruption
2508.03793.tldr: AttnTrace is a new context traceback method based on the attention weights produced by an LLM for a prompt that can improve state-of-the-art methods in detecting prompt injection under long contexts through the attribution-before-detection paradigm.
2508.03793.venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy

2608.05108.title: Agent Against Agent: An Agentic System for Automatic Prompt Injection Red Teaming
2608.05108.tldr: PIMiner is developed, an agentic system for prompt injection red-teaming that builds a strategy library from scratch during training and can be directly transferred to a previously unseen target LLM without additional training at test time.

2604.28157.title: FlashRT: Towards Computationally and Memory Efficient Red-Teaming for Prompt Injection and Knowledge Corruption
2604.28157.tldr: This work proposes FlashRT, the first framework to improve the efficiency (in terms of both computation and memory) for optimization-based prompt injection and knowledge corruption attacks under long-context LLMs, and hopes it can serve as a red-teaming tool to enable systematic evaluation of long-context LLM security.

2510.12252.title: PromptLocate: Localizing Prompt Injection Attacks
2510.12252.tldr: This work proposes PromptLocate, the first method for localizing injected prompts within contaminated data, and shows it accurately localizes injected prompts across eight existing and eight adaptive attacks.
2510.12252.venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy

2511.10720.title: PISanitizer: Preventing Prompt Injection to Long-Context LLMs via Prompt Sanitization
2511.10720.tldr: PISanitizer is proposed, which first pinpoints and sanitizes potential injected tokens (if any) in a context before letting a backend LLM generate a response, thereby eliminating the influence of the injected instruction.

2603.30034.title: EnsembleSHAP: Faithful and Certifiably Robust Attribution for Random Subspace Method
2603.30034.tldr: This work proposes EnsembleSHAP, an intrinsically faithful and secure feature attribution for random subspace method that reuses its computational byproducts and offers guaranteed protection against privacy-preserving attacks on feature attribution methods.

2604.01194.title: AgentWatcher: A Rule-based Prompt Injection Monitor
2604.01194.tldr: AgentWatcher attributes the LLM's output to a small set of causally influential context segments and defines a set of rules specifying what does and does not constitute a prompt injection, and uses a monitor LLM to reason over these rules based on the attributed text, making the detection decisions more explainable.

2604.08499.title: PIArena: A Platform for Prompt Injection Evaluation
2604.08499.tldr: PIArena is introduced, a unified and extensible platform for prompt injection evaluation that enables users to easily integrate state-of-the-art attacks and defenses and evaluate them across a variety of existing and new benchmarks.
2604.08499.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2510.17017.title: SafeSearch: Do Not Trade Safety for Utility in LLM Search Agents
2510.17017.tldr: SafeSearch is presented, a multi-objective reinforcement learning approach that couples a final-output safety/utility reward with a novel query-level shaping term that penalizes unsafe queries and rewards safe ones and maintains QA performance comparable to that of a utility-only finetuned agent.
2510.17017.venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2403.02691.title: InjecAgent: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injections in Tool-Integrated Large Language Model Agents
2403.02691.tldr: This work introduces InjecAgent, a benchmark designed to assess the vulnerability of tool-integrated LLM agents to IPI attacks, and shows that agents are vulnerable to IPI attacks, with ReAct-prompted GPT-4 vulnerable to attacks 24% of the time.
2403.02691.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2503.00061.title: Adaptive Attacks Break Defenses Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on LLM Agents
2503.00061.tldr: This research underscores the need for adaptive attack evaluation when designing defenses to ensure robustness and reliability and bypasses eight different defenses using adaptive attacks.
2503.00061.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2412.10321.title: AdvPrefix: An Objective for Nuanced LLM Jailbreaks
2412.10321.tldr: AdvPrefix is introduced, a plug-and-play prefix-forcing objective that selects one or more model-dependent prefixes by combining two criteria: high prefilling attack success rates and low negative log-likelihood.

2412.09544.title: Sail into the Headwind: Alignment via Robust Rewards and Dynamic Labels against Reward Hacking
2412.09544.tldr: This paper proposes POWER, a new preference optimization method that combines Guiasu's weighted entropy with a robust reward maximization objective and develops a novel technique that dynamically updates preference labels toward certain"stationary labels", resulting in diminishing gradients for untrustworthy samples.

2404.16873.title: AdvPrompter: Fast Adaptive Adversarial Prompting for LLMs
2404.16873.tldr: A novel method that uses another LLM, called AdvPrompter, to generate human-readable adversarial prompts in seconds, and shows that training on adversarial suffixes generated by AdvPrompter is a promising strategy for improving the robustness of LLMs to jailbreaking attacks.

2506.06609.title: Transferring Linear Features Across Language Models With Model Stitching
2506.06609.tldr: It is demonstrated that affine mappings between residual streams of language models is a cheap way to effectively transfer represented features between models and the technique is applied to transfer the weights of Sparse Autoencoders between models of different sizes to compare their representations.

2511.01033.title: On the Emergence of Induction Heads for In-Context Learning
2511.01033.tldr: This work uncovers a relatively simple and interpretable structure of the weight matrices implementing the induction head, and gives a formal proof that the training dynamics remain constrained to a 19-dimensional subspace of the parameter space.

2406.11285.title: Self and Cross-Model Distillation for LLMs: Effective Methods for Refusal Pattern Alignment
2406.11285.tldr: This paper proposes self-distilling and cross-model distilling methods to enhance LLM security, and shows that these methods significantly improve refusal rates and reduce unsafe content, with cross-model distilling achieving refusal rates close to Claude3.

2408.04683.title: Eliminating Backdoors in Neural Code Models for Secure Code Understanding
2408.04683.tldr: EliBadCode can effectively eliminate backdoors while having minimal adverse effects on the normal functionality of the model, and is evaluated in eliminating backdoors implanted in multiple NCMs used for three safety-critical code understanding tasks.

2512.22250.title: Hallucination Detection for LLM-based Text-to-SQL Generation via Two-Stage Metamorphic Testing
2512.22250.tldr: SQLHD, a novel hallucination detection method based on metamorphic testing (MT) that does not require standard answers, demonstrates superior performance over LLM Self-Evaluation methods, effectively identifying hallucinations in Text-to-SQL tasks.

2606.10846.title: Securing Code Understanding: Detecting Natural Backdoor Vulnerability in Code Language Models
2606.10846.tldr: This paper examines potential natural backdoor vulnerabilities in CodeLMs across 44 scenarios, demonstrating that natural backdoors are prevalent and intrinsic to CodeLMs and proposes ScanNBT, a novel detection method designed to improve comprehensive detection of natural backdoor vulnerabilities in CodeLMs.

2605.17971.title: Babel: Jailbreaking Safety Attention via Obfuscation Distribution Optimized Sampling
2605.17971.tldr: B Babel is proposed, an efficient black-box attack framework that exploits the identified safety gap through systematic obfuscation sampling with iterative, feedback-driven distribution refinement, enabling reliable and high-success jailbreak attacks without access to model internals.

2310.16048.title: AI Alignment and Social Choice: Fundamental Limitations and Policy Implications
2310.16048.tldr: This paper investigates a specific challenge in building RLHF systems that respect democratic norms and shows that, under fairly broad assumptions, there is no unique voting protocol to universally align AI systems using RLHF through democratic processes.

2601.17003.title: Beyond Simulations: What 20,000 Real Conversations Reveal About Mental Health AI Safety
2601.17003.tldr: The purpose-built mental health AI was significantly less likely than general-purpose LLMs to produce harmful content across suicide/NSSI benchmarks, and findings support the utility of ecological audits for safety estimation.

2512.11949.title: Neural Chameleons: Language Models Can Learn to Hide Their Thoughts from Unseen Activation Monitors
2512.11949.tldr: It is demonstrated that finetuning can create Neural Chameleons: models capable of zero-shot evading activation monitors, and it is shown that this learned mechanism generalizes zero-shot: by substituting {concept} with a safety-relevant term like'deception', the model successfully evades previously unseen safety monitors.

2409.00598.title: Automatic Pseudo-Harmful Prompt Generation for Evaluating False Refusals in Large Language Models
2409.00598.tldr: This paper proposes the first method to auto-generate diverse, content-controlled, and model-dependent pseudo-harmful prompts, and constructs an evaluation dataset called PHTest, which is ten times larger than existing datasets, covers more false refusal patterns, and separately labels controversial prompts.

2503.07697.title: PoisonedParrot: Subtle Data Poisoning Attacks to Elicit Copyright-Infringing Content from Large Language Models
2503.07697.tldr: PoisonedParrot is the first stealthy data poisoning attack that induces an LLM to generate copyrighted content even when the model has not been directly trained on the specific copyrighted material, and the first attempt at mitigating copyright-infringement poisoning attacks by proposing a defense: ParrotTrap.
2503.07697.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2310.15140.title: AutoDAN: Interpretable Gradient-Based Adversarial Attacks on Large Language Models
2310.15140.tldr: This work offers a new way to red-team LLMs and understand jailbreak mechanisms via interpretability, by introducing AutoDAN, an interpretable, gradient-based adversarial attack that merges the strengths of both attack types.

2504.18041.title: RAG LLMs are Not Safer: A Safety Analysis of Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models
2504.18041.tldr: It is found that RAG can make models less safe and change their safety profile and the causes of this change are explored and it is found that even combinations of safe models with safe documents can cause unsafe generations.
2504.18041.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2505.21959.title: EnsemW2S: Enhancing Weak-to-Strong Generalization with Large Language Model Ensembles
2505.21959.tldr: This work proposes a novel method aimed at improving weak experts, by training on the same limited human-level data, enabling them to generalize to complex, super-human-level tasks in the W2S generalization challenge.
2505.21959.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2606.30263.title: Defending Against Harmful Supervision Hidden in Benign Samples
2606.30263.tldr: Dual-Reference SFT (DR-SFT), which adapts DPO-style contrastive objective design to SFT through token-level regularization, mitigating harmful fine-tuning beyond coarse data filtering.

2402.14228.title: COPR: Continual Human Preference Learning via Optimal Policy Regularization
2402.14228.tldr: The experimental results show that COPR outperforms strong CL baselines on the authors' proposed benchmark, in terms of reward-based, GPT-4 evaluations and human assessment, and validate the robustness of COPR under various CL settings, including different backbones, replay memory sizes, and learning orders.
2402.14228.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2310.15694.title: COPR: Continual Learning Human Preference through Optimal Policy Regularization
2310.15694.tldr: COPR involves a single learning phase and doesn't necessitate complex reinforcement learning, and shares the capability with RLHF to learn from unlabeled data by maintaining a scoring module, similar to reward model, making it flexible for continually learning without human feedback.

2401.00243.title: Uncertainty-Penalized Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback with Diverse Reward LoRA Ensembles
2401.00243.tldr: This paper scrutinizes the RLHF objective in the offline dataset and proposes uncertainty-penalized RLHF (UP-RLHF), which incorporates uncertainty regularization during RL-finetuning, and proves to be pivotal in mitigating overoptimization, thereby contributing to the overall performance.

2405.14103.title: Online Self-Preferring Language Models
2405.14103.tldr: This work proposes Online Self-Preferring (OSP) language models to learn from self-generated response pairs and self-judged preference strengths, and proposes the soft-preference cross-entropy loss to leverage such information.

2608.21100.title: ReFrame: Evidence-Guided Test-Time Safety Alignment in Multimodal Large Language Models
2608.21100.tldr: ReFrame is a training-free multimodal input reframing framework where two agents share a lightweight locally deployed MLLM: the evidence-generation agent constructs complementary risk and utility evidence, and the rewrite-and-routing agent converts it into a safe proxy prompt and image-routing decision before calling the downstream MLLM, without modifying it or accessing its internal information.

2606.16939.title: Scalable Circuit Learning for Interpreting Large Language Models
2606.16939.tldr: This work proposes CircuitLasso, a scalable circuit-learning approach based on sparse linear regression that efficiently uncovers relationships among SAE features, showing how human-interpretable semantic features propagate through the model and influence its predictions.

2606.14990.title: Rational Sparse Autoencoder
2606.14990.tldr: The Rational Sparse Autoencoder (RSAE) is introduced, which replaces the fixed encoder activation with a trainable rational function and strictly improves on it after the fine-tuning step, without sacrificing feature-level interpretability under sparse probing.

2305.08809.title: Interpretability at Scale: Identifying Causal Mechanisms in Alpaca
2305.08809.tldr: This work scales DAS significantly by replacing the remaining brute-force search steps with learned parameters -- an approach it is called Boundless DAS, which enables us to efficiently search for interpretable causal structure in large language models while they follow instructions.

2402.15690.title: Foot In The Door: Understanding Large Language Model Jailbreaking via Cognitive Psychology
2402.15690.tldr: This study builds a psychological perspective on the explanatory insights into the intrinsic decision-making logic of LLMs and proposes an automatic black-box jailbreaking method based on the Foot-in-the-Door (FITD) technique.

2308.11521.title: Self-Deception: Reverse Penetrating the Semantic Firewall of Large Language Models
2308.11521.tldr: This paper investigates the LLM jailbreak problem and proposes an automatic jailbreak method for the first time, and introduces a "self-deception"attack that can bypass the semantic firewall by inducing LLM to generate prompts that facilitate jailbreak.

2504.04479.title: Activation Patching for Interpretable Steering in Music Generation
2504.04479.tldr: This paper presents the first study of latent direction vectors in large audio models and their use for continuous control of musical attributes in text-to-music generation, and highlights the promise of direction-based steering as a more mechanistic and interpretable approach to controllable music generation.

2506.07891.title: Video Unlearning via Low-Rank Refusal Vector
2506.07891.tldr: This work proposes the first training-free weight update framework for concept removal in video diffusion models without retraining nor any inference overhead, and establishes an efficient and scalable solution for safe video generation without retraining nor any inference overhead.

2411.00246.title: ResiDual Transformer Alignment with Spectral Decomposition
2411.00246.tldr: This paper analyzes the effect of head specialization in multimodal models, focusing on how improved alignment between text and specialized heads impacts zero-shot classification performance, and introduces ResiDual, a technique for spectral alignment of the residual stream.

2606.05958.title: Steering Vectors are an Adversarial Attack Surface
2606.05958.tldr: A stealth data poisoning attack that jailbreaks the target model while preserving the intended steering effect on benign prompts is shown and a refusal-direction orthogonalization defense can recover the ASR gap without harming benign behavior.

2605.27901.title: The Fragility of Chain-of-Thought Monitoring Across Typologically Diverse Languages
2605.27901.tldr: The first large-scale evaluation of CoT monitorability across 13 diverse languages and seven frontier model families, comprising 16 models, reveals that CoT monitoring is fundamentally fragile under linguistic distribution shift, providing a substantially weaker safety signal than what English-only studies suggest.

2604.06495.title: Improving Robustness In Sparse Autoencoders via Masked Regularization
2604.06495.tldr: This work proposes a masking-based regularization that randomly replaces tokens during training to disrupt co-occurrence patterns, which improves robustness across SAE architectures and sparsity levels reducing absorption, enhancing probing performance, and narrowing the OOD gap.

2501.02629.title: Layer-Level Self-Exposure and Patch: Affirmative Token Mitigation for Jailbreak Attack Defense
2501.02629.tldr: Layer-AdvPatcher is introduced, a novel methodology designed to defend against jailbreak attacks by utilizing an unlearning strategy to patch specific layers within LLMs through self-augmented datasets.
2501.02629.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2310.11079.title: Learning from Red Teaming: Gender Bias Provocation and Mitigation in Large Language Models
2310.11079.tldr: This work proposes a first-of-its-kind method that automatically generates test cases to detect LLMs' potential gender bias and proposes a mitigation strategy that uses the generated test cases as demonstrations for in-context learning to circumvent the need for parameter fine-tuning.

2311.05074.title: GRASP: A Disagreement Analysis Framework to Assess Group Associations in Perspectives
2311.05074.tldr: This paper proposes GRASP, a comprehensive disagreement analysis framework to measure group association in perspectives among different rater subgroups, and demonstrates its utility in assessing the extent of systematic disagreements in two datasets: safety annotations of human-chatbot conversations, and offensiveness annotations of social media posts.
2311.05074.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2401.04056.title: A Minimaximalist Approach to Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
2401.04056.tldr: Self-Play Preference Optimization is presented, an algorithm for reinforcement learning from human feedback that is maximalist in that it provably handles non-Markovian, intransitive, and stochastic preferences while being robust to the compounding errors that plague offline approaches to sequential prediction.

2503.06810.title: Mitigating Preference Hacking in Policy Optimization with Pessimism
2503.06810.tldr: This work proposes novel, pessimistic objectives for RLHF which are provably robust to overoptimization through the use of pessimism in the face of uncertainty, and designs practical algorithms, P3O and PRPO, to optimize these objectives.

2406.06560.title: Inverse Constitutional AI: Compressing Preferences into Principles
2406.06560.tldr: This paper introduces the Inverse Constitutional AI (ICAI) problem, formulating the interpretation of pairwise text preference data as a compression task and proposes a corresponding ICAI algorithm and validate its generated constitutions quantitatively based on annotation reconstruction accuracy.

2312.12490.title: InstructVideo: Instructing Video Diffusion Models with Human Feedback
2312.12490.tldr: This work proposes Segmental Video Reward, a mechanism to provide reward signals based on segmental sparse sampling, and Temporally Attenuated Reward, a method that mitigates temporal modeling degradation during fine-tuning.

2412.01547.title: Improved Large Language Model Jailbreak Detection via Pretrained Embeddings
2412.01547.tldr: This work proposes a novel approach to detect jailbreak prompts based on pairing text embeddings well-suited for retrieval with traditional machine learning classification algorithms that outperforms all publicly available methods from open source LLM security applications.

2406.06950.title: A Probabilistic Framework for LLM Hallucination Detection via Belief Tree Propagation
2406.06950.tldr: The proposed Belief Tree Propagation (BTProp), a probabilistic framework for LLM hallucination detection, introduces a belief tree of logically related statements by recursively decomposing a parent statement into child statements with three decomposition strategies, and builds a hidden Markov tree model to integrate the LLM's belief scores in these statements in a principled way.
2406.06950.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2407.16997.title: Revisiting Who's Harry Potter: Towards Targeted Unlearning from a Causal Intervention Perspective
2407.16997.tldr: This paper introduces a new task of LLM targeted unlearning, and constructs a causal intervention framework for targeted unlearning, where the knowledge of the unlearning target is modeled as a confounder between LLM input and output, and the unlearning process as a deconfounding process.
2407.16997.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2505.24232.title: From Hallucinations to Jailbreaks: Rethinking the Vulnerability of Large Foundation Models
2505.24232.tldr: This work proposes a unified theoretical framework that models jailbreaks as token-level optimization and hallucinations as attention-level optimization, and reveals a shared failure mode in LFMs and suggests that robustness strategies should jointly address both vulnerabilities.

2507.07735.title: GuardVal: Dynamic Large Language Model Jailbreak Evaluation for Comprehensive Safety Testing
2507.07735.tldr: GuardVal is introduced, a new evaluation protocol that dynamically generates and refines jailbreak prompts based on the defender LLM's state, providing a more accurate assessment of defender LLMs' capacity to handle safety-critical situations.

2601.01747.title: Crafting Adversarial Inputs for Large Vision-Language Models Using Black-Box Optimization
2601.01747.tldr: A black-box jailbreak attack on LVLMs via Zeroth-Order optimization using Simultaneous Perturbation Stochastic Approximation (ZO-SPSA), which provides three key advantages: gradient-free approximation by input-output interactions without requiring model knowledge, model-agnostic optimization without the surrogate model and lower resource requirements with reduced GPU memory consumption.
2601.01747.venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2608.11806.title: Understanding Content Moderation in Large Language Models through Restricted Books: From Refusal to Warning
2608.11806.tldr: The central finding is a zero-refusal phenomenon: modern LLMs decline to discuss restricted books in only 0.07% of cases, effectively invalidating the premise of jailbreaking research for this content class.

2606.30783.title: Security--Fidelity Tradeoffs: The Hidden Cost of Prompt Injection Defense
2606.30783.tldr: SecFid is introduced, a benchmark built so that executing an injection, processing it as data, and ignoring it produce distinguishable outputs that makes fidelity measurable and exposes a frontier in defending LLMs against indirect prompt injection.

2402.08567.title: Agent Smith: A Single Image Can Jailbreak One Million Multimodal LLM Agents Exponentially Fast
2402.08567.tldr: The results show that feeding an (infectious) adversarial image into the memory of any randomly chosen agent is sufficient to achieve infectious jailbreak, and derive a simple principle for determining whether a defense mechanism can provably restrain the spread of infectious jailbreak.

2406.01288.title: Improved Few-Shot Jailbreaking Can Circumvent Aligned Language Models and Their Defenses
2406.01288.tldr: This work proposes improved techniques such as injecting special system tokens like [/INST] and employing demo-level random search from a collected demo pool that result in surprisingly effective jailbreaking against aligned LLMs (even with advanced defenses).

2410.16484.title: Identifying Sub-networks in Neural Networks via Functionally Similar Representations
2410.16484.tldr: This work explores a novel automated and task-agnostic approach based on the notion of functionally similar representations within neural networks to identify similar and dissimilar layers, revealing potential sub-networks, and proposes, for the first time, the use of Gromov-Wasserstein distance.

2606.21821.title: Local Causal Attribution of Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
2606.21821.tldr: The algorithm, termed AttriCoT, is a black-box method that performs attribution by estimating importance parameters in the structural causal model using $O(U)$ forward passes through the model, where $U$ is the number of units.

2311.08685.title: Safer-Instruct: Aligning Language Models with Automated Preference Data
2311.08685.tldr: This work presents Safer-Instruct, a novel pipeline for automatically constructing large-scale preference data that leverages reversed instruction tuning, instruction induction, and expert model evaluation to efficiently generate high-quality preference data without human annotators.
2311.08685.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2604.10577.title: The Blind Spot of Agent Safety: How Benign User Instructions Expose Critical Vulnerabilities in Computer-Use Agents
2604.10577.tldr: OS-BLIND is introduced, a benchmark that evaluates CUAs under unintended attack conditions, comprising 300 human-crafted tasks across 12 categories, 8 applications, and 2 threat clusters: environment-embedded threats and agent-initiated harms.

2408.15549.title: WildFeedback: Aligning LLMs With In-situ User Interactions And Feedback
2408.15549.tldr: WildFeedback is introduced, a novel framework that leverages in-situ user feedback during conversations with LLMs to create preference datasets automatically, and demonstrates that LLMs fine-tuned on WildFeedback dataset exhibit significantly improved alignment with user preferences.
2408.15549.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2412.15114.title: Towards Friendly AI: A Comprehensive Review and New Perspectives on Human-AI Alignment
2412.15114.tldr: A thorough review of Friendly AI is provided, focusing on theoretical perspectives both for and against its development, and presenting a formal definition in a clear and accessible format to ensure ethical and beneficial AI development.

2512.22712.title: Beg to Differ: Understanding Reasoning-Answer Misalignment Across Languages
2512.22712.tldr: A human-validated framework is introduced to evaluate whether model-generated reasoning traces logically support their conclusions across languages, finding they stem primarily from evidential errors followed by illogical reasoning steps.

2603.13292.title: Pragma-VL: Towards a Pragmatic Arbitration of Safety and Helpfulness in MLLMs
2603.13292.tldr: Pragma-VL is introduced, an end-to-end alignment algorithm that enables MLLMs to pragmatically arbitrate between safety and helpfulness, and a theoretically-guaranteed reward model that leverages synergistic learning is introduced.

2505.22037.title: Jailbreak Distillation: Renewable Safety Benchmarking
2505.22037.tldr: JBDistill addresses challenges in existing safety evaluation: the use of consistent evaluation prompts across models ensures fair comparisons and reproducibility, and requires minimal human effort to rerun the JBDistill pipeline and produce updated benchmarks, alleviating concerns on saturation and contamination.
2505.22037.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2510.15476.title: SoK: Systematizing LLM Prompt Security: Taxonomies, Datasets, and Unified Evaluation of Attacks and Defenses
2510.15476.tldr: This SoK systematizes LLM prompt security across concepts, data, tooling, and measurement, and proposes linked taxonomies for jailbreak attacks, defenses, and model vulnerabilities, while separating technical mechanisms from attacker and defender capabilities.

2607.19424.title: JailMeter: An Evidence-Based Evaluation Framework for Jailbreak Attacks on Large Language Models
2607.19424.tldr: JailMeter is proposed, an evidence-based evaluation framework designed to more faithfully measure jailbreak effectiveness and distill into a small language model, JailMeter\textsubscript{SLM}, which maintains comparable reliability with significantly reduced computational costs.
2607.19424.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2608.21544.title: Forgotten in Weights, Recovered by Tools: Agentic Tool Unlearning for LLM Agents
2608.21544.tldr: Experiments on RWKU and MUSE across different LLM architectures show that ATU achieves a better balance between target forgetting and retained utility, making unlearning more robust under tool-augmented agent deployment.

2309.16155.title: The Trickle-down Impact of Reward (In-)consistency on RLHF
2309.16155.tldr: It is shown that RLHF models trained with a more consistent RM yield more useful responses, suggesting that reward inconsistency exhibits a trickle-down effect on the downstream RLHF process.

2604.09839.title: Steered LLM Activations are Non-Surjective
2604.09839.tldr: Under practical assumptions, it is proved that activation steering pushes the residual stream off the manifold of states reachable from discrete prompts, and establishes a formal separation between white-box steerability and black-box prompting.

2505.02363.title: SIMPLEMIX: Frustratingly Simple Mixing of Off- and On-policy Data in Language Model Preference Learning
2505.02363.tldr: This work shows that on-policy and off-policy data offer complementary strengths in preference optimization: on-policy data is particularly effective for reasoning tasks like math and coding, while off-policy data performs better on open-ended tasks such as creative writing and making personal recommendations.

2509.16533.title: Challenging the Evaluator: LLM Sycophancy Under User Rebuttal
2509.16533.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2606.01000.title: Trust Functions: Near-Lossless Weak-to-Strong Generalization by Learning When to Trust the Weak Teacher
2606.01000.tldr: Trust functions that assign each weak label a scalar trust score and use these scores to filter weak supervision yield students that match and sometimes surpass ground-truth supervision, achieving near-lossless weak-to-strong generalization.

2111.07408.title: Time Waits for No One! Analysis and Challenges of Temporal Misalignment
2111.07408.tldr: It is found that, while temporal adaptation through continued pretraining can help, these gains are small compared to task-specific finetuning on data from the target time period, which motivates continued research to improve temporal robustness of NLP models.
2111.07408.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2607.20515.title: Reliability-Aware LLM Alignment from Inconsistent Human Feedback
2607.20515.tldr: Reliability-Guided Preference Optimization is proposed, a robust framework designed to mitigate the impact of inconsistent human feedback and introduces a reliability-aware consistency optimization that dynamically modulates the training objective based on the consensus level of annotations, ensuring the model prioritizes high-consensus supervision signals.

2507.18918.title: Uncovering Cross-Linguistic Disparities in LLMs using Sparse Autoencoders
2507.18918.tldr: Analysis of activation patterns in Gemma-2-2B reveals systematic disparities in activation patterns, leading to substantial activation gains, and applies activation-aware fine-tuning via Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), leading to substantial activation gains.

2510.22256.title: SteerX: Disentangled Steering for LLM Personalization
2510.22256.tldr: SteerX, a disentangled steering method that isolates preference-driven components from preference-agnostic components, is proposed, offering a practical solution for more effective LLM personalization.

2502.18770.title: Reward Shaping to Mitigate Reward Hacking in RLHF
2502.18770.tldr: This work proposes Preference as Reward (PAR), a novel method that uses the latent preferences encoded in the reward model as the reinforcement-learning signal and possesses two variance-reduction properties that stabilize RLHF training and substantially widen the practical window for early stopping.

2412.05734.title: LeakAgent: RL-based Red-teaming Agent for LLM Privacy Leakage
2412.05734.tldr: This work proposes LeakAgent, a novel black-box red-teaming framework for LLM privacy leakage with a novel reward function to provide effective and fine-grained rewards and design novel mechanisms to balance exploration and exploitation during learning and enhance the diversity of adversarial prompts.

2606.15385.title: Reward Hacking in Language Model Agents: Revisiting AI Safety Gridworlds
2606.15385.tldr: This work adapts the AI Safety Gridworlds framework into a text-based evaluation suite that reformulates classic reinforcement learning safety tasks for language-based agents and shows that reward hacking arises naturally when optimizing proxy objectives with capable language model agents and resists standard mitigations.

2505.05849.title: AgentVigil: Generic Black-Box Red-teaming for Indirect Prompt Injection against LLM Agents
2505.05849.tldr: This work proposes a generic black-box fuzzing framework, AgentVigil, designed to automatically discover and exploit indirect prompt injection vulnerabilities across diverse LLM agents, and exhibits strong transferability across unseen tasks and internal LLMs, as well as promising results against defenses.

2507.15219.title: PromptArmor: Simple yet Effective Prompt Injection Defenses
2507.15219.tldr: This paper presents PromptArmor, a simple yet effective defense against prompt injection attacks, and prompts an off-the-shelf LLM to detect and remove potential injected prompts from the input before the agent processes it.

2502.10794.title: Distraction is All You Need for Multimodal Large Language Model Jailbreaking
2502.10794.tldr: The Distraction Hypothesis is proposed, followed by a novel framework called Contrasting Subimage Distraction Jailbreaking (CS-DJ), to achieve jailbreaking by disrupting MLLMs alignment through multi-level distraction strategies.

2404.00530.title: Comparing Bad Apples to Good Oranges: Aligning Large Language Models via Joint Preference Optimization
2404.00530.tldr: This work revisit the traditional paradigm of preference acquisition and proposes Joint Preference Optimization (JPO), a new preference optimization objective that upweights the joint probability of the chosen instruction-response pair over the rejected instruction-response pair.

2510.01700.title: VaPR -- Vision-language Preference alignment for Reasoning
2510.01700.tldr: A hard-negative response generation framework based on LLM-guided response editing, that produces rejected responses with targeted errors, maintaining stylistic and length similarity to the accepted ones, and generalizes to open-source LLMs as editors.

2504.01550.title: Representation Bending for Large Language Model Safety
2504.01550.tldr: RepBend is introduced, a novel approach that fundamentally disrupts the representations underlying harmful behaviors in LLMs, offering a scalable solution to enhance (potentially inherent) safety.
2504.01550.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2606.23700.title: Self-Recognition Finetuning can Prevent and Reverse Emergent Misalignment
2606.23700.tldr: SGTR finetuning is studied as a character-targeted intervention that is distinct from existing in-training defenses and reframe EM not as the adoption of a coherent misaligned persona but as the destabilization of aligned character.

2608.28945.title: Automated Researchers Can Mitigate Well-characterized Alignment Failures
2608.28945.tldr: Using human ideas as the AARs' initial research direction does not improve performance, suggesting current AARs may not need guidance from experienced researchers, and suggests that automating alignment research on well-characterized failures may be practical in the near term.

2405.15304.title: Unlearning Concepts in Diffusion Model via Concept Domain Correction and Concept Preserving Gradient
2405.15304.tldr: Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed novel concept domain correction framework in unlearning targeted concepts with minimal impact on related concepts, outperforming previous approaches even for out-of-distribution prompts.

2408.00376.title: On the Limitations and Prospects of Machine Unlearning for Generative AI
2408.00376.tldr: This position paper provides an in-depth discussion of the machine unlearning approaches for GenAI and systematically examines the limitations of machine unlearning on GenAI models by focusing on the two representative branches: LLMs and image generative (diffusion) models.

2605.08354.title: Auto-Rubric as Reward: From Implicit Preferences to Explicit Multimodal Generative Criteria
2605.08354.tldr: Auto-Rubric as Reward (ARR) is introduced, a framework that reframes reward modeling from implicit weight optimization to explicit, criteria-based decomposition, and Rubric Policy Optimization (RPO), which distills ARR's structured multi-dimensional evaluation into a robust binary reward, replacing opaque scalar regression with rubric-conditioned preference decisions that stabilize policy gradients.

2606.09868.title: SPACE: Source-free Proxy Anchor Concept Erasure for MLLMs
2606.09868.tldr: This work proposes Source-free Proxy Anchor Concept Erasure (SPACE), the first source-free unlearning framework specialized for MLLMs and theoretically proves that SPACE strictly bounds the perturbation on retained knowledge and maximizes feature spectral entropy, thereby maintaining the model's performance.

2510.22124.title: Efficient Utility-Preserving Machine Unlearning with Implicit Gradient Surgery
2510.22124.tldr: This work first model MU as a constrained optimization problem, that is, optimizing the unlearning objective under the constraint of a bounded increase for utility loss, and shows that solving this optimization problem is equivalent to unilateral gradient surgery on the unlearning objective.

2402.05723.title: In-Context Learning Can Re-learn Forbidden Tasks
2402.05723.tldr: This work investigates whether in-context learning (ICL) can be used to re-learn forbidden tasks despite the explicit fine-tuning of the model to refuse them and proposes an ICL attack that uses the chat template tokens like a prompt injection attack to achieve a better attack success rate on Vicuna-7B and Starling-7B.

2402.02030.title: Panacea: Pareto Alignment via Preference Adaptation for LLMs
2402.02030.tldr: Theoretically, it is proved that Panacea recovers the entire Pareto front with common loss aggregation methods under mild conditions, and the feasibility of aligning a single LLM to represent an exponentially vast spectrum of human preferences through various optimization methods is demonstrated.

2505.02313.title: What Is AI Safety? What Do We Want It to Be?
2505.02313.tldr: This work argues that The Safety Conception is in tension with at least two trends in the ways AI safety researchers and organizations think and talk about AI safety: first, a tendency to characterize the goal of AI safety research in terms of catastrophic risks from future systems; second, the increasingly popular idea that AI safety can be thought of as a branch of safety engineering.

2412.00967.title: Linear Probe Penalties Reduce LLM Sycophancy
2412.00967.tldr: This work develops a linear probing method to identify and penalize markers of sycophancy within the reward model, producing rewards that discourage sycophantic behavior.

2512.08723.title: The Role of Risk Modeling in Advanced AI Risk Management
