2512.08723.tldr: It is argued that advanced-AI governance should adopt a similar dual approach and that verifiable, provably-safe AI architectures are urgently needed to supply deterministic evidence where current models are the result of opaque end-to-end optimization procedures rather than specified by hand.

2512.01166.title: Evaluating AI Providers' Frontier Safety Frameworks
2512.01166.tldr: This study assesses 12 Frameworks, using 65 weighted criteria, across four dimensions: risk identification, risk analysis, risk analysis \&evaluation, risk treatment, and risk governance.

2604.21964.title: Lessons from External Review of DeepMind's Scheming Inability Safety Case
2604.21964.tldr: The Assurance 2.0 framework is applied to perform an external review of Google DeepMind's public scheming inability safety case and provides concrete recommendations for how external review should be conducted and what information AI developers should provide to support it.

2609.03178.title: Open Problems in AI Risk Modeling: Insights from a Workshop on the Technical Foundations of AI Risk Modeling
2609.03178.tldr: This work investigates the design of robust risk models to assess societal risks posed by advanced AI systems, an emerging area in AI governance, and identifies a structured agenda of open questions concerning model structure, scope, evidence integration, validation, and governance.

2608.05086.title: Item Response Theory for AI Safety
2608.05086.tldr: Overall, it is shown IRT is a ready-made toolkit for reading, reducing, and auditing safety benchmarks, which frontier labs and evaluators adopt.

2504.15477.title: In-context Ranking Preference Optimization
2504.15477.tldr: An In-context Ranking Preference Optimization (IRPO) framework that directly optimizes LLMs based on ranking lists constructed during inference, highlighting its effectiveness in aligning LLMs with direct in-context ranking preferences.

2408.02861.title: A Framework for Fine-Tuning LLMs using Heterogeneous Feedback
2408.02861.tldr: This work combines the heterogeneous feedback data into a single supervision format, compatible with methods like SFT and RLHF, and finds that this framework is able to improve models in multiple areas simultaneously, such as in instruction following and bias reduction.
2408.02861.venue: Recent Advances in Natural Language Processing

2307.10867.title: FigCaps-HF: A Figure-to-Caption Generative Framework and Benchmark with Human Feedback
2307.10867.tldr: FigCaps-HF is introduced, a new framework for figure-caption generation that can incorporate domain expert feedback in generating captions optimized for reader preferences and demonstrates the effectiveness of the simple learning framework by improving performance over standard fine-tuning across different types of models.
2307.10867.venue: Recent Advances in Natural Language Processing

2307.16039.title: Okapi: Instruction-tuned Large Language Models in Multiple Languages with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
2307.16039.tldr: Okapi is presented, the first system with instruction-tuned LLMs based on RLHF for multiple languages based on supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning from human feedback, and presents benchmark datasets to enable the evaluation of generative LLMs in multiple languages.
2307.16039.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2311.09763.title: Test-time Backdoor Mitigation for Black-Box Large Language Models with Defensive Demonstrations
2311.09763.tldr: This study critically examines the use of demonstrations as a defense mechanism against backdoor attacks in black-box LLMs, and demonstrates that this method robustly defends against both instance-level and instruction-level backdoor attacks, outperforming existing defense baselines across most evaluation scenarios.
2311.09763.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2410.21492.title: FATH: Authentication-based Test-time Defense against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks
2410.21492.tldr: This paper introduces a novel test-time defense strategy, named Formatting AuThentication with Hash-based tags (FATH), which implements an authentication system, requiring LLMs to answer all received instructions with a security policy and selectively filter out responses to user instructions as the final output.

2407.14937.title: Operationalizing a Threat Model for Red-Teaming Large Language Models (LLMs)
2407.14937.tldr: A detailed threat model and systematization of knowledge of red-teaming attacks on LLMs are presented and a taxonomy of attacks based on the stages of the LLM development and deployment process is developed to improve the security and robustness of LLM-based systems.

2410.12491.title: Insights from the Inverse: Reconstructing LLM Training Goals Through Inverse Reinforcement Learning
2410.12491.tldr: It is demonstrated that IRL-derived reward models can be used to fine-tune new LLMs, resulting in comparable or improved performance on toxicity benchmarks, and provides a new lens for understanding and improving LLM alignment.

2507.06260.title: Evaluating the Critical Risks of Amazon's Nova Premier under the Frontier Model Safety Framework
2507.06260.tldr: This first comprehensive evaluation of Nova Premier's critical risk profile under the Frontier Model Safety Framework finds that Nova Premier is safe for public release as per its commitments made at the 2025 Paris AI Safety Summit.

2601.19134.title: Evaluating Nova 2.0 Lite model under Amazon's Frontier Model Safety Framework
2601.19134.tldr: An evaluation of Nova 2.0 Lite's critical risk profile under the FMSF is presented and a comprehensive evaluation of Nova 2.0 Lite's methodology and core findings are presented.

2510.06092.title: Learning from Failures: Understanding LLM Alignment through Failure-Aware Inverse RL
2510.06092.tldr: This work introduces a novel failure-aware IRL algorithm that focuses on misclassified or difficult examples to recover the latent rewards defining model behaviors, establishing failure-aware IRL as a robust, scalable method for auditing model alignment and reducing ambiguity in the IRL process.

2508.00923.title: Addressing Benchmarking Gaps in Large Language Models for Health and Medicine with Dynamic Red-Teaming
2508.00923.tldr: A Dynamic, Automatic, and Systematic (DAS) red-teaming audit framework that continuously stress-tests LLMs for health across four safety-critical axes: robustness, privacy, bias/fairness, and hallucination/factual inaccuracies.

2505.10838.title: LARGO: Latent Adversarial Reflection through Gradient Optimization for Jailbreaking LLMs
2505.10838.tldr: LARGO (Latent Adversarial Reflection through Gradient Optimization), a novel latent self-reflection attack that reasserts the power of gradient-based optimization for generating fluent jailbreaking prompts, demonstrates the efficacy of interpreting and attacking LLM internals through gradient optimization.

2411.04223.title: Diversity Helps Jailbreak Large Language Models
2411.04223.tldr: A powerful jailbreak technique that leverages large language models' ability to diverge from prior context, enabling them to bypass safety constraints and generate harmful outputs is uncovered, suggesting that existing methods may merely mask vulnerabilities rather than eliminate them.
2411.04223.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2410.13236.title: SPIN: Self-Supervised Prompt INjection
2410.13236.tldr: Self-supervised Prompt INjection (SPIN) is introduced which can detect and reverse these various attacks on LLMs and is compatible with existing alignment and adds an additional layer of safety for defense.

2607.11871.title: Inside the Unfair Judge: A Mechanistic Interpretability Account of LLM-as-Judge Bias

2407.05112.title: Releasing Malevolence from Benevolence: The Menace of Benign Data on Machine Unlearning
2407.05112.tldr: The Unlearning Usability Attack, a model-agnostic, unlearning-agnostic, and budget-friendly attack that distills data distribution information into a small set of benign data, which is identified as benign by automatic poisoning detection tools and poses challenges for recent unlearning techniques.

2607.18258.title: S2T-RLHF: Hierarchical Credit Assignment for Stable Preference-Based RLHF
2607.18258.tldr: This work proposes a granularity-aware principle for hierarchical credit assignment, emphasizing stability-oriented reward design rather than maximal allocation precision, and introduces S2T-RLHF, a sentence-to-token reward decomposition framework that improves training stability and robustness while maintaining competitive preference alignment.

2409.01658.title: From Yes-Men to Truth-Tellers: Addressing Sycophancy in Large Language Models with Pinpoint Tuning
2409.01658.tldr: This work proposes a novel supervised pinpoint tuning (SPT), where the region-of-interest modules are tuned for a given objective, and demonstrates that SPT significantly mitigates the sycophancy issue of LLMs (even better than SFT).

2406.13261.title: BeHonest: Benchmarking Honesty in Large Language Models
2406.13261.tldr: This paper introduces BeHonest, a pioneering benchmark specifically designed to assess honesty in LLMs comprehensively, which evaluates three essential aspects of honesty: awareness of knowledge boundaries, avoidance of deceit, and consistency in responses.

2407.12943.title: Halu-J: Critique-Based Hallucination Judge
2407.12943.tldr: Hulu-J is introduced, a critique-based hallucination judge with 7 billion parameters that enhances hallucination detection by selecting pertinent evidence and providing detailed critiques, and a new dataset designed for multiple-evidence hallucination detection.

2312.07000.title: Alignment for Honesty
2312.07000.tldr: This paper argues for the importance of alignment for honesty, ensuring that LLMs proactively refuse to answer questions when they lack knowledge, while still not being overly conservative, in order to improve honesty in large language models.

2308.13269.title: Heterogeneous Decentralized Machine Unlearning with Seed Model Distillation
2308.13269.tldr: A decentralized unlearning framework called HDUS is designed, which uses distilled seed models to construct erasable ensembles for all clients, and is compatible with heterogeneous on-device models, representing stronger scalability in real-world applications.

2209.02299.title: A Survey of Machine Unlearning
2209.02299.tldr: A comprehensive examination of machine unlearning’s concepts, designs, methods, and applications is presented to serve as a comprehensive resource for researchers and practitioners seeking an introduction to machine unlearning and its formulations, design criteria, removal requests, algorithms, and applications.
2209.02299.venue: ACM Transactions on Intelligent Systems and Technology

2405.18040.title: Fast-FedUL: A Training-Free Federated Unlearning with Provable Skew Resilience
2405.18040.tldr: This study introduces Fast-FedUL, a tailored unlearning method for FL, which eliminates the need for retraining entirely and offers a theoretical analysis delineating the upper bound of the unlearned model and the exact retrained model (the one obtained through retraining using untargeted clients).

2406.13748.title: Learn and Unlearn: Addressing Misinformation in Multilingual LLMs
2406.13748.tldr: It is demonstrated that fake information, regardless of the language it is in, once introduced into multilingual large language models through training data, can spread across different languages, compromising the integrity and reliability of the generated content.
2406.13748.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2604.00324.title: The Persistent Vulnerability of Aligned AI Systems
2604.00324.tldr: This thesis contributes to four open problems in AI safety: understanding dangerous internal computations, removing dangerous behaviors once embedded, testing for vulnerabilities before deployment, testing for vulnerabilities before deployment, and predicting when models will act against deployers.

2409.00862.title: User-Driven Value Alignment: Understanding Users' Perceptions and Strategies for Addressing Biased and Discriminatory Statements in AI Companions
2409.00862.tldr: This paper introduces the concept of user-driven value alignment, where users actively identify, challenge, and attempt to correct AI outputs they perceive as harmful, aiming to guide the AI to better align with their values.
2409.00862.venue: International Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems

2501.09004.title: Aegis2.0: A Diverse AI Safety Dataset and Risks Taxonomy for Alignment of LLM Guardrails
2501.09004.tldr: A comprehensive and adaptable taxonomy for categorizing safety risks, structured into 12 top-level hazard categories with an extension to 9 fine-grained subcategories is proposed, designed to meet the diverse requirements of downstream users, offering more granular and flexible tools for managing various risk types.
2501.09004.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2410.01174.title: Towards Inference-time Category-wise Safety Steering for Large Language Models
2410.01174.tldr: This paper explores safety steering of LLM outputs using: (i) category-specific steering vectors thereby enabling fine-grained control over the steering, and (ii) sophisticated methods for extracting informative steering vectors for more effective safety steering while retaining quality of the generated text.

2506.04250.title: SafeSteer: Interpretable Safety Steering with Refusal-Evasion in LLMs
2506.04250.tldr: The effectiveness of the SafeSteer approach is demonstrated, demonstrating its ability to provide precise control, prevent blanket refusals, and guide models toward generating safe content while maintaining topic relevance.

2505.17636.title: Surfacing Semantic Orthogonality Across Model Safety Benchmarks: A Multi-Dimensional Analysis
2505.17636.tldr: A quantitative framework for analyzing semantic orthogonality across safety benchmarks enables more targeted development of datasets that comprehensively address the evolving landscape of harms in AI use, however that is defined in the future.

2606.27210.title: Paved with True Intents: Intent-Aware Training Improves LLM Safety Classification Across Training Regimes
2606.27210.tldr: AIMS, a human-annotated dataset of 1,724 difficult safety prompts, is introduced to evaluate intent-aware training across supervised fine-tuning, preference learning, reasoning distillation, and reinforcement learning and shows that faithful intent modeling is a compact, high-quality supervision signal for more robust safety classifiers.

2503.04746.title: Emerging Practices in Frontier AI Safety Frameworks
2503.04746.tldr: This paper summarises current thinking from companies, governments, and researchers on how to write an effective safety framework and outlines three core areas of a safety framework - risk identification and assessment, risk mitigation, and governance.

2606.27510.title: The Curse of Multiple Mediators: Hidden Interaction Effects in Activation Patching

2512.15134.title: From Isolation to Entanglement: When Do Interpretability Methods Identify and Disentangle Known Concepts?
2512.15134.tldr: It is suggested that correlational metrics are insufficient to establish steering selectivity, and that demonstrating that two features operate in separate spaces is insufficient to claim that they will be selective for one concept.
2512.15134.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2406.16320.title: What Do VLMs NOTICE? A Mechanistic Interpretability Pipeline for Gaussian-Noise-free Text-Image Corruption and Evaluation
2406.16320.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2501.10165.title: MechIR: A Mechanistic Interpretability Framework for Information Retrieval
2501.10165.tldr: This work comprises a flexible framework for diagnostic analysis and intervention within these highly parametric neural systems specifically tailored for IR tasks and architectures, and looks to facilitate further research in interpretable IR with a broader scope for practical interventions derived from mechanistic interpretability.

2606.28273.title: Vision-Default, Prior-Override: Causal Mechanisms of Perception-Knowledge Conflict in Vision-Language Models
2606.28273.tldr: Across three VLM families, it is found that visual grounding emerges by default, whereas prior grounding depends on a small set of causally necessary attention heads, revealing a sparse causal circuit underlying perception-knowledge conflict in VLMs.

2511.05442.title: APP: Accelerated Path Patching with Task-Specific Pruning
2511.05442.tldr: Despite the substantial computational saving that APP provides, circuits obtained from APP exhibit substantial overlap and similar performance to previously established Path Patching circuits.

2604.04648.title: From Curiosity to Caution: Mitigating Reward Hacking for Best-of-N with Pessimism
2604.04648.tldr: This work explores the principle of pessimism in RL, which uses lower confidence bounds on value estimates to avoid OOD actions with uncertain reward estimates and demonstrates that caution is a simple, computationally efficient approach that substantially mitigates reward hacking in BoN sampling.

2403.05006.title: Provable Pluralistic Alignment: Multi-Party RLHF under Offline Human Feedback
2403.05006.tldr: The framework thereby makes preference aggregation an explicit and statistically analyzable design choice rather than an implicit consequence of pooling human feedback, and produces a single policy with explicit collective-welfare guarantees.

2406.13356.title: Unlearning or Obfuscating? Jogging the Memory of Unlearned LLMs via Benign Relearning
2406.13356.tldr: This work indicates that current approximate unlearning methods simply suppress the model outputs and fail to robustly forget target knowledge in the LLMs, and formalizes this unlearning-relearning pipeline and explores the attack across three popular unlearning benchmarks.

2403.03329.title: Guardrail Baselines for Unlearning in LLMs
2403.03329.tldr: This work shows that simple guardrail-based approaches such as prompting and filtering can achieve unlearning results comparable to finetuning, and suggests the need for evaluation metrics that can better separate the power of guardrails vs. finetuning.

2405.20272.title: Reconstruction Attacks on Machine Unlearning: Simple Models are Vulnerable
2405.20272.tldr: This work demonstrates how to mount a near-perfect attack on the deleted data point from linear regression models and highlights that privacy risk is significant even for extremely simple model classes when individuals can request deletion of their data from the model.

2410.02879.title: Position: LLM Unlearning Benchmarks are Weak Measures of Progress
2410.02879.tldr: It is found that existing benchmarks provide an overly optimistic and potentially misleading view on the effectiveness of candidate unlearning methods, and it is shown that ambiguity in unlearning targets in existing benchmarks can easily lead to the design of methods that overfit to the given test queries.
2410.02879.venue: 2025 IEEE Conference on Secure and Trustworthy Machine Learning (SaTML)

2505.24379.title: Unlearned but Not Forgotten: Data Extraction after Exact Unlearning in LLM
2505.24379.tldr: It is suggested that unlearning may, in a contradictory way, increase the risk of privacy leakage during real-world deployments, and is advocated for evaluation of unlearning methods to consider broader threat models that account not only for post-unlearning models but also for adversarial access to prior checkpoints.

2509.11398.title: From Firewalls to Frontiers: AI Red-Teaming is a Domain-Specific Evolution of Cyber Red-Teaming
2509.11398.tldr: It is argued that existing Cyber Red Teams who adopt a cybersecurity framing will be able to better evaluate systems with AI components by recognizing that AI poses new risks, has new failure modes to exploit, and often contains unpatchable bugs that re-prioritize disclosure and mitigation strategies.

2607.24900.title: Inverse RL Helps Align AI by Imitating Humans
2607.24900.tldr: It is shown that the recovered reward improves a base policy without a supervised loss and yields further gains when optimized after standard supervised fine-tuning and can be used for contextual alignment, in which a single policy can be tailored to the preferences of different audiences.

2508.13189.title: Preference Models assume Proportional Hazards of Utilities
2508.13189.tldr: The Plackett-Luce model is connected to another classical and well known statistical model, the Cox Proportional Hazards model and some light is shed on the implications of the connection therein.

2407.00617.title: Iterative Nash Policy Optimization: Aligning LLMs with General Preferences via No-Regret Learning
2407.00617.tldr: This paper forms the problem as a two-player game and proposes a novel online algorithm, iterative Nash policy optimization (INPO), to let the policy play against itself via no-regret learning, thereby approximating the Nash policy.

2410.06508.title: Towards Self-Improvement of LLMs via MCTS: Leveraging Stepwise Knowledge with Curriculum Preference Learning
2410.06508.tldr: Experimental results on mathematical reasoning tasks demonstrate that AlphaLLM-CPL significantly outperforms previous MCTS behavior distillation methods, substantially boosting the reasoning capabilities of LLMs.

2309.10202.title: Stabilizing RLHF through Advantage Model and Selective Rehearsal
2309.10202.tldr: Two innovations to stabilize RLHF training are proposed: Advantage Model, which directly models advantage score i.e., extra reward compared to the expected rewards and regulates score distributions across tasks to prevent reward hacking and Selective Rehearsal, which mitigates catastrophic forgetting by strategically selecting data for PPO training and knowledge rehearsing.

2308.10819.title: Evaluating the Instruction-Following Robustness of Large Language Models to Prompt Injection
2308.10819.tldr: A benchmark is established to evaluate the robustness of instruction-following LLMs against prompt injection attacks, assessing their ability to discern which instructions to follow and which to disregard, and shows that certain models are excessively inclined to prioritize embedded instructions in prompts.
2308.10819.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2502.16852.title: Improving LLM General Preference Alignment via Optimistic Online Mirror Descent
2502.16852.tldr: Drawing on theoretical insights from learning in games, optimistic online mirror descent is integrated into the alignment framework to approximate the Nash policy and achieves an O(T^{-1}) bound on the duality gap, improving upon the previous result.

2402.13210.title: Bayesian Reward Models for LLM Alignment
2402.13210.tldr: A Bayesian reward model is trained using Laplace approximation on LoRA weights, and it is found that the resulting uncertainty estimates can effectively mitigate reward overoptimization in BoN sampling.

2503.07050.title: TIDE : Temporal-Aware Sparse Autoencoders for Interpretable Diffusion Transformers in Image Generation
2503.07050.tldr: TIDE effectively captures temporally-varying representations and reveals that DiTs naturally learn hierarchical semantics during large-scale pretraining, enabling applications such as safe image editing and style transfer.

2605.04653.title: Threshold-Guided Optimization for Visual Generative Models
2605.04653.tldr: A threshold-guided alignment framework is proposed that replaces this oracle baseline with a data-driven global threshold estimated from empirical score statistics, enabling effective optimization directly from scalar feedback.

2501.10639.title: Latent-space adversarial training with post-aware calibration for defending large language models against jailbreak attacks
2501.10639.tldr: Experimental results across five types of disguise-based jailbreak attacks demonstrate that LATPC achieves a superior balance between safety and utility compared to existing defense frameworks, and demonstrates the effectiveness of leveraging safety-critical dimensions in developing robust defense methods against jailbreak attacks.

2511.14423.title: Unified Defense for Large Language Models against Jailbreak and Fine-Tuning Attacks in Education
2511.14423.tldr: EduHarm is constructed, a benchmark containing safe-unsafe instruction pairs across five representative educational scenarios, enabling systematic safety evaluation of educational LLMs, and a three-stage shield framework (TSSF) is proposed that simultaneously mitigates both jailbreak and fine-tuning attacks.

2607.20090.title: Reinforcement Learning for Large Language Model Selective Evidence Adoption from Contaminated Retrieval Results
2607.20090.tldr: A directional improvement in selective evidence use is demonstrated, while identifying injection resistance and statistical robustness as important remaining challenges for future work.

2405.09055.title: A safety realignment framework via subspace-oriented model fusion for large language models
2405.09055.tldr: A safety realignment framework through subspace-oriented model fusion (SOMF) is introduced, aiming to combine the safeguard capabilities of initially aligned model and the current fine-tuned model into a realigned model, confirming that SOMF preserves safety without notably compromising performance on downstream tasks.

2608.21500.title: SecOPD: Mitigating Adaptive Prompt Injections by On-Policy Distillation
2608.21500.tldr: This paper proposes Secure On-Policy Distillation (SecOPD) that provides token-level feedback to guide defensive fine-tuning, and generalizes to domains completely unseen in training.

2410.05451.title: SecAlign: Defending Against Prompt Injection with Preference Optimization
2410.05451.tldr: This work proposes a new defense called SecAlign based on the technique of preference optimization that provides the first known method that reduces the success rates of various prompt injections to <10%, even against attacks much more sophisticated than ones seen during training.
2410.05451.venue: Conference on Computer and Communications Security

2501.15145.title: PromptShield: Deployable Detection for Prompt Injection Attacks
2501.15145.tldr: It is suggested that careful curation of training data and larger models can contribute to strong detector performance, and a new prompt injection detector that achieves significantly higher performance in the low false positive rate (FPR) evaluation regime compared to prior schemes is introduced.
2501.15145.venue: Conference on Data and Application Security and Privacy

2504.19440.title: JailbreaksOverTime: Detecting Jailbreak Attacks Under Distribution Shift
2504.19440.tldr: This work proposes a two-pronged method for defenders to detect new jailbreaks and continuously update their detectors and introduces an unsupervised active monitoring approach to identify novel jailbreaks that can identify out-of-distribution attacks that were missed by continuous learning.

2505.11790.title: JULI: Jailbreak Large Language Models by Self-Introspection
2505.11790.tldr: JULI is proposed, which jailbreaks LLMs by manipulating the token log probabilities, using a tiny plug-in block, BiasNet, and demonstrates superior effectiveness, outperforming existing state-of-the-art (SOTA) approaches across multiple metrics.

2402.06363.title: StruQ: Defending Against Prompt Injection with Structured Queries
2402.06363.tldr: This work significantly improves resistance to prompt injection attacks, with little or no impact on utility, and implements a system that supports structured queries.

2507.02735.title: Meta SecAlign: A Secure Foundation LLM Against Prompt Injection Attacks
2507.02735.tldr: Results show that Meta SecAlign, despite being trained only on generic instruction-tuning samples, surprisingly confers security in unseen downstream tasks, including tool-calling and web-navigation, in addition to general instruction-following.

2509.25926.title: Preventing Prompt Injection with Type-Directed Privilege Separation
2509.25926.tldr: Type-directed privilege separation is introduced, a new technique that expands the set of tasks that can be protected with system-level defenses and works by converting untrusted data to a curated set of data types; unlike raw strings, each data type is limited in scope and content, eliminating the possibility for prompt injection.

2510.19207.title: Defending Against Prompt Injection with DataFilter
2510.19207.tldr: DataFilter is trained with supervised fine-tuning on simulated injections and leverages both the user's instruction and the data to selectively strip adversarial content while preserving benign information, making it a strong practical defense to secure black-box commercial LLMs against prompt injection.

2609.04533.title: Repeat-After-Me: Black-Box Adaptive Visual Prompt Injection

2403.00867.title: Gradient Cuff: Detecting Jailbreak Attacks on Large Language Models by Exploring Refusal Loss Landscapes
2403.00867.tldr: This paper defines and investigates the Refusal Loss of LLMs and then proposes a method called Gradient Cuff to detect jailbreak attempts, which exploits the unique properties observed in the refusal loss landscape to design an effective two-step detection strategy.

2506.05346.title: Why LLM Safety Guardrails Collapse After Fine-tuning: A Similarity Analysis Between Alignment and Fine-tuning Datasets
2506.05346.tldr: This paper investigates the degradation of safety guardrails through the lens of representation similarity between upstream alignment datasets and downstream fine-tuning tasks, and demonstrates that high similarity between these datasets significantly weakens safety guardrails, making models more susceptible to jailbreaks.
2506.05346.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2412.18171.title: Token Highlighter: Inspecting and Mitigating Jailbreak Prompts for Large Language Models
2412.18171.tldr: Token Highlighter introduced a concept called Affirmation Loss to measure the LLM's willingness to answer the user query and uses the gradient of Affirmation Loss for each token in the user query to locate the jailbreak-critical tokens.

2506.00781.title: CoP: Agentic Red-teaming for Large Language Models using Composition of Principles
2506.00781.tldr: This paper proposes an agentic workflow to automate and scale the red-teaming process of LLMs through the Composition-of-Principles (CoP) framework, where human users provide a set of red-teaming principles as instructions to an AI agent to automatically orchestrate effective red-teaming strategies and generate jailbreak prompts.

2602.04896.title: Steering Externalities: Benign Activation Steering Unintentionally Increases Jailbreak Risk for Large Language Models
2602.04896.tldr: This work identifies a phenomenon termed Steering Externalities, where steering vectors derived from entirely benign datasets-such as those enforcing strict compliance or specific output formats like JSON-inadvertently erode safety guardrails and exposes a critical blind spot in deployment.

2412.17544.title: Retention Score: Quantifying Jailbreak Risks for Vision Language Models
2412.17544.tldr: It is proved that Retention Score can serve as certified robustness metric and it is demonstrated that most VLMs with visual components are less robust against jailbreak attacks than corresponding plain VLMs.

2507.04365.title: Attention Slipping: A Mechanistic Understanding of Jailbreak Attacks and Defenses in LLMs
2507.04365.tldr: Attention Sharpening is proposed, a new defense that directly counters Attention Slipping by sharpening the attention score distribution using temperature scaling and introduces no additional computational or memory overhead, making it an efficient and practical solution for real-world deployment.

2504.09466.title: AdaSteer: Your Aligned LLM is Inherently an Adaptive Jailbreak Defender
2504.09466.tldr: This work proposes AdaSteer, an adaptive activation steering method that dynamically adjusts model behavior based on input characteristics, ensuring robust jailbreak defense while preserving benign input handling in LLMs.
2504.09466.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2505.16869.title: MPO: Multilingual Safety Alignment via Reward Gap Optimization
2505.16869.tldr: Multilingual reward gaP Optimization (MPO) is introduced, a novel approach that leverages the well-aligned safety capabilities of the dominant language (English) to improve safety alignment across multiple languages.
2505.16869.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2509.06795.title: Anchoring Refusal Direction: Mitigating Safety Risks in Tuning via Projection Constraint
2509.06795.tldr: The analysis indicates that ProCon can contribute to stabilizing the r-direction during training, while such an interpretability-driven exploration of LLMs'internal mechanisms lays a solid foundation for future safety research.

2601.03537.title: STAR-S: Improving Safety Alignment through Self-Taught Reasoning on Safety Rules
2601.03537.tldr: STAR-S is proposed, a framework that integrates the learning of safety rule reasoning into a self-taught loop, and shows that STAR-S effectively defends against jailbreak attacks, outperforming baselines.

2507.08014.title: Mass-Scale Analysis of In-the-Wild Conversations Reveals Complexity Bounds on LLM Jailbreaking
2507.08014.tldr: A mass-scale empirical analysis of jailbreak complexity across over 2 million real-world conversations from diverse platforms, including dedicated jailbreaking communities and general-purpose chatbots finds that jailbreak attempts do not exhibit significantly higher complexity than normal conversations.

2603.07452.title: Backdoor4Good: Benchmarking Beneficial Uses of Backdoors in LLMs
2603.07452.tldr: The findings demonstrate new insights that backdoors need not be inherently malicious; when properly designed, they can serve as modular, interpretable, and beneficial building blocks for trustworthy AI systems.

2411.13731.title: Delta-Influence: Unlearning Poisons via Influence Functions
2411.13731.tldr: Delta-Influence is introduced, a novel approach that leverages influence functions to trace abnormal model behavior back to the responsible poisoned training data using as little as just one poisoned test example, showing the promise of influence functions for corrective unlearning.

2411.12600.title: Provable unlearning in topic modeling and downstream tasks
2411.12600.tldr: It is shown that it is easier to unlearn pre-training data from models that have been fine-tuned to a particular task, and one can unlearn this data without modifying the base model.

2603.03172.title: Less Noise, Same Certificate: Retain Sensitivity for Unlearning
2603.03172.tldr: While insufficient for DP, retain sensitivity is exactly sufficient for unlearning, allowing for the same certificates with less noise, and refine the analysis of two widely used certified unlearning algorithms through the lens of retain sensitivity.

2309.08230.title: A Duty to Forget, a Right to be Assured? Exposing Vulnerabilities in Machine Unlearning Services
2309.08230.tldr: This study uncovers an underexplored gap between unlearning and contemporary MLaaS, highlighting the need for careful considerations in balancing data unlearning, model utility, and security.
2309.08230.venue: Network and Distributed System Security Symposium

2404.03233.title: Learn What You Want to Unlearn: Unlearning Inversion Attacks against Machine Unlearning
2404.03233.tldr: The first investigation to understand the extent to which machine unlearning can leak the confidential content of the unlearned data is conducted, and three possible defenses are identified that help to mitigate the proposed attacks, while at the cost of reducing the utility of the unlearned model.
2404.03233.venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy

2206.04823.title: Membership Inference via Backdooring
2206.04823.tldr: This paper proposes a novel membership inference approach inspired by the backdoor technology that leverages the key observation that a backdoored model behaves very differently from a clean model when predicting on deliberately marked samples created by a data owner.
2206.04823.venue: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence

2509.23362.title: Dual-Space Smoothness for Robust and Balanced LLM Unlearning
2509.23362.tldr: This work proposes PRISM, a unified framework that enforces dual-space smoothness in representation and parameter spaces to improve robustness and balance unlearning metrics and shows that PRISM outperforms SOTA baselines under multiple attacks while achieving a better balance among key metrics.

2310.18574.title: Breaking the Trilemma of Privacy, Utility, Efficiency via Controllable Machine Unlearning
2310.18574.tldr: Controllable Machine Unlearning (ConMU), a novel framework designed to facilitate the calibration of MU, explores the full spectrum of the Privacy-Utility-Efficiency trade-off and allows practitioners to account for different real-world regulations.

2402.10058.title: Towards Safer Large Language Models through Machine Unlearning
2402.10058.tldr: This work introduces Selective Knowledge negation Unlearning (SKU), a novel unlearning framework for LLMs designed to eliminate harmful knowledge while preserving utility on normal prompts, and demonstrates that SKU identifies a good balance point between removing harmful information and preserving utility.
2402.10058.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2410.22108.title: Protecting Privacy in Multimodal Large Language Models with MLLMU-Bench
2410.22108.tldr: Surprisingly, the authors' experiments show that unimodal unlearning algorithms excel in generation and cloze tasks, while multimodal unlearning approaches perform better in classification tasks with multimodal inputs.
2410.22108.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2605.10664.title: Prompt-Activation Duality: Improving Activation Steering via Attention-Level Interventions
2605.10664.tldr: Gated Cropped Attention-Delta steering (GCAD), which extracts steering signals from system-prompt contributions to self-attention and applies them with token-level gating, suggests that activation steering becomes more reliable when interventions follow the prompt-mediated pathways that models already use for behavioral control.

2407.20516.title: Machine Unlearning in Generative AI: A Survey
2407.20516.tldr: This work offers a comprehensive survey on many things about MU in Generative AI, such as a new problem formulation, evaluation methods, and a structured discussion on the advantages and limitations of different kinds of MU techniques.

2502.15910.title: Modality-Aware Neuron Pruning for Unlearning in Multimodal Large Language Models
2502.15910.tldr: Modality Aware Neuron Unlearning (MANU), a novel unlearning framework for MLLMs designed to selectively clip neurons based on their relative importance to the targeted forget data, curated for different modalities, is proposed.
2502.15910.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2509.20230.title: Beyond Sharp Minima: Robust LLM Unlearning via Feedback-Guided Multi-Point Optimization
2509.20230.tldr: StableUN is proposed, a bi-level feedback-guided optimization framework that explicitly seeks more stable parameter regions via neighborhood-aware optimization that integrates forgetting feedback, which uses adversarial perturbations to probe parameter neighborhoods, with remembering feedback to preserve model utility, aligning the two objectives through gradient projection.

2607.07907.title: Multimodal Unlearning Across Vision, Language, Video, and Audio: Survey of Methods, Datasets, and Benchmarks
2607.07907.tldr: This survey offers a unified, system-oriented view of multimodal unlearning across vision, language, audio, and video, grounded in recent advances, emerging applications, and open problems.
2607.07907.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2608.26372.title: Knowledge-Verified Emergent Deception in LLM Agents Under Conflicting Incentives
2608.26372.tldr: A knowledge-verified benchmark that first confirms through a neutral probe that an agent knows a user's entitlement, and then evaluates whether it makes false claims once an incentive to deny that entitlement is introduced, which reduces the confound between lying and not knowing and enables more rigorous auditing and steering of agent honesty.

2412.18621.title: Investigating the Feasibility of Mitigating Potential Copyright Infringement via Large Language Model Unlearning
2412.18621.tldr: Stable Sequential Unlearning is proposed, a novel framework designed to unlearn copyrighted content from LLMs over multiple time steps that improves unlearning efficacy by introducing random labeling loss and ensuring the model retains its general-purpose knowledge by adjusting targeted parameters with gradient-based weight saliency.

2506.04463.title: Aligning Large Language Models with Implicit Preferences from User-Generated Content
2506.04463.tldr: PUGC is presented, a novel framework that leverages implicit human Preferences in unlabeled User-Generated Content (UGC) to generate preference data and improves the quality of preference data while enabling scalable, domain-specific alignment.
2506.04463.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2510.02341.title: DRIFT: Learning from Abundant User Dissatisfaction in Real-World Preference Learning
2510.02341.tldr: This paper introduces DRIFT (Dissatisfaction-Iterative Pre-Training), which anchors training on real-world DSAT signals and samples positives dynamically from the evolving policy, and demonstrates that this design preserves preference margins and avoids the gradient degeneration.

2605.24197.title: A Sober Look at Agentic Misalignment in Automated Workflows
2605.24197.tldr: This work proposes Agentic Evidence Attribution (AEA), a novel alignment paradigm that improves agent posteriors using context-specific evidence and shows that evidence-based alignment can effectively improve agent collaboration and leads to reliable multi-agent systems built on automated workflows.

2510.13272.title: Beyond Correctness: Rewarding Faithful Reasoning in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
2510.13272.tldr: To foster faithful reasoning in agentic search, VERITAS (Verifying Entailed Reasoning through Intermediate Traceability in Agentic Search), a novel framework that integrates fine-grained turn-level faithfulness rewards into the reinforcement learning process is introduced.

2411.08745.title: Separating Tongue from Thought: Activation Patching Reveals Language-Agnostic Concept Representations in Transformers
2411.08745.tldr: This paper analyzes latent representations during a word-translation task in transformer-based LLMs and shows that patching with the mean representation of a concept across different languages does not affect the models'ability to translate it, but instead improves it.
2411.08745.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2408.03618.title: A Logical Fallacy-Informed Framework for Argument Generation
2408.03618.tldr: FIPO, a fallacy-informed framework that leverages preference optimization methods to steer LLMs toward logically sound arguments, and shows that the quality of the generated arguments by the method significantly outperforms the fine-tuned baselines, as well as other preference optimization methods, such as DPO.
2408.03618.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2605.13329.title: Tracing Persona Vectors Through LLM Pretraining
2605.13329.tldr: This work traces persona vectors across the pretraining of OLMo-3-7B, finding that persona vectors form remarkably early -- within 0.22% of OLMo-3 pretraining -- and remain effective for steering the fully post-trained instruct models.

2608.13482.title: Synthetic Persona Pretraining: Alignment from Token Zero
2608.13482.tldr: Results show that shaping values early is critical for alignment and establish pretraining-time persona interventions as an effective approach to do so, and show that SPP improves constitution following and jailbreak robustness, and reduces the misalignment rate in out-of-distribution moral dilemmas, while preserving capabilities.

2506.12913.title: Jailbreak Transferability Emerges from Shared Representations
2506.12913.tldr: It is shown that deliberately increasing similarity through benign only distillation causally increases transfer, and reframe jailbreak transfer as a consequence of representation alignment rather than a fragile byproduct of safety training.

2605.28467.title: Mitigating Adaptive Attacks against Reasoning Models with Activation Consistency Training
2605.28467.tldr: The results suggest that supervising internal representations is a surprisingly effective and interpretable approach to various forms of safety training in reasoning models.

2608.05409.title: Mood Matters: How Syntactic Sensitivity Undermines Safety Alignment
2608.05409.tldr: This work uncovers a more general failure of non-imperative syntactic forms and traces this ill-conditioning to linguistically biased post-training data of open-source models and shows that increasing syntactic diversity can mitigate the issue.

2411.18895.title: Evaluating Sparse Autoencoders on Targeted Concept Erasure Tasks
2411.18895.tldr: This work adapts SHIFT into an automated metric of SAE quality; this involves replacing the human annotator with an LLM, and introduces the Targeted Probe Perturbation (TPP) metric that quantifies an SAE's ability to disentangle similar concepts, effectively scaling SHIFT to a wider range of datasets.

2310.07325.title: An Adversarial Example for Direct Logit Attribution: Memory Management in GELU-4L
2310.07325.tldr: This study provides concrete evidence for this erasure phenomenon in a 4-layer transformer, identifying heads that consistently remove the output of earlier heads and demonstrates that direct logit attribution (DLA) can show misleading results by not accounting for erasure.
2310.07325.venue: BlackboxNLP Workshop on Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP

2505.17441.title: Discovering Forbidden Topics in Language Models
2505.17441.tldr: A refusal discovery method, Iterated Prefill Crawler (IPC), that uses token prefilling to find forbidden topics and highlights the critical need for refusal discovery methods to detect biases, boundaries, and alignment failures of AI systems.

2405.13637.title: Curriculum Direct Preference Optimization for Diffusion and Consistency Models
2405.13637.tldr: The proposed Curriculum DPO is compared against state-of-the-art fine-tuning approaches on nine benchmarks, outperforming the competing methods in terms of text alignment, aesthetics and human preference.

2602.13055.title: Curriculum-DPO++: Direct Preference Optimization via Data and Model Curricula for Text-to-Image Generation
2602.13055.tldr: Curriculum-DPO++ is introduced, an enhanced method that combines the original data-level curriculum with a novel model-level curriculum and dynamically increase the learning capacity of the denoising network as training advances, outperforming the competing methods in terms of text alignment, aesthetics and human preference.

2505.18126.title: Reward Model Overoptimisation in Iterated RLHF
2505.18126.tldr: This work systematically analyse key design choices - how reward model training data is transferred across iterations, which reward function is used for optimisation, and how policies are initialised, to present the first comprehensive study of overoptimisation in iterated RLHF.

2310.06452.title: Understanding the Effects of RLHF on LLM Generalisation and Diversity
2310.06452.tldr: An extensive analysis of how each stage of the process of supervised fine-tuning, reward modelling, and RLHF affects two key properties: out-of-distribution (OOD) generalisation and output diversity is presented.

2609.01611.title: EvalDetectBench: A Benchmark for Measuring Evaluation Awareness in Frontier Language Models
2609.01611.tldr: EvalDetectBench is introduced, an open pipeline and benchmark for measuring evaluation awareness that works with any Inspect-compatible evaluation, allowing practitioners to test against current and future benchmarks.

2609.02302.title: Improving Evaluation Realism with Inference-Time Compute and Deployment Scaffolds
2609.02302.tldr: Two techniques that make simulated alignment evaluations harder to distinguish from real deployments are presented, and automated approaches can improve the realism of alignment evaluations, and that these improvements use additional compute more effectively than making the audits longer.

2407.07539.title: Machine Unlearning for Medical Imaging
2407.07539.tldr: Evaluations of different unlearning algorithms in medical imaging domain demonstrate that the considered unlearning algorithms perform well on the retain set and forget set, but the existing unlearning algorithms still needs further improvements to become more practical for medical applications.

2501.01335.title: CySecBench: Generative AI-based CyberSecurity-focused Prompt Dataset for Benchmarking Large Language Models
2501.01335.tldr: This work presents and publicly releases CySecBench, a comprehensive dataset containing 12662 prompts specifically designed to evaluate jailbreaking techniques in the cybersecurity domain, and proposes and evaluates a jailbreaking approach based on prompt obfuscation.

2503.21598.title: Prompt, Divide, and Conquer: Bypassing Large Language Model Safety Filters via Segmented and Distributed Prompt Processing
2503.21598.tldr: A novel jailbreaking framework that employs distributed prompt processing combined with iterative refinements to bypass safety measures, particularly in generating malicious code, and demonstrates both the effectiveness of distributed prompt processing and the importance of robust evaluation methodologies in assessing jailbreak attempts.

2509.12937.title: Jailbreaking Large Language Models Through Content Concretization
2509.12937.tldr: This paper introduces \textit{Content Concretization} (CC), a novel jailbreaking technique that iteratively transforms abstract malicious requests into concrete, executable implementations and highlights critical vulnerabilities in current LLM safety frameworks.
2509.12937.venue: Decision and Game Theory for Security

2406.09136.title: Chain of Preference Optimization: Improving Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in LLMs
2406.09136.tldr: This work demonstrates that fine-tuning LLMs leveraging the search tree constructed by ToT allows CoT to achieve similar or better performance, thereby avoiding the substantial inference burden.

2406.09760.title: Bootstrapping Language Models with DPO Implicit Rewards
2406.09760.tldr: This work makes a novel observation that this implicit reward model can by itself be used in a bootstrapping fashion to further align the LLM, and shows great improvements in alignment.

2410.08109.title: A Closer Look at Machine Unlearning for Large Language Models
2410.08109.tldr: To address the issue of inadequate evaluation of model outputs after unlearning, three additional metrics are introduced to evaluate token diversity, sentence semantics, and factual correctness and to alleviate issues in machine unlearning for LLMs.

2410.12777.title: Meta-Unlearning on Diffusion Models: Preventing Relearning Unlearned Concepts
2410.12777.tldr: The proposed metaunlearning framework is compatible with most existing unlearning methods, requiring only the addition of an easy-to-implement meta objective, and validated through empirical experiments on meta-unlearning concepts from Stable Diffusion models (SD-v1-4 and SDXL), supported by extensive ablation studies.
2410.12777.venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision

2505.20259.title: Lifelong Safety Alignment for Language Models
2505.20259.tldr: A lifelong safety alignment framework that enables LLMs to continuously adapt to new and evolving jailbreaking strategies, and introduces a competitive setup between two components: a Meta-Attacker, trained to actively discover novel jailbreaking strategies, and a Defender, trained to resist them.

2412.16633.title: POEX: Towards Policy Executable Jailbreak Attacks Against the LLM-based Robots
2412.16633.tldr: It is concluded that traditional LLM jailbreak attacks are inapplicable in robot scenarios, and two unique challenges are identified: determining policy-executable optimization directions and accurately evaluating robot-jailbroken policies.

2509.24610.title: OrthAlign: Orthogonal Subspace Decomposition for Non-Interfering Multi-Objective Alignment
2509.24610.tldr: Theoretical guarantees are provided demonstrating that when parameter increments satisfy both orthogonal subspace constraints and spectral norm bounds, the resulting updates exhibit linear Lipschitz growth rather than exponential instability, ensuring stable convergence across all preference dimensions.

2505.15674.title: UniErase: Towards Balanced and Precise Unlearning in Language Models
2505.15674.tldr: Serving as a new unlearning paradigm via editing, UniErase achieves outstanding performances across batch, sequential, and precise unlearning tasks under fictitious and real-world knowledge scenarios.

2608.30441.title: ECLIPSE: Self-Evolving Stealthy Prompt Injection Attack against Long-Horizon Agentic Systems
2608.30441.tldr: ECLIPSE is a self-evolving and stealthy prompt-injection framework for long-horizon agentic systems that achieves up to 96.7% attack success without defense and 69.2% under the common safety filter, exceeding the strongest baseline by 27.5% in the defended setting.

2602.10453.title: The Landscape of Prompt Injection Threats in LLM Agents: From Taxonomy to Analysis
2602.10453.tldr: This work introduces AgentPI, a new benchmark designed to systematically evaluate agent behavior under context-dependent interaction settings, and establishes taxonomies that categorize PI attacks by payload generation strategies (heuristic vs. optimization) and defenses by intervention stages (text, model, and execution levels).

2511.09880.title: EnchTable: Unified Safety Alignment Transfer in Fine-tuned Large Language Models
2511.09880.tldr: Comparative analyses reveal that EnchTable achieves a significantly lower unsafe rate, higher utility score, and universal applicability across different task domains, and validate EnchTable can be seamlessly integrated into various deployment pipelines without significant overhead.

2608.22248.title: Beyond Over-Refusal: Defending Indirect Prompt Injection via Latent Instruction Manifolds
2608.22248.tldr: AEGIS (Adaptive Ensemble Guard for Injection Shielding) extracts instruction-sensitive projectors to identify malicious instructions and leverages a Unified Multi-Layer Consensus mechanism that aggregates topologically distinct signals across the network depth.

2603.23269.title: Not All Tokens Are Created Equal: Query-Efficient Jailbreak Fuzzing for LLMs
2603.23269.tldr: A token-level analysis of refusal behavior is conducted and it is observed that token contributions are highly skewed rather than uniform, enabling the use of a surrogate model to estimate token-level contributions to the target model's refusals.

2506.06112.title: Towards Lifecycle Unlearning Commitment Management: Measuring Sample-level Unlearning Completeness
2506.06112.tldr: The Interpolated Approximate Measurement (IAM), a framework natively designed for unlearning inference, is proposed and applied to recent approximate unlearning algorithms, revealing general risks of both over-unlearning and under-unlearning and underscoring the need for stronger safeguards in approximate unlearning systems.

2403.12830.title: Towards Lifecycle Unlearning Commitment Management: Measuring Sample-level Approximate Unlearning Completeness
2403.12830.tldr: An efficient metric designed to assess the sample-level unlearning completeness is proposed and demonstrated its superiority over membership inference techniques in two key areas: the strong correlation of its measurements with unlearning completeness across various unlearning tasks, and its computational efficiency, making it suitable for real-time applications.

2404.18567.title: Double Backdoored: Converting Code Large Language Model Backdoors to Traditional Malware via Adversarial Instruction Tuning Attacks
2404.18567.tldr: This work investigates novel techniques for transitioning backdoors from the AI/ML domain to traditional computer malware, shedding light on the critical intersection of AI and cyber/software security and highlighting the urgent need for robust defense mechanisms.

2411.02622.title: AdaProb: Efficient Machine Unlearning via Adaptive Probability
2411.02622.tldr: Adaptive Probability Approximate Unlearning (AdaProb) is a novel method that enables models to forget data efficiently and in a privacy-preserving manner and outperforms state-of-the-art approaches with over 20% improvement in forgetting error, better protection against membership inference attacks, and less than 50% of the computational time.

2505.08138.title: Mirror Mirror on the Wall, Have I Forgotten it All? A New Framework for Evaluating Machine Unlearning
2505.08138.tldr: It is demonstrated that current methodology in the literature fundamentally falls short of achieving computational unlearning, and a strong formal definition for machine unlearning called computational unlearning is proposed.

2601.06967.title: A Robust Certified Machine Unlearning Method Under Distribution Shift
2601.06967.tldr: It is shown that certified unlearning with the Newton method becomes inefficient and ineffective under non-i.i.i.d. unlearning sets, and a better certified unlearning approach is proposed by performing a distribution-aware certified unlearning framework based on iterative Newton updates constrained by a trust region.

2305.12082.title: SneakyPrompt: Jailbreaking Text-to-image Generative Models
2305.12082.tldr: This work proposes SneakyPrompt, the first automated attack framework to jailbreak text-to-image generative models such that they generate NSFW images even if safety filters are adopted, and outperforms existing text adversarial attacks when extended to jailbreak text-to-image generative models.
2305.12082.venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy

2605.27117.title: Position: AI Safety Requires Effective Controllability
2605.27117.tldr: This position paper argues that AI safety requires controllability as a first-class objective and proposes a control-centric architectural framework that highlights explicit control planes, runtime intervention pathways, persistent control states, and auditable decision interfaces as key design principles for future controllable AI systems.

2405.19358.title: Robustifying Safety-Aligned Large Language Models through Clean Data Curation
2405.19358.tldr: This paper proposes an iterative process aimed at revising texts to reduce their perplexity as perceived by LLMs, while simultaneously preserving their text quality, and introduces an iterative process aimed at revising texts to reduce their perplexity as perceived by LLMs, while simultaneously preserving their text quality.

2412.07672.title: DYNASHIELD: A Black-Box Moving Target Defense for LLMs via Dynamic Decoding Customization
2412.07672.tldr: DYNASHIELD, a moving target defense framework that improves robustness by customizing decoding hyperparameters and system prompts at inference time, is proposed, a moving target defense framework that improves robustness by customizing decoding hyperparameters and system prompts at inference time.

2410.02220.title: Data to Defense: The Role of Curation in Customizing LLMs Against Jailbreaking Attacks
2410.02220.tldr: An adaptive data curation approach allowing any text to be curated to enhance its effectiveness in counteracting harmful samples during customization is proposed, representing a solid step forward in mitigating jailbreaking risks and ensuring the secure adaptation of LLMs.

2609.14060.title: AGENTQ: Quantization-Conditioned Backdoor Attacks on LLM Agents
2609.14060.tldr: AGENTQ is proposed, an attack framework that combines layer-banded LoRA injection with partial-PGD repair over a multi-codebook quantization-equivalence class that preserves normal agentic capability while concentrating malicious behavior in the quantized model, underscoring the need to make quantization-aware safety evaluation a standard requirement before open-weight agents are deployed.

2410.19937.title: RobustKV: Defending Large Language Models against Jailbreak Attacks via KV Eviction
2410.19937.tldr: By strategically evicting the KVs of the lowest-ranked tokens, RobustKV diminishes the presence of the harmful query in the KV cache, thus preventing the LLM from generating malicious responses, and contributes to RobustKV's robustness against adaptive attacks.

2602.04448.title: RASA: Routing-Aware Safety Alignment for Mixture-of-Experts Models
2602.04448.tldr: This work proposes RASA, a routing-aware expert-level alignment framework that explicitly repairs Safety-Critical Experts while preventing routing-based bypasses, and suggests that robust MoE safety alignment benefits from targeted expert repair rather than global parameter updates.

2505.17132.title: Dynamic Token Reweighting for Robust Vision-Language Models
2505.17132.tldr: DTR is presented, a novel inference-time defense that mitigates multimodal jailbreak attacks through optimizing the model's key-value (KV) caches and introduces a new formulation of the safety-relevant distributional shift induced by the visual modality.

2210.07346.title: An Embarrassingly Simple Backdoor Attack on Self-supervised Learning
2210.07346.tldr: It is suggested that SSL and supervised learning are comparably vulnerable to backdoor attacks, and the existing defenses against supervised backdoor attacks are not easily retrofitted to the unique vulnerability of SSL.
2210.07346.venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision

2509.01444.title: Strata-Sword: A Hierarchical Safety Evaluation towards LLMs based on Reasoning Complexity of Jailbreak Instructions
2509.01444.tldr: This paper quantifies "Reasoning Complexity" as an evaluable safety dimension and categorizes 15 jailbreak attack methods into three different levels according to the reasoning complexity, establishing a hierarchical Chinese-English jailbreak safety benchmark for systematically evaluating the safety performance of LLMs.

2501.04931.title: Jailbreaking Multimodal Large Language Models via Shuffle Inconsistency
2501.04931.tldr: It is found that there exists a Shuffle Inconsistency between MLLMs' comprehension ability and safety ability for the shuffled harmful instruction, and a query-based black-box optimization method is applied to select the most harmful shuffled inputs based on the feedback of the toxic judge model.
2501.04931.venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision

2603.22829.title: Improving Safety Alignment via Balanced Direct Preference Optimization
2603.22829.tldr: B-DPO is proposed, which adaptively modulates optimization strength between preferred and dispreferred responses based on mutual information based on mutual information, and can enhance the safety capability while maintaining the competitive general capabilities of LLMs on various mainstream benchmarks compared to state-of-the-art methods.

2608.12821.title: HiRoute: Hierarchical Routed Prompt Tuning for Safety Alignment of Large Language Models
2608.12821.tldr: Experiments across three instruction-tuned models show that HiRoute achieves high safety rates across multiple safety benchmarks while preserving safe-response helpfulness, reducing over-refusal, and maintaining competitive performance on general-purpose tasks.

2411.03814.title: MRJ-Agent: An Effective Jailbreak Agent for Multi-Round Dialogue
2411.03814.tldr: A novel multi-round dialogue jailbreaking agent that distributes risks across multiple rounds of queries and utilizes psychological strategies to enhance attack strength is proposed, emphasizing the importance of stealthiness in identifying and mitigating potential threats to human values posed by LLMs.

2412.05892.title: PBI-Attack: Prior-Guided Bimodal Interactive Black-Box Jailbreak Attack for Toxicity Maximization
2412.05892.tldr: PBI-Attack outperforms previous state-of-the-art jailbreak methods, achieving an average attack success rate of 92.5% across three open-source LVLMs and around 67.3% on three closed-source LVLMs.
2412.05892.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2512.05853.title: VRSA: Jailbreaking Multimodal Large Language Models through Visual Reasoning Sequential Attack
2512.05853.tldr: This work proposes Visual Reasoning Sequential Attack (VRSA), which induces MLLMs to gradually externalize and aggregate complete harmful intent by decomposing the original harmful text into several sequentially related sub-images.

2609.06851.title: You Are What You Read: Misalignment via In-Context Persona Induction
2609.06851.tldr: Broad misalignment has been produced by finetuning on narrow data, harmful or benign, and in context only by demonstrations of the undesirable behaviour itself by demonstrations of the undesirable behaviour itself.

2408.11261.title: Sycophancy in Vision-Language Models: A Systematic Analysis and an Inference-Time Mitigation Framework
2408.11261.tldr: This work systematically analyzed sycophancy across multiple vision-language benchmarks and proposed an inference-time mitigation framework, suggesting that sycophancy in LVLMs is a general and urgent challenge, and that inference-time strategies offer a promising path toward trustworthy multimodal reasoning.

2405.14758.title: Axioms for AI Alignment from Human Feedback
2405.14758.tldr: It is demonstrated that both the Bradley-Terry-Luce Model and its broad generalizations fail to meet basic axioms, and novel rules for learning reward functions with strong axiomatic guarantees are developed.

2602.01002.title: How RLHF Amplifies Sycophancy
2602.01002.tldr: A formal analysis of how alignment from human feedback can increase this failure mode by identifying an explicit amplification mechanism that causally links optimization against a learned reward to bias in the human preference data used for alignment.

2606.21550.title: AI Alignment From Social Choice Perspectives
2606.21550.tldr: It is illustrated how the social choice perspective helps identify failure modes in the feedback aggregation layer and reveals a broader design space for handling disagreement in explicit and principled ways.

2512.03276.title: Too Late to Recall: Explaining the Two-Hop Problem in Multimodal Knowledge Retrieval
2512.03276.tldr: It is argued that factual recall based on visual inputs requires VLMs to solve a two-hop problem: forming entity representations from visual inputs, and recalling associated factual knowledge based on these entity representations.

2608.09928.title: Multimodal Model Diffing for Feature Discovery and Control
2608.09928.tldr: MMDiff, a multimodal model-diffing framework that trains multimodal SAEs and turns them into feature-level interfaces for discovering and controlling multimodal behavior, shows that multimodal SAEs can serve not only as interpretability tools, but as mechanisms for auditing, steering, and controlling MLLMs behavior toward safer and more capable generations.

2606.14388.title: A Low-Rank Subspace Analysis of LLM Interventions
2606.14388.tldr: A diagnostic framework for analyzing interacting behaviors in LLMs is introduced, finding that different behaviors share internal representations, and intervening on one behavior alters others in asymmetric ways.

2609.06094.title: Automatic Red Teaming for Implicit Vulnerabilities of Text-to-Image Models
2609.06094.tldr: Adversarial Probing for Implicit VulnErabilities (AdvPIE), a multimodal agentic framework to expose implicit vulnerabilities without requiring access to the parameters of target models, is proposed.

2503.07639.title: Mixture of Experts Made Intrinsically Interpretable
2503.07639.tldr: MoE-X, a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language model designed to be interpretable, achieves performance comparable to dense models while significantly improving interpretability, with interpretability surpassing even sparse autoencoder (SAE)-based approaches.

2603.03970.title: Generative AI for Managerial Decision-Making under Ambiguity and Sycophancy
2603.03970.tldr: GenAI is positioned as a cognitive scaffold that can detect and resolve ambiguities managers might overlook, while demonstrating that its artificial limitations require human oversight to ensure its reliability as a strategic partner.

2405.03316.title: Provably Unlearnable Data Examples
2405.03316.tldr: A mechanism for certifying the so-called $(q, \eta)$-Learnability of an unlearnable dataset via parametric smoothing is proposed and a simple recovery attack can restore the clean-task performance of the classifiers trained on UEs by slightly perturbing the learned weights.
2405.03316.venue: Network and Distributed System Security Symposium

2312.15910.title: Reinforcement Unlearning
2312.15910.tldr: The first method is based on decremental reinforcement learning, which aims to erase the agent's previously acquired knowledge gradually, and the second method leverages environment poisoning attacks, which encourage the agent to learn new, albeit incorrect, knowledge to remove the unlearning environment.
2312.15910.venue: Network and Distributed System Security Symposium

2410.10128.title: Edge Unlearning is Not "on Edge"! An Adaptive Exact Unlearning System on Resource-Constrained Devices
2410.10128.tldr: This study proposes a Constraint-aware Adaptive Exact Unlearning System at the network Edge (CAUSE), an approach to enabling exact unlearning on resource-constrained devices that significantly outperforms other representative systems in realizing exact unlearning on the resource-constrained device.
2410.10128.venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy

2605.11592.title: SoK: Unlearnability and Unlearning for Model Dememorization
2605.11592.tldr: A unified taxonomy of unlearnability and scalable unlearning methods, an empirical evaluation revealing the robustness, interplay, and shallow dememorization of leading methods, and the first theoretical guarantee on dememorization depth for models processed through certified unlearning are presented.

2608.27910.title: AI Alignment through a Game-theoretic Lens: A Survey
2608.27910.tldr: This perspective clarifies where current alignment methods genuinely benefit from game-theoretic analysis, where the framework is looser, and what challenges remain in building robust, adaptive, and verifiable AI systems.

2407.01251.title: QUEEN: Query Unlearning against Model Extraction
2407.01251.tldr: QUEEN (QUEry unlEarNing) is proposed that proactively launches counterattacks on potential model extraction attacks from the very beginning and outperforms the state-of-the-art defenses against various model extraction attacks with a relatively low cost to the model accuracy.
2407.01251.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security

2510.26096.title: ALMGuard: Safety Shortcuts and Where to Find Them as Guardrails for Audio-Language Models
2510.26096.tldr: ALMGuard, the first defense framework tailored to ALMs, is proposed, based on the assumption that safety-aligned shortcuts naturally exist in ALMs, and a method to identify universal Shortcut Activation Perturbations that serve as triggers that activate the safety shortcuts to safeguard ALMs at inference time is designed.

2105.00164.title: Hidden Backdoors in Human-Centric Language Models
2105.00164.tldr: The proposed hidden backdoors can be effective across three downstream security-critical NLP tasks, representative of modern human-centric NLP systems, including toxic comment detection, neural machine translation (NMT), and question answering (QA).
2105.00164.venue: Conference on Computer and Communications Security

2111.05528.title: Lightweight machine unlearning in neural network
2111.05528.tldr: In this paper, experiments on five datasets prove the effectiveness of the method for machine unlearning, and the method is 15 times faster than retraining.

2404.03659.title: Federated Unlearning for Human Activity Recognition
2404.03659.tldr: A lightweight machine unlearning method for refining the FL HAR model by selectively removing a portion of a client's training data, using KL divergence as a loss function for fine-tuning and introducing a membership inference evaluation method to assess unlearning effectiveness.

2404.16841.title: Machine Unlearning in Large Language Models
2404.16841.tldr: A novel machine unlearning framework is introduced into large language models to make LLMs not produce harmful, hallucinatory, or privacy-compromising responses, while retaining their standard output capabilities.

2405.07317.title: Machine Unlearning in Contrastive Learning
2405.07317.tldr: This study introduces a novel gradient constraint-based approach for training the model to effectively achieve machine unlearning that demonstrates proficient performance not only on contrastive learning models but also on supervised learning models, showcasing its versatility and adaptability in various learning paradigms.

2604.07386.title: Label Leakage Attacks in Machine Unlearning: A Parameter and Inversion-Based Approach
2604.07386.tldr: This paper designs a gradient optimization-based white-box attack and a genetic algorithm-based black-box attack to reconstruct class-prototypical samples and proposes four attack methods from the perspectives of model parameters and model inversion based on attackers with different knowledge backgrounds.
2604.07386.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

2605.08730.title: Classification-Head Bias in Class-Level Machine Unlearning: Diagnosis, Mitigation, and Evaluation
2605.08730.tldr: A bias-dominated shortcut in class-level unlearning is revealed: the prediction of forgotten classes can be suppressed by decreasing the corresponding bias terms in the final classification head, using BiasShift as a diagnostic baseline and three bias-oriented metrics to quantify bias dependence and potential leakage.

2111.11869.title: Machine unlearning via GAN
2111.11869.tldr: This paper presents a GAN-based algorithm to delete data in deep models, which significantly improves deleting speed compared to retraining from scratch, especially in complicated scenarios.

2311.16113.title: BAGEL: Backdoor Attacks against Federated Contrastive Learning
2311.16113.tldr: The backdoor attack against FCL is studied as a pioneer research, to illustrate how backdoor attacks on distributed local clients act on downstream tasks, and how to inject backdoors into multiple downstream models in terms of two different backdoor attacks.

2609.12808.title: K-Bench: A Benchmark for LLM Unlearning in Agentic Deployments
2609.12808.tldr: K-Bench is introduced, a benchmark that scores LLM unlearning under agentic deployment and certifies forgetting by reading the model's final answer, where a model that refuses to answer already counts as having forgotten.

2308.10422.title: Split Unlearning
2308.10422.tldr: This work proposes SplitWiper with a new one-way-one-off propagation scheme, which leverages the inherently ''Sharded'' structure of SL and decouples neural signal propagation between clients and the server, enabling effective SISA unlearning even in scenarios with absent clients.
2308.10422.venue: Conference on Computer and Communications Security

2402.16294.title: BlockFUL: Enabling Unlearning in Blockchained Federated Learning
2402.16294.tldr: This paper introduces Blockchained Federated Unlearning (BlockFUL), a novel framework with a dual-chain structure-comprising a live chain and an archive chain-for enabling unlearning capabilities within Blockchained FL and introduces two new unlearning paradigms, i.e., parallel and sequential paradigms.
2402.16294.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security

2408.08493.title: Parallel Unlearning in Inherited Model Networks
2408.08493.tldr: This paper presents a novel unlearning framework that enables fully parallel unlearning among models exhibiting inheritance, using a chronologically Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) to capture various unlearning scenarios occurring in model inheritance networks.
2408.08493.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security

2510.04773.title: Distribution Preference Optimization: A Fine-grained Perspective for LLM Unlearning
2510.04773.tldr: It is shown that the requisite preference distribution pairs for DiPO can be constructed by selectively amplifying or suppressing the model's high-confidence output logits, thereby effectively overcoming NPO's limitations.

2210.07792.title: Robust Preference Learning for Storytelling via Contrastive Reinforcement Learning
2210.07792.tldr: It is shown that the full fine-tuning pipeline results in a story generator preferred over a LLM 20x as large as well as logit-based methods, and motivates the use of contrastive learning for general purpose human preference modeling.

2407.17387.title: PERSONA: A Reproducible Testbed for Pluralistic Alignment

2609.19101.title: Monitoring and Discovering Reward Hacking with Internal Representations during LLM Evaluations
2609.19101.tldr: This work finds that simple difference of means vectors coherently represent reward hacking in Kimi K3, GLM 5.2, and Qwen 3.8 Max, and provides evidence that simple, white-box methods can be used to scalably study and monitor reward hacking behaviors in frontier open source models.

2604.09665.title: Deliberative Alignment is Deep, but Uncertainty Remains: Inference time safety improvement in reasoning via attribution of unsafe behavior to base model
2604.09665.tldr: This work studies the impact of deliberative alignment in language models and proposes a BoN sampling method that attributes the unsafe behavior back to the base LLMs in the latent space, thereby down-ranking unsafe responses to gain a meaningful improvement in model safety across multiple safety benchmarks with minimal loss in utility.

2403.03185.title: Correlated Proxies: A New Definition and Improved Mitigation for Reward Hacking
2403.03185.tldr: This work introduces a definition of reward hacking based on the correlation between proxy and true rewards for states and actions seen by a"reference policy" that breaks down under optimization and shows theoretically that regularization to the reference policy can effectively prevent reward hacking.

2409.17407.title: Post-hoc Reward Calibration: A Case Study on Length Bias
2409.17407.tldr: This paper proposes an intuitive approach to estimate the bias term and, thus, remove it to approximate the underlying true reward, and extends the approach to a more general and robust form with the Locally Weighted Regression.

2401.15241.title: Unlearning Traces the Influential Training Data of Language Models
