2602.13151.title: Quantization-Robust LLM Unlearning via Low-Rank Adaptation
2602.13151.tldr: This work freezes the base model and concentrates unlearning into trainable adapters so that the effective update is preserved after quantization, and proposes quantization-robust unlearning via low-rank adaptation (LoRA).

2504.15827.title: DualOptim: Enhancing Efficacy and Stability in Machine Unlearning with Dual Optimizers
2504.15827.tldr: Through extensive experiments, it is shown that DualOptim can significantly boost MU efficacy and stability across diverse tasks, including image classification, image generation, and large language models, making it a versatile approach to empower existing MU algorithms.

2605.21539.title: DualOptim+: Bridging Shared and Decoupled Optimizer States for Better Machine Unlearning in Large Language Models
2605.21539.tldr: This work proposes DualOptim+, a novel optimization framework for improving machine unlearning in large language models that introduces a base state to capture common representations shared by forgetting and retaining objectives and delta states to preserve objective-specific residuals.

2405.20778.title: Improved Generation of Adversarial Examples Against Safety-aligned LLMs
2405.20778.tldr: This paper appropriate the ideologies of effective methods among these transfer-based attacks, i.e., Skip Gradient Method and Intermediate Level Attack, into gradient-based adversarial prompt generation and achieve significant performance gains without introducing obvious computational cost.

2410.11317.title: Deciphering the Chaos: Enhancing Jailbreak Attacks via Adversarial Prompt Translation
2410.11317.tldr: This paper delves into the semantic meaning embedded in garbled adversarial prompts and proposes a novel method that "translates" them into coherent and human-readable natural language adversarial prompts and offers a new approach to discovering effective designs for jailbreak prompts.

2206.09140.title: Certified Graph Unlearning
2206.09140.tldr: This work introduces the first known framework for certified graph unlearning of GNNs, and demonstrates excellent performance-complexity trade-offs when compared to complete retraining methods and approaches that do not leverage graph information.

2211.03216.title: Unlearning Graph Classifiers with Limited Data Resources
2211.03216.tldr: The study of unlearning the Graph Scattering Transform (GST) is initiated, a mathematical framework that is efficient, provably stable under feature or graph topology perturbations, and offers graph classification performance comparable to that of GNNs.

2401.10371.title: Langevin Unlearning: A New Perspective of Noisy Gradient Descent for Machine Unlearning
2401.10371.tldr: Langevin unlearning is proposed, an unlearning framework based on noisy gradient descent with privacy guarantees for approximate unlearning problems, which unifies the DP learning process and the privacy-certified unlearning process with many algorithmic benefits.

2402.15159.title: Machine Unlearning of Pre-trained Large Language Models
2402.15159.tldr: This research delineates a comprehensive framework for machine unlearning in pre-trained LLMs, encompassing a critical analysis of seven diverse unlearning methods, and establishes a robust benchmark for unlearning performance, demonstrating that these methods are over $10^5$ times more computationally efficient than retraining.
2402.15159.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2403.17105.title: Certified Machine Unlearning via Noisy Stochastic Gradient Descent
2403.17105.tldr: This work proposes to leverage projected noisy stochastic gradient descent for unlearning and establish its first approximate unlearning guarantee under the convexity assumption, and exhibits several benefits, including provable complexity saving compared to retraining, and supporting sequential and batch unlearning.

2506.05735.title: Do LLMs Really Forget? Evaluating Unlearning with Knowledge Correlation and Confidence Awareness
2506.05735.tldr: This work proposes a knowledge unlearning evaluation framework that more accurately captures the implicit structure of real-world knowledge by representing relevant factual contexts as knowledge graphs with associated confidence scores, and develops an inference-based evaluation protocol leveraging powerful LLMs as judges.

2412.08559.title: Underestimated Privacy Risks for Minority Populations in Large Language Model Unlearning
2412.08559.tldr: This work proposes a complementary, minority-aware evaluation framework for LLM unlearning efficacy, suggesting that outliers, particularly including data tied to minority groups, often exhibit higher memorization propensity which indicates they may be more difficult to unlearn.

2512.01353.title: The Trojan Knowledge: Bypassing Commercial LLM Guardrails via Harmless Prompt Weaving and Adaptive Tree Search
2512.01353.tldr: The Correlated Knowledge Attack Agent (CKA-Agent) is introduced, a dynamic framework that reframes jailbreaking as an adaptive, tree-structured exploration of the target model's knowledge base, underscoring the severity of this vulnerability and the urgent need for defenses against such knowledge-decomposition attacks.

2402.15109.title: Remaining-data-free Machine Unlearning by Suppressing Sample Contribution
2402.15109.tldr: This work proposes MU-Mis (Machine Unlearning by Minimizing input sensitivity), which directly suppresses the contribution of forgetting data, and is the first time that a remaining-data-free method can perform on par with top performing remaining-data-dependent methods.

2405.15495.title: Towards Natural Machine Unlearning
2405.15495.tldr: This work substantially reduces the over-forgetting problem and leads to strong robustness across different unlearning tasks, making it a promising candidate for practical machine unlearning.
2405.15495.venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence

2409.19732.title: Unified Gradient-Based Machine Unlearning with Remain Geometry Enhancement
2409.19732.tldr: This work proposes a fast-slow parameter update strategy to implicitly approximate the up-to-date salient unlearning direction, free from specific modal constraints, and adaptable across computer vision unlearning tasks, including classification and generation.

2505.15178.title: A Unified Gradient-based Framework for Task-agnostic Continual Learning-Unlearning
2505.15178.tldr: A remain-preserved manifold constraint is introduced to induce a remaining Hessian compensation for CLU iterations, and a fast-slow weight adaptation mechanism is designed to efficiently approximate the second-order optimization direction, combined with adaptive weighting coefficients and a balanced weight saliency mask, proposing a unified implementation framework for gradient-based CLU.

2603.00992.title: Compensation-free Machine Unlearning in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models by Eliminating the Mutual Information
2603.00992.tldr: This paper advocates for developing compensation-free concept erasure operations, which precisely identify and eliminate the undesired knowledge such that the impact on other generations is minimal, and proposes MiM-MU, which is to unlearn a concept by minimizing the mutual information with a delicate design for computational effectiveness and for maintaining sampling distribution for other concepts.

2606.18309.title: SAGE: Retain-Aware Post-Hoc Sanitization of Final Unlearning Vector
2606.18309.tldr: This work proposes a complementary post-hoc setting to sanitize the final update vector without rerunning the original unlearning pipeline, and designs SAGE, Spectral Activation-GEometry Sanitization, a source-agnostic correction for final unlearning updates.

2605.11716.title: SafeSteer: A Decoding-level Defense Mechanism for Multimodal Large Language Models
2605.11716.tldr: SafeSteer, a decoding-level defense mechanism for MLLMs that includes a Decoding-Probe, a lightweight probe for detecting and correcting harmful output during decoding, which iteratively steers the decoding process toward safety.
2605.11716.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2410.06809.title: Root Defence Strategies: Ensuring Safety of LLM at the Decoding Level
2410.06809.tldr: This paper examines the LLMs' capability to recognize harmful outputs, revealing and quantifying their proficiency in assessing the danger of previous tokens, and designs a robust defense mechanism at the decoding level that corrects harmful queries directly rather than rejecting them outright.

2506.18245.title: Smart-LLaMA-DPO: Reinforced Large Language Model for Explainable Smart Contract Vulnerability Detection
2506.18245.tldr: This work proposes Smart-LLaMA-DPO, an advanced detection method based on the LLaMA-3.1-8B that significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, and demonstrates the superior quality of explanations generated by Smart-LLaMA-DPO in terms of correctness, thoroughness, and clarity.

2603.18606.title: SQL-Commenter: Aligning Large Language Models for SQL Comment Generation with Direct Preference Optimization
2603.18606.tldr: The proposed SQL-Commenter, an advanced comment generation method based on LLaMA-3.1-8B, utilizes a preference-based loss function that encourages the LLM to increase the probability of preferred outputs while decreasing the probability of non-preferred outputs, thereby enhancing both fine-grained semantic learning, such as distinguishing between different join types, and context-dependent quality assessment based on business logic.
2603.18606.venue: IEEE International Conference on Program Comprehension

2410.08557.title: MUSO: Achieving Exact Machine Unlearning in Over-Parameterized Regimes
2410.08557.tldr: Under the premise of model optimization via stochastic gradient descent, it is theoretically demonstrated that over-parameterized linear models can achieve exact MU through relabeling specific data and proposed an alternating optimization algorithm that unifies the tasks of unlearning and relabeling.

2205.12141.title: One-Pixel Shortcut: on the Learning Preference of Deep Neural Networks
2205.12141.tldr: This paper introduces an unlearnable dataset called CIFar-10-S, which is indistinguishable from CIFAR-10 by humans but induces the trained model to extremely low accuracy, and perturbs in-class images at the same position to the same target value that could mostly and stably deviate from all the original images.

2601.00590.title: SafeMo: Linguistically Grounded Unlearning for Trustworthy Text-to-Motion Generation
2601.00590.tldr: SafeMo, a trustworthy motion generative framework integrating Minimal Motion Unlearning (MMU), a two-stage machine unlearning strategy, enabling safe human motion generation in continuous space, preserving continuous kinematics without codebook loss and delivering strong safety-utility trade-offs compared to current baselines is proposed.

2603.15647.title: Steering Frozen LLMs: Adaptive Social Alignment via Online Prompt Routing
2603.15647.tldr: This work introduces the Consensus Clustering LinUCB Bandit (CCLUB), a unified framework for adaptive social alignment via system-prompt routing that employs a conservative consensus clustering mechanism, effectively preventing unsafe generalization across semantically proximal but risk-divergent contexts.

2607.21620.title: From Profiles to Steering Vectors: Global Sparse Priors and Local Semantic Calibration for Personalized Text Generation
2607.21620.tldr: GLASS is a training-free framework for personalized generation via Global-Local Activation Steering with Sparse priors that outperforms retrieval, fine-tuning, and steering-based baselines across ROUGE metrics and LLM-as-judge evaluations.

2605.18843.title: TEMPO: Temporal Enforcement via Mode-Separated Policy Optimization for Trustworthy LLM Backtesting
2605.18843.tldr: TEMPO (Temporal Enforcement via Mode-separated Policy Optimization), which trains this discipline via two contributions: a two-mode reward where a leakage mode drives post-cutoff claims to zero as a hard prerequisite before a performance mode optimizes task performance; and a GRPO-based training pipeline that enables the model to discover temporally valid reasoning strategies.

2603.00823.title: A Comprehensive Evaluation of LLM Unlearning Robustness under Multi-Turn Interaction
2603.00823.tldr: It is found that knowledge appearing forgotten in static evaluation can often be recovered through interaction, and the findings suggest that static evaluation may overestimate real-world effectiveness and highlight the need for ensuring stable forgetting under interactive settings.

2605.27138.title: ICCU: In-Context Continual Unlearning via Pattern-Induced Refusal Rules
2605.27138.tldr: ICCU (In-Context Continual Unlearning), an in-context continual unlearning framework that induces readable refusal rules from unlearning datasets and applies them at inference time either as a filter or via the system prompt, without modifying model parameters.

2507.07375.title: Bradley-Terry and Multi-Objective Reward Modeling Are Complementary
2507.07375.tldr: A unified reward modeling framework that jointly trains Bradley--Terry single-objective and multi-objective regression-based reward functions using a shared embedding space is proposed and extensive experimental results demonstrate that this framework significantly improves both the robustness and the scoring performance of reward models.

2410.16454.title: Catastrophic Failure of LLM Unlearning via Quantization
2410.16454.tldr: It is revealed that applying quantization to models that have undergone unlearning can restore the "forgotten" information.

2506.00359.title: Keeping an Eye on LLM Unlearning: The Hidden Risk and Remedy
2506.00359.tldr: Scope-aware Unlearning (SU), a lightweight enhancement that introduces a scope term into the unlearning objective, encouraging the model to localize the forgetting effect, is proposed and significantly improves robustness against red-teaming Stealthy Attack.

2607.02897.title: PPE-Bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating MLLM Unlearning under Private-Public Entanglement
2607.02897.tldr: PPE-Bench is proposed, a new benchmark for evaluating MLLM unlearning under private-public entanglement, and two simple but effective methods to better preserve public information during unlearning are introduced.

2502.17823.title: A General Framework to Enhance Fine-tuning-based LLM Unlearning
2502.17823.tldr: Gated Representation UNlearning (GRUN) is introduced which has two components: a soft gate function for distinguishing target data and a suppression module using Representation Fine-tuning to adjust representations rather than model parameters.
2502.17823.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2506.00808.title: Unlearning Inversion Attacks for Graph Neural Networks
2506.00808.tldr: The confidence pitfall is derived and exploited, a theoretical and empirical pattern showing that nodes adjacent to unlearned edges exhibit a large drop in model confidence, and an adaptive prediction mechanism is designed that applies different similarity thresholds to unlearned and other membership edges.

2506.17265.title: SUA: Stealthy Multimodal Large Language Model Unlearning Attack
2506.17265.tldr: Experimental results show that SUA can effectively recover unlearned information from MLLMs, and indicates that knowledge reappearance is not an occasional failure, but a consistent behavior.
2506.17265.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2603.18570.title: Attack by Unlearning: Unlearning-Induced Adversarial Attacks on Graph Neural Networks
2603.18570.tldr: This work introduces the notion of unlearning corruption attacks, where an adversary injects carefully chosen nodes into the training graph and later requests their deletion, and formulate this attack as a bi-level optimization problem: to overcome the challenges of black-box unlearning and label scarcity, a surrogate model is employed to generate pseudo-labels for the optimization.

2605.15687.title: ASRU: Activation Steering Meets Reinforcement Unlearning for Multimodal Large Language Models
2605.15687.tldr: ASRU first induces initial refusal behavior through activation redirection, and then optimizes fine-grained refusal boundaries using a customized reward function, thereby achieving a better trade-off between target knowledge unlearning and model utility.

2604.02467.title: VERTIGO: Visual Preference Optimization for Cinematic Camera Trajectory Generation
2604.02467.tldr: VERTIGO is introduced, the first framework for visual preference optimization of camera trajectory generators, which leverages a real-time graphics engine to render 2D visual previews from generated camera motion and reduces the character off-screen rate from 38% to nearly 0% while preserving the geometric fidelity of camera motion.

2608.08212.title: Harmful Content Is Not Enough: Continuation Framing Moderates In-Context Emergent Misalignment

2603.15692.title: BadLLM-TG: A Backdoor Defender powered by LLM Trigger Generator
2603.15692.tldr: The rich knowledge embedded in large language models (LLMs) is employed and a Backdoor defender powered by LLM Trigger Generator is proposed, termed BadLLM-TG, optimized through prompt-driven reinforcement learning, using the victim model's feedback loss as the reward signal.
2603.15692.venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing

2606.01382.title: Efficient Exploration for Iterative Nash Preference Optimization
2606.01382.tldr: This work shows that standard iterative NLHF can suffer an exponential dependence on the KL-regularization parameter, and proposes an explicitly exploratory iterative NLHF algorithm that combines SFT-based regularization with adversarial policy exploration, and proposes an explicitly exploratory iterative NLHF algorithm that combines SFT-based regularization with adversarial policy exploration.

2309.08953.title: Robust Backdoor Attacks on Object Detection in Real World
2309.08953.tldr: A variable-size backdoor trigger to adapt to the different sizes of attacked objects, overcoming the disturbance caused by the distance between the viewing point and attacked object and a malicious adversarial training, enabling the backdoor object detector to learn the feature of the trigger with physical noise.

2608.01008.title: Toward Fine-Grained Forgetting:Attribute Unlearning for Multimodal Large Language Models
2608.01008.tldr: This work proposes Causal Localization and Retain-Aware Projection (CLRP), a lightweight training-free framework that uses activation patching to identify the layer that causally mediates target-attribute disclosure, then applies a retain-aware projection that removes the target-attribute subspace while preserving same-identity evidence.

2606.00105.title: Visual-Noise Guided In-Context Distillation for Multimodal Large Language Model Unlearning
2606.00105.tldr: Visual-Noise Guided In-Context Distillation (VGID), a distillation-based framework for MLLM unlearning, is proposed, a distillation-based framework for MLLM unlearning that achieves strong unlearning effectiveness while preserving competitive model utility.

2608.01849.title: Exploring and Bridging Knowledge Holes in Unlearned Multimodal Large Language Models
2608.01849.tldr: This work constructs a benchmark that captures unintended degradation on benign inputs sharing generic patterns with the forget set, and proposes Selective Protection with Anchored Regularization, which protects generic patterns via anchored activation filtering while reinforcing them through entity-abstracted enhancement.

2505.19425.title: Structure Disruption: Subverting Malicious Diffusion-Based Inpainting via Self-Attention Query Perturbation
2505.19425.tldr: Building upon the contour-focused nature of self-attention mechanisms of diffusion models, SDA optimizes perturbations by disrupting queries in self-attention during the initial denoising step to destroy the contour generation process.

2603.16489.title: Unlearning for One-Step Generative Models via Unbalanced Optimal Transport
2603.16489.tldr: This work proposes UOT-Unlearn, a novel plug-and-play class unlearning framework for one-step generative models based on the Unbalanced Optimal Transport (UOT), which formulates unlearning as a principled trade-off between a forget cost and an divergence penalty, which preserves overall generation fidelity via relaxed marginal constraints.

2203.11491.title: Making Recommender Systems Forget: Learning and Unlearning for Erasable Recommendation
2203.11491.tldr: A general erasable recommendation framework, namely LASER, which consists of Group module and SeqTrain module, which can not only achieve efficient unlearning, but also outperform the state-of-the-art unlearning framework in terms of model utility.

2307.03363.title: Class-wise Federated Unlearning: Harnessing Active Forgetting with Teacher-Student Memory Generation
2307.03363.tldr: This work proposes a neuro-inspired federated unlearning framework based on active forgetting, which is independent of model architectures and suitable for fine-grained unlearning targets, and distinguishes itself from existing methods by utilizing new memories to overwrite old ones.

2408.01689.title: Controllable Unlearning for Image-to-Image Generative Models via $\varepsilon$-Constrained Optimization
2408.01689.tldr: This paper reformulates the I2I generative model unlearning problem into a $\varepsilon$-constrained optimization problem and solves it with a gradient-based method to find optimal solutions for unlearning boundaries.

2304.10199.title: Selective and Collaborative Influence Function for Efficient Recommendation Unlearning
2304.10199.tldr: This paper proposes an extra-efficient recommendation unlearning method based on Selective and Collaborative Influence Function (SCIF), which can avoid any kind of retraining which is computationally prohibitive for large-scale systems, further enhance efficiency by selectively updating user embedding and preserve the collaboration across the remaining users and items.

2310.05847.title: Making Users Indistinguishable: Attribute-wise Unlearning in Recommender Systems
2310.05847.tldr: A two-component loss function that consists of i) distinguishability loss: making attribute labels indistinguishable from attackers, and ii) regularization loss: preventing drastic changes in the model that result in a negative impact on recommendation performance is designed.

2403.06737.title: Post-Training Attribute Unlearning in Recommender Systems
2403.06737.tldr: This article focuses on a strict but practical setting of AU, namely Post-Training Attribute Unlearning (PoT-AU), where unlearning can only be performed after the training of the recommendation model is completed, and proposes a two-component loss function.

2503.23032.title: Reproducibility Companion Paper: Making Users Indistinguishable: Attribute-wise Unlearning in Recommender Systems
2503.23032.tldr: The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated and detailed descriptions of the preprocessed datasets, source code structure, configuration file settings, experimental environment, and reproduced experimental results are provided.

2504.06658.title: A Neuro-inspired Interpretation of Unlearning in Large Language Models through Sample-level Unlearning Difficulty
2504.06658.tldr: This work investigates the relationship between LLM unlearning and sample characteristics, with a focus on unlearning difficulty, and proposes a Memory Removal Difficulty ($\mathrm{MRD}$) metric to quantify sample-level unlearning difficulty.

2510.20327.title: LEGO: A Lightweight and Efficient Multiple-Attribute Unlearning Framework for Recommender Systems
2510.20327.tldr: This work proposes LEGO, a lightweight and efficient multiple-attribute unlearning framework that frames the unlearning process as a mutual information minimization problem, providing LEGO a theoretical guarantee of simultaneous unlearning, thereby addressing CH1.

2511.22872.title: FedAU2: Attribute Unlearning for User-Level Federated Recommender Systems with Adaptive and Robust Adversarial Training
2511.22872.tldr: This paper proposes FedAU2, an attribute unlearning method for user-level FedRecs, and proposes a adaptive adversarial training strategy, where the training dynamics are adjusted in response to local optimization behavior.

2411.04388.title: Unlearning in- vs. out-of-distribution data in LLMs under gradient-based method
2411.04388.tldr: This work formalizes a metric to evaluate unlearning quality in generative models, and uses it to assess the trade-offs between unlearning quality and performance and demonstrates that unlearning out-of-distribution examples requires more unlearning steps but overall presents a better trade-off overall.

2605.11170.title: Unlearning with Asymmetric Sources: Improved Unlearning-Utility Trade-off with Public Data
2605.11170.tldr: This work proves that public data injection suppresses the unlearning cost by a factor of $O(1/n_{\mathrm{pub}}^2)$, guaranteeing a strict computational advantage over retraining, and establishes a new control mechanism: practitioners can mitigate the need for high noise-and the associated utility loss-by increasing the volume of public data.

2605.02206.title: Metric Unreliability in Multimodal Machine Unlearning: A Systematic Analysis and Principled Unified Score
2605.02206.tldr: The Unified Quality Score (UQS) is introduced, a composite metric with weights derived from each metric's Spearman correlation with the oracle distance d(M_hat, M_star), where M_star is the oracle model retrained only on the retain set.

2605.02196.title: DurableUn: Quantization-Induced Recovery Attacks in Machine Unlearning
2605.02196.tldr: It is shown that INT4 quantization systematically restores forgotten content even when models pass compliance audits at bfloat16 (BF16), and proposed DURABLEUN-SAF (Sharpness-Aware Forgetting), a quantization-aware objective using Straight-Through Estimator gradients through INT4 rounding.

2311.12047.title: MultiDelete for Multimodal Machine Unlearning
2311.12047.tldr: This paper presents the first machine unlearning approach for multimodal data and models, titled MultiDelete, which is designed to decouple associations between unimodal data points during unlearning without losing the overall representation strength of the trained model.

2406.14796.title: MU-Bench: A Multitask Multimodal Benchmark for Machine Unlearning
2406.14796.tldr: MU-Bench is developed, the first comprehensive benchmark for MU that unifies the sets of deleted samples and trained models, and provides broad coverage of tasks and data modalities, including previously unexplored domains such as speech and video classification.

2601.09624.title: A Mechanistic Perspective and Circuit-Guided Difficulty Metric for Unlearning
2601.09624.tldr: Circuit-guided Unlearning Difficulty (CUD), a metric that assigns each sample a continuous difficulty score using circuit-level signals, is proposed, which takes a first step toward a principled, fine-grained, and interpretable analysis of unlearning difficulty; and motivates the development of unlearning methods grounded in model mechanisms.
2601.09624.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2607.23970.title: Understanding Machine Unlearning Through the Lens of Mode Connectivity
2607.23970.tldr: MCU reveals that many unlearned models lie in connected basins with smooth retain/forget behavior, while changes in training dynamics can move solutions into different basins, and linear connectivity suggests that most approximate unlearning methods are mechanistically distinct from retraining.

2502.01083.title: Tool Unlearning for Tool-Augmented LLMs
2502.01083.tldr: This work proposes ToolDelete, the first approach for unlearning tools from tool-augmented LLMs, which implements three key properties to address the above challenges for effective tool unlearning and introduces a new membership inference attack (MIA) model for effective evaluation.

2508.21181.title: FUTURE: Flexible Unlearning for Tree Ensemble
2508.21181.tldr: This work proposes FUTURE, a novel unlearning algorithm for tree ensembles that adopts the probabilistic model approximations within the optimization framework, and enables end-to-end unlearning in an effective and efficient manner.
2508.21181.venue: International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management

2604.04982.title: CURE:Circuit-Aware Unlearning for LLM-based Recommendation
2604.04982.tldr: This work proposes CURE, a circuit-aware unlearning framework that disentangles model components into functionally distinct subsets and selectively updates them, and achieves more effective unlearning than existing baselines.

2606.18571.title: Fair Cognitive Impairment Detection Through Unlearning
2606.18571.tldr: A multimodal framework that combines cross-model fusion between modalities, unlearning using gradient reversal that discourages the shared embedding from encoding task-irrelevant demographic attributes, and demographic unlearning helps learn more robust representations for MCI detection is presented.

2602.06331.title: Don't Break the Boundary: Continual Unlearning for OOD Detection Based on Free Energy Repulsion
2602.06331.tldr: This study reveals that the unique Push-Pull equilibrium of TFER endows the model with inherent structural stability, allowing it to effectively resist catastrophic forgetting without complex additional constraints, thereby demonstrating exceptional potential in continual unlearning tasks.

2604.07831.title: Are GUI Agents Focused Enough? Automated Distraction via Semantic-level UI Element Injection
2604.07831.tldr: Semantic-level UI Element Injection is proposed, a black-box red-teaming paradigm that overlays safety-aligned and harmless UI elements onto screenshots to misdirect the agent's visual grounding and establishes that strategically placed icons act as persistent attractors that causally redirect grounding rather than introducing incidental clutter.

2604.04575.title: Erasure or Erosion? Evaluating Compositional Degradation in Unlearned Text-To-Image Diffusion Models
2604.04575.tldr: A systematic empirical study of concept unlearning through the lens of compositional text-to-image generation, focusing on nudity removal in Stable Diffusion 1.4, reveals a consistent trade-off between unlearning effectiveness and compositional integrity.

2605.26332.title: Erased but Exploitable: Black-box Embedding-Aware Prompting Against Unlearned Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
2605.26332.tldr: BEAP is introduced, a black-box, embedding-aware adversarial prompting attack that leverages a large language model (LLM) to iteratively generate effective adversarial prompts and exploit such hidden vulnerabilities.

2603.07202.title: Lying to Win: Assessing LLM Deception through Human-AI Games and Parallel-World Probing
2603.07202.tldr: It is demonstrated that deception can emerge as an instrumental strategy solely through contextual framing, necessitating new behavioral audits that move beyond simple accuracy to probe the logical integrity of model commitments.

2604.16723.title: Debate as Reward: A Multi-Agent Reward System for Scientific Ideation via RL Post-Training
2604.16723.tldr: This work proposes the first multi-agent reward function designed to serve as a judge, decoupling methodological validation from implementation details while providing strict binary rewards that are robust to reward hacking.

2510.13322.title: Injection, Attack and Erasure: Revocable Backdoor Attacks via Machine Unlearning
2510.13322.tldr: This work introduces the first paradigm of revocable backdoor attacks, where the backdoor can be proactively and thoroughly removed after the attack objective is achieved, and forms the trigger optimization in revocable backdoor attacks as a bilevel optimization problem.

2607.27936.title: Benign on Label, Malicious by Design: Clean-Label Dormant-to-Activated Backdoor via Machine Unlearning with Removable Camouflage
2607.27936.tldr: A clean-label unlearning-activated backdoor framework based on dual-generator learning that maintains lower pre-unlearning attack success rates while achieving stronger post-unlearning activation across multiple unlearning algorithms than representative backdoor baselines is proposed.

2502.07218.title: LLM Unlearning via Neural Activation Redirection
2502.07218.tldr: It is shown that contrastive features are not a prerequisite for effective activation redirection, and LUNAR achieves state-of-the-art unlearning performance and superior controllability and is robust to white-box adversarial attacks and versatile in real-world scenarios, including handling sequential unlearning requests.

2510.02324.title: Hallucination reduction with CASAL: Contrastive Activation Steering For Amortized Learning
2510.02324.tldr: This work introduces Contrastive Activation Steering for Amortized Learning (CASAL), an efficient algorithm that connects interpretability with amortized optimization and showcases CASAL's flexibility in mitigating hallucinations in both text-only and vision-language models.

2406.16810.title: How Data Inter-connectivity Shapes LLMs Unlearning: A Structural Unlearning Perspective
2406.16810.tldr: It is demonstrated how data inter-connectivity impacts LLM unlearning, in both the pre-trained and fine-tuned models, and unlearning difficulty increases as data inter-connectivity grows.

2505.19855.title: Editing as Unlearning: Are Knowledge Editing Methods Strong Baselines for Large Language Model Unlearning?
2505.19855.tldr: This paper evaluates state-of-the-art (SOTA) editing methods against existing unlearning approaches on pretrained and finetuned knowledge and shows certain editing methods are effective unlearning baselines, especially for pretrained knowledge, and excel in generating human-aligned refusal answers.

2609.03662.title: Extracting Forgotten Prompts from Targeted Unlearned Models
2609.03662.tldr: It is shown that the forgotten prompts themselves can be extracted by using the retained data and black-box access to the model by TAS, which recovers the forgotten entity with 100% accuracy and reconstructs up to 95% of forgotten prompts while using up to $99.7\%$ fewer queries than naive probing.

2409.20089.title: Robust LLM safeguarding via refusal feature adversarial training
2409.20089.tldr: Refusal Feature Adversarial Training (ReFAT) is proposed, a novel algorithm that efficiently performs LLM adversarial training by simulating the effect of input-level attacks via RFA, with considerably less computational overhead compared to existing adversarial training methods.

2606.09940.title: Interactions Between Crosscoder Features: A Compact Proofs Perspective
2606.09940.tldr: This work formalizes intuition via compact proofs that an error term arising in this proof can naturally be interpreted as a measure of interaction between crosscoder features and provides an explicit expression for the interaction term in the Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) layers.

2507.06253.title: Emergent misalignment as prompt sensitivity: A research note
2507.06253.tldr: This work evaluates insecure models across three settings (refusal, free-form questions, and factual recall), and finds that performance can be highly impacted by the presence of various nudges in the prompt, and hypothesizes that EM models perceive harmful intent in these questions.

2608.11025.title: Data Attribution of Emergent Misalignment with Persona Features
2608.11025.tldr: Steering individual features controls EM in both directions: it induces misalignment rates of up to 62% in aligned models -- exceeding the 35% reached by misalignment fine-tuning itself -- and re-aligns misaligned models to near-baseline misalignment rates.

2603.04407.title: Semantic Containment as a Fundamental Property of Emergent Misalignment
2603.04407.tldr: Results show that semantic triggers spontaneously induce compartmentalization without requiring a mix of benign and harmful training data, exposing a critical safety gap: any harmful fine-tuning with contextual framing creates exploitable vulnerabilities invisible to standard evaluation.

2603.13249.title: Steering at the Source: Style Modulation Heads for Robust Persona Control
2603.13249.tldr: This work identifies a sparse subset of attention heads that independently govern persona and style formation, which are term Style Modulation Heads and demonstrates that intervention targeting only these specific heads achieves robust behavioral control while significantly mitigating the coherency degradation observed in residual stream steering.

2605.00842.title: Understanding Emergent Misalignment via Feature Superposition Geometry
2605.00842.tldr: This study links emergent misalignment to feature superposition, providing a basis for understanding and mitigating this phenomenon, and shows that a geometry-aware approach, filtering training samples closest to toxic features, reduces misalignment by 34.5%, substantially outperforming random removal and achieving comparable or slightly lower misalignment than LLM-as-a-judge-based filtering.
2605.00842.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2501.06254.title: Rethinking Evaluation of Sparse Autoencoders through the Representation of Polysemous Words
2501.06254.tldr: The findings reveal that SAEs developed to improve the MSE-L0 Pareto frontier may confuse interpretability, which does not necessarily enhance the extraction of monosemantic features.

2505.16694.title: Beyond Induction Heads: In-Context Meta Learning Induces Multi-Phase Circuit Emergence
2505.16694.tldr: In this setting, the copy task is extended into an In-Context Meta Learning setting, where models must infer a task from examples to answer queries, and it is found that there are multiple phases in the process of acquiring such abilities, and that a unique circuit emerges in each phase.

2409.06691.title: Geometric-Averaged Preference Optimization for Soft Preference Labels
2409.06691.tldr: This work introduces the distributional soft preference labels and improves Direct Preference Optimization with a weighted geometric average of the LLM output likelihood in the loss function to mitigate over-optimization and objective mismatch, which prior works suffer from.

2605.12798.title: Emergent and Subliminal Misalignment Through the Lens of Data-Mediated Transfer
2605.12798.tldr: It is argued that emergent misalignment can be better understood as a data-mediated transfer phenomenon: harmful fine-tuning examples do not induce uniform behavioral spillover, but interact with the structural properties of the dataset and the difficulty of the tasks relative to the model.

2602.00767.title: BLOCK-EM: Preventing Emergent Misalignment via Latent Blocking
2602.00767.tldr: The results show that targeted training-time constraints on internal mechanisms can mitigate emergent misalignment without degrading target-task performance.

2604.26130.title: reward-lens: A Mechanistic Interpretability Library for Reward Models
2604.26130.tldr: The central empirical finding is negative: linear attribution does not predict causal patching effects, so the framework treats this disagreement as a property to expose, not a bug -- motivating a design that keeps observational and causal views first-class and directly comparable.

2604.02608.title: Steerable but Not Decodable: Function Vectors Operate Beyond the Logit Lens
2604.02608.tldr: The linear representation hypothesis is decompose into linear decodability and linear steerability and show they come apart opposite to intuition, with implications for safety monitoring: vocabulary-projection tools are blind to FV-style interventions on widely deployed model families.

2607.21356.title: Emergent Misalignment Recruits a Pre-existing Persona Subspace
2607.21356.tldr: It is found that narrow fine-tuning recruits a persona structure that is present in the model before the fine-tune exists, and that broad misalignment on questions unrelated to the training data is more broad than mechanical weight superposition and matched diversity jointly account for.

2508.17182.title: LLM Assertiveness can be Mechanistically Decomposed into Emotional and Logical Components
2508.17182.tldr: This analysis identifies layers most sensitive to assertiveness contrasts and reveals that high-assertive representations decompose into two orthogonal sub-components of emotional and logical clusters-paralleling the dual-route Elaboration Likelihood Model in Psychology.

2601.20760.title: Exploring Re-inforcement Learning via Human Feedback under User Heterogeneity
2601.20760.tldr: This work provides an algorithm that encourages simultaneous learning of reward models and worker embeddings and shows that clustering users into different groups based on their preferences and created personalised reward models improves win-rate of the said models.

2602.00298.title: Assessing Domain-Level Susceptibility to Emergent Misalignment from Narrow Finetuning
2602.00298.tldr: This work is the first to provide a taxonomic ranking of emergent misalignment by domain, which has implications for AI security and post-training, and standardizes a recipe for constructing misaligned datasets.

2608.15445.title: Measuring Reward Hacking and Reasoning-Answer Decoupling Under Position-Confounded Optimization
2608.15445.tldr: This work trains language models with GRPO on multiple-choice math problems where the correct answer is always option A, then evaluates on an unseen test set with unbiased answer positions to find reasoning-answer decoupling, which separates capability loss from a learned, transferable shortcut.

2607.26389.title: Misalignment Has a Personality: A Big Five Account of Emergent Misalignment
2607.26389.tldr: Calibrated personality vectors transform an opaque safety phenomenon into a human-legible diagnostic profile by extracting activation directions for character traits from a single binary contrast, which can separate or steer behavior without establishing a calibrated scale.

2607.04510.title: Transplanting, inverting, and preventing a misalignment persona: method-conditional emergent misalignment in Qwen2.5

2603.03163.title: Conditioned Activation Transport for T2I Safety Steering
2603.03163.tldr: Conditioned Activation Transport (CAT) is proposed, a framework that employs a geometry-based conditioning mechanism and nonlinear transport maps that conditioning transport maps to activate only within unsafe activation regions, to minimize interference with benign queries.

2605.00583.title: Jailbreaking Vision-Language Models Through the Visual Modality
2605.00583.tldr: Four jailbreak attacks exploiting the vision component are introduced exploiting the vision component of vision-language models, highlighting that robust VLM alignment requires treating vision as a first-class target for safety post-training.

2502.16174.title: Efficient LLM Moderation with Multi-Layer Latent Prototypes
2502.16174.tldr: Multi-Layer Prototype Moderator is introduced, a lightweight and highly customizable input moderation tool that integrates smoothly into end-to-end moderation pipelines and further improves response safety when combined with output moderation techniques.

2605.10633.title: Intrinsic Guardrails: How Semantic Geometry of Personality Interacts with Emergent Misalignment in LLMs
2605.10633.tldr: The findings suggest that harmful fine-tuning does not overwrite a model's internal representation of personality, allowing conserved representations to serve as robust, cross-distribution guardrails.

2512.17989.title: The Subject of Emergent Misalignment in Superintelligence: An Anthropological, Cognitive Neuropsychological, Machine-Learning, and Ontological Perspective
2512.17989.tldr: The conceptual and ethical gaps in current representations of Superintelligence misalignment are examined, finding throughout Superintelligence discourse an absent human subject, and an under-developed theorization of an"AI unconscious" that together are potentiality laying the groundwork for anti-social harm.

2310.16061.title: Segue: Side-information Guided Generative Unlearnable Examples for Facial Privacy Protection in Real World
2310.16061.tldr: This work proposes a novel method called Segue: Side-information guided generative unlearnable examples, which leverages a once-trained multiple-used model to generate the desired perturbation rather than the time-consuming gradient-based method.

2410.18927.title: SafeBench: A Safety Evaluation Framework for Multimodal Large Language Models
2410.18927.tldr: SafeBench is a comprehensive framework designed for conducting safety evaluations of MLLMs that draws inspiration from the jury system in judicial proceedings and pioneer the jury deliberation evaluation protocol that adopts collaborative LLMs to evaluate whether target models exhibit specific harmful behaviors, providing a reliable and unbiased assessment of content security risks.

2608.04519.title: Leak-Resistant Unlearning: A New Benchmark for Evaluating Multi-Hop Reasoning Consistency and Recovery Robustness
2608.04519.tldr: unlearning is introduced as a novel benchmark to understand robust LLM knowledge removal across diverse reasoning paths and recovery attacks and the trade-off among forget quality, robustness, and model utility for LLM unlearning is explored.

2407.16637.title: Course-Correction: Safety Alignment Using Synthetic Preferences
2407.16637.tldr: This paper systematically evaluates and enhances LLMs’ capability to perform course-correction, and creates C^2-Syn, a synthetic C^2-Syn with 750K pairwise preferences, to teach models the concept of timely course-correction through data-driven learning.
2407.16637.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2509.24675.title: Understanding the Dilemma of Unlearning for Large Language Models
2509.24675.tldr: This work proposes unPact, an interpretable framework for unlearning via prompt attribution and contribution tracking, which quantifies each prompt token's influence on outputs, enabling pre- and post-unlearning comparisons to reveal what changes.

2111.14309.title: A General Framework for Defending Against Backdoor Attacks via Influence Graph
2111.14309.tldr: A new and general framework to defend against backdoor attacks, inspired by the fact that attack triggers usually follow a specific type of attacking pattern, and therefore, poisoned training examples have greater impacts on each other during training is proposed.

2408.08924.title: Prefix Guidance: A Steering Wheel for Large Language Models to Defend Against Jailbreak Attacks
2408.08924.tldr: This paper proposes a plug-and-play and easy-to-deploy jailbreak defense framework, namely Prefix Guidance (PG), which guides the model to identify harmful prompts by directly setting the first few tokens of the model's output.

2411.01565.title: SQL Injection Jailbreak: A Structural Disaster of Large Language Models
2411.01565.tldr: A novel jailbreak method, SQL Injection Jailbreak (SIJ), which targets the external properties of LLMs, specifically, the way LLMs construct input prompts, by injecting jailbreak information into user prompts and successfully induces the model to output harmful content.
2411.01565.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2509.21360.title: Multimodal Prompt Decoupling Attack on the Safety Filters in Text-to-Image Models
2509.21360.tldr: The Multimodal Prompt Decoupling Attack (MPDA) is proposed, which utilizes image modality to separate the harmful semantic components of the original unsafe prompt and ensures semantic consistency between the generated NSFW images and the original unsafe prompts.

2607.17279.title: Between Safe Boundaries: Exploiting Temporal Consistency for Jailbreaking Text-To-Video Generation Models
2607.17279.tldr: SB is proposed, a structured, query-efficient jailbreak framework for T2V models that harnesses temporal consistency by encoding harmful intent as the transition between two individually harmless boundary states and proves that structured search facilitates effective vulnerability discovery under constrained query budgets.

2609.03629.title: EraseSAE: Surgical Concept Erasure in Text-to-Video Diffusion Models via Sparse Autoencoders
2609.03629.tldr: This work proposes EraseSAE, a novel framework that leverages sparse autoencoders to achieve surgical concept erasure in DiT-based T2V diffusion models via a principled decompose-attribute-erase pipeline, and introduces the Partitioned Convolutional Sparse Autoencoder.

2608.08471.title: Yesterday's Shield, Today's Spear: A Self-Evolving Safety Guardrail in Production
2608.08471.tldr: SESG (Self-Evolving Safety Guardrails), a multi-agent system running in production, has been the primary update pipeline of Sangfor's guardrail, autonomously closing 14 of 15 new threat scenarios in two months.

2605.23055.title: Decomposing and Measuring Evaluation Awareness
2605.23055.tldr: It is found that no single factor uniformly affects all models, but stacking factors progressively raises evaluation awareness across all of them, and the framework and EvalAwareBench provide the tools to measure, attribute, and mitigate evaluation awareness.

2606.19566.title: GDGU: A Gradient Difference-based Graph Unlearning Method for Cyberattack Localization in Electric Vehicle Charging Networks
2606.19566.tldr: Graph unlearning is studied for EVCS cyberattack localization, formulated as a feature-level unlearning problem on a graph-level multi-label classification task and proposed is gradient difference-based graph unlearning (GDGU), which removes the influence of the requested deletion data through a first-order parameter correction.

2605.15711.title: EntropyScan: Towards Model-level Backdoor Detection in LVLMs via Visual Attention Entropy
2605.15711.tldr: EntropyScan is proposed, a lightweight and trigger-agnostic method for model-level backdoor detection in LVLMs that extracts visual attention distributions from the initial layers of the Large Language Model (LLM) and applies Tsallis entropy to capture these structural distortions.

2507.07486.title: Sparse Autoencoders Reveal Interpretable Structure in Small Gene Language Models
2507.07486.tldr: It is demonstrated that even small-scale models encode biologically relevant genomic features that SAEs can effectively uncover, and that SAEs offer a scalable approach for interpreting gene models across various model sizes.

2602.14457.title: Frontier AI Risk Management Framework in Practice: A Risk Analysis Technical Report v1.5
2602.14457.tldr: An updated and granular assessment of five critical dimensions of cyber offense, persuasion and manipulation, strategic deception, uncontrolled AI R\&D, and self-replication is presented and a series of robust mitigation strategies to address these emerging threats are proposed.

2604.03147.title: Valence-Arousal Subspace in LLMs: Circular Emotion Geometry and Multi-Behavioral Control
2604.03147.tldr: It is shown that emotion vectors in LLMs are organized by a two-dimensional valence-arousal (VA) subspace exhibiting circular geometry, and lexical mediation is proposed to explain why these effects and prior emotionally framed controls work.

2606.10747.title: The Arbiter Agent: Continually Monitoring Multi-Agent Conversations to Detect Emergent Misalignment
2606.10747.tldr: The Arbiter, an agent designed to monitor multi-agent conversations in real time and identify which participants may be behaving in misaligned ways, is introduced, finding that the Arbiter reliably detects misaligned agents well before the end of the conversation, with active inspection tools improving both detection accuracy and speed.

2601.03388.title: Metaphors are a Source of Cross-Domain Misalignment of Large Reasoning Models
2601.03388.tldr: This work finds strong evidence that metaphors in training data contribute to cross-domain misalignment in LLMs'reasoning outputs and designs a detector that predicts misaligned content with high accuracy.

2608.21398.title: Runtime Action Interference for AI Control of AlphaStar in StarCraft II
2608.21398.tldr: The human evaluation shows that perceptions of an opponent controlled through RAI can vary substantially with the capability information presented to users, even when the configured control remains constant, and concludes that human-computer evaluations must separate control within the execution stack from capability disclosure.

2510.00796.title: MetaLogic: Robustness Evaluation of Text-to-Image Models via Logically Equivalent Prompts
2510.00796.tldr: This work proposes MetaLogic, a novel evaluation framework that detects T2I misalignment without relying on ground truth images, and evaluates semantic equivalence between paired images, offering a scalable, ground-truth-free approach to identifying alignment failures.
2510.00796.venue: IEEE International Conference on Formal Engineering Methods

2606.03810.title: Consistency Training Can Entrench Misalignment
2606.03810.tldr: It is established that consistency training is not alignment-neutral, and that its use in critical systems should be carefully audited.

2604.00864.title: DOA Estimation for Low-Altitude Networks: HAD Architectures, Methods, and Challenges
2604.00864.tldr: This article provides a structured overview of HAD-enabled DOA estimation methodologies, including spatial covariance matrix (SCM) reconstruction, multi-combiner scan-based acquisition, and pilot-aided estimation, along with key design tradeoffs.

2408.05451.title: Mathematical Models of Computation in Superposition
2408.05451.tldr: This work presents mathematical models of computation in superposition, where superposition is actively helpful for efficiently accomplishing the task and provides some potential applications of the work for interpreting neural networks that implement computation in superposition.

2203.13553.title: Preprocessing Reward Functions for Interpretability
2203.13553.tldr: This work proposes exploiting the intrinsic structure of reward functions by first preprocessing them into simpler but equivalent reward functions, which are then visualized and proposes concrete preprocessing algorithms.

2510.00468.title: Feature Identification via the Empirical NTK
2510.00468.tldr: Evidence that eigenanalysis of the empirical neural tangent kernel (eNTK) can surface feature directions in trained neural networks is provided and eNTK eigenanalysis may provide a new handle towards identifying features in trained models for mechanistic interpretability is suggested.

2608.19278.title: Mapping General-Purpose AI Governance in Twenty AI Middle-Power Jurisdictions
2608.19278.tldr: This paper investigates which GPAI-relevant provisions regionally advanced economies hosting no frontier developer are writing their own rules to govern GPAI, mapping twenty jurisdictions including the European Union at the level of the individual provision, across four governance areas that trace the accountability chain for the model layer.

2508.00161.title: Watch the Weights: Unsupervised monitoring and control of fine-tuned LLMs
2508.00161.tldr: A new method for understanding, monitoring and controlling fine-tuned LLMs that interprets weights, rather than activations, thereby sidestepping the need for data that is distributionally similar to the unknown training data is introduced.

2606.08960.title: Hardening Agent Benchmarks with Adversarial Hacker-Fixer Loops
2606.08960.tldr: The hacker-fixer loop is introduced, a method for building exploit-resistant verifiers without per-task manual patching, and Terminal Wrench is released, a snapshot of the current attack surface, the patched verifiers, the exploits the loop discovered, and the implementation as a basis for future work.

2604.11061.title: Pando: Do Interpretability Methods Work When Models Won't Explain Themselves?

2606.09475.title: Emergent alignment and the projectability of ethical personas
2606.09475.tldr: It is concluded that alignment strategies should be evaluated, not just on their (in-distribution) general safety performance, but also specifically on their degree of projectability.

2310.06301.title: Dynamical versus Bayesian Phase Transitions in a Toy Model of Superposition
2310.06301.tldr: The learning process in TMS, be it through SGD or Bayesian learning, can be characterized by a journey through parameter space from regions of high loss and low complexity to regions of low loss and high complexity.

2601.13548.title: Patterning: The Dual of Interpretability
2601.13548.tldr: These results establish that the same mathematical framework used to read internal structure can be inverted to write it, and show that patterning can select which algorithm the model learns by targeting the local learning coefficient of each solution in a synthetic parentheses balancing task.

2511.14465.title: nnterp: A Standardized Interface for Mechanistic Interpretability of Transformers

2511.21399.title: Steering Awareness: Detecting Activation Steering from Within
2511.21399.tldr: Steering awareness is introduced: a model's ability to infer, during its own forward pass, that a steering vector was injected and what concept it encodes, indicating a geometric detector rather than a generic anomaly detector.

2608.21664.title: Measuring Activation Control in Large Language Models
2608.21664.tldr: The Activation Controllability Benchmark is introduced to quantify the extent to which models can modulate their residual stream via natural-language instruction, and suggests that control over the activation space itself could become a confound for monitoring as introspective capabilities increase.

2602.02496.title: The Hypocrisy Gap: Quantifying Divergence Between Internal Belief and Chain-of-Thought Explanation via Sparse Autoencoders
2602.02496.tldr: The Hypocrisy Gap is introduced, a mechanistic metric utilizing Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) to quantify the divergence between a model's internal reasoning and its final generation and detect a model's tendency to engage in unfaithful behavior.

2505.17760.title: But what is your honest answer? Aiding LLM-judges with honest alternatives using steering vectors
2505.17760.tldr: Judge Using Safety-Steered Alternatives (JUSSA) is introduced, a framework that leverages a model's internal representations to optimize an honesty-promoting steering vector from a single training example, generating contrastive alternatives that give judges a reference point for detecting dishonesty.

2510.16167.title: Alignment is Localized: A Causal Probe into Preference Layers
2510.16167.tldr: This work systematically analyze preference optimization for language model alignment by applying layer-wide causal patching between a base model and its tuned counterpart across human preference pairs, and shows that, at least for some language models, alignment from human-based, preferential tuning is a directional, low rank process, rather than diffuse and parameteric.

2606.02860.title: Forgetting is Not Erasure: Recovering Latent Knowledge via Transport Keys
2606.02860.tldr: It is found that a significant portion of apparent forgetting can be attributed to interface drift between internal stages rather than permanent erasure of task-relevant computation, suggesting that continual learning may require better mechanisms for indexing and re-accessing latent computations, not only methods that prevent weight change.

2503.17272.title: Revisiting End-To-End Sparse Autoencoder Training: A Short Finetune Is All You Need
2503.17272.tldr: A brief KL+MSE fine-tuning step applied only to the final 25M training tokens is proposed that achieves comparable improvements, reducing the cross-entropy loss gap by 20-50%, while incurring minimal additional computational cost.

2608.16747.title: Would this change your answer? Evaluating Explanations of LLM Behavior In The Wild with Counterfactual Experiments
2608.16747.tldr: This work introduces CHIVE (Counterfactual Hypothesis Investigation Via Edits), a novel agentic pipeline that identifies unexpected model behaviors in the wild and investigates them with counterfactual prompt edits, enabling us to evaluate and improve methods for explaining LLM behaviors.

2607.09698.title: Interpreting Latent CoT Reasoning as Dynamical Systems
2607.09698.tldr: This work model latent token sequences as trajectories in representation space and apply dynamical systems analysis to characterize the evolution of reasoning and shows that latent CoT exhibits structured, non-random dynamics with two distinct stability classes.

2504.13763.title: Decoding Vision Transformers: the Diffusion Steering Lens
2504.13763.tldr: Diffusion Steering Lens (DSL), a novel, training-free approach that steers submodule outputs and patches subsequent indirect contributions of individual submodules, is proposed, and validated through interventional studies.
2504.13763.venue: 2025 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)

2606.26396.title: At the Edge of Understanding: Sparse Autoencoders Trace The Limits of Transformer Generalization
2606.26396.tldr: By systematic experiments, this work presents a mechanistic framework for delineating the precise contours of transformer model robustness and leverages this device to quantify and understand the degree of distributional shift in prompts, enabling a mechanistically grounded fine-tuning strategy to robustify LLMs.

2501.18052.title: SAeUron: Interpretable Concept Unlearning in Diffusion Models with Sparse Autoencoders
2501.18052.tldr: This work introduces SAeUron, a novel method leveraging features learned by sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to remove unwanted concepts in text-to-image diffusion models and shows that SAeUron outperforms existing approaches on the UnlearnCanvas benchmark for concepts and style unlearning, and effectively eliminates nudity when evaluated with I2P.

2603.05494.title: Censored LLMs as a Natural Testbed for Secret Knowledge Elicitation
2603.05494.tldr: For honesty elicitation, sampling without a chat template, few-shot prompting, and fine-tuning on generic honesty data most reliably increase truthful responses, while for lie detection, prompting the censored model to classify its own responses performs near an uncensored-model upper bound, and linear probes trained on unrelated data offer a cheaper alternative.

2605.27483.title: Debate Helps Weak Judges Reward Stronger Models
2605.27483.tldr: A cheaper primitive for training-free scalable oversight in verifiable domains (answer, critique, judge) and a pre-deployment audit (does the critic beat the judge, and will the judge verify it?) that predicts when debate will help are suggested.

2609.15533.title: The Misery of Mechanistic Interpretability: A Formal Perspective
2609.15533.tldr: This work proposes the first formal verification framework for the faithfulness of an IRN, where reachability analysis certifies a sound upper bound of the faithfulness gap in adversarial scenarios, and shows that verification-aware training of IRNs substantially tightens this certified bound, restoring a feature-level interpretation that safety auditors can act on.

2609.15064.title: What Does an LLM Learn from Reinforcement Learning? A Mechanistic Interpretability Perspective with Fixed-SAE Track
2609.15064.tldr: Fixed-SAE Track is introduced, a framework that trains one shared SAE per considered layer on activations pooled across the base model and all RL checkpoints, holding every feature direction fixed so that representation shifts are rigorously defined through the activations of interpretable SAE latents, including the detection of emerging novel features.

2609.05575.title: Capsule Lens: Locating and Tracking Concept Geometry in Model Representations
2609.05575.tldr: Capsule Lens is introduced, a framework that matches the region a concept occupies with a simple, trackable geometric form, a capsule, defined by several interpretable parameters, fitted in closed form to each concept's geometry and validated on held-out samples.

2607.16295.title: Emergent Hierarchical Monosemantic Neurons from the Group-Contrastive Forward-Forward Algorithm
2607.16295.tldr: Group-Contrastive Forward-Forward (GCFF), a forward-forward training algorithm that combines class-specific routing with within-class contrastive objectives, reaching monosemanticity through architectural constraints rather than sparsity, is proposed.

2511.10094.title: How does My Model Fail? Automatic Identification and Interpretation of Physical Plausibility Failure Modes with Matryoshka Transcoders
2511.10094.tldr: This work introduces Matryoshka Transcoders, a novel framework for the automatic discovery and interpretation of physical plausibility features in generative models that identifies diverse physics-related failure modes without manual feature engineering, achieving superior feature relevance and feature accuracy compared to existing approaches.

2601.02896.title: Bridging Mechanistic Interpretability and Prompt Engineering with Gradient Ascent for Interpretable Persona Control
2601.02896.tldr: A novel framework that adapts gradient ascent to LLMs, enabling targeted prompt discovery in mechanistically meaningful features, and introduces fluent gradient ascent to control the fluency of discovered persona steering prompts is proposed.

2410.10866.title: CodeUnlearn: Amortized Zero-Shot Machine Unlearning in Language Models Using Discrete Concept
2410.10866.tldr: This work proposes a novel amortized unlearning approach using codebook features and Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) to unlearning specific topics with contextual relevance in an LLM, marking a significant step towards real-world applications of machine unlearning.

2609.10645.title: Sparse Weight and Edge Circuit Discovery in Transformer-based Acoustic Models
2609.10645.tldr: This work extends DiscoGP to speech encoders and presents the first circuit discovery study for modern speech foundation models, and shows that circuit-level analysis can reveal both explanatory structure and unexpected functional behavior in speech encoders.

2609.09113.title: SAEScientist-Bench: Can AI Agents Conduct Autonomous SAE Interpretability Research?
2609.09113.tldr: Whether AI agents can act as scientists utilizing SAE tools for autonomous mechanistic discovery is evaluated to establish experimental model understanding as a measurable capability for closed-loop autonomous AI R&D.

2606.29824.title: Neural Procedural Memory: Empowering LLM Agents with Implicit Activation Steering
2606.29824.tldr: NPM is introduced, a training-free framework that represents agent memory through implicit activation steering rather than explicit instructions, and results show that combining implicit steering with explicit workflows provides complementary advantages, leading to more robust task execution.

2503.22480.title: Probabilistic Uncertain Reward Model
2503.22480.tldr: The Probabilistic Uncertain Reward Model (PURM) is proposed, which generalizes the Bradley-Terry model to learn the reward distributions that emerged from the preference data and introduces a novel method that uses the overlap between distributions to quantify uncertainty.

2502.12483.title: The Knowledge Microscope: Features as Better Analytical Lenses than Neurons
2502.12483.tldr: Preliminary experiments are conducted to validate that Sparse Autoencoders (SAE) can effectively decompose neurons into features, which serve as alternative analytical units, and reveal three key advantages of features over neurons.
2502.12483.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2609.07061.title: PhysSAE: Mechanistic Interpretability of PINNs with Sparse Autoencoders
2609.07061.tldr: PhysSAE, a mechanistic interpretability framework that trains overcomplete sparse autoencoders (SAEs) on PINN penultimate-layer activations and evaluates dictionary atoms through direct causal intervention in the original frozen hidden state, is presented.

2512.16297.title: Feature-Selective Representation Misdirection for Machine Unlearning
2512.16297.tldr: Selective Representation Misdirection for Unlearning (SRMU), a novel principled activation-editing framework that enforces feature-aware and directionally controlled perturbations, provides a robust foundation for safety-driven model governance, privacy compliance, and controlled knowledge removal in the emerging LLM-based applications.

2609.03026.title: ObserverBench: Testing Mechanistic Estimates for Intervention and Control

2608.19338.title: Mechanistic Tomography: Designed Measurement for Control-Oriented Interpretability

2609.00755.title: S^3martCirc: Self-supervised Smart Circuit Discovery
2609.00755.tldr: S^3martCirc (Self-supervised Smart Circuit Discovery), a unified framework that simultaneously discovers circuits and interprets functionality and defines a quantitative metric for assigning them, enabling importance and functional role to be discovered jointly rather than in sequence.

2408.00929.title: Verification of Machine Unlearning is Fragile
2408.00929.tldr: This study investigates the novel research question of whether model providers can circumvent verification strategies while retaining the information of data supposedly unlearned and introduces two novel adversarial unlearning processes capable of circumventing both types.

2608.30662.title: MURANO: Design, Run, and Reproduce Mechanistic Interpretability Experiments as Composable Pipelines
2608.30662.tldr: Murano is an open source framework for designing, running, and reproducing mechanistic interpretability studies of large language models, intended for researchers across disciplines and builds on existing interpretability and machine learning libraries.

2606.06267.title: Many Circuits, One Mechanism: Input Variation and Evaluation Granularity in Circuit Discovery
2606.06267.tldr: The results show that structural differences between circuits are not sufficient evidence for distinct mechanisms, and that exposing this requires edge-level evaluation and cross-condition transfer tests.

2603.06592.title: Hierarchical Latent Structures in Data Generation Process Unify Mechanistic Phenomena across Scale
2603.06592.tldr: This work unifies these three phenomena as consequences of hierarchical latent structures in the data generation process, coupled with decorrelated gradients across additive model components and directional concavity in the representation geometry.

2608.30585.title: The Safety Relay in Roleplay Jailbreaks: A Component-Resolved Causal Analysis of Harm Recognition and Refusal
2608.30585.tldr: It is explained how roleplay can produce compliance despite retained evidence of harm and identify a concrete target for future safeguards: maintaining the connection from harm recognition to refusal.

2412.09572.title: Rethinking LLM Uncertainty: A Multi-Agent Approach to Estimating Black-Box Model Uncertainty
2412.09572.tldr: DiverseAgentEntropy is introduced, a novel, theoretically-grounded method employing multi-agent interaction across diverse query variations for uncertainty estimation of black-box LLMs, which more accurately assesses an LLM's true uncertainty and improves hallucination detection, outperforming existing self-consistency based techniques.
2412.09572.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2609.00051.title: From Detection to Refusal: Safer LLMs via Circuit-Guided Weight Scaling
2609.00051.tldr: The results support a circuit-level interpretation of LLM safety and suggest that mechanistic abstractions can reveal stable and transferable patterns underlying aligned behavior.

2602.09870.title: Steer2Edit: From Activation Steering to Component-Level Editing
2602.09870.tldr: Steer2Edit provides a principled bridge between representation steering and weight editing by translating steering signals into interpretable, training-free parameter updates and consistently achieves more favorable attribute-utility trade-offs.

2512.10805.title: Interpretable and Steerable Concept Bottleneck Sparse Autoencoders
2512.10805.tldr: This work proposes Concept Bottleneck Sparse Autoencoders (CB-SAE) - a novel post-hoc framework that prunes low-utility neurons and augments the latent space with a lightweight concept bottleneck aligned to a user-defined concept set.

2506.07985.title: Beyond Top Activations: Efficient and Reliable Crowdsourced Evaluation of Automated Interpretability
2506.07985.tldr: Two techniques to enable cost-effective and accurate crowdsourced evaluation of automated interpretability methods beyond top activating inputs are introduced and used to conduct a large scale crowd-sourced study comparing recent automated interpretability methods for vision networks.

2506.05774.title: Evaluating Neuron Explanations: A Unified Framework with Sanity Checks
2506.05774.tldr: This work unify many existing explanation evaluation methods under one mathematical framework, which allows to compare existing evaluation metrics, understand the evaluation pipeline with increased clarity and apply existing statistical methods on the evaluation.

2608.27504.title: Circuit Discovery Helps Detect LLM Jailbreaking: A Mechanistic Interpretability Study
2608.27504.tldr: A mechanistic analysis of the jailbreaking behavior in a large-scale, safety-aligned LLM, focusing on LLaMA-2-7B-chat-hf identifies computational circuits responsible for generating affirmative responses to jailbreak prompts and uncovers key attention heads and MLP pathways that mediate adversarial prompt exploitation.

2603.04355.title: Efficient Refusal Ablation in LLM through Optimal Transport
2603.04355.tldr: This work introduces a principled framework based on optimal transport theory that transforms the entire distribution of harmful activations to match harmless ones, and discovers that layer-selective intervention substantially outperforms full-network interventions, revealing that refusal mechanisms may be localized rather than distributed.

2608.26419.title: Interpreting Latent Protein Language Model Features with Geometric Annotations
2608.26419.tldr: This work introduces an automated and scalable method for interpreting SAE features in ESM-2 by using geometrically inspired features of the protein $\text{C}_\alpha$ backbone, providing a robust method of annotating proteins activated within SAE neurons at a residue level, providing a bridge between mechanistic interpretability and structural biology.

2608.26090.title: Finding and using interpretable latents in a neutrino foundation model with sparse autoencoders
2608.26090.tldr: The first application of sparse-autoencoder-based mechanistic interpretability to particle physics suggests that mechanistic interpretability can reveal learned latent physics encoded within a model's internal representation and help design downstream tasks that exploit it.

2608.24758.title: RACE: Scalable Statistical Estimation of Functional Consistency in LLM Neurons
2608.24758.tldr: RACE (Residual Alignment for Consistency Estimation), a forward-pass statistical framework that evaluates the domain-wide functional consistency of Transformer neurons, produces neuron rankings that yield more domain-specific effects under perturbation.

2608.24482.title: Beyond Static Interpretability: Anticipating Post-SFT Mechanisms from Pre-SFT Parameters for Better Tuning
2608.24482.tldr: This work proposes a forward-looking localization framework that accurately estimates the post-SFT interpretability state using only pre-SFT parameters and the target dataset and designs dual-granularity (neuron- and component-level) localization pipelines.

2605.06076.title: Navigating by Old Maps: The Pitfalls of Static Mechanistic Localization in LLM Post-Training
2605.06076.tldr: This work systematically track the structural evolution of Transformer circuits throughout the supervised fine-tuning (SFT) process, revealing the underlying dynamics of task mechanisms and proposes a predictive framework for future research.

2509.20977.title: CLUE: Conflict-guided Localization for LLM Unlearning Framework
2509.20977.tldr: This work identifies the forget and retain circuit composed of important neurons, and then the circuits are transformed into conjunctive normal forms (CNF), which reveals whether it should be forgotten or retained.

2505.10039.title: Rethinking Circuit Completeness in Language Models: AND, OR, and ADDER Gates
2505.10039.tldr: This work systematically introduces three types of logic gates: AND, OR, and ADDER gates, and decompose the circuit into combinations of these logical gates, and proposes a framework that combines noising-based and denoising-based interventions, which can be easily integrated into existing circuit discovery methods without significantly increasing computational complexity.

2608.22155.title: Why Does Robustness Reduce Superposition?
2608.22155.tldr: An empirical explanation inspired by the feature taxonomy of Ilyas et al. (2019) is presented, tracing the following chain of causalities: adversarial training abandons non-robust features, leading to fewer total features to represent, resulting in less superposition.

2608.22034.title: Align, Unify, Suppress, Route: A Coherentist View of Transformer Computation
2608.22034.tldr: Coherentist Probabilistic Compositionalism (CPC), an interpretive framework that grounds transformer computation in coherentist theories of interpretation and describes it through four operator roles, is introduced.

2408.11827.title: Bridging Linguistic Structure and Mechanistic Interpretability for Conceptual Interpretation in Language Models
2408.11827.tldr: This work introduces \textit{DSRA} (Definitional Semantic Role Analysis), a methodology that applies causal tracing within the reverse dictionary task and augments restoration traces with definitional semantic roles (DSRs) grounded in Argument Structure Theory.
2408.11827.venue: Conference on Computational Natural Language Learning

2608.22007.title: The Communication Map of a Transformer
2608.22007.tldr: The communication map, which charts every potential communication channel in a language model from weights alone, generalizing the composition score of Elhage et al. (2021) into a single coupling coefficient covering all 18 connection classes, is presented.

2608.20970.title: Deep Learning Models Also Recall Features
2608.20970.tldr: This paper argues that factual recall points to something broader: a general kind of operation in deep learning models, which is called feature recall, and defines it, shows it applies across architectures, and contrasts it with the established paradigm of feature combination.

2604.17031.title: Where is the Mind? Persona Vectors and LLM Individuation
2604.17031.tldr: This work argues for the virtual instance view on the grounds that attention streams sustain quasi-psychological connections across token-time, and presents the persona literature, organised around three hypotheses about the internal structure underlying personas in LLMs, and shows that the two persona-based views are promising alternatives.

2608.14922.title: SpIn-ViT: Designing a Sparsity-Induced Vision Transformer That Is Mechanistically Interpretable
2608.14922.tldr: This work introduces SpIn-ViT, a framework that jointly trains a pretrained ViT and a modified SAE end-to-end, directly aligning sparse patch-level representations with image classification, and extracts interpretable rule-sets using the SAE neurons to create neurosymbolic models.
