2608.13754.title: Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation
2608.13754.tldr: The filability criterion is given as a standalone protocol, and one of the seven documented discovery objectives does not execute at all on the library's own canonical task, and whether the conclusion holds at scale is untested.

2603.09988.title: Causally Grounded Mechanistic Interpretability for LLMs with Faithful Natural-Language Explanations
2603.09988.tldr: A pipeline is presented that bridges circuit-level analysis and natural language explanations by identifying causally important attention heads via activation patching, generating explanations using both template-based and LLM-based methods, and evaluating faithfulness using ERASER-style metrics adapted for circuit-level attribution.

2608.13474.title: Decoding Task Progress from VLA Representations
2608.13474.tldr: The results suggest that VLAs have rich, linearly readable internal representations of semantic quantities like task progress, and that learning to read these signals offers a lightweight, interpretable path toward monitoring deployed visuomotor policies.

2608.10172.title: Intrinsic Structure: Spectral Identifiability for Mechanistic Interpretability
2608.10172.tldr: The Koopman spectrum is an identifiable, model-intrinsic fingerprint with a stated error bar, not a legible decomposition, and the spectrum is recoverable from calibration samples at rate $M^{-1/2}$ up to permutation.

2512.22496.title: Hierarchical Pedagogical Oversight: A Multi-Agent Adversarial Framework for Reliable AI Tutoring
2512.22496.tldr: This work introduces Hierarchical Pedagogical Oversight (HPO), a framework that adapts structured adversarial synthesis to educational assessment, and establishes adversarial reasoning as a critical mechanism for deploying reliable, low-compute pedagogical oversight in resource-constrained environments.

2511.19218.title: Adversarial Attack-Defense Co-Evolution for LLM Safety Alignment via Tree-Group Dual-Aware Search and Optimization
2511.19218.tldr: Evaluations demonstrate that ACE-Safety (Adversarial Co-Evolution for LLM Safety) outperforms existing attack and defense approaches, and provides a feasible pathway for developing LLMs that can sustainably support responsible AI ecosystems.

2608.09095.title: Who Bridges Safety? Identifying and Targeting Cross-Lingual Shared Safety Pathways
2608.09095.tldr: This work identifies monolingual safety pathways and validate their impact on refusing harmful requests and proposes a pathways-targeted alignment method based on the cross-lingual shared safety pathways, which shows that updating only a small fraction of pathway parameters significantly improves safety in NHR languages while largely preserving the model's general capabilities.

2601.19231.title: LLMs Can Unlearn Refusal with Only 1,000 Benign Samples
2601.19231.tldr: The findings suggest that current safety alignment of Large Language Models may rely heavily on token sequence memorization rather than reasoning, motivating future work beyond simple refusal mechanisms.

2608.06969.title: Finding Usable Weight Mechanisms with Tiled SVD
2608.06969.tldr: This work proposes extracting mechanism mounts directly from linear sites by column-tiled SVD: each mount is a triple read as trigger, write, and strength, and evaluates mounts with a pre-registered suite judged on full-write energy lift rather than tile-local lift.

2608.06638.title: MI-MIDI: Mechanistic Interpretability of Text-to-MIDI Generation Models via Probing, Lenses and Steering
2608.06638.tldr: This work analyzes two public text-to-MIDI systems of contrasting design: the purpose-built encoder--decoder text2midi and MIDI-LLM, and provides a practical toolkit for tracing and controlling musical concepts in symbolic generators.

2605.08218.title: Deep Dreams Are Made of This: Visualizing Monosemantic Features in Diffusion Models

2602.11910.title: TADA! Tuning Audio Diffusion Models through Activation Steering
2602.11910.tldr: This work uses activation patching to demonstrate that recent audio diffusion architectures exhibit a semantic bottleneck, where a small, shared subset of consecutive attention layers controls distinct musical concepts, such as the presence of specific instruments, vocals, or genres.

2607.25459.title: Emergent Latent-State Computation under Stochastic Volatility
2607.25459.tldr: Stochastic volatility models provide a useful benchmark for mechanistic interpretability under noisy latent dynamics and partial observability, and output-head replacement shows that part of the degradation under noisy MSE training arises from readout misalignment rather than representation failure.

2605.30482.title: Discovering a Zeta Map Algorithm on Dyck Paths via Mechanistic Interpretability
2605.30482.tldr: A controlled example of AI-assisted mathematical discovery in which mechanistic interpretability turns model behavior into a precise, human-verifiable combinatorial algorithm is given.

2607.17770.title: Measuring Monosemanticity in Sparse Autoencoders via Latent Activation Coherence
2607.17770.tldr: The Tversky Monosemanticity Score (TMS) is introduced, a label-free metric that operationalizes monosemanticity as activation-set coherence of binarized SAE latents, and does not require external embedding encoders.

2607.16693.title: Are Arithmetic Heuristic Neurons Form-Invariant? A Mechanistic Analysis of Symbols, Text, and Code in LLMs
2607.16693.tldr: This work investigates whether arithmetic heuristic neurons are form-invariant across symbolic arithmetic, natural language word problems, and Python code in three Llama-3 models, and identifies arithmetic heuristic neurons using a two-stage pipeline combining attribution patching and activation patching.

2607.14943.title: Steering Robustness into World Action Models via Mechanistic Interpretability and Optimal Control
2607.14943.tldr: This work uses mechanistic interpretability to study how robustness-relevant perturbations are represented in WAM activation space and predicts strong steerability in the Cosmos-Policy and DiT4DiT models but weak steerability in LingBot-VA, consistent with steering intervention results.

2606.04775.title: Activation Steering of Video Generation Models via Reduced-Order Linear Optimal Control
2606.04775.tldr: The proposed Latent Activation Linear-Quadratic Regulator (LA-LQR), a reduced-order optimal control framework for minimally invasive T2V steering, provides theoretical bounds relating latent setpoint tracking to raw activation-space feature control, and empirically validate the fidelity of the reduced latent dynamics.

2604.19018.title: Local Linearity of LLMs Enables Activation Steering via Model-Based Linear Optimal Control
2604.19018.tldr: This work model LLM inference as a linear time-varying dynamical system and adapt the classical linear quadratic regulator to compute feedback controllers using layer-wise Jacobians, resulting in robust, fine-grained behavior control across models, scales, and tasks, surpassing baseline steering methods.

2607.14791.title: Transcoders for Investigating Deception in Language Models
2607.14791.tldr: The use of transcoders to analyse deceptive behaviour in language models is investigated and it is suggested that deception emerges from internal model mechanisms and highlights the potential of transcoders for behavioural monitoring and early detection of security vulnerabilities related to malicious behaviours in language models.

2607.08605.title: When Structured Sparse Autoencoders Learn Consistent Concepts Across Modalities
2607.08605.tldr: A Structured Sparse AutoEncoder that enforces concept consistency from both semantic and spatial perspectives in the visual modality is proposed and introduced, and enhances neuronal monosemanticity by this visual structural prior.

2509.20146.title: EchoBench: Benchmarking Sycophancy in Medical Large Vision-Language Models
2509.20146.tldr: EchoBench, a benchmark to systematically evaluate sycophancy in medical LVLMs, is introduced and it is shown that higher data quality/diversity and stronger domain knowledge reduce sycophancy without harming unbiased accuracy.

2607.08499.title: Cross-seed explainability using Procrustes-conditioned Joint End-to-end Top-K Sparse Autoencoders
2607.08499.tldr: A Procrustes-conditioned Joint End-to-end Top-K Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) for extracting cross-seed universal features from independently trained BERT models and confirms that high-universality features encode interpretable sociolinguistic patterns.

2607.08349.title: Certified Interventional Fidelity: Anytime-Valid, Adaptive Evaluation of Causal Claims in Mechanistic Interpretability
2607.08349.tldr: Certified Interventional Fidelity (CIF) is introduced, a statistical layer for interventional interpretability evaluations that certifies high-fidelity claims, shows when apparent method differences are not statistically supported, and makes sensitivity to the intervention distribution explicit.

2607.07316.title: Mechanistic Interpretability for Neural Networks: Circuits, Sparse Features and Symbolic Reasoning
2607.07316.tldr: This article offers a comprehensive overview of mechanistic interpretability, an emerging field that seeks to reverse-engineer the internal algorithms of modern neural networks, and explores methods for actively controlling and modifying model behavior through steering vectors and causal interventions.

2605.01555.title: Automated Interpretability and Feature Discovery in Language Models with Agents
2605.01555.tldr: An autonomous multiagent framework for mechanistic interpretability that automates both explaining and finding internal features in large language models is introduced, showing that agent-driven empirical loops yield sharper and more falsifiable explanations than one-shot labels.

2607.01336.title: Mechanistic Interpretability and Causal Feature Steering of Neural Quantum States via Sparse Autoencoders
2607.01336.tldr: This work presents a systematic approach to analyze the internal activations of NQS using sparse autoencoders, and demonstrates that NQS are not merely functional approximators, but encode rich, interpretable internal representations of physical information.

2607.00089.title: Representation as a Bottleneck for Mechanistic Interpretability: The Manifestation Unit Protocol

2606.30219.title: EvalSafetyGap: A Hybrid Survey and Conceptual Framework for LLM Evaluation-Safety Failures
2606.30219.tldr: EvalSafetyGap is introduced, a conceptual framework that unifies benchmark-validity and alignment-failure research as a shared proxy-target divergence problem under optimization pressure, formalized through a Goodhart-inspired Instability Decomposition and an Alignment Trilemma.

2606.28770.title: Mechanistic Personality Analysis of LLMs Steering Personality via Latent Feature Interventions
2606.28770.tldr: This work proposes a mechanistic interpretability approach that directly intervenes on the model's latent features and identifies latent directions in the residual stream corresponding to a target OCEAN trait using sparse autoencoders and contrastive activation analysis.

2606.23583.title: Evaluation Awareness Is Not One Capability: Evidence from Open Language Models
2606.23583.tldr: Because detectability, behavioral manifestation, and controllability vary independently, it is multivariate rather than a single number, so no single awareness score is a reliable proxy for deployment safety, so the benchmark illusion is called.

2509.19464.title: Evaluation-Aware Reinforcement Learning
2509.19464.tldr: Evaluated-Aware Reinforcement Learning is introduced, a general policy learning framework that considers evaluation accuracy at train-time, as opposed to standard post-hoc policy evaluation methods, and can be co-learned to mitigate this tradeoff.

2606.26523.title: Radical AI Interpretability
2606.26523.tldr: A framework for interpreting AI systems as agents is developed, drawing on the philosophical tradition of radical interpretation and the tools of mechanistic interpretability, to propose criteria on both representationalist and interpretationist approaches and tie each to tests current interpretability methods can carry out.

2606.24952.title: Perfect Detection, Failed Control: The Geometry of Knowing vs. Steering in Language Models

2603.18523.title: Counting Circuits: Mechanistic Interpretability of Visual Reasoning in Large Vision-Language Models
2603.18523.tldr: A lightweight intervention strategy is proposed that exploits simple and abundantly available synthetic images to fine-tune arbitrary pretrained LVLMs exclusively on counting, and not only enhances counting accuracy on in-distribution synthetic data, but also yields an average improvement on out-of-distribution counting benchmarks.

2510.10271.title: MetaBreak: Jailbreaking Online LLM Services via Special Token Manipulation
2510.10271.tldr: It is demonstrated that special tokens can be exploited to construct four attack primitives, with which malicious users can reliably bypass the internal safety alignment of online LLM services and circumvent state-of-the-art (SOTA) external content moderation systems simultaneously.
2510.10271.venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy

2605.31295.title: Latent Space Disentanglement via Activation Steering for Interpretable Attribute Control in Symbolic Music Generation
2605.31295.tldr: This paper investigates the mechanistic interpretability of the Multitrack Music Transformer and proposes a framework for deterministic attribute modulation without retraining to bridge this gap via inference-time activation steering.

2606.18538.title: Effects of sparsity and superposition on loss in simple autoencoders
2606.18538.tldr: The present work analyzes the mathematical basis for the occurrence and optimality of superposition, while rigorously corroborating some of their findings, and provides upper and lower bounds for the L2 reconstruction loss, tight in the very sparse regime, for power activation functions.

2606.16920.title: Demystifying Variance in Circuit Discovery of LLMs
2606.16920.tldr: It is demonstrated that CEAP, the new circuit discovery method that improves upon EAP-IG with a theoretical guarantee, can substantially lessen resampling variance and rephrasing variance, and shows that the magnitude of unfaithfulness is affected by selective contribution scaling, a neural mechanism that accounts for the extremely poor scores sometimes observed.

2605.28617.title: LACUNA: Safe Agents as Recursive Program Holes
2605.28617.tldr: A programming model for agents that closes this split between the runtime that drives the agent and the code the model writes while preserving safety, and expresses ReAct loops, sub-agents, skills, parallel decomposition, and multi-model planning as ordinary control flow.

2602.16400.title: Easy Data Unlearning Bench
2602.16400.tldr: This work introduces a unified and extensible benchmarking suite that simplifies the evaluation of unlearning algorithms using the KLoM (KL divergence of Margins) metric, and enables reproducible, scalable, and fair comparison across unlearning methods.

2606.16044.title: Circuit Tracing in Autoregressive Protein Language Models
2606.16044.tldr: ProGenMech is introduced, a mechanistic interpretability framework for generative protein language models that extends cross-layer transcoders (CLTs) to ProGen3, a sparse Mixture-of-Experts model trained for both causal generation and span infilling.

2602.12026.title: Protein Circuit Tracing via Cross-layer Transcoders
2602.12026.tldr: ProtoMech is introduced, a framework for discovering computational circuits in pLMs using cross-layer transcoders that learn sparse latent representations jointly across layers to capture the model's full computational circuitry.

2508.18567.title: Sparse Autoencoders for Low-$N$ Protein Function Prediction and Design
2508.18567.tldr: Evaluated SAEs trained on fine-tuned ESM2 embeddings across diverse fitness extrapolation and protein engineering tasks show that SAEs, with as few as 24 sequences, consistently outperform or compete with their ESM2 baselines in fitness prediction, indicating that their sparse latent space encodes compact and biologically meaningful representations that generalize more effectively from limited data.

2606.15796.title: DifFRACT: Diffusion Feature Reconstruction and Attribution for Circuit Tracing
2606.15796.tldr: This work trains timestep-conditioned transcoders that faithfully approximate the input-output behavior of MLP sublayers in FLUX and obtains exact feature-to-feature attribution and recover compact, interpretable circuits.

2606.15507.title: Frame-Conditioned Moral Computation in LLaMA 3.1-8B-Instruct: A Mechanistic Interpretability Audit of Ethical Reasoning
2606.15507.tldr: Behavioral audits of Large Language Models on moral prompts measure what the model says, not the internal computation producing it, and unify these as Frame-Conditioned Moral Computation: the prompt's surface vocabulary selects a feature manifold, and the moral conclusion is downstream of that selection.

2606.15036.title: Transformers Learn the Mestre-Nagao Heuristic
2606.15036.tldr: Techniques from mechanistic interpretability such as attention analysis, linear probing, activation patching, activation patching, logit attribution, and neuron-level circuit analysis are applied to reverse-engineer the algorithm the (centroid in function space) model learned.

2607.22595.title: xMIx: High-Performance Serving-Time Platform for Mechanistic Interpretability Apps

2606.12209.title: Interpretable enzyme function prediction via sparse autoencoder features of ESMC across the microbial protein universe
2606.12209.tldr: This work shows that ESMC-SAE features enable accurate and interpretable enzyme commission (EC) number prediction without task-specific training or GPU-intensive computation, and establishes a paradigm for enzyme function discovery in microbial dark matter: interpretable by design, scalable without GPU clusters, and applicable to the billions of proteins in the ESM Atlas.

2606.10080.title: VFUSE: Virulent Feature Understanding with Sparse autoEncoders
2606.10080.tldr: VFUSE is introduced, a mechanistic interpretability approach that trains SAEs on diffusiontransformer activations to audit protein models for hazard-aware features and identifies monosemantic features from the SAE that fire only on hazardous designs at up to AUROC 0.84.

2602.05183.title: Data-Centric Interpretability for LLM-based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
2602.05183.tldr: This work analyzes large-scale reinforcement learning training runs from the sophisticated environment of Full-Press Diplomacy by applying pretrained SAEs, alongside LLM-summarizer methods, and introduces Meta-Autointerp, a method for grouping SAE features into interpretable hypotheses about training dynamics.

2606.09287.title: Trajectory Geometry of Transformer Representations Across Layers
2606.09287.tldr: This work recast the transformer forward pass as a discrete population trajectory through a high-dimensional representation manifold, drawing on geometric tools from computational neuroscience, and argues that trajectory geometry constitutes a principled, probe-free lens for mechanistic interpretability.

2606.08236.title: Shared Semantics, Divergent Mechanisms: Unsupervised Feature Discovery by Aligning Semantics and Mechanisms
2606.08236.tldr: This work introduces distribution-level unsupervised feature discovery, which clusters sampled continuations using both semantic content and sequence-level mechanistic attributions, without manually specifying target outputs, for scalable audit of the mechanisms underlying a model's continuation distribution.

2603.06745.title: Enhancing Instruction Following of LLMs via Activation Steering with Dynamic Rejection
2603.06745.tldr: DIRECTER (Dynamic rejection steering), a novel steering method that dynamically modulates steering strength by scaling the KV cache without extra dataset, demonstrates its potential as a general mechanism for mitigating oversteering that is compatible with existing baselines.

2511.01375.title: Align to Misalign: Automatic LLM Jailbreak with Meta-Optimized LLM Judges
2511.01375.tldr: AMIS (Align to MISalign), a meta-optimization framework that jointly evolves jailbreak prompts and scoring templates through a bi-level structure, is introduced, which achieves state-of-the-art performance.

2606.09899.title: When Attribution Patching Lies: Diagnosis and a Second-Order Correction
2606.09899.tldr: This work characterize the source of this unreliability, demonstrating that the dominant error stems from the non-linearities in the downstream network rather than local curvature at the patched component.

2606.06664.title: Inside the Visual Mind: Neuroscience-Motivated Concept Circuits for Interpreting and Steering Vision Transformers
2606.06664.tldr: This work proposes ViSAE, a mechanistic interpretability toolbox for understanding ViT inner workings through concept circuits, and improves the worst-group accuracy on WaterBirds by 48.2%, outperforming existing methods by 23.8%.

2606.06333.title: Subspace-Aware Sparse Autoencoders for Effective Mechanistic Interpretability
2606.06333.tldr: Subspace-Aware Sparse Autoencoders (SASA), which replace single-vector decoders with learned decoder subspaces, enforce block sparsity via Top-$s$ group gating, and adapt each group's effective rank with a nuclear-norm regularizer are introduced.

2607.10517.title: Conditional Optimal Bridge for Riemannian Activation Steering
2607.10517.tldr: This formulation yields the first principled derivation of the log-density-ratio steering objective from a well-posed optimization problem, and consistently outperforms prior activation steering baselines while avoiding the OOD degradation commonly observed in existing methods.

2606.30899.title: Curvature-Guided Module Localization for Low-Rank Detoxification of Backdoored Large Language Models
2606.30899.tldr: A mechanistically guided weight-space repair framework that first localizes modules involved in propagating trigger-induced behavior using activation patching and Fisher/K-FAC curvature analysis, and then applies targeted low-rank repair to only the most influential modules is proposed.

2606.02061.title: Ablating Archetypes: The Stability of Archetypal SAEs is an Artifact of Initialization and Metric Design
2606.02061.tldr: This study supports the value of studying SAEs within the larger dictionary-learning tradition while showing that stability claims require trajectory diagnostics and initialization ablations, and identifies a preprocessing-dependent cosine geometry issue that complicates interpretation of endpoint stability metrics.

2606.01243.title: Unlocking the Black Box of Latent Reasoning: An Interpretability-Guided Approach to Intervention
2606.01243.tldr: This paper bridges the gap between mechanistic interpretability and actionable control by operationalizing interpretability insights into a suite of training-free, decode-time interventions that refine the latent reasoning process by imposing the identified geometric and semantic priors.
2606.01243.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2605.28896.title: Feature Geometry of LoRA Adapters: A Sparse Autoencoder Analysis of Representational Divergence in Fine-Tuned Language Models
2605.28896.tldr: Empirical evidence is provided that LoRA fine-tuning can induce feature structures that are not fully captured by pretrained interpretability dictionaries, with implications for mechanistic interpretability, adaptation analysis, and safety auditing of fine-tuned language models.

2605.27997.title: Where Does Toxicity Live? Mechanistic Localization and Targeted Suppression in Language Models
2605.27997.tldr: This work introduces Meow2X and TRNE, two complementary retraining-free frameworks that localize toxicity to specific layers and neurons by analyzing activation differentials between toxic and neutral prompts, then suppress them via inference-time scaling or minimal rank-one weight edits -- without any gradient descent.

2604.19260.title: Understanding the Mechanism of Altruism in Large Language Models
2604.19260.tldr: The mechanisms underlying LLM altruism are investigated using sparse autoencoders to enhance the understanding of artificial cognition by translating altruistic behaviors into identifiable network states and provide a framework for aligning LLM behavior with human values, thereby informing more transparent and value-aligned deployment.

2505.16146.title: Steering LVLMs via Sparse Autoencoder for Hallucination Mitigation
2505.16146.tldr: This work proposes Steering LVLMs via SAE Latent Directions (SSL), a plug-and-play method based on SAE-derived latent directions to mitigate hallucinations in LVLMs, and demonstrates that SSL significantly outperforms existing decoding approaches in mitigating hallucinations, while maintaining transferability across different model architectures with negligible additional time overhead.
2505.16146.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2605.26343.title: MechRL: Reinforcement Learning Agents Perform Circuit Discovery for Mechanistic Interpretability
2605.26343.tldr: This work frames the circuit discovery problem of GPT-2 small as a sequential decision problem over the computation graph of GPT-2 small, in which a policy removes edges until it reaches a compact subgraph that preserves the behaviour, guided by a faithfulness reward defined through causal intervention.

2605.25225.title: Transformer Field Theory: A Response-Theoretic Approach to Mechanistic Interpretability
2605.25225.tldr: This paper develops Transformer Field Theory: a response-theoretic framework in which the residual stream of a fixed forward pass is treated as a Transformer field over layer depth and token position, providing the forward mathematical basis for patch-site inference and cross-scale response transfer.

2605.06480.title: Patch-Effect Graph Kernels for LLM Interpretability
2605.06480.tldr: A framework that reframes mechanistic analysis as a graph machine-learning problem by representing activation-patching profiles as patch-effect graphs over model components is proposed, finding that patch-effect graphs preserve discriminative structural signals.

2605.23393.title: Every Component is a Lookup: Token Attribution and Composition from a Single Decomposition
2605.23393.tldr: Unpack is developed, a backward recursion that decomposes credit through both sublayers, producing interaction strengths between any two components, named end-to-end paths with K/Q/V composition labels, and per-token attribution, all from a single forward pass, without intervention, gradients, or auxiliary training.

2507.22928.title: How does Chain of Thought Think? Mechanistic Interpretability of Chain-of-Thought Reasoning with Sparse Autoencoding
2507.22928.tldr: The results indicate that CoT can induce more interpretable internal structures in high-capacity LLMs, validating its role as a structured prompting method.

2511.21514.title: Mechanistic Interpretability for Transformer-based Time Series Classification
2511.21514.tldr: This paper systematically probes the internal causal roles of individual attention heads and timesteps within transformer models, revealing causal structures within these models, and demonstrates the potential of sparse autoencoders for uncovering interpretable latent features.
2511.21514.venue: International Joint Conference on Computational Intelligence

2606.18389.title: Want Better Synthetic Data? Steer It: Activation Steering for Low-Resource Language Generation
2606.18389.tldr: This work investigates activation steering as an alternative for low-resource synthetic data generation and studies two steering strategies: Language Steering, which targets the linguistic identity of a language, and Quality Steering, which captures well-formedness by contrasting human-written and backtranslated text representations.

2605.23069.title: DFKI-MLT at SemEval-2026 TASK 7: Steering Multilingual Models Towards Cultural Knowledge
2605.23069.tldr: The DFKI-MLT system for SemEval-2026 Task 7 on cultural awareness is presented, where activation steering is applied to multilingual LLMs using language vectors extracted from parallel FLORES data.

2609.08410.title: Compositional Multilingual and Behavioral Attribute Steering

2605.23035.title: Sparse Autoencoders Map Brain-LLM Alignment onto Cortical Semantic Topography
2605.23035.tldr: This work decomposes GPT-2 XL and Llama-3.1-8B into 16K-32K interpretable features per layer, bridging sparse autoencoders from mechanistic interpretability with neural encoding models, and tests a novel cortical topography prediction: five semantic subcategories derived a priori from three independent neuroscience programs should map onto distinct brain regions.

2605.24033.title: Towards Verifiable Transformers: Solver-Checkable Circuit Explanations
2605.24033.tldr: Verifiable Transformers, a framework for turning task-localized circuits into bounded, solver-checkable claims: projected functional equivalence, task-relevant invariance, edge necessity, and robustness to continuous final-residual perturbations is introduced.

2605.21849.title: Geometry-Adaptive Explainer for Faithful Dictionary-Based Interpretability under Distribution Shift
2605.21849.tldr: The Geometry-Adaptive Explainer (GAE) is proposed, which realigns the explainer's dictionary with the OOD-active subspace while preserving the original feature structure, and proves that GAE improves over the unadapted ID explainer, with excess loss bounded quadratically by the second-moment shift.

2605.20607.title: Mechanistic Interpretability for Learning Assurance of a Vision-Based Landing System
2605.20607.tldr: This work delivers the first concrete piece of the representation-level evidence that EASA learning-assurance guidance demands, and points to mechanistic interpretability as a practical building block of future aviation safety cases.

2505.18441.title: DB-KSVD: Scalable Alternating Optimization for Disentangling High-Dimensional Embedding Spaces
2505.18441.tldr: This work proposes Double-Batch KSVD (DB-KSVD), a scalable dictionary learning algorithm that adapts the classic KSVD algorithm and suggests that SAEs do find strong solutions to the dictionary learning problem and traditional optimization approaches can be scaled to the required problem sizes.

2603.03291.title: One Bias After Another: Mechanistic Reward Shaping and Persistent Biases in Language Reward Models
2603.03291.tldr: This work categorizes RM failures as tractable or resistant to linear intervention and proposes a simple post-hoc intervention to mitigate low-complexity biases that arise from spurious correlations.

2605.27996.title: Reward Bias Substitution: Single-Axis Bias Mitigations Redirect Optimization Pressure

2605.17493.title: Beyond Linear Superposition: Discovering Climate Features in AI Weather Models with KAN-SAE
2605.17493.tldr: KAN-SAE is introduced, a sparse autoencoder whose encoder replaces the standard ReLU with learnable per-feature B-spline activations drawn from Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs), allowing each latent dimension to develop its own nonlinear gating profile.

2607.01951.title: Robust for the Wrong Reasons: The Representational Geometry of LLM Robustness to Science Skepticism
2607.01951.tldr: It is argued that behavioral evaluation alone cannot distinguish a model that resists skepticism because it understands the signal from one that only appears to resist because it fails to perceive it, and that robustness does not transfer: it attenuates across domains and can reverse, with myth-rebuttal weakening under skeptical pressure.

2605.17204.title: Event-Grounded Sparse Autoencoders for Vision-Language-Action Policies
2605.17204.tldr: Overall, event-grounded SAE analysis emerges as a practical starting point for behavior-anchored VLA interpretability, motivating future work on SAE features beyond action-aligned coordinates, finer-grained closed-loop evaluation, and safe interventions for high-stakes VLA deployments.

2605.15183.title: When Are Two Networks the Same? Tensor Similarity for Mechanistic Interpretability
2605.15183.tldr: A weight-based metric, tensor similarity, is introduced that captures global functional equivalence and accounts for cross-layer mechanisms using an efficient recursive algorithm and reduces measuring similarity and verifying faithfulness into a solved algebraic problem rather than one of empirical approximation.

2605.08934.title: From Mechanistic to Compositional Interpretability
2605.08934.tldr: This work introduces compositional interpretability, a category-theoretic framework grounded in the principles of compositionality and minimum description length, and derives a parsimony criterion under which syntactic compression theoretically guarantees more concise, human-aligned explanations.

2605.08891.title: Bilinear autoencoders find interpretable manifolds
2605.08891.tldr: This paper implements bilinear autoencoders with bilinear autoencoders, which decompose activations into low-rank quadratic forms, compose linearly in weight space, and admit input-independent geometric analysis to close the gap in what concepts quadratic latents can detect.

2605.14694.title: The Rate-Distortion-Polysemanticity Tradeoff in SAEs
2605.14694.tldr: It is shown that polysemanticity is a data problem that should be accounted for when addressing it at the architectural and optimization level when the data-generating process is unknown.

2605.14535.title: Exploring Geographic Relative Space in Large Language Models through Activation Patching
2605.14535.tldr: This extended abstract examines how LLMs process relative geographic space using activation patching, an emerging tool for mechanistic interpretability.

2505.03368.title: Geospatial Mechanistic Interpretability of Large Language Models
2505.03368.tldr: This chapter establishes a novel framework for the study of geospatial mechanistic interpretability - using spatial analysis to reverse engineer how LLMs handle geographical information, and uses spatial autocorrelation to show how features obtained for placenames display spatial patterns related to their geographic location and can be interpreted geospatially.

2605.14075.title: Rethinking Layer Relevance in Large Language Models Beyond Cosine Similarity
2605.14075.tldr: It is demonstrated that cosine similarity is a poor proxy for the actual performance degradation caused by layer removal, and a more robust metric is proposed for assessing layer relevance: the actual drop in model accuracy resulting from the removal of a layer.

2605.13922.title: XAI and Statistical Analysis for Reliable Intrusion Detection in the UAVIDS-2025 Dataset: From Tree to Hybrid and Tabular DNN Ensembles
2605.13922.tldr: The findings provide robust, reliable and explainable models for UAV intrusion detection, along with statistical insights, which capture and clarify the masked nature of the attacks, regarding the challenge of Density Support Intersection, between these attacks, in this dataset.
2605.13922.venue: International Conference on Computer, Information and Telecommunication Systems

2605.09881.title: Dissecting Jet-Tagger Through Mechanistic Interpretability
2605.09881.tldr: It is demonstrated that mechanistic interpretability methods developed for natural language models can be used for jet physics classifiers and indicate that gradient descent may rediscover physically meaningful aspects of jet tagging without supervision.

2505.01372.title: Evaluating Explanations: An Explanatory Virtues Framework for Mechanistic Interpretability -- The Strange Science Part I.ii

2505.00808.title: A Mathematical Philosophy of Explanations in Mechanistic Interpretability -- The Strange Science Part I.i
2505.00808.venue: AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society

2605.08853.title: Architecture, Not Scale: Circuit Localization in Large Language Models
2605.08853.tldr: It is shown that grouped query attention produces circuits that are far more concentrated and mechanistically stable than standard multi-head attention at comparable scales, suggesting that some architectural choices make large models more tractable to study and that interpretability difficulty is not a fixed consequence of model size.

2605.05653.title: Negative Before Positive: Asymmetric Valence Processing in Large Language Models
2605.05653.tldr: It is found that negative and positive valence are processed at different network depths, and activation patching and steering on open-source LLMs finds emotional valence in LLMs is localized, causal and steerable, making it a concrete target for interpretability-based oversight.

2602.06801.title: On the Non-Identifiability of Steering Vectors in Large Language Models
2602.06801.tldr: It is shown that under white-box single-layer access, steering vectors are fundamentally non-identifiable due to large equivalence classes of behaviorally indistinguishable interventions, and it is shown that non-identifiability is a robust geometric property that persists across diverse prompt distributions.

2605.08012.title: Position: Mechanistic Interpretability Must Disclose Identification Assumptions for Causal Claims

2511.03731.title: MimiTalk: Revolutionizing Qualitative Research with Dual-Agent AI
2511.03731.tldr: Results across studies indicate that MimiTalk reduces interview anxiety, maintains conversational coherence, and outperforms human interviews in information richness, coherence, and stability.

2605.07324.title: Activation Differences Reveal Backdoors: A Comparison of SAE Architectures
2605.07324.tldr: It is suggested that backdoors manifest as directional activation shifts rather than sparse feature activations, making difference-based representations fundamentally more effective for detection, and have important implications for AI safety monitoring and the development of interpretability tools for detecting model manipulation.

2509.00691.title: CE-Bench: Towards a Reliable Contrastive Evaluation Benchmark of Interpretability of Sparse Autoencoders
2509.00691.tldr: CE-Bench is introduced, a novel and lightweight contrastive evaluation benchmark for sparse autoencoders, built on a curated dataset of contrastive story pairs that reliably measures the interpretability of sparse autoencoders and aligns well with existing benchmarks without requiring an external LLM judge.
2509.00691.venue: Proceedings of the 8th BlackboxNLP Workshop: Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP

2605.06979.title: PLOT: Progressive Localization via Optimal Transport in Neural Causal Abstraction
2605.06979.tldr: PLOT (Progressive Localization via Optimal Transport), a transport-based framework that localizes causal variables from the output effect geometry of abstract and neural interventions, is introduced, providing an efficient localization engine for causal abstraction research at scale.

2605.06610.title: SoftSAE: Dynamic Top-K Selection for Adaptive Sparse Autoencoders
2605.06610.tldr: The proposed SoftSAE, a sparse autoencoder with a Dynamic Top-K selection mechanism, uses a differentiable Soft Top-K operator to learn an input-dependent sparsity level k, which allows the model to adjust the number of active features based on the complexity of each input.

2502.07587.title: SEMU: Singular Value Decomposition for Efficient Machine Unlearning
2502.07587.tldr: This work proposes Singular Value Decomposition for Efficient Machine Unlearning (SEMU), a novel approach designed to optimize MU in two key aspects that minimizes the number of model parameters that need to be modified, effectively removing unwanted knowledge while making only minimal changes to the model's weights.

2605.06494.title: From Token Lists to Graph Motifs: Weisfeiler-Lehman Analysis of Sparse Autoencoder Features
2605.06494.tldr: A graph-structured representation in which each SAE feature is modelled as a token co-occurrence graph, which recovers heuristic motif families (punctuation-heavy patterns, language and script clusters, and code-like templates) that are not recovered by clustering on decoder cosine similarity.

2605.31042.title: From Prompt Injection to Persistent Control: Defending Agentic Harness Against Trojan Backdoors
2605.31042.tldr: DASGuard is proposed, which scans control-like text in sensitive local files, traces its origin, and removes control content that does not originate from a trusted source in order to address multi-step trojan attacks in local agentic harnesses.

2605.03058.title: Neuron-Anchored Rule Extraction for Large Language Models via Contrastive Hierarchical Ablation
2605.03058.tldr: MechaRule is introduced, a pipeline that grounds rule extraction in LLM circuits by localizing sparse agonist activations whose ablation disrupts rule-related behavior, and spectral splits provide a rule-free fallback, whereas unfaithful splits degrade localization.
2605.03058.venue: Proceedings of the 32nd ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining V.2

2601.22012.title: Putting a Face to Forgetting: Continual Learning meets Mechanistic Interpretability
2601.22012.tldr: This work introduces a mechanistic framework that offers a geometric interpretation of catastrophic forgetting as the result of transformations to the encoding of individual features as the result of transformations to the encoding of individual features.

2605.00474.title: From Local to Global to Mechanistic: An iERF-Centered Unified Framework for Interpreting Vision Models
2605.00474.tldr: An iERF-centric framework that unifies local, global, and mechanistic interpretability around a single analysis unit: the pointwise feature vector paired with its instance-specific Effective Receptive Field (iERF), and introduces Concept-Anchored Feature Explanation (CAFE), which utilizes the iERF as a semantic label.
2605.00474.venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence

2509.00749.title: Causal Interpretation of Sparse Autoencoder Features in Vision
2509.00749.tldr: Causal Feature Explanation (CaFE), which leverages Effective Receptive Field, is proposed, which considers each activation of an SAE feature to be a target and applies input-attribution methods to identify the image patches that causally drive that activation.

2604.25866.title: Why Are Some Emotions Harder for LLMs? Uncovering the Causal Mechanisms of Emotion Inference via Sparse Autoencoders
2604.25866.tldr: This work systematically identifies causal sparse emotion features that drive emotion inference and analyzes their sparse causal organization within and across emotions, showing that some emotions, such as surprise and fear, rely on highly concentrated feature sets, whereas disgust exhibits a more distributed sparse causal organization.

2604.23719.title: AIPsy-Affect: A Keyword-Free Clinical Stimulus Battery for Mechanistic Interpretability of Emotion in Language Models
2604.23719.tldr: AIPsy-Affect is released, a 480-item clinical stimulus battery that removes the confound at the stimulus level that removes the confound at the stimulus level and is released openly under MIT license.

2603.22295.title: Whether, Not Which: Mechanistic Interpretability Reveals Dissociable Affect Reception and Emotion Categorization in LLMs

2604.22345.title: Preference Heads in Large Language Models: A Mechanistic Framework for Interpretable Personalization
2604.22345.tldr: This work introduces Differential Preference Steering (DPS), a training free framework that identifies Preference Heads through causal masking analysis and leverages them for controllable and interpretable personalization at inference time and provides a mechanistic explanation of where and how personalization emerges within transformer architectures.
2604.22345.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2604.12806.title: Interpretable Relational Inference with LLM-Guided Symbolic Dynamics Modeling
2604.12806.tldr: COSINE is proposed, a differentiable framework that jointly discovers interaction graphs and sparse symbolic dynamics and incorporates an outer-loop large language model that adaptively prunes and expands the hypothesis space using feedback from the inner optimization loop.

2604.10031.title: CoSToM:Causal-oriented Steering for Intrinsic Theory-of-Mind Alignment in Large Language Models
2604.10031.tldr: This work introduces CoSToM (Causal-oriented Steering for ToM alignment), a framework that transitions from mechanistic interpretation to active intervention and significantly enhances human-like social reasoning capabilities and downstream dialogue quality.
2604.10031.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2510.07884.title: Contrastive Weak-to-strong Generalization
2510.07884.tldr: This work proposes Contrastive Weak-to-Strong Generalization (ConG), a framework that employs contrastive decoding between pre- and post-alignment weak models to generate higher-quality samples and highlights the potential of ConG to advance weak-to-strong generalization and provide a promising pathway toward AGI.

2511.06048.title: Visual Exploration of Feature Relationships in Sparse Autoencoders with Curated Concepts
2511.06048.tldr: This work presents an interactive visualization system that combines topology-based visual encoding with dimensionality reduction to faithfully represent both local and global relationships among selected features and enables users to investigate SAE behavior through targeted, interpretable subsets.

2604.06256.title: Spectral Edge Dynamics Reveal Functional Modes of Learning
2604.06256.tldr: It is suggested that spectral edge dynamics identify low-dimensional functional subspaces governing learning, whose representation depends on the algebraic structure of the task.

2604.02685.title: Finding Belief Geometries with Sparse Autoencoders
2604.02685.tldr: A pipeline for discovering candidate simplex-structured subspaces in transformer representations is introduced, combining sparse autoencoders (SAEs), $k-subspace clustering of SAE features, and simplex fitting using AANet, and is validated on a transformer trained on a multipartite hidden Markov model with known belief-state geometry.

2603.26494.title: Entanglement as Memory: Mechanistic Interpretability of Quantum Language Models
2603.26494.tldr: This work introduces the first mechanistic interpretability study of quantum language models, combining causal gate ablation, entanglement tracking, and density-matrix interchange interventions on a controlled long-range dependency task and reveals a noise-expressivity tradeoff governing which learned strategies survive deployment.

2603.25052.title: Closing the Confidence-Faithfulness Gap in Large Language Models
2603.25052.tldr: A two-stage adaptive steering pipeline is introduced that reads the model's internal accuracy estimate and steers verbalized output to match it, substantially improving calibration alignment across all evaluated models.

2605.17144.title: Contrastive Conceptor Activation Steering (COAST): Unlocking Vision-Language-Action Models through Hidden States
2605.17144.tldr: The results suggest that current VLAs retain substantial task-relevant knowledge in their latent representations, and that the action expert's decoding bottleneck could be mitigated by steering its residual stream toward task-relevant subspaces.

2603.23301.title: Steering LLMs for Culturally Localized Generation
2603.23301.tldr: It is shown that CuE-based steering is complementary to black-box localization methods, offering gains when applied on top of prompt-augmented inputs, and suggests that models do benefit from better elicitation strategies, and don't necessarily lack long-tail knowledge representation, though this varies across cultures.

2603.23268.title: SafeSeek: Universal Attribution of Safety Circuits in Language Models
2603.23268.tldr: A unified safety interpretability framework that identifies functionally complete safety circuits in LLMs via optimization that introduces differentiable binary masks to extract multi-granular circuits through gradient descent on safety datasets, while integrates Safety Circuit Tuning to utilize these sparse circuits for efficient safety fine-tuning.

2509.21761.title: Backdoor Attribution: Elucidating and Controlling Backdoor in Language Models
2509.21761.tldr: This work pioneers the exploration of mechanistic interpretability in LLM backdoors, demonstrating a powerful method for backdoor control and revealing actionable insights for the community.

2509.24296.title: DiffuGuard: How Intrinsic Safety is Lost and Found in Diffusion Large Language Models
2509.24296.tldr: An in-depth analysis of dLLM vulnerabilities to jailbreak attacks across two distinct dimensions: intra-step and inter-step dynamics reveals a harmful bias inherent in the standard greedy remasking strategy and identifies a critical phenomenon the authors term Denoising-path Dependence.

2603.02635.title: SaFeR-ToolKit: Structured Reasoning via Virtual Tool Calling for Multimodal Safety
2603.02635.tldr: SaFeR-ToolKit formalizes safety decision-making as a checkable protocol that trains a single policy with a three-stage curriculum (SFT $\to$ DPO $\to$ GRPO), where GRPO directly supervises tool usage beyond answer-level feedback.

2603.26743.title: Steering Sparse Autoencoder Latents to Control Dynamic Head Pruning in Vision Transformers (Student Abstract)
2603.26743.tldr: Results show that sparse latent features enable class-specific control of dynamic pruning, effectively bridging pruning efficiency and mechanistic interpretability in ViTs.

2602.09784.title: Circuit Fingerprints: How Answer Tokens Encode Their Geometrical Path
2602.09784.tldr: This Circuit Fingerprint hypothesis enables circuit discovery without gradients or causal intervention -- recovering comparable structure to gradient-based methods through geometric alignment alone.

2603.20381.title: The production of meaning in the processing of natural language
2603.20381.tldr: This work explores the CHSH parameter---the metric associated with the inequality---across the inference parameter space of models spanning four orders of magnitude in scale and finds that the interquartile range of the $|S|$ distribution is completely orthogonal to all external benchmarks, while overall violation rate shows weak anticorrelation with all three benchmarks.

2603.18353.title: Interpretability without actionability: mechanistic methods cannot correct language model errors despite near-perfect internal representations
2603.18353.tldr: Current mechanistic interpretability methods cannot reliably translate internal knowledge into corrected outputs, with implications for AI safety frameworks that assume interpretability enables effective error correction.

2603.17624.title: Do Language Models Encode Semantic Relations? Probing and Sparse Feature Analysis
2603.17624.tldr: This work studies three models of increasing scale: Pythia-70M, GPT-2, and Llama 3.1 8B, focusing on four semantic relations: synonymy, antonymy, hypernymy, and hyponymy, and combines linear probing with mechanistic interpretability techniques to identify where and how reliably semantic relations are represented inside LLMs.
2603.17624.venue: International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation

2603.18056.title: Fundamental Limits of Neural Network Sparsification: Evidence from Catastrophic Interpretability Collapse
2603.18056.tldr: It is established that interpretability collapse under sparsification is intrinsic to the compression process rather than an artifact of any particular algorithm, training duration, or threshold choice, and the collapse pattern is robust across all tested threshold definitions.

2505.03530.title: A Multi-Level Causal Intervention Framework for Mechanistic Interpretability in Variational Autoencoders
2505.03530.tldr: This paper presents the first general-purpose multilevel causal intervention framework for mechanistic interpretability of VAEs, comprising four manipulation types: input manipulation, latent-space perturbation, activation patching, and causal mediation analysis.

2603.14923.title: Directional Routing in Transformers
2603.14923.tldr: Direction routing is introduced, a lightweight mechanism that gives each transformer attention head learned suppression directions controlled by a shared router, at 3.9% parameter cost, and becomes the model's dominant computational pathway.

2603.11142.title: Attention Gathers, MLPs Compose: A Causal Analysis of an Action-Outcome Circuit in VideoViT
2603.11142.tldr: The existence of this sophisticated circuit for representing complex outcomes, even within a model trained only for simple classification, highlights the potential for models to develop forms of 'hidden knowledge' beyond their explicit task, underscoring the need for mechanistic oversight for building genuinely Explainable and Trustworthy AI systems intended for deployment.

2603.10573.title: Implicit Statistical Inference in Transformers: Approximating Likelihood-Ratio Tests In-Context
2603.10573.tldr: It is suggested that ICL emerges from the construction of task-adaptive statistical estimators rather than simple similarity matching, and appears to adapt the point at which decisions become linearly decodable.

2605.05341.title: Feature Starvation as Geometric Instability in Sparse Autoencoders
2605.05341.tldr: Adapt elastic net SAEs (AEN-SAEs), a fully differentiable architecture grounded in classical sparse regression, are introduced, showing that AEN-SAEs mitigate feature starvation without auxiliary heuristics while maintaining competitive reconstruction abilities.

2603.09972.title: From Data Statistics to Feature Geometry: How Correlations Shape Superposition
2603.09972.tldr: BOWS, a controlled setting to encode binary bag-of-words representations of internet text in superposition, finds that when features are correlated, interference can be constructive rather than just noise to be filtered out, and is more prevalent in models trained with weight decay.

2603.10071.title: Dissecting Chronos: Sparse Autoencoders Reveal Causal Feature Hierarchies in Time Series Foundation Models
2603.10071.tldr: It is shown that mechanistic interpretability transfers effectively to TSFMs and that Chronos-T5 relies on abrupt-dynamics detection rather than periodic pattern recognition, demonstrating that mechanistic interpretability transfers effectively to TSFMs.

2505.17073.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of GPT-like Models on Summarization Tasks
2505.17073.tldr: This paper presents an interpretability framework for analyzing how GPT-like models adapt to summarization tasks, identifying specific layers and attention heads that undergo significant transformation and locating the summarization circuit within the model architecture.

2603.08234.title: The Struggle Between Continuation and Refusal: A Mechanistic Analysis of the Continuation-Triggered Jailbreak in LLMs
2603.08234.tldr: This work focuses on a continuation-triggered jailbreak phenomenon, whereby simply relocating a continuation-triggered instruction suffix can substantially increase jailbreak success rates and proposes Head Competition Steering (HCS), a mechanistically grounded inference-time strategy that explicitly leverages the competition between safety heads and continuation heads to suppress harmful generation.

2609.02168.title: FUSE: An Evaluating Framework for Dangerous Capabilities of LLMs
2609.02168.tldr: A modular framework that evaluates each model through three orthogonal pipelines under a unified protocol, aggregating results into a standardized dangerous-capability profile $\phi$, showing that scaling and alignment progress do not uniformly translate into safety.

2603.23517.title: Beyond Accuracy: Introducing a Symbolic-Mechanistic Approach to Interpretable Evaluation
2603.23517.tldr: This position paper argues for mechanism-aware evaluation that combines task-relevant symbolic rules with mechanistic interpretability, yielding algorithmic pass/fail scores that show exactly where models generalize versus exploit patterns.

2603.05228.title: The Geometric Inductive Bias of Grokking: Bypassing Phase Transitions via Architectural Topology
2603.05228.tldr: Together, these findings provide interventional evidence that architectural degrees of freedom substantially influence grokking, suggesting a predictive structural perspective on training dynamics.

2602.22968.title: Certified Circuits: Stability Guarantees for Mechanistic Circuits
2602.22968.tldr: Certified Circuits puts circuit discovery on formal ground by producing mechanistic explanations that are provably stable and better aligned with the target concept.

2606.07451.title: TEVI: Text-Conditioned Editing of Visual Representations via Sparse Autoencoders for Improved Vision-Language Alignment
2606.07451.tldr: This work proposes TEVI, a framework that uses captions as a signal for what to retain from image embeddings and uses sparse autoencoders to disentangle image embeddings and train a masking module to selectively reconstruct the embedding based on a given caption.

2504.12939.title: Disentangling Polysemantic Channels in Convolutional Neural Networks
2504.12939.tldr: This work proposes an algorithm to disentangle a specific kind of polysemantic channel into multiple channels, each responding to a single concept, restructures weights in a CNN, utilizing that different concepts within the same channel exhibit distinct activation patterns in the previous layer.
2504.12939.venue: 2025 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)

2602.21442.title: MINAR: Mechanistic Interpretability for Neural Algorithmic Reasoning
2602.21442.tldr: This work introduces Mechanistic Interpretability for Neural Algorithmic Reasoning (MINAR), an efficient circuit discovery toolbox that adapts attribution patching methods from mechanistic interpretability to the GNN setting and shows that MINAR recovers faithful neuron-level circuits from GNNs trained on algorithmic tasks.

2602.22253.title: AR&D: A Framework for Retrieving and Describing Concepts for Interpreting AudioLLMs
2602.22253.tldr: This work introduces the first mechanistic interpretability framework for AudioLLMs, leveraging sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to disentangle polysemantic activations into monosemantic features and provides a foundation for trustworthy deployment in high-stakes domains.
2602.22253.venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing

2602.19396.title: Hiding in Plain Text: Detecting Concealed Jailbreaks via Activation Disentanglement
2602.19396.tldr: This work introduces a self-supervised framework for disentangling semantic factor pairs in LLM activations at inference and proposes FrameShield, an anomaly detector operating on the framing representations that improves model-agnostic detection across multiple LLM families with minimal computational overhead.

2602.16980.title: Discovering Universal Activation Directions for PII Leakage in Language Models
2602.16980.tldr: UniLeak is presented, a mechanistic-interpretability framework that identifies universal activation directions: latent directions in a model's residual stream whose linear addition at inference time consistently increases the likelihood of generating PII across prompts.

2602.16977.title: Fail-Closed Alignment for Large Language Models
2602.16977.tldr: The authors' mechanistic analyses confirm that models trained with the proposed fail-closed alignment framework encode multiple, causally independent refusal directions that prompt-based jailbreaks cannot suppress simultaneously, providing empirical support for fail-closed alignment as a principled foundation for robust LLM safety.

2602.16823.title: Formal Mechanistic Interpretability: Automated Circuit Discovery with Provable Guarantees
2602.16823.tldr: This work leverage recent advances in neural network verification to propose a suite of automated algorithms that yield circuits with provable guarantees, focusing on three types of guarantees: *input domain robustness*, ensuring the circuit agrees with the model across a continuous input region; *robust patching*, certifying circuit alignment under continuous patching perturbations; and *minimality*, formalizing and capturing a wide array of various notions of succinctness.

2602.16740.title: Quantifying LLM Attention-Head Stability: Implications for Circuit Universality
2602.16740.tldr: The cross-instance robustness of circuits is established as an essential yet underappreciated prerequisite for scalable oversight, drawing contours around possible white-box monitorability of AI systems.

2602.13483.title: Finding Interpretable Prompt-Specific Circuits in Language Models
2602.13483.tldr: This work introduces ACC++, an improved circuit-tracing method based on the principle of attention-causal communication (ACC), and uses ACC++'s interpretable circuits to characterize the sensitivity of indirect object identification (IOI) circuits to prompt structure.

2602.11091.title: Can Large Language Models Make Everyone Happy?
2602.11091.tldr: The MisAlign-Profile is introduced, a unified benchmark for measuring misalignment trade-offs inspired by mechanistic profiling, and general-purpose, fine-tuned, and open-weight LLMs are benchmarked on MISALIGNTRADE, revealing 12%-34% misalignment trade-offs across dimensions.

2602.11180.title: Mechanistic Interpretability for Large Language Model Alignment: Progress, Challenges, and Future Directions
2602.11180.tldr: This paper surveys recent progress in mechanistic interpretability techniques applied to LLM alignment, examining methods ranging from circuit discovery to feature visualization, activation steering, and causal intervention and proposes future research directions focusing on automated interpretability, cross-model generalization of circuits, and the development of interpretability-driven alignment techniques that can scale to frontier models.

2603.27518.title: Over-Refusal and Representation Subspaces: A Mechanistic Analysis of Task-Conditioned Refusal in Aligned LLMs
2603.27518.tldr: It is shown that harmful-refusal directions are task-agnostic and can be captured by a single global vector, whereas over-refusal directions are task-dependent: they reside within the benign task-representation clusters, vary across tasks, and span a higher-dimensional subspace.

2510.25179.title: Agentic Moderation: Multi-Agent Design for Safer Vision-Language Models
2510.25179.tldr: This work introduces Agentic Moderation, a model-agnostic framework that leverages specialized agents to defend multimodality models against jailbreak attacks and provides modular, scalable, and fine-grained safety enforcement, highlighting the potential of agentic systems as a foundation for automated safety governance.

2602.07381.title: When the Model Said 'No Comment', We Knew Helpfulness Was Dead, Honesty Was Alive, and Safety Was Terrified
2602.07381.tldr: AlignX, a two-stage framework that uses prompt-injected fine-tuning to extract axis-specific task features, mitigating catastrophic forgetting, and a MoCaE module that calibrates expert routing using fractal and natural geometry, improving inference reliability is proposed.
2602.07381.venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2609.03887.title: Beyond Shallow Alignment: How Post-Training Methods Determine Refusal Circuits And Steering Robustness
2609.03887.tldr: No post-training method achieves all three properties the authors would want from safe alignment at once: refusal that isn't concentrated in a few fragile components, safety gains that don't cost general capability, and safety behavior correctable through small, targeted edits.

2601.17642.title: Health-ORSC-Bench: A Benchmark for Measuring Over-Refusal and Safety Completion in Health Context
2601.17642.tldr: Health-ORSC-Bench provides a rigorous standard for calibrating the next generation of medical AI assistants toward nuanced, safe, and helpful completions, and facilitates reproducible evaluation, encourages safety calibration, and supports development of clinically reliable, context-aware, human-aligned medical AI systems.
2601.17642.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2509.22510.title: We Think, Therefore We Align LLMs to Helpful, Harmless and Honest Before They Go Wrong
2509.22510.tldr: Adaptive Multi-Branch Steering (AMBS), a two-stage framework in a 1-to-N Transformer setting that parameterizes objective-specific transformations relative to a shared representation, is proposed.

2602.10437.title: Control Reinforcement Learning: Interpretable Token-Level Steering of LLMs via Sparse Autoencoder Features
2602.10437.tldr: Control Reinforcement Learning is introduced, which trains a policy to select SAE features for steering at each token, producing interpretable intervention logs that establish learned feature steering as a mechanistic interpretability tool that complements static feature analysis with dynamic intervention probes.

2607.20596.title: Are Single-Token Sparse Autoencoder Features Causally Necessary? Layer-Depth and SAE-Family Effects
2607.20596.tldr: This work analyzesparse autoencoder features across six models and three SAE families and zero-ablate at full layer depth, finding cross-family claims are sensitive to training methodology, not just activation function or scale.

2508.12535.title: CorrSteer: Generation-Time LLM Steering via Correlated Sparse Autoencoder Features
2508.12535.tldr: CorrSteer is established, which selects features by correlating sample correctness with SAE activations from generated tokens at inference time to extract more relevant features, thereby reducing spurious correlations.

2506.17673.title: FaithfulSAE: Towards Capturing Faithful Features with Sparse Autoencoders without External Dataset Dependencies
2506.17673.tldr: FaithfulSAE, a method that trains SAEs on the model's own synthetic dataset, eliminates the dependency on external datasets, advancing interpretability by better capturing model-internal features while highlighting the often neglected importance of SAE training datasets.

2602.06852.title: The Quantum Sieve Tracer: A Hybrid Framework for Layer-Wise Activation Tracing in Large Language Models
2602.06852.tldr: The Quantum Sieve Tracer is introduced, a hybrid quantum-classical framework designed to characterize factual recall circuits, and it is demonstrated that quantum kernels can distinguish between these constructive (recall) and reductive (suppression) mechanisms.

2602.18458.title: The Story is Not the Science: Execution-Grounded Evaluation of Mechanistic Interpretability Research
2602.18458.tldr: This work proposes the first execution-grounded evaluation framework that verifies research beyond narrative review by examining code and data alongside the paper and develops MechEvalAgent, an automated evaluation framework that assesses the coherence of the experimental process, the reproducibility of results, and the generalizability of findings.

2507.00239.title: Linearly Decoding Refused Knowledge in Aligned Language Models
2507.00239.tldr: The results suggest that instruction-tuning does not wholly eliminate or even relocate harmful information in representation space-they merely suppress its direct expression, leaving it both linearly accessible and indirectly influential in downstream behavior.

2605.01130.title: Iterative Finetuning is Mostly Idempotent
2605.01130.tldr: The results suggest that amplification most likely comes from continual post-training, and limiting this stage may be an effective defense against trait amplification.

2608.29118.title: Emergent Misalignment Is Not Magical
2608.29118.tldr: The EM generalization metric is extended from a scalar distance to a dataset-specific generalization direction, which robustly predicts EM models'evilness under semantics-preserving prompt perturbations including appending random tokens and paraphrasing, where other methods do not reliably generalize.

2602.05859.title: DLM-Scope: Mechanistic Interpretability of Diffusion Language Models via Sparse Autoencoders
2602.05859.tldr: DLM-Scope is presented, the first SAE-based interpretability framework for DLMs, and it is demonstrated that trained Top-K SAEs can faithfully extract interpretable features, and it is found that inserting SAEs affects DLMs differently than autoregressive LLMs.

2510.03659.title: Does higher interpretability imply better utility? A Pairwise Analysis on Sparse Autoencoders
2510.03659.tldr: This work trains 90 SAEs across three LLMs, and evaluates their interpretability and steering utility, and proposes a novel selection criterion called Delta Token Confidence, which measures how much amplifying a feature changes the next token distribution.

2505.24428.title: Model Unlearning via Sparse Autoencoder Subspace Guided Projections
2505.24428.tldr: This work proposes SAE-Guided Subspace Projection Unlearning (SSPU), a novel framework that leverages SAE features to drive targeted updates in the model's parameter space, enabling precise, interpretable, and robust unlearning.
2505.24428.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2505.05111.title: Unveiling Language-Specific Features in Large Language Models via Sparse Autoencoders
2505.05111.tldr: A novel metric is introduced to assess the monolinguality of features obtained from SAEs, discovering that some features are strongly related to specific languages, and ablating them together yields greater improvement than ablating individually.
2505.05111.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2602.05444.title: Causal Front-Door Adjustment for Robust Jailbreak Attacks on LLMs
2602.05444.tldr: The Causal Front-Door Adjustment Attack (CFA{$^2$}) is proposed to jailbreak LLM, which is a framework that leverages Pearl's Front-Door Criterion to sever the confounding associations for robust jailbreaking.

2508.04216.title: Causal Reward Adjustment: Mitigating Reward Hacking in External Reasoning via Backdoor Correction
2508.04216.tldr: Causal Reward Adjustment (CRA), a method that mitigates reward hacking by estimating the true reward of a reasoning path and corrects confounding by using backdoor adjustment, is proposed.

2605.25525.title: SAE-FD: Sparse Autoencoder Feature Distillation for Continual Learning of Large Language Models
2605.25525.tldr: Sparse Autoencoder Feature Distillation is proposed, which anchors model representations in the sparse feature space of a pre-trained Sparse Autoencoder, where dense activations are decomposed into a sparse overcomplete basis that reduces representational entanglement, enabling more targeted regularization with less interference to new-task learning.

2602.04613.title: Translation Heads: Disentangling meaning from language in LLM-based machine translation
2602.04613.tldr: This work constructs subtask-specific steering vectors and shows that modifying just 1% of the relevant heads enables instruction-free MT performance comparable to instruction-based prompting, while ablating these heads selectively disrupts their corresponding translation functions.

2609.07746.title: LLM Forensics: Where Do Backdoors Hide? Localizing and Controlling Trigger Mechanisms with Sparse Autoencoders
2609.07746.tldr: These token-trigger mechanisms decompose into distinct SAE feature directions, with separate features for trigger detection, residual-stream propagation, and later language tracking, with this role-level decomposition most likely to transfer to other trigger-based backdoors, even when the payload, layers, or circuit locations differ.

2602.10382.title: Language Triggers Hijack Language Circuits: A Mechanistic Analysis of Backdoor Behaviors in Large Language Models
2602.10382.tldr: This work presents the first mechanistic analysis of trigger-induced language-switching backdoors injected during pre-training, studying the Gaperon model family, finding that trigger heads substantially overlap with heads naturally encoding output language across model scales.

2602.04902.title: Momentum Attention: The Physics of In-Context Learning and Spectral Forensics for Mechanistic Interpretability
2602.04902.tldr: An Orthogonality Theorem is formalized proving that DC (semantic) and AC (mechanistic) signals segregate into orthogonal frequency bands when Low-Pass RoPE interacts with High-Pass Momentum.

2602.03506.title: Explaining the Explainer: Understanding the Inner Workings of Transformer-based Symbolic Regression Models
2602.03506.tldr: PATCHES is introduced, an evolutionary circuit discovery algorithm that identifies compact and correct circuits for SR and provides the first circuit-level characterisation of an SR transformer, establishing SR as a high-potential application domain for mechanistic interpretability and proposing a principled methodology for circuit discovery.

2602.01605.title: Universal Redundancies in Time Series Foundation Models
2602.01605.tldr: This study develops a theoretical framework framing transformers as kernel regressors, motivating a purely intrinsic strategy for ablating heads based on the stable rank of the per-head projection matrices, and uncovers the specific heads responsible for degenerate phenomena widely observed in TSFMs.

2602.01442.title: Hidden Heroes and Gradient Bloats: Layer-Wise Redundancy Inverts Attribution in Transformers
2602.01442.tldr: A systematic inversion of early-layer feature extraction and late-layer computation motivates causal validation as a prerequisite for circuit-level claims by uncovering a systematic, layer-wise failure of gradient attribution.

2602.01247.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Brain-to-Speech Models Across Speech Modes
2602.01247.tldr: This work uses mechanistic interpretability to causally investigate the internal representations of a neural speech decoder, showing that speech modes lie on a shared continuous causal manifold, and cross-mode transfer is mediated by compact, layer-specific subspaces rather than diffuse activity.

2602.00924.title: Supervised sparse auto-encoders for interpretable and compositional representations
2602.00924.tldr: This work supervises (decoder-only) SAEs to reconstruct feature vectors by jointly learning sparse concept embeddings and decoder weights, and demonstrates compositional generalization, enabling feature-level intervention for semantic image editing without prompt modification.

2601.21996.title: Mechanistic Data Attribution: Tracing the Training Origins of Interpretable LLM Units
2601.21996.tldr: Mechanistic Data Attribution (MDA) is introduced, a scalable framework that employs Influence Functions to trace interpretable units back to specific training samples, providing a principled methodology for steering the developmental trajectories of LLMs.

2512.02004.title: AlignSAE: Concept-Aligned Sparse Autoencoders
2512.02004.tldr: AlignSAE is introduced, a method that aligns SAE features with a predefined ontology through a"pre-train, then post-train"curriculum that enables precise causal interventions, such as reliable"concept swaps", by targeting single, semantically aligned slots.

2601.20420.title: Concept Component Analysis: A Principled Approach for Concept Extraction in LLMs
2601.20420.tldr: It is shown that, under mild assumptions, LLM representations can be approximated as a {linear mixture} of the log-posteriors over concepts given the input context, through the lens of a latent variable model where concepts are treated as latent variables.

2601.17952.title: A Monosemantic Attribution Framework for Stable Interpretability in Clinical Neuroscience Transformer-Based Language Models
2601.17952.tldr: This work introduces a unified interpretability framework that integrates attributional and mechanistic perspectives through monosemantic feature extraction and produces stable input-level importance scores, advancing the safe and trustworthy application of LMs in cognitive health and neurodegenerative disease.

2601.11020.title: From Interpretability to Performance: Optimizing Retrieval Heads for Long-Context Language Models
2601.11020.tldr: Experiments demonstrate that RetMask consistently improves long-context performance, where gains correlate with the sparsity of the retrieval score distribution: models with sparser distributions respond more strongly, while those with less sparse distributions show more modest gains.
2601.11020.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2601.04398.title: Interpreting Transformers Through Attention Head Intervention
2601.04398.tldr: The evolution from visualization to intervention represents a paradigm shift from observing correlations to causally validating mechanistic hypotheses through direct intervention, validating the practical utility of interpretability research for AI safety.

2601.03047.title: When the Coffee Feature Activates on Coffins: An Analysis of Feature Extraction and Steering for Mechanistic Interpretability
2601.03047.tldr: An initial stress-test of mechanistic interpretability claims by replicating their main results with open-source SAEs for Llama 3.1 finds that feature steering exhibits substantial fragility, with sensitivity to layer selection, steering magnitude, and context.

2512.23837.title: Adversarial Lens: Exploiting Attention Layers to Generate Adversarial Examples for Evaluation
2512.23837.tldr: This work exploits the property of intermediate attention layers to generate adversarial examples directly from attention-layer token distributions, and highlights both the promise and current limitations of using intermediate-layer representations as a principled source of adversarial examples for stress-testing LLM-based evaluation pipelines.

2512.18092.title: Faithful and Stable Neuron Explanations for Trustworthy Mechanistic Interpretability
2512.18092.tldr: It is observed that neuron identification can be viewed as the inverse process of machine learning, which allows for guarantees for neuron explanations, and the first theoretical analysis of two fundamental challenges is presented, presenting the first theoretical analysis of two fundamental challenges.

2512.15938.title: SALVE: Sparse Autoencoder-Latent Vector Editing for Mechanistic Control of Neural Networks
2512.15938.tldr: This work contributes a principled methodology for turning feature discovery into actionable model edits, advancing the development of transparent and controllable AI systems.

2601.08837.title: From Adversarial Poetry to Adversarial Tales: An Interpretability Research Agenda
2601.08837.tldr: Adversarial Tales is introduced, a jailbreak technique that embeds harmful content within cyberpunk narratives and prompts models to perform functional analysis inspired by Vladimir Propp's morphology of folktales, suggesting that structurally-grounded jailbreaks constitute a broad vulnerability class rather than isolated techniques.

2605.12128.title: Metaphor Is Not All Attention Needs
