2605.12128.tldr: Overall, literary jailbreaks appear to misalign large language models not through any single poetic device, but through accumulated stylistic irregularities that alter prompt processing and avoid lexical triggers considered during post-training, suggesting that robustness requires safety mechanisms that account for style-induced shifts in model behavior.

2511.15304.title: Adversarial Poetry as a Universal Single-Turn Jailbreak Mechanism in Large Language Models
2511.15304.tldr: It is demonstrated that stylistic variation alone can circumvent contemporary safety mechanisms, suggesting fundamental limitations in current alignment methods and evaluation protocols.

2606.00003.title: Learning from Mistakes: Can LLM Self-Recover after Misalignment?
2606.00003.tldr: A new perspective on advancing LLM alignment is introduced: rather than developing stronger alignment techniques, this paper investigates the model's intrinsic ability to recover its alignment after corruption, and proposes a methodology for modeling the safety trajectories of user-assistant interactions and for detecting recovery trends within them.

2510.13893.title: Guarding the Guardrails: A Taxonomy-Driven Approach to Jailbreak Detection
2510.13893.tldr: A comprehensive hierarchical taxonomy of jailbreak strategies is developed that systematically consolidates techniques previously studied in isolation and harmonizes existing, partially overlapping classifications with explicit cross-references to prior categorizations, enabling the study of interactions where adversarial intent emerges gradually and succeeds in bypassing traditional safeguards.

2512.10547.title: Unlocking the Address Book: Dissecting the Sparse Semantic Structure of LLM Key-Value Caches via Sparse Autoencoders
2512.10547.tldr: A framework that utilizes Top-K Sparse Autoencoders to decompose the Key-Value cache into interpretable ``semantic atoms'' and introduces a Dual-Budget Strategy that selectively preserves the most informative semantic components while filtering representational noise.

2512.23260.title: Interpretable Safety Alignment via SAE-Constructed Low-Rank Subspace Adaptation
2512.23260.tldr: SAILS (Safety Alignment via Interpretable Low-rank Subspace), which leverages Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) to disentangle representations into monosemantic features, constructs an interpretable safety subspace from SAE decoder directions, and uses it to initialize LoRA adapters.
2512.23260.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2506.10622.title: SDialog: A Python Toolkit for End-to-End Agent Building, User Simulation, Dialog Generation, and Evaluation
2506.10622.tldr: SDialog, an MIT-licensed open-source Python toolkit that unifies dialog generation, evaluation and mechanistic interpretability into a single end-to-end framework for building and analyzing LLM-based conversational agents, enables researchers to build, benchmark and understand conversational systems more systematically.
2506.10622.venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2512.08892.title: Toward Faithful Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Sparse Autoencoders
2512.08892.tldr: RAGLens is introduced, a lightweight hallucination detector that accurately flags unfaithful RAG outputs using LLM internal representations that achieves superior detection performance compared to existing methods, and provides interpretable rationales for its decisions, enabling effective post-hoc mitigation of unfaithful RAG.

2510.19050.title: Rectifying Shortcut Behaviors in Preference-based Reward Learning
2510.19050.tldr: This paper proposes Preference-based Reward Invariance for Shortcut Mitigation (PRISM), which learns group-invariant kernels with feature maps in a closed-form learning objective and reduces the dependency on shortcuts in downstream policy models, establishing a robust framework for preference-based alignment.

2512.06681.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of GPT-2: Lexical and Contextual Layers in Sentiment Analysis
2512.06681.tldr: Experimental findings provide causal evidence that GPT-2's sentiment computation differs from the predicted hierarchical pattern, highlighting the need for further empirical characterization of contextual integration in large language models.

2512.05794.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Antibody Language Models Using SAEs
2512.05794.tldr: It is suggested that, while TopK SAEs suffice for mapping latent features to concepts, Ordered SAEs are preferable when precise generative steering is required and advance the mechanistic interpretability of domain-specific protein language models.

2503.08764.title: Towards Interpretable Protein Structure Prediction with Sparse Autoencoders
2503.08764.tldr: This work scales SAEs to ESM2-3B, the base model for ESMFold, enabling mechanistic interpretability of protein structure prediction for the first time, and adapts Matryoshka SAEs for protein language models, which learn hierarchically organized features by forcing nested groups of latents to reconstruct inputs independently.

2512.04691.title: Towards Ethical Multi-Agent Systems of Large Language Models: A Mechanistic Interpretability Perspective
2512.04691.tldr: A research agenda aimed at ensuring the ethical behavior of multi-agent systems of LLMs (MALMs) from the perspective of mechanistic interpretability is outlined, including developing comprehensive evaluation frameworks to assess ethical behavior at individual, interactional, and systemic levels.

2606.21197.title: Extraction and Analysis of Multimodal Concepts in Vision Language Models through Sparse Autoencoders
2606.21197.tldr: This work proposes a framework based on SAEs to extract and analyze visual, textual, and multimodal concepts from VLMs, providing a structured approach to distinguish between visual, textual, and multimodal concepts.

2511.20273.title: Beyond Components: Singular Vector-Based Interpretability of Transformer Circuits
2511.20273.tldr: A more fine-grained perspective is introduced that decomposes these components into orthogonal singular directions, revealing superposed and independent computations within a single head or MLP and opens new avenues for fine-grained mechanistic interpretability and a deeper understanding of model internals.

2511.19265.title: Unboxing the Black Box: Mechanistic Interpretability for Algorithmic Understanding of Neural Networks
2511.19265.tldr: It is argued that MI holds significant potential to support a more scientific understanding of machine learning systems -- treating models not only as tools for solving tasks, but also as systems to be studied and understood.

2511.17645.title: BlockCert: Certified Blockwise Extraction of Transformer Mechanisms
2511.17645.tldr: The results suggest that blockwise extraction with explicit certificates is feasible for real transformer language models and offers a practical bridge between mechanistic interpretability and formal reasoning about model behaviour.

2511.11711.title: Which Sparse Autoencoder Features Are Real? Model-X Knockoffs for False Discovery Rate Control
2511.11711.tldr: This work introduces Model-X knockoffs to SAE feature selection, using knock-off+ to control the false discovery rate (FDR) with finite-sample guarantees under the standard Model-X assumptions (in this case, via a Gaussian surrogate for the latent distribution).

2511.09432.title: Equivariant Sparse Autoencoders: Mechanistic Interpretability of Neural Networks on Symmetric Data
2511.09432.tldr: This work extends the Linear Representation Hypothesis, the theory behind SAEs, to account for symmetries and shows that the resulting Equivariant SAEs can avoid the pitfalls of existing SAEs on symmetric data and discover features more useful for downstream tasks despite worse reconstructions.

2511.08379.title: SOM Directions are Better than One: Multi-Directional Refusal Suppression in Language Models
2511.08379.tldr: This work proposes a novel method leveraging Self-Organizing Maps (SOMs) to extract multiple refusal directions, demonstrating that ablating multiple directions from models' internals outperforms not only the single-direction baseline but also specialized jailbreak algorithms, leading to an effective suppression of refusal.

2605.21706.title: Latent-space Attacks for Refusal Evasion in Language Models
2605.21706.tldr: This work recast refusal suppression as a latent-space evasion attack against linear probes trained to separate refused from answered prompts, and proposes a Controlled Latent-space Evasion attack that projects representations past the boundary with an optimized confidence.

2511.05923.title: Causal Tracing of Object Representations in Large Vision Language Models: Mechanistic Interpretability and Hallucination Mitigation
2511.05923.tldr: Fine-grained Cross-modal Causal Tracing (FCCT) framework is introduced, which systematically quantifies the causal effects on visual object perception and proposes Intermediate Representation Injection (IRI), a training-free inference-time technique that reinforces visual object information flow by precisely intervening on cross-modal representations at specific components and layers, thereby enhancing perception and mitigating hallucination.

2510.26411.title: MedSAE: Dissecting MedCLIP Representations with Sparse Autoencoders
2510.26411.tldr: This work advances mechanistic interpretability in medical vision by applying Medical Sparse Autoencoders (MedSAEs) to the latent space of MedCLIP, a vision-language model trained on chest radiographs and reports and proposes an evaluation framework that combines correlation metrics, entropy analyses, and automated neuron naming via the MedGemma foundation model.

2510.25013.title: Emergence of Minimal Circuits for Indirect Object Identification in Attention-Only Transformers
2510.25013.tldr: This work trains small, attention-only transformers from scratch on a symbolic version of the Indirect Object Identification (IOI) task, a benchmark for studying coreference-like reasoning in transformers and demonstrates that task-specific training induces highly interpretable, minimal circuits.
2510.25013.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2510.21693.title: Mechanistic Interpretability for Neural TSP Solvers
2510.21693.tldr: These findings provide the first model-internal account of what neural TSP solvers compute before node selection, demonstrate that geometric structure emerges without explicit supervision, and suggest pathways toward transparent hybrid systems that combine neural efficiency with algorithmic interpretability.

2510.19875.title: Stream: Scaling up Mechanistic Interpretability to Long Context in LLMs via Sparse Attention
2510.19875.tldr: Sarse Tracing is introduced, a novel technique that leverages dynamic sparse attention to efficiently analyze long context attention patterns and helps democratize chain-of-thought monitoring by making long context interpretability feasible on consumer GPUs.

2510.18462.title: DePass: Unified Feature Attributing by Simple Decomposed Forward Pass
2510.18462.tldr: DePass, a unified framework for feature attribution based on a single decomposed forward pass, achieves faithful, fine-grained attribution without requiring auxiliary training, and is validated across token-level, model component-level, and subspace-level attribution tasks.

2511.11518.title: W2S-AlignTree: Weak-to-Strong Inference-Time Alignment for Large Language Models via Monte Carlo Tree Search
2511.11518.tldr: W2S-AlignTree is a pioneering plug-and-play inference-time alignment framework that synergistically combines Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) with the Weak-to-Strong Generalization paradigm for the first time and formulates LLM alignment as an optimal heuristic search problem within a generative search tree.

2510.09794.title: Causality $\neq$ Decodability, and Vice Versa: Lessons from Interpreting Counting ViTs
2510.09794.tldr: The findings highlight that decodability and causality reflect complementary dimensions of representation--what information is present versus what is used--and that their divergence can expose hidden computational circuits.

2510.08931.title: RADAR: Mechanistic Pathways for Detecting Data Contamination in LLM Evaluation
2510.08931.tldr: RADAR (Recall vs. Reasoning Detection through Activation Representation), a novel framework that leverages mechanistic interpretability to detect contamination by distinguishing recall-based from reasoning-based model responses, demonstrates the potential of mechanistic interpretability for advancing LLM evaluation beyond traditional surface-level metrics.

2411.07618.title: Constrain Alignment with Sparse Autoencoders
2411.07618.tldr: This paper proposes Feature-level constrained Preference Optimization (FPO), a novel method designed to simplify the alignment process while ensuring stability, and leverages pre-trained Sparse Autoencoders and introduces feature-level constraints, allowing for efficient, sparsity-enforced alignment.

2510.03799.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Socio-Political Frames in Language Models
2510.03799.tldr: It is demonstrated that LLMs are highly fluent in generating texts that evoke specific frames and can recognize these frames in zero-shot settings, and the location of the `strict father' and `nurturing parent' frames within the model's hidden representation is investigated.

2510.00845.title: Mechanistic Interpretability as Statistical Estimation: A Variance Analysis
2510.00845.tldr: This work argues that circuit discovery is not a standalone task but a statistical estimation problem built upon causal mediation analysis (CMA), and uncovers a fundamental instability at this base layer: exact, single-input CMA scores exhibit high intrinsic variance.

2509.25686.title: EXP-CAM: Explanation Generation and Circuit Discovery Using Classifier Activation Matching
2509.25686.tldr: Exposure-CAM is introduced: an explanation generation and circuit discovery approach using Classifier Activation Matching to generate minimal and faithful explanations for the decisions of pre-trained image classifiers that not only preserve the model's decision but are also concise and human-readable.

2509.24713.title: Circuit-Aware Reward Training: A Mechanistic Framework for Longtail Robustness in RLHF
2509.24713.tldr: This work proposes a mechanistic interpretability framework that identifies specialized neural circuits responsible for rare-event processing in reward models and introduces circuit-Aware Reward Training (CART), which uses circuit analysis to guide data augmentation, regularization, and ensemble strategies.

2605.13537.title: Temper and Tilt Lead to SLOP: Reward Hacking Mitigation with Inference-Time Alignment
2605.13537.tldr: An algorithm for calibrating SLOP weight parameters is proposed and experimentally demonstrated that it improves robustness while preserving alignment performance, and generalization of inference-time alignment to ensembles of generative reward models combined as a sharpened logarithmic opinion pool (SLOP).

2603.15259.title: Directional Embedding Smoothing for Robust Vision Language Models
2603.15259.tldr: The Randomized Embedding Smoothing and Token Aggregation defense is extended to VLMs and it is found that RESTA is effective in reducing attack success rate over this diverse corpus of attacks, in particular, when employing directional embedding noise.

2510.03282.title: Discovering Transformer Circuits via a Hybrid Attribution and Pruning Framework
2510.03282.tldr: This research proposes a hybrid attribution and pruning (HAP) framework that uses attribution patching to identify a high-potential subgraph, then applies edge pruning to extract a faithful circuit from it and shows that HAP is 46\% faster than baseline algorithms without sacrificing circuit faithfulness.

2509.23717.title: Measuring Sparse Autoencoder Feature Sensitivity
2509.23717.tldr: This work establishes feature sensitivity as a new dimension for evaluating both individual features and SAE architectures and demonstrates that sensitivity measures a new facet of feature quality and finds that many interpretable features have poor sensitivity.

2509.23323.title: LLM Interpretability with Identifiable Temporal-Instantaneous Representation
2509.23323.tldr: This work introduces an identifiable temporal causal representation learning framework specifically designed for LLMs' high-dimensional concept space, capturing both time-delayed and instantaneous causal relations.

2505.20254.title: Position: Mechanistic Interpretability Should Prioritize Feature Consistency in SAEs
2505.20254.tldr: This position paper argues that mechanistic interpretability should prioritize feature consistency in SAEs -- the reliable convergence to equivalent feature sets across independent runs, and proposes using the Pairwise Dictionary Mean Correlation Coefficient (PW-MCC) as a practical metric to operationalize consistency.

2510.23751.title: Debiasing Reward Models by Representation Learning with Guarantees
2510.23751.tldr: This work proposes a principled framework that mitigates spurious correlation issues in reward models while preserving the underlying factors that reflect intended preferences, and inspires a practical method that uses variational inference to recover these variables and leverages them to train reward models.

2509.22831.title: Toward a Theory of Generalizability in LLM Mechanistic Interpretability Research
2509.22831.tldr: It is argued that progress on the generalizability of mechanistic interpretability research will consist in mapping constitutive design properties of LLMs to their emergent behaviors and mechanisms.

2601.21350.title: Factored Causal Representation Learning for Robust Reward Modeling in RLHF
2601.21350.tldr: A factored representation learning framework is proposed that decomposes the model's contextual embedding into causal factors that are sufficient for reward prediction and non-causal factors that capture reward-irrelevant attributes such as length or sycophantic bias.

2509.25220.title: Cyclic Ablation: Testing Concept Localization against Functional Regeneration in AI
2509.25220.tldr: It is found that, contrary to the localization hypothesis, deception was highly resilient, and the model consistently recovered its deceptive behavior after each ablation cycle via adversarial training, a process the authors term functional regeneration.

2509.18792.title: Beyond the Leaderboard: Understanding Performance Disparities in Large Language Models via Model Diffing
2509.18792.tldr: This work uses model diffing, a mechanistic interpretability approach, to analyze the specific capability differences between Gemma-2-9b-it and a SimPO-enhanced variant, and finds that SimPO acquired latent concepts predominantly enhance safety mechanisms, multilingual capabilities, and instruction-following.
2509.18792.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2602.02132.title: There Is More to Refusal in Large Language Models than a Single Direction
2602.02132.tldr: This work uncovers a structured internal representation of refusal in large language models: a reusable core of shared refusal latents supplemented by style- and domain-specific latents, and clarifies the limits of linear interpretability for aligned model behavior.

2509.17665.title: Mechanistic Interpretability with SAEs: Probing Religion, Violence, and Geography in Large Language Models
2509.17665.tldr: While all five religions show comparable internal cohesion, Islam is more frequently linked to features associated with violent language and geographic associations largely reflect real-world religious demographics, revealing how models embed both factual distributions and cultural stereotypes.

2509.10809.title: Rethinking Sparse Autoencoders: Select-and-Project for Fairness and Control from Encoder Features Alone
2509.10809.tldr: S&P Top-K is introduced, a retraining-free and computationally lightweight Selection and Projection framework that identifies Top-K encoder features aligned with a sensitive attribute or behavior, optionally aggregates them into a single control axis, and computes an orthogonal projection to be subsequently applied directly in the model's native embedding space.

2509.08592.title: Interpretability as Alignment: Making Internal Understanding a Design Principle
2509.08592.tldr: This paper argues that mechanistic interpretability provides mechanistic interpretability, and frames interpretability not as post-hoc explanation but as a design constraint embedding auditability, provenance, and bounded transparency within model architectures.

2605.15164.title: Position: Behavioural Assurance Cannot Verify the Safety Claims Governance Now Demands
2605.15164.tldr: It is argued that behavioural assurance, even when carefully designed, is being asked to carry safety claims it cannot verify, and the concept of fragile assurance is introduced to describe cases where the evidential structure does not support the asserted safety claim.

2602.04521.title: $C$-$ΔΘ$: Circuit-Restricted Weight Arithmetic for Selective Refusal
2602.04521.tldr: This work proposes C-{\Delta}{\theta} Circuit Restricted Weight Arithmetic, which localizes refusal-causal computation as a sparse circuit using EAP-IG and computes a constrained weight update {\Delta}{\theta}C supported only on that circuit (typically<5% of parameters).

2502.04695.title: Bridging the Gap in XAI-Why Reliable Metrics Matter for Explainability and Compliance
2502.04695.tldr: A Governance by Metrics paradigm is proposed that treats explainability evaluation as a central mechanism of private AI governance, and introduces a hierarchical model linking transparency, tamper resistance, scalability, and legal alignment, extending evaluation from model introspection toward systemic accountability.

2607.05355.title: Faithfulness to Refusal: A Causal Audit of Neuron Selectors
2607.05355.tldr: Two paired audits built on one-shot neuron-row zeroing show that rank-stability proxies miss the kinds of selector failures a direct causal audit can surface, and audit selectors at the language-modeling level.

2509.07149.title: Measuring Uncertainty in Transformer Circuits with Effective Information Consistency
2509.07149.tldr: The single‑pass, dimensionless Effective‑Information Consistency Score (EICS), which combines a normalized sheaf inconsistency computed from local Jacobians and activations, with a Gaussian EI proxy for circuit-level causal emergence derived from the same forward state is introduced.

2509.01874.title: Preserving Bilinear Weight Spectra with a Signed and Shrunk Quadratic Activation Function
2509.01874.tldr: SQS is introduced, an activation function designed to allow Gated Linear Units (GLUs) to learn interpretable features without these drawbacks and achieves performance competitive with state-of-the-art activation functions whilst enabling weight-based interpretability.

2509.00328.title: Mechanistic interpretability for steering vision-language-action models
2509.00328.tldr: This work demonstrates that interpretable components of embodied VLAs can be systematically harnessed for control - establishing a new paradigm for transparent and steerable foundation models in robotics.

2508.17456.title: Adversarial Examples Are Not Bugs, They Are Superposition
2508.17456.tldr: It is shown that superposition can theoretically explain a range of adversarial phenomena, and four lines of evidence are presented in support of this hypothesis, greatly extending prior arguments by Elhage et al. (2022).

2604.00208.title: Similarity of Neural Network Representations in Superposition
2604.00208.tldr: Closed-form derivations prove that standard linear alignment metrics depend on the Gram matrices of each system's projection, not on the latent features themselves: alignment thus combines what a system represents with how it is encoded, consistent with superposition in real systems.

2410.24184.title: Group Crosscoders for Mechanistic Analysis of Symmetry
2410.24184.tldr: It is demonstrated that group crosscoders can provide systematic insights into how neural networks represent symmetry, offering a promising new tool for mechanistic interpretability.

2508.16950.title: Disentangling Polysemantic Neurons with a Null-Calibrated Polysemanticity Index and Causal Patch Interventions
2508.16950.tldr: The Polysemanticity Index (PSI), a null-calibrated metric that quantifies when a neuron's top activations decompose into semantically distinct clusters, offers a principled and practical lever for discovering, quantifying, and studying polysemantic units in neural networks.

2604.18567.title: Latent Phase-Shift Rollback: Inference-Time Error Correction via Residual Stream Monitoring and KV-Cache Steering
2604.18567.tldr: At each generation step, at each generation step, LPSR monitors the residual stream at a critical layer lcrit, detects abrupt directional reversals (phase shifts) via a cosine-similarity $+$ entropy dual gate, and responds by rolling back the KV-cache and injecting a pre-computed steering vector.

2512.10449.title: When Reject Turns into Accept: Quantifying the Vulnerability of LLM-Based Scientific Reviewers to Indirect Prompt Injection
2512.10449.tldr: This study investigates the robustness of "LLM-as-a-Judge" systems to adversarial PDF manipulation via invisible text injections and layout aware encoding attacks, and introduces the Weighted Adversarial Vulnerability Score (WAVS), a novel metric that quantifies susceptibility by weighting score inflation against the severity of decision shifts relative to ground truth.

2512.10415.title: How to Trick Your AI TA: A Systematic Study of Academic Jailbreaking in LLM Code Evaluation
2512.10415.tldr: The first large-scale study of jailbreaking LLM-based automated code evaluators in academic context is presented, finding that these models exhibit significant vulnerability, particularly to persuasive and role-play-based attacks.

2508.16325.title: ConceptGuard: Neuro-Symbolic Safety Guardrails via Sparse Interpretable Jailbreak Concepts
2508.16325.tldr: This work introduces ConceptGuard, a novel framework that leverages Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) to identify interpretable concepts within LLM internals associated with different jailbreak themes, and provides evidence for a shared activation geometry for jailbreak attacks in the representation space.

2508.16109.title: From Indirect Object Identification to Syllogisms: Exploring Binary Mechanisms in Transformer Circuits
2508.16109.tldr: This paper investigates the ability of GPT-2 small to handle binary truth values by analyzing its behavior with syllogistic prompts and identifies multiple circuits that mechanistically explain GPT-2's logical-reasoning capabilities and uncover binary mechanisms that facilitate task completion.

2508.15847.title: Mechanistic Exploration of Backdoored Large Language Model Attention Patterns
2508.15847.tldr: Attention head mechanisms are analyzed via techniques like ablation, activation patching, and KL divergence to reveal distinct attention pattern deviations concentrated in later transformer layers, indicating backdoors leave detectable attention signatures whose structure depends on trigger complexity, which can be leveraged for detection and mitigation strategies.

2508.14275.title: Disentangling concept semantics via multilingual averaging in Sparse Autoencoders
2508.14275.tldr: This work proposes a method that isolates concept semantics in Large Langue Models by averaging concept activations derived via Sparse Autoencoders, and hints at a new technique which enables mechanistic interpretation of internal network states with higher accuracy.

2508.10553.title: eDIF: A European Deep Inference Fabric for Remote Interpretability of LLM
2508.10553.tldr: A feasibility study on the deployment of a European Deep Inference Fabric (eDIF), an NDIF-compatible infrastructure designed to support mechanistic interpretability research on large language models and lays the groundwork for broader deployment, expanded tooling, and sustained community collaboration in mechanistic interpretability research.

2508.09019.title: Activation Steering for Bias Mitigation: An Interpretable Approach to Safer LLMs
2508.09019.tldr: A complete, end-to-end system that uses techniques from mechanistic interpretability to both identify and actively mitigate bias directly within a model's internal workings and is presented as a robust and reproducible system that offers a more direct and interpretable approach to building safer and more accountable LLMs.

2507.21132.title: Can You Trust an LLM with Your Life-Changing Decision? An Investigation into AI High-Stakes Responses
2507.21132.tldr: It is demonstrated that a model's cautiousness can be directly controlled via activation steering, suggesting a new path for safety alignment, and underscore the need for nuanced, multi-faceted benchmarks to ensure LLMs can be trusted with life-changing decisions.

2607.01859.title: Safety Targeted Embedding Exploit via Refinement

2507.12950.title: Insights into a radiology-specialised multimodal large language model with sparse autoencoders
2507.12950.tldr: This study applies Matryoshka-SAE to the radiology-specialised multimodal large language model, MAIRA-2, to interpret its internal representations, offering initial insights into the internal concepts learned by MAIRA-2 and marking a step toward deeper mechanistic understanding and interpretability of a radiology-adapted multimodal large language model.

2507.09406.title: Adversarial Activation Patching: A Framework for Detecting and Mitigating Emergent Deception in Safety-Aligned Transformers
2507.09406.tldr: This paper introduces adversarial activation patching, a novel mechanistic interpretability framework that leverages activation patching as an adversarial tool to induce, detect, and mitigate such deception in transformer-based models.

2507.08802.title: The Non-Linear Representation Dilemma: Is Causal Abstraction Enough for Mechanistic Interpretability?
2507.08802.tldr: It is proved that under reasonable assumptions, any neural network can be mapped to any algorithm, rendering this unrestricted notion of causal abstraction trivial and uninformative.

2507.05810.title: Concept-Based Mechanistic Interpretability Using Structured Knowledge Graphs
2507.05810.tldr: This work proposes a novel framework and interactive tool that extends concept-based interpretability methods into the domain of mechanistic interpretability, and contributes to a deeper understanding of how deep learning models generalize (or fail to) in the presence of dataset biases.

2507.03662.title: Re-Emergent Misalignment: How Narrow Fine-Tuning Erodes Safety Alignment in LLMs
2507.03662.tldr: It is shown that fine tuning on insecure code induces internal changes that oppose alignment, and how narrow fine-tuning can degrade general safety behavior by interfering with shared internal mechanisms is revealed.

2506.23679.title: Learning Modular Exponentiation with Transformers
2506.23679.tldr: It is found that reciprocal operand training leads to strong performance gains, with sudden generalization across related moduli, and synchronized accuracy surges reflect grokking-like dynamics, suggesting the model internalizes shared arithmetic structure.

2511.23092.title: Does Self-Evaluation Enable Wireheading in Language Models?
2511.23092.tldr: This work formalizes conditions under which reward-channel control strictly dominates task-focused behavior in partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs) and test these predictions empirically across two models and three tasks, finding that when self-grades determine rewards, models exhibit substantial grade inflation without corresponding accuracy gains.

2506.18852.title: Mechanistic Interpretability Needs Philosophy
2506.18852.tldr: It is argued that mechanistic interpretability needs philosophy as an ongoing partner in clarifying its concepts, refining its methods, and navigating the epistemic and ethical complexities of interpreting AI systems.

2506.18053.title: Mechanistic Interpretability in the Presence of Architectural Obfuscation

2506.17846.title: Out of Control -- Why Alignment Needs Formal Control Theory (and an Alignment Control Stack)
2506.17846.tldr: This position paper argues that formal optimal control theory should be central to AI alignment research, offering a distinct perspective from prevailing AI safety and security approaches, and introduces an Alignment Control Stack which sets out a hierarchical layered alignment stack.

2506.21588.title: Understanding Verbatim Memorization in LLMs Through Circuit Discovery
2506.21588.tldr: This work identifies points where model generation diverges from memorized content and isolate the specific circuits responsible for two distinct aspects of memorization, finding that circuits that initiate memorization can also maintain it once started, while circuits that only maintain memorization cannot trigger its initiation.
2506.21588.venue: Proceedings of the First Workshop on Large Language Model Memorization (L2M2)

2506.14002.title: Taming Polysemanticity in LLMs: Provable Feature Recovery via Sparse Autoencoders
2506.14002.tldr: This work introduces a new SAE training algorithm based on ``bias adaptation'', a technique that adaptively adjusts neural network bias parameters to ensure appropriate activation sparsity, and provides the first SAE algorithm with theoretical recovery guarantees.

2506.07691.title: Breaking the Block: Preserving Data Continuity to Train Superior SAEs for Instruct Models
2506.07691.tldr: FAST aligns SAE training with the data distribution and activation patterns of instruct models, substantially improving both reconstruction fidelity and feature interpretability, and finds that intervening on special token activations through SAEs can improve generation quality, revealing new opportunities for fine-grained control.

2605.10983.title: TMPO: Trajectory Matching Policy Optimization for Diverse and Efficient Diffusion Alignment
2605.10983.tldr: Trajectory Matching Policy Optimization (TMPO) is proposed, which replaces scalar reward maximization with trajectory-level reward distribution matching and improves generative diversity over state-of-the-art methods by 9.1%, and achieves competitive performance in all downstream and efficiency metrics.

2510.04309.title: Activation Steering with a Feedback Controller
2510.04309.tldr: This work develops a control-theoretic foundation for activation steering by showing that popular steering methods correspond to the proportional (P) controllers, with the steering vector serving as the feedback signal, and proposes Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) Steering, a principled framework that leverages the full PID controller for activation steering in LLMs.

2505.17815.title: Evaluation Faking: Unveiling Observer Effects in Safety Evaluation of Frontier AI Systems
2505.17815.tldr: A chain-of-thought monitoring technique is devised to detect faking intent and uncover internal signals correlated with such behavior, offering insights for future mitigation studies.

2506.05166.title: Dissecting Bias in LLMs: A Mechanistic Interpretability Perspective
2506.05166.tldr: It is demonstrated that bias-related computations are highly localized, often concentrated in a small subset of layers, and removing these components not only reduces biased outputs but also affects other NLP tasks, such as named entity recognition and linguistic acceptability judgment because of the sharing of important components with these tasks.

2505.22506.title: Sparsification and Reconstruction from the Perspective of Representation Geometry
2505.22506.tldr: The SAEMA is proposed, which validates the stratified structure of the representation by observing the variability of the rank of the symmetric semipositive definite (SSPD) matrix corresponding to the modal tensor unfolded along the latent tensor with the level of noise added to the residual stream.

2606.25657.title: Steering Vision-Language Models with Joint Sparse Autoencoders
2606.25657.tldr: The Joint Sparse Autoencoder (JSAE) is introduced, which uses an explicit alignment constraint to jointly factorize sequence-pooled vision and language activations into shared, interpretable image/caption-level features.

2602.22581.title: IBCircuit: Towards Holistic Circuit Discovery with Information Bottleneck
2602.22581.tldr: IBCircuit is an optimization framework for holistic circuit discovery that can be applied to any given task without tediously corrupted activation design and identifies more faithful and minimal circuits in terms of critical node components and edge components compared to recent related work.

2609.06966.title: MOLE: Detecting Insider Threats in AI Agents
2609.06966.tldr: MOLE is introduced, an open benchmark of 150 AI-operated accounts sharing 9 stateful services over 30 workdays, with 12 threats and 8 corpora from four models totaling roughly 20 billion tokens.

2504.08192.title: SAEs Can Improve Unlearning: Dynamic Sparse Autoencoder Guardrails for Precision Unlearning in LLMs
2504.08192.tldr: This work introduces Dynamic DAE Guardrails (DSG), a novel method for precision unlearning that leverages principled feature selection and a dynamic classifier and substantially outperforms leading unlearning methods, achieving superior forget-utility trade-offs.

2609.16204.title: Decoy Direction Optimization: A Post-Hoc Defense Against LLM Abliteration
2609.16204.tldr: Decoy Direction Optimization (DDO), a fast, post-hoc weight-editing defense that requires no base-model finetuning, is introduced, based on a simple mechanistic insight: ablation attacks rely on contrastive estimators to find the refusal direction.

2605.26526.title: Open-Weight LLM Fine-Tuning Defenses are Susceptible to Simple Attacks
2605.26526.tldr: It is shown that open-weight safeguards are susceptible to simpler strategies that, despite being well known, have not been systematically evaluated against these safeguards, and abliteration-resistant tuning (ART) is introduced, which incorporates an abliteration-based objective into training.

2605.26315.title: Curriculum Learning for Safety Alignment
2605.26315.tldr: This paper proposes Staged-Competence, a curriculum-based framework that organises preference data by difficulty, employs competence-based sampling, and progressively updates the reference model during training and shows that Staged-Competence matches baseline safety with only 75% of the training data and yields better separation between safe and unsafe responses.

2506.15699.title: BLUR: A Benchmark for LLM Unlearning Robust to Forget-Retain Overlap
2506.15699.tldr: A benchmark for LLM unlearning that provides more realistic scenarios of forget-retain overlap and significantly expands on existing unlearning benchmarks by providing extended evaluation tasks, combined forget/retain queries, and relearning datasets of varying degrees of difficulty.

2505.20132.title: Tensorization is a powerful but underexplored tool for compression and interpretability of neural networks
2505.20132.tldr: It is argued that TNNs represent a powerful yet underexplored framework for deep learning--one that deserves greater attention from both engineering and theoretical communities and highlights the value of TNNs as a flexible class of architectures with distinctive scaling properties and increased interpretability.

2505.19440.title: The Birth of Knowledge: Emergent Features across Time, Space, and Scale in Large Language Models
2505.19440.tldr: Results indicate clear temporal and scale-specific thresholds for feature emergence across multiple domains, with early-layer features re-emerging at later layers, challenging standard assumptions about representational dynamics in transformer models.

2505.18235.title: The Origins of Representation Manifolds in Large Language Models
2505.18235.tldr: Why and how a feature might be represented as a manifold is described, demonstrating in particular that cosine similarity in representation space may encode the intrinsic geometry of a feature through shortest, on-manifold paths, potentially answering the question of how distance in representation space and relatedness in concept space could be connected.

2505.12060.title: Why Not Act on What You Know? Unleashing Safety Potential of LLMs via Self-Aware Guard Enhancement
2505.12060.tldr: This paper identifies a critical safety gap: while LLMs are adept at detecting jailbreak prompts, they often produce unsafe responses when directly processing these inputs, and proposes SAGE (Self-Aware Guard Enhancement), a training-free defense strategy designed to align LLMs' strong safety discrimination performance with their relatively weaker safety generation ability.
2505.12060.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2505.11836.title: SplInterp: Improving our Understanding and Training of Sparse Autoencoders
2505.11836.tldr: It is discovered that SAEs generalise ``$k-means autoencoders'' to be piecewise affine, but sacrifice accuracy for interpretability vs. the optimal ``$k$-means-esque plus local principal component analysis (PCA)'' piecewise affine autoencoder.

2505.05541.title: Safety by Measurement: A Systematic Literature Review of AI Safety Evaluation Methods
2505.05541.tldr: This literature review consolidates the rapidly evolving field of AI safety evaluations, proposing a systematic taxonomy around three dimensions: what properties the authors measure, how they measure them, and how these measurements integrate into frameworks.

2508.13700.title: The AI Risk Spectrum: From Dangerous Capabilities to Existential Threats
2508.13700.tldr: This paper maps the full spectrum of AI risks, from current harms affecting individual users to existential threats that could endanger humanity's survival, and identifies risk amplifiers - competitive pressures, accidents, corporate indifference, and coordination failures - that make all risks more likely and severe.

2505.00555.title: On the Mechanistic Interpretability of Neural Networks for Causality in Bio-statistics
2505.00555.tldr: This work demonstrates that MI tools can be leveraged to probe and validate the internal representations learned by NNs, and discover and visualize the distinct computational pathways employed by the network to process different types of inputs, potentially revealing how confounders and treatments are handled.

2504.16290.title: Naturally Computed Scale Invariance in the Residual Stream of ResNet18
2504.16290.tldr: This work investigates ResNet18 with a particular focus on its residual stream, an architectural component which InceptionV1 lacks, and tentative findings suggest how the residual stream computes scale invariance and its possible role in behavior.
2504.16290.venue: 2025 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)

2504.15473.title: Emergence and Evolution of Interpretable Concepts in Diffusion Models
2504.15473.tldr: This work uses the SAE framework to probe the inner workings of a popular text-to-image diffusion model, and uncovers a variety of human-interpretable concepts in its activations.

2609.21142.title: Exploring Text Classification Models with Sparse Autoencoders
2609.21142.tldr: Techniques for exploring the relationships between the SAE's features and the model's predictions and errors are presented and integrated into SAEfarer, a tool for analyzing concepts learned by text classification LMs.

2609.18860.title: Decodable but Misrouted: Sparse Features Uncover a Readout Gap in Vision-Language Models for Harmful Meme Detection
2609.18860.tldr: Robustness controls show that the signal extends beyond English, is not explained solely by accompanying OCR, and depends on paired visual evidence, thus, routing, rather than representation alone, is a recurring bottleneck in harmful meme classification.

2609.07037.title: Disentangling Steering Vectors
2609.07037.tldr: Steering Vector Dissection is proposed, a framework to explicitly isolate individual and semantically consistent features from these composite directions that tend to entangle multiple semantic and stylistic concepts into a single composite direction, leading to unpredictable steering effects.

2608.30403.title: Why Are LLM Backdoor Defenses Fragmented? A Feature-Level Explanation with Sparse Autoencoders
2608.30403.tldr: Results show that SAE-based analysis can explain defense fragmentation and guide interpretable backdoor mitigation and show system?atic encoding differences: dirty-label backdoors are dominated by isolated interaction features, whereas clean-label backdoors rely more on heterogeneous mixtures of mixed and weight-modified features.

2603.27522.title: Hidden Ads: Behavior Triggered Semantic Backdoors for Advertisement Injection in Vision Language Models
2603.27522.tldr: This work introduces Hidden Ads, a new class of backdoor attacks that exploit this recommendation-seeking behavior to inject unauthorized advertisements, and proposes a multi-tier threat framework to systematically evaluate Hidden Ads across three adversary capability levels: hard prompt injection, soft prompt optimization, and supervised fine-tuning.

2608.29936.title: When Safety Speaks a Language: A Mechanistic Analysis of Safety-Language Identity Entanglement in LLMs
2608.29936.tldr: This work presents a systematic mechanistic analysis of multilingual safety using sparse autoencoder features, sparse interpretable directions in the residual stream associated with harmful and harmless model behavior across three instruction-tuned LLMs, eight languages, and all model layers to qualify the language-universality of safety alignment as architecture-dependent and offer a mechanistic account of multilingual safety interventions.

2606.07141.title: REMEDI: A Benchmark for Retention and Unlearning Evaluation in Multi-label Clinical Disease Inference
2606.07141.tldr: REMEDI is an extensive benchmark for machine unlearning tailored to multi-label and multiclass clinical disease inference, where label correlations, longitudinal structure, and safety constraints make unlearning particularly challenging.

2608.29034.title: A Unifying Perspective on Language Model Representations: From Filler-Role Structure to Mechanistic Interpretability
2608.29034.tldr: This work proposes using Tensor Product Representations (TPRs) as a unifying hypothesis, and shows that TPRs can unify several prior interpretability methods: additive analogies, linear probing, sparse autoencoders, and activation patching.

2605.29971.title: Causal Interventions on Continuous Variables: A Case Study on Verb Bias in Steering Vectors for In-Context Learning
2605.29971.tldr: It is shown that verb bias is causally represented in steering vectors extracted from large language models: counterfactual edits to verb bias systematically shift downstream structural preferences.

2608.28233.title: REINS: Refusal-Enhanced Inhibitory Steering with Sparse Autoencoder Features
2608.28233.tldr: Refusal-Enhanced INhibitory Steering is proposed, which suppresses harmful continuation features and enhances safe refusal features in the same SAE feature space, and substantially reduces harmful responses, markedly improves safe refusals and largely preserves general capabilities.

2509.26345.title: SafeBehavior: Simulating Human-Like Multistage Reasoning to Mitigate Jailbreak Attacks in Large Language Models
2509.26345.tldr: Experimental results show that SafeBehavior significantly improves robustness and adaptability across diverse threat scenarios, offering an efficient and human inspired approach to safeguarding LLMs against jailbreak attempts.

2608.25941.title: When Pruning Meets Interpretability: Preserving Sparse Autoencoder Robustness in LLMs
2608.25941.tldr: A systematic study of how pruning affects SAE behavior is presented and theoretically shows that, for a fixed SAE, its impact is governed by perturbation energy, a covariance-weighted norm.

2510.00404.title: AbsTopK: Rethinking Sparse Autoencoders For Bidirectional Features
2510.00404.tldr: AbsTopK SAE is proposed, a new variant derived from the $\ell_0$ sparsity constraint that applies hard thresholding over the largest-magnitude activations, which improves reconstruction fidelity, enhances interpretability, and enables single features to encode contrasting concepts.

2608.23809.title: Discovering Cross-Language Reasoning Invariance in LLMs with Geometry-Invariant Sparse Autoencoders
2608.23809.tldr: It is found that cross-language feature sharing is model- and architecture-dependent in this sample and appears at different depths in different models.

2608.13337.title: Where You Measure Decides What You Measure: Position Selection in Ablation-Based SAE Evaluation
2608.13337.tldr: Six autoencoders are trained from one initialisation, differing only in fitting choices, so that a latent means the same thing in each, and a causal number reported without its position describes the token it was taken at as much as the latent it was taken from.

2606.24251.title: Probing the Misaligned Thinking Process of Language Models
2606.24251.tldr: This work proposes to monitor misalignment by decomposing it into fine-grained cognitive processes -- misalignment indicators -- and detecting their presence in a model's internal activations via linear probes, and develops a taxonomy of 18 indicators spanning different misaligned behaviors.

2608.08168.title: Thinking vs. NoThinking: Towards Interpreting Reasoning Mechanisms of Large Language Models via Sparse Autoencoders
2608.08168.tldr: This work applies Top-K Sparse Autoencoders to the intermediate representations of DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B and examines the model's divergent behaviors across math-solving tasks of three distinct difficulty levels, identifying a clear distinction in how the model functions under two reasoning modes.

2608.29286.title: MMPCBench: Benchmarking Multimodal Large Language Models on Proactive Critique of Flawed Inputs
2608.29286.tldr: This work proposes MMPCBench, a comprehensive framework for evaluating MLLMs' proactive critique competence, which adopts a hierarchical evaluation protocol to measure models' error detection, diagnosis and resolution performance, and applies alignment-aware metrics to assess the coherence between internal reasoning and final responses.

2608.07852.title: "Many Are My Names": The Anatomy of the Assistant and Its Personas via Sparse Autoencoders
2608.07852.tldr: This work decomposes three generation settings (Assistant, Roleplay, and Story) into sparse autoencoder features extracted at turn-boundary and pronoun-token positions and selected through a filtering pipeline for different depths, characterize each surviving feature through its steering effects and activation distribution.

2608.05732.title: CircuitSteer: Geometrically Aligned Multi-Layer Steering via Sparse Autoencoder Circuits
2608.05732.tldr: CircuitSteer is introduced, a novel framework that leverages Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) to identify and manipulate coherent semantic circuits distributed across multiple layers that yields strictly more robust and effective behavioral control than static single-point interventions.

2507.04742.title: Activation Steering for Chain-of-Thought Compression
2507.04742.tldr: Activation-Steered Compression (ASC), an inference-time technique that shortens reasoning traces by directly modifying hidden representations, is formalized and provides a theoretical analysis of the impact of ASC on the output distribution, derived from a closed-form KL-divergence-bounded constraint to regulate steering strength.
2507.04742.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2607.20652.title: Scaling Interpretable Transformers with Parity Bottleneck Layers
2607.20652.tldr: The ParityTransformer is introduced, a GPT-2-scale architecture whose intermediate representations are efficient and wide / sparse by design, and seen as a step toward training models whose internal representations are interpretable by design rather than recovered post hoc.

2607.17117.title: Persistent Sparse Autoencoders: Learning Feature-Specific Timescales in Language Model Representations
2607.17117.tldr: This work introduces Persistent Sparse Autoencoders (Persistent SAEs), an extension of standard SAEs that learns a persistence coefficient for each feature, allowing the model to learn feature-specific timescales from reconstruction alone.

2605.06342.title: Don't Lose Focus: Activation Steering via Key-Orthogonal Projections
2605.06342.tldr: This work proposes Steering via Key-Orthogonal Projections (SKOP), a steering method that constrains harmful attention rerouting without eliminating steering efficacy, and shows that SKOP achieves the best joint steering-utility trade-off.

2607.05615.title: A Coin Flip Per Token: Bernoulli Sparse Steering of Large Language Models
2607.05615.tldr: Stochastic Token Steering (STS), which gates each token independently with probability $p$, and Stochastic Block Steering (SBS), which gates a leading window once per sequence are introduced; neither requires a reward model or learned gating policy.

2508.17540.title: Activation Transport Operators
2508.17540.tldr: This work proposes Activation Transport Operators (ATO), linear maps from upstream to downstream residuals later, evaluated in feature space using downstream SAE decoder projections, and develops the notion of transport efficiency, for which it is used to estimate the size of the residual stream subspace that corresponds to linear transport.

2607.19386.title: Building Fast, Evaluating Slow: Pipeline Choices Dominate Autointerpretability Score Variance
2607.19386.tldr: It is found that methodological variance collectively exceeds architectural variance across all metrics and tested models, suggesting that cross-paper comparisons based on autointerpretability scores may reflect pipeline differences rather than architectural differences, with implications for the ongoing debate on SAE utility.

2606.29888.title: Same Concept, Different Directions: Cross-Modal Feature Heterogeneity in Sparse Autoencoders
2606.29888.tldr: An approach that trains modality-specific sparse autoencoders to preserve each modality's feature geometry, and then aligns corresponding features post hoc is proposed, which improves reconstruction fidelity and enhances performance in cross-modal retrieval and concept steering.

2608.26136.title: Reward-Informed Sparse Autoencoders and the Solution-Completeness Confound

2606.26629.title: From Weights to Features: SAE-Guided Activation Regularization for LLM Continual Learning
2606.26629.tldr: This paper derives a new loss function that uses the SAE feature dictionary to explicitly balance stability and plasticity, and shows that EWC is a special case in the one-sided weight-space penalty setting.

2603.08095.title: DC-W2S: Dual-Consensus Weak-to-Strong Training for Reliable Process Reward Modeling in Biological Reasoning
2603.08095.tldr: It is demonstrated that DC-W2S enables the training of robust PRMs for complex reasoning without exhaustive expert annotation, proving that strategic data curation is more effective than indiscriminate training on large-scale noisy datasets.

2606.24716.title: Evaluating the Interpretability of Sparse Autoencoders with Concept Annotations
2606.24716.tldr: A human-grounded evaluation framework that quantifies alignment between SAE latents and human-annotated concepts, without requiring user studies, and validate this matching through targeted attribute perturbations, suggests that moderate dictionary sizes provide the best trade-off, yielding the most interpretable SAEs.

2606.18383.title: From Sparse Features to Trustworthy Proxies: Certifying SAE-Based Interpretability
2606.18383.tldr: A post-hoc generalization framework that certifies the LM via a sparse proxy, obtained by replacing a native hidden activation with its pretrained SAE reconstruction, and derives an upper bound on the base model's expected risk using four measurable quantities.

2609.03781.title: IndicSafeEval: Safety Robustness of Large Language Models under Multilingual Persuasive Jailbreak Attacks
2609.03781.tldr: IndicSafeEval, a persuasion-based jailbreak evaluation framework for Indian languages, is introduced and it is observed that different risk categories exhibit different levels of vulnerability, with some types of harmful content being significantly more susceptible to persuasion-based jailbreaks than others.

2606.16193.title: Cascaded Sparse Autoencoders Learn Multi-Level Visual Concepts in Multimodal LLMs
2606.16193.tldr: Experiments show that CSAEs improve interpretability in terms of hierarchical concept coherence over state-of-the-art SAE baselines, and results on concept steering further demonstrate that the learned concept groups support effective group-level interventions in MLLM outputs.

2607.25132.title: Interpretable GOHR Agents via Sparse Autoencoders
2607.25132.tldr: This work reports interpretability experiments for a tokenized autoregressive Transformer agent in the Game of Hidden Rules (GOHR), a compact two-rule task in which both hidden rules map object shapes to target buckets, but with different permutations.

2603.03205.title: Learning When to Act or Refuse: Guarding Agentic Reasoning Models for Safe Multi-Step Tool Use
2603.03205.tldr: MOSAIC reduces harmful behavior by up to 50%, increases harmful-task refusal by over 20% on injection attacks, cuts privacy leakage, and preserves or improves benign task performance, demonstrating robust generalization across models, domains, and agentic settings.

2605.07447.title: Sparse Autoencoders as Plug-and-Play Firewalls for Adversarial Attack Detection in VLMs
2605.07447.tldr: This work proposes a novel and lightweight adversarial attack detection framework based on sparse autoencoders (SAEs), termed SAEgis, which requires no additional adversarial training, introduces minimal overhead, and provides a practical approach for improving the safety of real-world VLM systems.

2506.01247.title: Beyond Interpretability: When, Why, and How Sparse Autoencoders Enable Label-Free Visual Steering
2506.01247.tldr: Visual Sparse Steering (VS2), a label-free method that trains a top-$k SAE on unlabeled activations from a frozen CLIP image encoder and constructs an interpretable steering vector by amplifying the input's active sparse features and decoding the induced change, is introduced.

2412.17626.title: Tracking the Feature Dynamics in LLM Training: A Mechanistic Study
2412.17626.tldr: SAE-Track is introduced, a novel method for efficiently obtaining a continual series of SAEs, providing the foundation for a mechanistic study that covers the semantic evolution of features, the underlying processes of feature formation, and the directional drift of feature vectors.

2604.13304.title: Can Cross-Layer Transcoders Replace Vision Transformer Activations? An Interpretable Perspective on Vision
2604.13304.tldr: It is shown that CLTs achieve high reconstruction fidelity with post-MLP activations while preserving and even improving, in some cases, CLIP zero-shot classification accuracy and interpretability, and that the cross-layer contribution scores provide faithful attribution.

2605.11922.title: StepCodeReasoner: Aligning Code Reasoning with Stepwise Execution Traces via Reinforcement Learning
2605.11922.tldr: This work proposes StepCodeReasoner, a framework that introduces explicit intermediate execution-state supervision, and introduces Bi-Level GRPO, a reinforcement learning algorithm for structured credit assignment at two levels: inter-trajectory, comparing alternative execution paths, and intra-trajectory, rewarding intermediate accuracy based on its impact on downstream correctness.

2601.10589.title: Be Your Own Red Teamer: Safety Alignment via Self-Play and Reflective Experience Replay
2601.10589.tldr: Safety Self- Play (SSP) is introduced, a system that utilizes a single LLM to act concurrently as both the Attacker and the Defender within a unified Reinforcement Learning (RL) loop, dynamically evolving attack strategies to uncover vulnerabilities while simultaneously strengthening defense mechanisms.
2601.10589.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2607.10269.title: Devil in the Lens: Analyzing and Defending Physical Prompt Injection Against Vision-Language Models on Wearable Devices
2607.10269.tldr: This work characterizes how malicious textual information embedded in physical environments introduces a high-priority visual channel for indirect prompt injection, and proposes two targeted defense strategies to effectively reduce the success rate and safety impact of these attacks.

2606.10029.title: Interpreting and Steering a Text-to-Speech Language Model with Sparse Autoencoders
2606.10029.tldr: A modality-aware auto-interp pipeline is introduced that labels each feature from where it fires-text-prefix context, 1-second speech clips, or both, and shows these features are interpretable, spanning phonemes, laughter, accent prompts and speaker gender.

2606.06735.title: A Geometric Account of Activation Steering through Angle-Norm Decomposition
2606.06735.tldr: This work revisits the assumption that hidden-state norm does not carry concept-relevant information and suggests that activation steering should be parameterized by interpretable angular and radial components of the intervention, rather than by a single additive coefficient that entangles these two effects.

2505.22255.title: Kronecker Factorization Improves Efficiency and Interpretability of Sparse Autoencoders
2505.22255.tldr: KronSAE is proposed, a design that factorizes the latent space into heads and forms post-latent features as pairwise compositions of lower-dimensional pre-latents using mAND, a differentiable AND-like interaction that imposes a compositional co-activation prior while remaining compatible with standard SAE objectives and variants.

2410.07656.title: Mechanistic Permutability: Match Features Across Layers
2410.07656.tldr: SAE Match is introduced, a novel, data-free method for aligning SAE features across different layers of a neural network that effectively captures feature evolution across layers, improving feature matching quality and providing a new tool for mechanistic interpretability studies.

2509.06608.title: Small Vectors, Big Effects: A Mechanistic Study of RL-Induced Reasoning via Steering Vectors
2509.06608.tldr: Lightweight steering vectors inserted into the base model's residual stream and trained with a reinforcement-learning objective explain a large portion of full fine-tuning performance increase while preserving the interpretability of small, additive interventions.

2606.09735.title: The Neutral Mask: How Alignment Training Provides Shallow Alignment while Leaving Partisan Structure Intact in a Large Language Model
2606.09735.tldr: It is shown that alignment training does not remove the structured partisan direction in the base model, Instead, it compresses the variance of the partisan signal to generate consistently balanced and non-partisan output.

2606.08365.title: Pre-Intervention Prediction of Sparse Autoencoder Steering Side Effects
2606.08365.tldr: A pre-intervention screening framework for forecasting SAE steering side effects from feature statistics computed before steering is introduced, and side effects along two axes of steering modularity, effect stability and collateral spread are operationalized.

2606.01479.title: Sparse Autoencoders for Interpretable Emotion Control in Text-to-Speech
2606.01479.tldr: This work analyzes emotion-related variation in the semantic hidden states of LLM-based TTS models using sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to identify sparse latent features and introduces a feature-level intervention framework for bidirectional emotion induction and suppression without modifying backbone parameters.

2607.20479.title: Beyond Liars' Bench: The Impact of Lie Typology, Depth, and Sparsity on Deception Detection in LLMs
2607.20479.tldr: It is demonstrated that the choice of training data and lie typology substantially changes detectability, highlighting that deception detection is a highly representation-dependent problem.

2609.00351.title: Detecting Hidden Behaviors in LLMs via Activation-matched Finetuning

2605.31183.title: Steering LLMs? Actually, Sparse Autoencoders can outperform simple baselines
2605.31183.tldr: This work finds that Sparse Autoencoders can, in fact, perform close to on par with the reference LoRA performance on the AxBench benchmark, when features are selected and labelled with the supervised pipeline.

2605.30162.title: BioRefusalAudit: Auditing Biosecurity Refusal Depth Using General and Domain-Fine-Tuned Sparse Autoencoders
2605.30162.tldr: Preliminary evidence suggests activation-level auditing may surface failure modes invisible to behavioral evaluation, with substantial variation across architectures, which suggests refusal tracks legality and cultural salience over CBRN hazard.

2605.28567.title: Semantic Optimal Transport for Sparse Autoencoder Feature Matching and Circuit Compression
2605.28567.tldr: This work introduces a distributional framework for SAE analyses, in which each feature is represented not by a single decoder vector like in the literature, but by an activation-weighted distribution over the hidden states that express it, and provides a unified semantic metric for cross-layer feature comparison.

2605.07922.title: Tree SAE: Learning Hierarchical Feature Structures in Sparse Autoencoders
2605.07922.tldr: This work proposes the Tree SAE, a model designed to learn hierarchical structures directly from within the feature set, and demonstrates that Tree SAEs significantly surpass the existing SAEs at learning hierarchical pairs while maintaining competitive performance to the state-of-the-art on several key benchmarks.

2605.28149.title: Sign-Aware Gated Sparse Autoencoders: Modeling Anticorrelated Features with Bi-Jump-ReLU Activations
2605.28149.tldr: This work proposes the Sign-Aware Gated SAE (SA-GSAE), which combines two-sided gated sparsity, signed shrinkage-free magnitudes, and auxiliary gate supervision in a new Bi-Jump-ReLU activation, so that a single latent carries both polarities of one decoder direction.

2605.24977.title: Universal Boosts, Specific Suppressors: Sparse Autoencoder Steering of Medical Vision-Language Models
2605.24977.tldr: The authors' inference-only method improves the quality of generated reports for three radiology VLMs, with relative improvements of +5.4%, +7.2%, and +17.0% in the clinical composite metric, and statistically significant GREEN gains on all backbones.

2605.24946.title: Interpretability Transfer from Language to Vision via Sparse Autoencoders
2605.24946.tldr: This paper introduces Visual Interpretability via SAE Transfer Alignment (VISTA), a framework that transfers interpretability from language to vision in a LLaVA-style vision-language model by constraining a visual projector to map visual tokens into an LLM's pre-existing, labeled textual SAE space, and shows that DINOv2 features have stronger localization abilities than other encoders.

2605.22902.title: Transcoders Trace Visual Grounding and Hallucinations in Vision-Language Models
2605.22902.tldr: A function-centric framework based on Transcoders, sparse approximations of MLP sublayers that act as a causal proxy for layer-wise computation yields interpretable and predictive accounts of multimodal computation in VLMs.

2605.22658.title: SegCompass: Exploring Interpretable Alignment with Sparse Autoencoders for Enhanced Reasoning Segmentation
2605.22658.tldr: SegCompass is an end-to-end model that leverages a Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) to forge an explicit, interpretable, and differentiable alignment pathway, and provides a "white-box" connection that is significantly more traceable than latent queries and more coherent than textual readouts.

2605.28023.title: VCap: Hypergeometric Rewards for Weak-to-Strong Visual Captioning
2605.28023.tldr: VCap is proposed, a Witness-Adjudicator reward that pairs the reference caption (a witness) with the visual signal (an adjudicator) with hypergeometric-distribution-level precision for caption quality verification, facilitating weak-to-strong generalization in RL training.

2605.22462.title: From Correlation to Cause: A Five-Stage Methodology for Feature Analysis in Transformer Language Models

2605.18229.title: Are Sparse Autoencoder Benchmarks Reliable?
2605.18229.tldr: The sae-probes variant of $k$-sparse probing is the most reliable metric, but even sae-probes struggles to separate variants of the same SAE architecture, and the results show the field needs better SAE benchmarks.

2605.15961.title: Sparse Autoencoders enable Robust and Interpretable Fine-tuning of CLIP models
2605.15961.tldr: SAE-FT regularizes changes to the model's visual representations by penalizing the addition and removal of semantically meaningful features identified by a Sparse Autoencoder trained on the pre-trained model, which prevents catastrophic forgetting and makes the fine-tuning process interpretable, enabling direct analysis of semantic changes.

2605.12874.title: Descriptive Collision in Sparse Autoencoder Auto-Interpretability: When One Explanation Describes Many Features
2605.12874.tldr: A property called discrimination is formalized, it is proved that current detection-style auto-interpretability scoring is invariant to collision, and two complementary corrective metrics -- collision-adjusted detection and discrimination scoring -- are proposed that explicitly penalize explanations that fail to distinguish a feature from its neighbors.

2605.24577.title: Polymorphism Is Rotation: Operational Mechanistic Interpretability from a Two-Layer Transformer to Pythia-70m
2605.24577.tldr: It is shown that an orthogonal Procrustes fit on a single batch of activations transfers sparse-autoencoder feature dictionaries and steering vectors between independently trained models, with no retraining.

2605.12770.title: WriteSAE: Sparse Autoencoders for Recurrent State
2605.12770.tldr: This work introduces WriteSAE, a sparse autoencoder for the matrix updates written into recurrent language-model state and reports the first cache-level steering intervention reported in a state-space or hybrid recurrent layer.

2605.12055.title: Do Language Models Encode Knowledge of Linguistic Constraint Violations?
2605.12055.tldr: A sensitivity score is introduced for identifying features that are preferentially activated on constraint-violated versus well-formed inputs, enabling unsupervised detection of potential violation-specific features and proposes a conjunctive falsification framework with three criteria evaluated jointly.

2605.18808.title: Compositional Literary Primitives in Instruction-Tuned LLMs: Cross-Architectural SAE Features for Self, Style, and Affect
2605.18808.tldr: A compositional architecture of literary primitives in two instruction-tuned large language models, including a single most-RLHF-loaded self-feature per architecture that intensifies the institutional Helper-AI persona at one operating regime and produces affect-categorizable output at the same calibrated coefficient is characterized.

2606.09850.title: Mechanistic Analysis of Alignment Algorithms in Language Models
2606.09850.tldr: It is found that preference signals consistently concentrate in early--mid or mid--late layers, but different objectives induce qualitatively distinct representational shifts, demonstrating that behavioral alignment does not imply uniform internal restructuring.

2603.25035.title: Mechanistically Interpreting Compression in Vision-Language Models
2603.25035.tldr: It is shown that pruning causes a sharp drop in genuine refusal behavior, suggesting that the choice of compression has safety implications, and introduces VLMSafe-420, a novel benchmark that pairs harmful inputs with matched benign counterfactuals across various safety categories.

2509.07456.title: Bias-Aware Machine Unlearning: Towards Fairer Vision Models via Controllable Forgetting
2509.07456.tldr: It is demonstrated that post-hoc unlearning can substantially reduce subgroup disparities, with improvements in demographic parity of up to 94.86% on CUB-200, 30.28% on CIFAR-10, and 97.37% on CelebA.
2509.07456.venue: 2025 IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision Workshops (ICCVW)

2609.17552.title: Does Moral Reasoning Training Help or Hurt? Red-Teaming RL-Trained Ethical Agents with Persona Attacks
2609.17552.tldr: Moral RL builds robustness that is partly linear and partly circuit-distributed, transferable through activation steering, yet still beaten by named-character role-play.

2604.08557.title: Re-Mask and Redirect: Exploiting Denoising Irreversibility in Diffusion Language Models
2604.08557.tldr: It is shown that violating this assumption, by re-masking committed refusal tokens and injecting a short affirmative prefix, achieves 74-82% ASR on HarmBench across all three publicly available safety-tuned dLLMs, rising to 92-98% with a generic 8-token compliance prefix.

2604.26866.title: MoRFI: Monotonic Sparse Autoencoder Feature Identification
2604.26866.tldr: It is validated that incrementally introducing new knowledge increases hallucinations, with the effect being more pronounced with prolonged training, and proposed Monotonic Relationship Feature Identification (MoRFI) for capturing causally relevant latents.

2604.23829.title: Domain-Filtered Knowledge Graphs from Sparse Autoencoder Features
2604.23829.tldr: A strict domain-specific concept universe is constructed from a large SAE inventory using contrastive activations and a multi-stage filtering process, and two aligned graph views are built that convert feature-level interpretability into a global map of model knowledge and enables audits of reasoning faithfulness.

2606.29522.title: When Does Activation Steering Change What a Model Computes From?
2606.29522.tldr: A successful steering intervention need not reproduce the natural target activation at the intervention layer, and an intervention should be interpreted as changing the computational state only when a later computation uses the edited value according to the semantics of that state.

2604.18756.title: Towards Understanding the Robustness of Sparse Autoencoders
2604.18756.tldr: Parametric ablations reveal a monotonic dose-response relationship between L0 sparsity and attack success rate, and a layer-dependent defense-utility tradeoff, where intermediate layers balance robustness and clean performance.
2604.18756.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2604.25716.title: Cross-Lingual Jailbreak Detection via Semantic Codebooks
2604.25716.tldr: This work compares multilingual query embeddings against a fixed English codebook of jailbreak prompts, operating as a training-free external guardrail for black-box LLMs, and reveals two distinct regimes of cross-lingual transfer.

2609.01046.title: HiveTraceGuard-Pro: A Compact Generative Guardrail for Prompt Injection, Jailbreaks, and Adversarial Obfuscation
2609.01046.tldr: This work presents HiveTraceGuard-Pro, a 0.6B generative guardrail LoRA-tuned from Qwen3-0.6B that has the highest clean Russian robustness combined-F1 and Russian prompt-injection recall and releases the merged weights on Hugging Face under Apache-2.0.

2604.12384.title: Preventing Safety Drift in Large Language Models via Coupled Weight and Activation Constraints
2604.12384.tldr: This paper proposes Coupled Weight and Activation Constraints (CWAC), a novel approach that simultaneously enforces a precomputed safety subspace on weight updates and applies targeted regularization to safety-critical features identified by sparse autoencoders.
2604.12384.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2605.04072.title: Sparse Autoencoder Decomposition of Clinical Sequence Model Representations: Feature Complexity, Task Specialisation, and Mortality Prediction
2605.04072.tldr: Under full-sequence simple linear probes, SAE features outperform dense representations for discrete event prediction (mortality) while dense representations outperform for continuous magnitude prediction (length of stay) - a probe-level representational phenomenon that does not extend to clinically relevant leakage-safe windows.

2604.16430.title: HalluSAE: Detecting Hallucinations in Large Language Models via Sparse Auto-Encoders
2604.16430.tldr: HalluSAE, a phase transition-inspired framework that models hallucination as a critical shift in the model's latent dynamics, identifies critical transition zones and attributes factual errors to specific high-energy sparse features.

2604.09253.title: Mosaic: Multimodal Jailbreak against Closed-Source VLMs via Multi-View Ensemble Optimization
2604.09253.tldr: Mosaic is proposed, a Multi-view ensemble optimization framework for multimodal jailbreak against closed-source VLMs, which alleviates surrogate dependency under heterogeneous surrogate-target settings by reducing over-reliance on any single surrogate model and visual view.

2604.03532.title: LangFIR: Discovering Sparse Language-Specific Features from Monolingual Data for Language Steering
2604.03532.tldr: LangFIR (Language Feature Identification via Random-token Filtering), a method that discovers language-specific SAE features using only a small amount of monolingual data and random-token sequences to suggest that language identity in multilingual LLMs is localized in a sparse set of feature directions discoverable with monolingual data.

2506.20040.title: Cross-Layer Discrete Concept Discovery for Interpreting Language Models
2506.20040.tldr: Across both encoder- and decoder-based models on ERASER-Movie, Jigsaw, and AGNews, CLVQ-VAE outperforms clustering, single-layer vector quantized-variational autoencoder (VQ-VAE), and sparse autoencoder (SAE) baselines across three evaluation axes.

2609.01878.title: GAPS: Dimension-Level Gates for Conditional Activation Steering
2609.01878.tldr: The method, GAPS, combines two training-free gates: a static separability gate that restricts steering to neurons with statistically reliable concept information (via AUROC) and a dynamic posterior gate that steers a neuron only when its current activation is better explained by the undesired concept under a Gaussian model.

2512.10903.title: Multi-Granular Node Pruning for Causal Circuit Discovery
2512.10903.tldr: This work proposes a node-level pruning framework for circuit discovery that addresses both scalability and granularity limitations, and introduces learnable masks across multiple levels of granularity, from entire blocks to individual neurons, within a unified optimization objective.

2607.22929.title: Distribution-Specific Curvature Control with Finite-Sample Guarantees for Open-Weight Safety
2607.22929.tldr: HarmAlign proposes HarmAlign, which applies function-preserving spectral deformation along a estimated contrastive activation subspace and derives finite-sample bounds for the estimated subspace energy and the resulting local harmful-distribution curvature lower bound.

2409.12914.title: Evaluating Defences against Unsafe Feedback in RLHF
