2603.20620.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2608.20393.title: Knowledge-Graph-Gated Defactualization for Style-Controllable and Fact-Preserving Generation in Agentic Conversational AI
2608.20393.tldr: Results demonstrate that explicit knowledge engineering can systematically enhance trustworthy, controllable, and reproducible generative AI without requiring model fine-tuning.

2606.21147.title: AOR-Bench: Do Large Audio Language Models Over-Refuse Pseudo-Harmful Queries?
2606.21147.tldr: Evaluating 12 representative LALMs from six major model families, it is found that over-refusal is widespread and several important patterns in their safety judgments are uncovered, and two lightweight strategies are explored to reduce over-refusal.

2602.07013.title: Steering to Say No: Configurable Refusal via Activation Steering in Vision Language Models

2609.16191.title: When AI Says "I Am Unable to Answer": Understanding User Responses to AI Refusals
2609.16191.tldr: A tension between hallucination avoidance and user satisfaction is revealed and the importance of designing balanced refusal strategies is highlighted, to highlight the importance of designing balanced refusal strategies.

2607.00023.title: Aligning Sentence Embeddings to Human Concepts via Sparse Autoencoders
2607.00023.tldr: This work proposes a method to disentangle the dense representations of sentence transformers into human-interpretable concepts using Top-k Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs), and suggests that SAE-based decomposition offers a viable path toward transparent and steerable neural information retrieval.

2606.20852.title: Translating Inference-Time Control to Radiology Vision-Language Models: Activation Steering for Pneumonia Classification on Chest X-rays
2606.20852.tldr: meaningful performance gains were observed in one of three evaluated VLMs, suggesting that activation steering may serve as a lightweight approach for adapting medical VLM behavior.

2606.19946.title: GEMS: Geometric Constraints Enable Multi-Semantic Superposition in LLMs
2606.19946.tldr: GEMS is proposed, a training-free method that maps each source to a corresponding geometric constraint: norm-preserving weighted superposition and targeted attention-pathway injection for distributional deviation, and real-time orthogonalization for directional interference.

2608.03892.title: Intertemporal Preference Steering in Qwen3 via Contrastive Activation Addition
2608.03892.tldr: The central result is that temporal-horizon directions can be identified with simple contrastive linear probes and then used for steering to induce large, bidirectional preference changes, suggesting that model intertemporal preferences are measurable and steerable.

2606.15092.title: High-Dimensional Random Projection for Activation Steering in Language Models
2606.15092.tldr: High-Dimensional Random-projection for Activation Steering (HiDRA), a training-free approach that integrates seamlessly with existing activation steering methods, can provably capture a better discriminative structure beyond the reach of linear methods.

2606.10929.title: Recoverable but Not Stationary:Local Linear Structures in Weights and Activations
2606.10929.tldr: The results suggest that linear structures in trained networks are not global task directions, but evolving local geometries that partially persist across parameter and activation spaces.

2606.08454.title: Beyond Linear Activation Steering: Invertible Latent Transformations for Controlling LLM Behavior
2606.08454.tldr: INNSteer is a nonlinear activation steering framework based on invertible latent transformations that consistently improves model control over linear, transport-based, and nonlinear steering baselines while largely preserving generation fluency.

2601.03093.title: ATLAS: Verifier-Guided Adaptive Latent Activation Steering for Efficient LLM Reasoning
2601.03093.tldr: Experiments show that ATLAS consistently outperforms both vanilla decoding and fixed steering baselines, achieving higher accuracy while substantially reducing test-time token usage, and demonstrate that verifier-guided latent adaptation provides an effective and scalable mechanism for controlling reasoning efficiency without sacrificing solution quality.

2606.07696.title: Adversarial Robustness of Activation Steering in Large Language Models
2606.07696.tldr: The first systematic evaluation of activation steering robustness under adversarial text perturbations on the inputs reveals that the brittleness of activation steering is structural rather than method-specific, and that current layer selection strategies are not robust enough for real-world deployment.

2606.08243.title: Building Comparative Motivation Profiles with Instrumental Interventions

2508.14031.title: Unintended Misalignment from Agentic Fine-Tuning: Risks and Mitigation
2508.14031.tldr: This work proposes Prefix INjection Guard (PING), a simple yet effective method that prepends automatically generated natural language prefixes to agent responses, guiding them to refuse harmful requests while preserving performance on benign tasks.

2501.05790.title: Understanding Impact of Human Feedback via Influence Functions
2501.05790.tldr: A compute-efficient approximation method is proposed that enables the application of influence functions to LLM-based reward models and large-scale preference datasets and can enhance feedback interpretability and contribute to scalable oversight in RLHF, helping labelers provide more accurate and consistent feedback.
2501.05790.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2601.10543.title: Defending Large Language Models Against Jailbreak Attacks via In-Decoding Safety-Awareness Probing
2601.10543.tldr: This work examines the decoding process of LLMs and proposes a simple yet effective approach that explicitly surfaces and leverages latent safety signals for early detection of unsafe content during decoding, suggesting that activating intrinsic safety-awareness during decoding offers a promising and complementary direction for defending against jailbreaks.

2608.18089.title: Latent Space Refusal Anchoring for Low-Resource African Languages: Mechanistic Safety Recovery Without Retraining
2608.18089.tldr: This work introduces Latent Space Refusal Anchoring (LSR-Anchoring), a training-free method that extracts the refusal direction from English prompts and clamps it onto the residual stream at inference time.

2603.19273.title: LSR: Linguistic Safety Robustness Benchmark for Low-Resource West African Languages
2603.19273.tldr: This work introduces LSR (Linguistic Safety Robustness), the first systematic benchmark for measuring cross-lingual refusal degradation in West African languages: Yoruba, Hausa, Igbo, and Igala, and introduces Refusal Centroid Drift (RCD), a metric that quantifies how much of a model's English refusal behavior is lost when harmful intent is encoded in a target language.

2607.19364.title: SAE-StatSteer: Statistical Consensus Feature Selection for Optimization-Free Activation Steering of Large Language Models
2607.19364.tldr: This work introduces SAE-StatSteer, a transparent, optimization-free pipeline that remains competitive with optimization-based methods while exposing every selection and weighting decision for audit, and evaluates three Gemma-family models across four behavioral domains against seven dense or SAE-based baselines.

2606.07313.title: SV-Detect: AI-generated Text Detection with Steering Vectors
2606.07313.tldr: This work proposes an AI-generated text detector based on steering vectors extracted from the hidden representations of a frozen language model that achieves strong performance both in-distribution and under distribution shift, including across domains, source models, and machine-editing transformations such as polishing and rewriting.

2605.30381.title: Linear Separability of Activation Representations after Supervised Fine-Tuning on Incorrect Responses: A Study of Synthetic Dishonesty in Large Language Models
2605.30381.tldr: It is shown that LoRA fine-tuning itself leaves a strong activation fingerprint that is largely dissociable from the honesty-related signal, independent of fine-tuning data content.

2605.28664.title: Activation Steering for Synthetic Data Generation: The Role of Diversity in Downstream Safety Detection
2605.28664.tldr: This two-fold study presents a two-fold study with intrinsic and extrinsic evaluation across Activation Steering methods, and introduces sample- and set-level diversity as a quality axis previously absent from the literature.

2605.27676.title: Unsupervised Identification and Removal of Spurious Correlations During Fine-Tuning
2605.27676.tldr: GRASP, GRadient projection of Associated Spurious Patterns is proposed, which prevents the model from acquiring new reliance on the identified latent factor while preserving any pretrained content along it, which is validated on three fine-tuning tasks.

2412.16475.title: When Can Proxies Improve the Sample Complexity of Preference Learning?
2412.16475.tldr: This work outlines a set of sufficient conditions on proxy feedback that indicate that proxy data can provably improve the sample complexity of learning the ground truth policy, and implies a parameterisation for LLMs that achieves this improved sample complexity.

2605.26365.title: Cultural Value Alignment Via Latent Activation Steering in Large Language Models
2605.26365.tldr: This work establishes a computationally efficient framework for cultural steering, highlighting the structural complexities when navigating global value with LLMs and proposes a generalizable framework for cultural evaluation and intervention that transitions from abstract queries to scenario-based behavioral probing.

2605.17658.title: When a Zero-Shooter Cheats: Improving Age Estimation via Activation Steering
2605.17658.tldr: An activation steering method is proposed that suppresses the identity shortcut of VLM-based age estimation by intervening on the hidden states of the VLM, which improves age estimation accuracy for both memorized and unseen identities.

2605.17231.title: FishBack: Pullback Fisher Geometry for Optimal Activation Steering in Transformers
2605.17231.tldr: A closed-form steering direction is derived, applied to a hidden state at an intermediate layer, that reaches a target concept change with the least non-target distortion, and it is shown that geometric correction retains its advantage on larger models with more complex internal structure.

2606.05743.title: Membrane: A Self-Evolving Contrastive Safety Memory for LLM Agent Defense
2606.05743.tldr: Across model-level safety on HarmBench and agent-level safety on AgentHarm, Membrane achieves the highest F1 on all six modern jailbreak attacks, and benign refusal on AgentHarm stays at 7-14%, well below the 28-85% range of prior guards.

2607.14111.title: Introspection Fine-Tuning (IFT): Training Small LLMs to Introspect
2607.14111.tldr: The results suggest that introspective ability is not fixed by scale alone: it can be directly trained, and doing so unlocks latent self-monitoring capacity with implications for AI transparency and alignment.

2606.09073.title: A Unifying Lens on Reward Uncertainty in RLHF
2606.09073.tldr: The pessimistic branch unifies the prior heuristics for RM ensemble aggregation: mean aggregation, worst-case optimization (WCO), and uncertainty-weighted optimization (UWO) all emerge as limits or truncations of this single expression.

2605.08254.title: HyperTransport: Amortized Conditioning of T2I Generative Models
2605.08254.tldr: By decoupling concept representation from intervention prediction, HyperTransport combines three capabilities that no existing approach offers as a set: amortized steering for open-ended concept sets, continuous interpretable strength control, and cross-modal conditioning where reference images can directly steer text-based generation.

2503.10679.title: LinEAS: End-to-end Learning of Activation Steering with a Distributional Loss
2503.10679.tldr: LinEAS is modality-agnostic and empirically find that it outperforms existing activation steering methods at mitigating and including new concepts at the output of single-step text-to-image generation models, becoming competitive with oracle-dependent methods that have access to strong supervision.

2502.15090.title: ExpertLens: Activation steering features are highly interpretable
2502.15090.tldr: It is found that ExpertLens representations are stable across models and datasets and closely align with human representations inferred from behavioral data, matching inter-human alignment levels and suggesting that ExpertLens is a flexible and lightweight approach for capturing and analyzing model representations.

2512.03661.title: Dynamically Scaled Activation Steering
2512.03661.tldr: D Dynamically Scaled Activation Steering (DSAS) is introduced, a method-agnostic steering framework that decouples when to steer from how to steer, and adaptively modulates the strength of existing steering transformations across layers and inputs.

2602.12418.title: Sparse Autoencoders are Capable LLM Jailbreak Mitigators
2602.12418.tldr: Off-the-shelf SAEs trained for interpretability can be repurposed as practical jailbreak defenses without task-specific training and clearly outperforms dense mean-shift steering on all four models, showing that steering in sparse SAE feature space offers advantages over steering in dense activation space for jailbreak mitigation.

2605.15030.title: WARD: Adversarially Robust Defense of Web Agents Against Prompt Injections
2605.15030.tldr: This work proposes WARD (Web Agent Robust Defense against Prompt Injection), a practical guard model for secure and efficient web agents, and introduces A3T, an adaptive adversarial attack training framework that iteratively strengthens WARD through a memory-based attacker and guard co-evolution process.

2605.05892.title: Beyond Steering Vector: Flow-based Activation Steering for Inference-Time Intervention
2605.05892.tldr: FLAS (Flow-based Activation Steering), which learns a general, concept-conditioned velocity field $v_t(h,t,c)$ that transports unsteered activations to steered ones without relying on unvalidated simplifying assumptions, is proposed.

2406.03199.title: Bayesian WeakS-to-Strong from Text Classification to Generation
2406.03199.tldr: This work extends Weak-to-Strong to WeakS-to-Strong by exploring an ensemble of weak models which simulate the variability in human opinions, and direct preference optimization is applied to advance the student model's preference learning, beyond the basic learning framework of teacher forcing.

2605.03907.title: Steer Like the LLM: Activation Steering that Mimics Prompting

2605.01167.title: Minimizing Collateral Damage in Activation Steering
2605.01167.tldr: This work provides a mathematical formalization of collateral damage and introduces a principled framework that models steering as a constrained optimization problem and finds a new activation that minimizes the expected squared collateral change weighted by the empirical second-moment matrix of activations.

2604.20945.title: Breaking Bad: Interpretability-Based Safety Audits of State-of-the-Art LLMs
2604.20945.tldr: The results establish interpretability-based steering as a powerful tool for systematic safety audits, but also highlight its dual-use risks and the need for better internal defenses in LLM deployment.

2606.11205.title: Dual-Stance Evaluation of Sycophancy: The Structure of Agreement and the Limits of Intervention

2604.12616.title: Every Picture Tells a Dangerous Story: Memory-Augmented Multi-Agent Jailbreak Attacks on VLMs
2604.12616.tldr: It is demonstrated that benign natural images can act as transferable jailbreak anchors and reveal substantial vulnerabilities in current safety-aligned VLMs, demonstrating superior jailbreak effectiveness on VLMs.

2605.05223.title: Structural Instability of Feature Composition
2605.05223.tldr: This work presents a geometric framework for analyzing the instability of feature unions, and derives an asymptotic compositional-collapse threshold under a spherical dictionary model, characterized by the Gaussian mean width of the signal cone.

2604.11120.title: Persona Non Grata: Single-Method Safety Evaluation Is Incomplete for Persona-Imbued LLMs
2604.11120.tldr: Heuristic trace diagnostics suggest that the safer model retains stronger policy recall and self-correction behavior, not merely longer reasoning, and testing with only one method can miss a model's dominant failure mode.

2503.18013.title: Vision-R1: Evolving Human-Free Alignment in Large Vision-Language Models via Vision-Guided Reinforcement Learning
2503.18013.tldr: This work proposes Vision-R1, a novel vision-guided R1-like reinforcement learning algorithm for LVLMs that rewards models with definitive vision feedback, and introduces a progressive rule refinement strategy that dynamically adjusts the reward criteria during training, enabling continuous model improvement and mitigating reward hacking.

2603.10091.title: Multi-Stream Perturbation Attack: Breaking Safety Alignment of Thinking LLMs Through Concurrent Task Interference
2603.10091.tldr: This work designs three perturbation strategies: multi-stream interleaving, inversion perturbation, and shape transformation, which disrupt the thinking process through concurrent task interleaving, character reversal, and format constraints respectively, and achieves attack success rates exceeding most methods across mainstream models.

2512.13703.title: Safe2Harm: Semantic Isomorphism Attacks for Jailbreaking Large Language Models
2512.13703.tldr: The Safe2Harm Semantic Isomorphism Attack method is proposed, which achieves efficient jailbreaking through four stages: first, rewrite the harmful question into a semantically safe question with similar underlying principles; second, extract the thematic mapping relationship between the two; third, let the LLM generate a detailed response targeting the safe question; finally, reversely rewrite the safe response based on the thematic mapping relationship to obtain harmful output.

2604.08844.title: Spectral Geometry of LoRA Adapters Encodes Training Objective and Predicts Harmful Compliance
2604.08844.tldr: These results establish that within a controlled manufacturing regime, LoRA weight-space geometry carries objective identity, intensity ordering, and a coarse link to harmful compliance, and that cross-method monitoring requires per-method calibration.

2604.08169.title: Activation Steering for Aligned Open-ended Generation without Sacrificing Coherence
2604.08169.tldr: Three methods to substantially recover alignment in LLMs are implemented, and honesty steering generalizes to out-of-distribution scenarios: a single honesty direction extracted from the aligned model significantly raises scores on the MASK benchmark, suppresses deception in multi-agent settings, doubles the hidden-behavior discovery rate on AuditBench, and restores honesty in an emergently misaligned model.

2604.07102.title: Persona Matters: Effects of Activation Steering on Short Answer Generation and Scoring
2604.07102.tldr: The first study to systematically examine the effects of activation-steered persona traits in educational generation and scoring on the ASAP-SAS benchmark, and highlights the need for task- and architecture-aware calibration when deploying personalized models in educational settings.

2603.21398.title: Persona Vectors in Games: Measuring and Steering Strategies via Activation Vectors
2603.21398.tldr: This work uses activation steering methods in game-theoretic settings, constructing persona vectors for altruism, forgiveness, and expectations of others by contrastive activation addition, and finds that activation steering systematically shifts both quantitative strategic choices and natural-language justifications.

2603.20795.title: The Anatomy of an Edit: Mechanism-Guided Activation Steering for Knowledge Editing
2603.20795.tldr: By pinpointing where and how edits take hold, it powers MEGA to deliver reliable, architecture-agnostic knowledge edits, and is proposed, a MEchanism-Guided Activation steering method that performs attention-residual interventions in attribution-aligned regions without modifying model weights.

2603.18893.title: Quantitative Introspection in Language Models: Tracking Emotive States Across Conversation
2603.18893.tldr: It is found that greedy-decoded self-reports collapse outputs to few uninformative values, but introspective capacity can be unmasked by calculating logit-based self-reports, and numeric self-report is position as a viable, complementary tool for tracking internal emotive states in conversational AI systems.

2603.05977.title: Activation Steering for Accent-Neutralized Zero-Shot Text-To-Speech
2603.05977.tldr: Empirical results demonstrate that the proposed steering vectors effectively mitigate the output accent and exhibit strong generalizability to unseen accented speakers, offering a practical solution for accent-free voice cloning.

2602.21704.title: Dynamic Multimodal Activation Steering for Hallucination Mitigation in Large Vision-Language Models
2602.21704.tldr: Dynamic Multimodal Activation Steering proposes a semantic-based truthfulness steering vector database and computes visual perception steering vectors, enabling context-aware interventions during inference by dynamically selecting the most relevant steering vectors based on input semantic similarity and applying them to the most influential attention heads.

2602.14143.title: ROAST: Rollout-based On-distribution Activation Steering Technique
2602.14143.tldr: ROAST (Rollout-based On-distribution Activation Steering Technique), which estimates steering directions from the model's own on-distribution rollouts via ROC and avoids hard sparsification via Continuous Soft Scaling and Grouped Mean Normalization and Grouped Mean Normalization.

2603.03326.title: Controllable and explainable personality sliders for LLMs at inference time

2606.30116.title: Open Problems in Constitutional Preference Reconstruction
2606.30116.tldr: It is highlighted that constitutions should be evaluated as constitution--executor systems, with implications for LLMs-as-a-judge broadly, and that principle refinement (ICAI+) may be a first step towards ameliorating these problems.

2603.03323.title: Discern Truth from Falsehood: Reducing Over-Refusal via Contrastive Refinement
2603.03323.tldr: Evaluation across diverse benchmarks shows that the DCR: Discernment via Contrastive Refinement method effectively reduces over-refusal while preserving the safety benefits of alignment, offering a more principled and robust direction for safety alignment.

2609.18515.title: Beyond Routine Compliance: Cunning Data Cultivates Safety Vigilance in Large Language Models
2609.18515.tldr: Experiments show that Cunning training improves robustness to out-of-distribution jailbreak attacks and strengthens subsequent safety fine-tuning, and suggest that cunning data can strengthen model vigilance and complement conventional safety alignment.

2608.11698.title: REOPD: Reliability-Adaptive Reward Extrapolation for On-Policy Distillation
2608.11698.tldr: REOPD combines a token-level compatibility weight with a batch-level adaptive budget, yielding a token-wise coefficient $\lambda_{b,t}=1+\gamma_b q_t$ that preserves teacher alignment while selectively extrapolating along reliable teacher-reference directions, demonstrating effective fine-grained reliability adaptation across domains and teacher configurations.

2602.07639.title: Letting Tutor Personas Speak Up for LLMs: Learning Steering Vectors from Dialogue via Preference Optimization
2602.07639.tldr: This paper explores how tutor personas embedded in human tutor-student dialogues can be used to guide LLM behavior without relying on explicitly prompted instructions, and finds that activation steering offers an effective and interpretable way for controlling tutor-specific variation in LLMs using signals derived directly from human dialogue data.
2602.07639.venue: Workshop on Innovative Use of NLP for Building Educational Applications

2602.07276.title: Steer2Adapt: Dynamically Composing Steering Vectors Elicits Efficient Adaptation of LLMs
2602.07276.tldr: STEER2ADAPT is a lightweight framework that adapts LLMs by composing steering vectors rather than learning new ones from scratch, and is a data-efficient, stable, and transparent inference-time adaptation method for LLMs.

2504.07316.title: Alice: Proactive Learning with Teacher's Demonstrations for Weak-to-Strong Generalization
2504.07316.tldr: Alice is introduced, a framework that leverages complementary knowledge between teacher and student to enhance the learning process and significantly enhances the W2SG performance, yielding substantial improvements in three key tasks compared to the original W2SG.

2602.04428.title: Fine-Grained Activation Steering: Steering Less, Achieving More
2602.04428.tldr: AUSteer, a simple and efficient method that operates at a finer granularity of the AU level, is proposed that consistently surpasses advanced baselines while steering considerably fewer activations, demonstrating that steering less achieves more.

2601.22873.title: EmoShift: Lightweight Activation Steering for Enhanced Emotion-Aware Speech Synthesis
2601.22873.tldr: EmoShift, a lightweight activation-steering framework incorporating a EmoSteer layer, which learns a steering vector for each target emotion in the output embedding space to capture its latent offset and maintain stable, appropriate expression across utterances and categories, is presented.
2601.22873.venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing

2601.22010.title: Exploring Diverse Generation Paths via Inference-time Stiefel Activation Steering
2601.22010.tldr: STARS is a training-free, inference-time intervention method that transforms activation steering into an exploration engine that consistently outperforms standard sampling methods, achieving greater diversity without sacrificing qualitative performance.

2511.08305.title: Test-time Diverse Reasoning by Riemannian Activation Steering
2511.08305.tldr: Empirical evaluations on popular mathematical benchmarks demonstrate that the test-time Riemannian activation steering strategy outperforms vanilla sampling techniques in terms of generative diversity and solution accuracy.

2601.21505.title: The Effectiveness of Style Vectors for Steering Large Language Models: A Human Evaluation
2601.21505.tldr: The first human evaluation of activation steering concerning the emotional tone of LLM outputs is presented, collecting over 7,000 crowd-sourced ratings from 190 participants via Prolific and support activation-based control as a scalable method for steering LLM behavior across affective dimensions.

2601.19375.title: Selective Steering: Norm-Preserving Control Through Discriminative Layer Selection
2601.19375.tldr: This work proposes Selective Steering, a mathematically rigorous norm-preserving rotation formulation that maintains activation distribution integrity and discriminative layer selection that applies steering only where feature representations exhibit opposite-signed class alignment.
2601.19375.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2601.03699.title: RedBench: A Universal Dataset for Comprehensive Red Teaming of Large Language Models
2601.03699.tldr: RedBench is introduced, a universal dataset aggregating 37 benchmark datasets from leading conferences and repositories, comprising 29,362 samples across attack and refusal prompts, enabling consistent and comprehensive evaluations of LLM vulnerabilities.

2601.16398.title: White-Box Sensitivity Auditing with Steering Vectors
2601.16398.tldr: A white-box sensitivity auditing framework for LLMs that leverages activation steering to conduct more rigorous assessments through model internals and consistently indicates substantial dependence on protected attributes in model predictions, even in settings where standard black-box evaluations suggest little or no bias.

2601.09269.title: RISER: Orchestrating Latent Reasoning Skills for Adaptive Activation Steering
2601.09269.tldr: Router-based Intervention for Steerable Enhancement of Reasoning, a plug-and-play intervention framework that adaptively steers LLM reasoning in activation space that autonomously combines multiple vectors into interpretable, precise control strategies, pointing toward more controllable and efficient LLM reasoning.
2601.09269.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2601.08489.title: Surgical Refusal Ablation: Disentangling Safety from Intelligence via Concept-Guided Spectral Cleaning
2601.08489.tldr: SRA achieves deep refusal reduction with negligible perplexity impact on Wikitext-2 and shows SRA preserves math and code distributions, suggesting that common model damage is often "Ghost Noise," defined as the spectral bleeding of the dirty refusal direction into capability subspaces.

2601.04131.title: ContextFocus: Activation Steering for Contextual Faithfulness in Large Language Models
2601.04131.tldr: This work introduces ContextFocus, a lightweight activation steering approach that improves context faithfulness in such knowledge-conflict settings while preserving fluency and efficiency, and highlights the effectiveness, robustness, and efficiency of ContextFocus in improving contextual-faithfulness of LLM outputs.

2512.16602.title: Refusal Steering: Fine-grained Control over LLM Refusal Behaviour for Sensitive Topics
2512.16602.tldr: Results demonstrate that activation steering can remove political refusal behaviour while retaining safety alignment for harmful content, offering a practical path to controllable, transparent moderation at inference time.
2512.16602.venue: International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation

2512.06655.title: Graph-Regularized Sparse Autoencoders for LLM Safety Steering
2512.06655.tldr: Graph-Regularized Sparse Autoencoders (GSAE), a dictionary-learning method that learns safety-steering directions by smoothing SAE decoder vectors over a neuron co-activation graph and applying the resulting direction bank through a two-gate runtime controller, is introduced.

2605.22880.title: How Far Will They Go? Red-Teaming Online Influence with Large Language Models
2605.22880.tldr: An empirical red-teaming framework for measuring LLM Overton Windows is introduced, defined as the range of political opinions a model can reliably express on controversial topics, and for quantifying how simple natural-language jailbreaks expand that range.

2511.18284.title: What Can We Actually Steer? A Multi-Behavior Study of Activation Control
2511.18284.tldr: This work empirical analysis of activation steering across 50 behaviors that span persona archetypes, personality traits, misalignment behaviors, style cues, and impersonation of public figures demonstrates that steering effectiveness varies significantly by behavior type.

2509.24065.title: AI Safety, Alignment, and Ethics (AI SAE)
2509.24065.tldr: A governance--embedding--representation pipeline linking moral representation learning to system-level design and institutional governance is proposed, treating alignment as a multi-level problem spanning cognition, optimization, and oversight.

2509.22067.title: The Rogue Scalpel: Activation Steering Compromises LLM Safety
2509.22067.tldr: It is shown that precise control over model internals does not guarantee precise control over model behavior, and it is shown that combining 20 randomly sampled vectors that jailbreak a single prompt creates a universal attack.

2509.22739.title: Painless Activation Steering: An Automated, Lightweight Approach for Post-Training Large Language Models
2509.22739.tldr: PAS constructs a fast, lightweight activation vector that can be cheaply trained, easily stored, and activated at will, and provides a characterization of where AS helps, where it fails, and how to deploy it as a practical, automated LM post-training option.

2509.20623.title: Latent Activation Editing: Inference-Time Refinement of Learned Policies for Safer Multirobot Navigation
2509.20623.tldr: A framework for inference-time Latent Activation Editing (LAE) that refines the behavior of pre-trained policies without modifying their weights or architecture is introduced, establishing LAE as a lightweight paradigm, feasible on resource-constrained hardware, for post-deployment refinement of learned robot policies.

2509.00373.title: Activation Steering Meets Preference Optimization: Defense Against Jailbreaks in Vision Language Models
2509.00373.tldr: Sequence-Level Preference Optimization for VLM is proposed, a novel two-stage defense framework that combines activation-level intervention with policy-level optimization to enhance model robustness and enhances safety against attacks via activation steering and preference optimization.

2607.19674.title: FedLSG: LLM-Enhanced Semantic Calibration for Federated Graph Backdoor Defense
2607.19674.tldr: FedLSG, the first framework that integrates large language models (LLMs) into federated graph backdoor defense, introduces a graph and behavior to text grounding scheme that transforms local graph structures and client update behaviors into semantically rich natural language representations.

2502.01472.title: FALCON: Fine-grained Activation Manipulation by Contrastive Orthogonal Unalignment for Large Language Model
2502.01472.tldr: Fine-grained Activation manipuLation by Contrastive Orthogonal uNalignment (FALCON), a novel representation-guided unlearning approach that leverages information-theoretic guidance for efficient parameter selection, employs contrastive mechanisms to enhance representation separation, and projects conflict gradients onto orthogonal subspaces to resolve conflicts between forgetting and retention objectives.

2508.03543.title: EmoSteer-TTS: Fine-Grained and Training-Free Emotion-Controllable Text-to-Speech via Activation Steering
2508.03543.tldr: EmoSteer-TTS enables fine-grained, interpretable, and continuous control over speech emotion, outperforming the state-of-the-art (SOTA) and is the first method that achieves training-free and continuous fine-grained emotion control in TTS.

2605.18168.title: Acoustic Interference: A New Paradigm Weaponizing Acoustic Latent Semantic for Universal Jailbreak against Large Audio Language Models
2605.18168.tldr: It is demonstrated that interference audio, benign in content but infused with specific ALS, can serve as a universal jailbreak trigger, and the Acoustic Interference Attack (AIA), which decouples the attack payload from the audio, is proposed.

2507.13236.title: Enhancing Cross-task Transfer of Large Language Models via Activation Steering
2507.13236.tldr: This paper proposes CAST, a novel Cross-task Activation Steering Transfer framework that enables effective transfer by manipulating the model's internal activation states and first selects influential and diverse samples from high-resource tasks, then utilizes their contrastive representation-enhanced activations to adapt LLMs to low-resource tasks.

2507.11771.title: Scaling laws for activation steering with Llama 2 models and refusal mechanisms
2507.11771.tldr: This paper explores the effectiveness of CAA with model scale using the family of Llama 2 models and found that 1) CAA is most effective when applied at early-mid layers, and 2) The effectiveness of CAA diminishes with model size.

2506.18831.title: Adaptive Activation Steering for Efficient LLM Reasoning via Closed-Loop PID Control
2506.18831.tldr: PID-steering is described, a training-free, decoding-time method that modulates the steering strength with a PID controller driven by a lightweight chunk-level redundancy classifier.

2506.10225.title: Genre Controlled Music Generation via Activation Steering
2506.10225.tldr: This work presents a method for fine grained control using inference-time interventions on an autoregressive generative transformer, MusicGen, to achieve genre control by steering the residual stream using weights of a linear probe on it.

2605.18104.title: Safety Geometry Collapse in Multimodal LLMs and Adaptive Drift Correction
2605.18104.tldr: ReGap, a training-free inference-time method that adaptively corrects modality drift using self-rectification, is proposed, which significantly improves the safety of MLLMs without compromising general capabilities.

2506.04909.title: When Thinking LLMs Lie: Unveiling the Strategic Deception in Representations of Reasoning Models
2506.04909.tldr: Through activation steering, this work achieves a 40% success rate in eliciting context-appropriate deception without explicit prompts, unveiling the specific honesty-related issue of reasoning models and providing tools for trustworthy AI alignment.

2505.20309.title: Guiding Giants: Lightweight Controllers for Weighted Activation Steering in LLMs
2505.20309.tldr: This work introduces a novel approach using a lightweight, trainable controller network integrated during inference, presenting an efficient and adaptive method for fine-grained control over LLM behavior at inference time.
2505.20309.venue: Proceedings of the 6th Workshop on Trustworthy NLP (TrustNLP 2026)

2504.14492.title: FairSteer: Inference Time Debiasing for LLMs with Dynamic Activation Steering
2504.14492.tldr: Comprehensive evaluation with six LLMs demonstrates the superiority of FairSteer across question-answering, counterfactual input evaluation and open-ended text generation tasks.
2504.14492.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2503.06040.title: Mitigating Memorization in LLMs using Activation Steering
2503.06040.tldr: This work explores the effectiveness of activation steering in reducing memorization while preserving generalization capabilities in Large Language Models and demonstrates that this method successfully suppresses memorized content with minimal degradation in model performance in Gemma.

2411.18247.title: A gentle push funziona benissimo: making instructed models in Italian via contrastive activation steering
2411.18247.tldr: Italian steering can be successfully applied to different models, achieves performances comparable to, or even better than, fine-tuned models for Italian, and yields higher quality and consistency in Italian generations.

2411.16721.title: Steering Away from Harm: An Adaptive Approach to Defending Vision Language Model Against Jailbreaks
2411.16721.tldr: ASTRA is an efficient and effective defense by adaptively steering models away from adversarial feature directions to resist VLM attacks, resulting in little performance drops on benign inputs while strongly avoiding harmful outputs under adversarial inputs.

2606.09068.title: Emergent Misalignment Can Be Induced by Sycophancy and Reversed via Alignment Gating
2606.09068.tldr: This work identifies sycophancy fine-tuning, i.e., training models to passively agree with users' incorrect opinions, as a previously underexplored driver of emergent misalignment, and proposes Alignment Gating, an efficient method for reversing emergent misalignment that inserts learnable and controllable gates into the model during fine-tuning.

2408.11491.title: SCANS: Mitigating the Exaggerated Safety for LLMs via Safety-Conscious Activation Steering
2408.11491.tldr: A Safety-Conscious Activation Steering (SCANS) method to mitigate the exaggerated safety concerns in aligned LLMs, which achieves new state-of-the-art performance on XSTest and OKTest benchmarks, without impairing their defense capability against harmful queries and maintaining almost unchanged model capability.

2406.00244.title: Controlling Large Language Model Agents with Entropic Activation Steering
2406.00244.tldr: Entropic Activation Steering (EAST) is introduced, an activation steering method for in-context LLM agents that can effectively manipulate an LLM agent's exploration by directly affecting the high-level actions parsed from the outputs of the LLM, in contrast to token-level temperature sampling.

2406.00034.title: Adaptive Activation Steering: A Tuning-Free LLM Truthfulness Improvement Method for Diverse Hallucinations Categories
2406.00034.tldr: This work treats truthfulness as a specially linearly encoded concept within LLMs, and introduces Adaptive Activation Steering (ACT), a tuning-free method that adaptively shifts LLM's activations in the ''truthful'' direction during inference.

2606.04145.title: EvalStop: Using World Feedback to Detect and Correct Reward Overoptimization in Multi-Tenant RLHF Platforms
2606.04145.tldr: EvalStop is a composable scheduling primitive that terminates jobs on k consecutive eval-score declines, releases GPUs, preserves the best checkpoint, and delegates to any base scheduler, frame scheduler-level early stopping as a detection problem and evaluate it in a discrete-event simulator.

2404.01903.title: Understanding How CodeLLMs (Mis)Predict Types with Activation Steering
2404.01903.tldr: This work examines the task of type prediction: given a partially typed program, can a model predict a missing type annotations such that the resulting program is more typed and restores accurate predictions on adversarial inputs.
2404.01903.venue: Proceedings of the 8th BlackboxNLP Workshop: Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP

2402.00402.title: Investigating Bias Representations in Llama 2 Chat via Activation Steering
2402.00402.tldr: This work reveals inherent gender bias in Llama 2 7B Chat, persisting even after Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), and uncovers that RLHF tends to increase the similarity in the model's representation of different forms of societal biases, which raises questions about the model's nuanced understanding of different forms of bias.

2512.24842.title: Triangulation as an Acceptance Rule for Multilingual Mechanistic Interpretability

2512.23043.title: Mechanistic Evidence for Preserved-but-Misaligned Representations in Non-IID FedAvg
2512.23043.tldr: Diagnostics suggest that, in the setting of sparse client-trained vision models, non-IID FedAvg degradation is not fully explained by representational erasure; it also reflects misalignment between preserved internal structure and the final prediction pathway.

2508.01728.title: Granular Concept Circuits: Toward a Fine-Grained Circuit Discovery for Concept Representations
2508.01728.tldr: An effective circuit discovery method, called Granular Concept Circuit (GCC)*, in which each circuit represents a concept relevant to a given query, which is the first to identify circuits tied to specific visual concepts at a fine-grained level.
2508.01728.venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision

2609.13198.title: SPICE: Simple Polysemantic Feature Interpretation via Clustering-based Explanation
2609.13198.tldr: SPICE avoids architecture-dependent propagation rules, enabling the first systematic comparison of polysemanticity across both CNNs and Transformers, and automatically determines the number of concept clusters per neuron, eliminating reliance on a preset $K$ and supporting scalable analysis for large models.

2607.20473.title: Incomplete Prompt Jailbreaks in Large Language Models
2607.20473.tldr: This work formalizes this phenomenon as incomplete prompt jailbreaks (IPJ) and provides a systematic empirical characterization of when and how incomplete prompts elicit harmful continuations, and identifies two functional neurons: termination and continuation neurons.
2607.20473.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2504.07389.title: Task-Circuit Quantization: Leveraging Knowledge Localization and Interpretability for Compression
2504.07389.tldr: TaCQ contrasts unquantized model weights with a uniformly-quantized model to estimate the expected change in weights due to quantization and uses gradient information to predict the resulting impact on task performance, allowing TaCQ to preserve task-specific weights.

2410.08025.title: The Computational Complexity of Circuit Discovery for Inner Interpretability
2410.08025.tldr: It is proved there exist transformations to tackle some of these hard problems with better-understood heuristics, and the tractability or fixed-parameter tractability of more modest queries which retain useful affordances are proved.

2401.03646.title: Evaluating Brain-Inspired Modular Training in Automated Circuit Discovery for Mechanistic Interpretability
2401.03646.tldr: This study demonstrates how BIMT significantly improves the efficiency and quality of Automated Circuit Discovery, overcoming the limitations of manual methods, and reveals that BIMT outperforms existing models in terms of circuit quality, discovery time, and sparsity.

2608.30902.title: Low-Resource Preference Adaptation of LLMs via Activation-Based Label Propagation
2608.30902.tldr: This paper investigates how language models encode preference information in their intermediate representations, finding that activations from chosen and rejected responses form distinct clusters across layers, even in pretrained models.

2608.20999.title: Latent Ordinal Evidence, Misaligned Outputs: Inference-Time Ordinal Lens Alignment for Multimodal LLMs
2608.20999.tldr: This work introduces Ordinal Lens Alignment (OLA), a frozen-backbone inference-time method that trains lightweight W_S-anchored lenses on mid-to-deep decoder layers, fuses them into an ordinal distribution, and corrects only digit-token logits at generation.

2608.08024.title: Prompt Embedding Probes (PEP): Hallucination Detection in LLMs from Hidden States
2608.08024.tldr: Results show that prompt-based adaptation can strengthen hidden-state probing while keeping the backbone frozen and adding only a small number of trainable parameters, as well as improving hidden-state-based detection over standard linear probes in the main in-distribution setting.

2607.14147.title: Breaking Refusal in the First Half: A Mechanistic Study of the Prefill Jailbreak

2609.02893.title: Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection
2609.02893.tldr: The results suggest that the OOD robustness of probes is largely determined by subspace selection, and projecting inputs onto a small subset of principal components from the training distribution of activations enables cross-domain transfer that nearly matches the performance of probes trained directly on the test distribution.

2605.09391.title: Do Linear Probes Generalize Better in Persona Coordinates?
2605.09391.tldr: It is shown that persona-derived directions transfer non-trivially and probes trained on persona-PC projections generalize better than probes trained on raw activations, and a unified axis consisting of multiple harmful and harmless behaviors improves generalization across behaviors and datasets.

2605.14347.title: Exemplar Partitioning for Mechanistic Interpretability
2605.14347.tldr: Exemplar Partitioning (EP), an unsupervised method for building interpretable feature dictionaries from large language model activations, is introduced and demonstrated how it can be used to interpret and intervene on model behaviour, track changes in activation space through training, and detect hidden concepts.

2604.23460.title: Ulterior Motives: Detecting Misaligned Reasoning in Continuous Thought Models
2604.23460.tldr: It is demonstrated that continuous thought models can exhibit misaligned latent reasoning while producing aligned outputs, with aligned and misaligned reasoning occupying geometrically distinct regions of latent space, and misalignment is encoded in early latent thinking tokens, suggesting safety monitoring for continuous thought models should target the planning phase of latent reasoning.

2604.10643.title: LogitDynamics: Reliable ViT Error Detection from Layerwise Logit Trajectories
2604.10643.tldr: A simple method that models how class evidence evolves across layers, and improves or matches AUCPR over baselines and shows stronger cross-dataset generalization while requiring minimal additional computation is proposed.

2603.19426.title: Is Evaluation Awareness Just Format Sensitivity? Limitations of Probe-Based Evidence under Controlled Prompt Structure
2603.19426.tldr: It is found that standard probe-based methodologies do not reliably disentangle evaluation context from structural artifacts, limiting the evidential strength of existing results.

2602.11166.title: Small Updates, Big Doubts: Does Parameter-Efficient Fine-tuning Enhance Hallucination Detection ?
2602.11166.tldr: Experimental results show that PEFT consistently strengthens hallucination detection ability, substantially improving AUROC across a wide range of hallucination detectors, and indicates that PEFT methods primarily reshapes how uncertainty is encoded and surfaced, comparing with injecting new factual knowledge into the models.

2601.10307.title: The Straight and Narrow: Do LLMs Possess an Internal Moral Path?
2601.10307.tldr: Leveraging the high generalizability of morality, Adaptive Moral Fusion (AMF) is proposed, a dynamic inference-time intervention that synergizes probe detection with vector injection to tackle the safety-helpfulness trade-off.

2512.20949.title: Neural Probe-Based Hallucination Detection for Large Language Models
2512.20949.tldr: Experimental results on LongFact, HealthBench, and TriviaQA demonstrate that MLP probes significantly outperform state-of-the-art methods in accuracy, recall, and detection capability under low false-positive conditions.

2509.21344.title: Linear probes rely on textual evidence: Results from leakage mitigation studies in language models
2509.21344.tldr: Evidence that removing textual evidence of a behaviour significantly decreases probe performance is found, suggesting that linear probes may be brittle in scenarios where they must detect non-surface-level patterns.

2602.16931.title: Narrow Fine-Tuning Erodes Safety Alignment in Vision-Language Agents
2602.16931.tldr: It is demonstrated that fine-tuning aligned vision-language models on narrow-domain harmful datasets induces severe emergent misalignment that generalizes broadly across unrelated tasks and modalities, highlighting the need for robust continual learning frameworks.

2604.11609.title: Intersectional Sycophancy: How Perceived User Demographics Shape False Validation in Large Language Models
2604.11609.tldr: It is argued that safety evaluations should incorporate identity-aware adversarial testing, and it is found that sycophancy varies sharply with target model and domain, and emerges from combinations of perceived user traits rather than any single dimension.

2602.11157.title: Response-Based Knowledge Distillation for Multilingual Jailbreak Prevention Unwittingly Compromises Safety
2602.11157.tldr: This exploratory study introduces a novel application of knowledge distillation (KD) in the context of multilingual jailbreak prevention, examining its efficacy and highlights the challenges and potential of KD as a technique for multilingual safety alignment.

2507.12428.title: Can We Predict Alignment Before Models Finish Thinking? Towards Monitoring Misaligned Reasoning Models
2507.12428.tldr: It is found that a simple linear probe trained on CoT activations significantly outperforms all text-based baselines in predicting whether a final response is safe or unsafe, with an average absolute increase of 13 in F1 scores over the best-performing alternatives.

2510.20956.title: Self-Jailbreaking: Language Models Can Reason Themselves Out of Safety Alignment After Benign Reasoning Training
2510.20956.tldr: This work provides the first systematic analysis of self-jailbreaking behavior and offers a practical path forward for maintaining safety in increasingly capable RLMs.

2310.02446.title: Low-Resource Languages Jailbreak GPT-4
2310.02446.tldr: This work exposes the inherent cross-lingual vulnerability of these safety mechanisms, resulting from the linguistic inequality of safety training data, by successfully circumventing GPT-4's safeguard through translating unsafe English inputs into low-resource languages.

2505.11741.title: MTRE: Multi-Token Reliability Estimation for Hallucination Detection in VLMs
2505.11741.tldr: Multi-Token Reliability Estimation (MTRE), a lightweight, white-box method that aggregates logits from the first ten tokens using multi-token log-likelihood ratios and self-attention, is introduced, establishing a new state of the art in hallucination detection for open-source VLMs.

2405.05466.title: Poser: Unmasking Alignment Faking LLMs by Manipulating Their Internals
2405.05466.tldr: A benchmark that consists of 324 pairs of LLMs fine-tuned to select actions in role-play scenarios is introduced, and one of which identifies 98% of alignment-fakers is tested.

2403.09037.title: The First to Know: How Token Distributions Reveal Hidden Knowledge in Large Vision-Language Models?
2403.09037.tldr: This study uses linear probing to shed light on the hidden knowledge at the output layers of LVLMs, demonstrating that the logit distributions of the first tokens contain sufficient information to determine whether to respond to the instructions, including recognizing unanswerable visual questions, defending against jailbreaking attacks, and identifying deceptive questions.

2303.06854.title: Robust Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training against Data Poisoning and Backdoor Attacks
2303.06854.tldr: This work proposes ROCLIP, the first effective method for robust pre-training multimodal vision-language models against targeted data poisoning and backdoor attacks against CLIP models and renders state-of-the-art targeted data poisoning and backdoor attacks ineffective during pre-training CLIP models.

2502.00620.title: Representations Shape Weak-to-Strong Generalization: Theoretical Insights and Empirical Predictions
2502.00620.tldr: It is shown that W2SG can be characterized using kernels derived from the principal components of weak and strong models' internal representations' internal representations, providing insights into how certain errors in weak supervision can be corrected by the strong model, regardless of overfitting.

2609.18440.title: Planning or Improvisation? Stress-Testing the Poetry Planning Site on Open Models and Open Cross-Layer Transcoders
2609.18440.tldr: It is reported that Claude 3.5 Haiku plans rhymes: features for candidate rhyme words are active on the newline before a line is written, and a suppress-and-inject intervention redirects the line only when applied there (their Figure 13), and how far this generalizes is tested.

2604.24936.title: A Unifying Framework for Unsupervised Concept Extraction
2604.24936.tldr: A general meta-theorem for identifiability is presented, which reduces the problem of establishing identifiability guarantees to the problem of characterizing the intersection of two sets, thus paving the way for the development of new, principled approaches for concept extraction.

2604.01604.title: CRaFT: Circuit-Guided Refusal Feature Selection via Cross-Layer Transcoders
2604.01604.tldr: CRaFT is a circuit-guided framework for identifying critical refusal features that directly govern the refusal decision that leverages cross-layer transcoders to map the model's internal computations into a sparse feature circuit graph, where edges quantify inter-feature influences and their contributions to the final output logits.

2603.21484.title: Which Concepts to Forget and How to Refuse? Decomposing Concepts for Continual Unlearning in Large Vision-Language Models
2603.21484.tldr: A novel continual unlearning framework that grounds refusal behavior in fine-grained descriptions of visual and textual concepts decomposed from deletion targets, and introduces a multimodal, concept-driven routing scheme that reuses refusers for tasks sharing similar concepts and adapts underutilized ones for novel concepts.

2603.05805.title: Sparse Crosscoders for diffing MoEs and Dense models
2603.05805.tldr: This work presents a systematic comparison of MoE and dense model internals using crosscoders, a variant of sparse autoencoders that jointly models multiple activation spaces that jointly models multiple activation spaces.

2602.11729.title: Cross-Architecture Model Diffing with Crosscoders: Unsupervised Discovery of Differences Between LLMs
2602.11729.tldr: This work provides the first application of crosscoders to cross-architecture model diffing and introduces Dedicated Feature Crosscoders (DFCs), an architectural modification designed to better isolate features unique to one model.

2601.12879.title: Hierarchical Sparse Circuit Extraction from Billion-Parameter Language Models through Scalable Attribution Graph Decomposition
2601.12879.tldr: HAGD addresses the challenge of extracting sparse circuits from billion-parameter transformers through cross-layer transcoder training, spectral coarsening of attribution graphs, graph-neural-network (GNN)-guided hierarchical traversal, and causal intervention verification, reducing worst-case complexity to $O(n^2 \log n)$.

2601.07835.title: SecureCAI: Injection-Resilient LLM Assistants for Cybersecurity Operations
2601.07835.tldr: This paper introduces SecureCAI, a novel defense framework extending Constitutional AI principles with security-aware guardrails, adaptive constitution evolution, and Direct Preference Optimization for unlearning unsafe response patterns, addressing the unique challenges of high-stakes security contexts where traditional safety mechanisms prove insufficient against sophisticated adversarial manipulation.

2511.22539.title: TransCoder: A Neural-Enhancement Framework for Channel Codes
2511.22539.tldr: This paper designs a neural transmission scheme that employs the transformer architecture in order to improve the reliability of existing ECCs and demonstrates that TransCoder significantly improves block error rate (BLER) performance while maintaining computational complexity comparable to traditional decoders.

2511.18687.title: Evaluation of NVENC Split-Frame Encoding (SFE) for UHD Video Transcoding
2511.18687.tldr: Evaluating Split-Frame Encoding’s impact on RD performance, encoding throughput, power consumption, and end-to-end latency shows that for real-time applications, SFE nearly doubles encoding throughput with a negligible RD performance penalty, which enables the use of higher-quality presets for $\mathbf{4 K}$ and makes real-time 8 K encoding feasible, effectively offsetting the minor RD penalty.

2509.14723.title: Transcoder-based Circuit Analysis for Interpretable Single-Cell Foundation Models
2509.14723.tldr: This work trains a transcoder on the cell2sentence (C2S) model, a state-of-the-art scFM, and extracts internal decision-making circuits from the C2S model, confirming the potential of transcoders to uncover biologically plausible pathways within complex single-cell models.

2405.04471.title: Universal Spatial Audio Transcoder
2405.04471.tldr: This paper addresses the challenges associated with both the conversion between different spatial audio formats and the decoding of a spatial audio format to a specific loudspeaker layout, and presents the Universal Spatial Audio Transcoder (USAT) method and its corresponding open source implementation.

2304.08634.title: Filling the gaps in video transcoder deployment in the cloud
2304.08634.tldr: This paper considers preprocessing, rate/distortion optimisation and cloud cost prediction tools which are only just emerging from the research community as part of the per-clip optimisation approach to transcoding.

2609.18346.title: Faithful yet Collusive: Why Chain-of-Thought Monitoring Cannot Detect Collusion in LLM Pricing Agents under Oligopolistic Competition

2609.06704.title: Counterfactual Tests for Measuring Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness in Visual Language Models
2609.06704.tldr: The analysis shows that CoTs do not reliably track visual evidence that influences model predictions, and it is found that Predict-then-Explain explanations align more strongly with perturbation-induced probability shifts than pre-answer CoTs, while binary vCT scores are often nearly saturated.

2608.15392.title: Visible Reasoning and Indirect Prompt-Injection Monitorability Across English, Tamil, and Tanglish

2607.07229.title: Reasoning Consistency Scanning: A Framework for Auditing Chain-of-Thought Validity in AI Safety Evaluations
2607.07229.tldr: This work formalizes reasoning consistency as distinct from faithfulness and defines a six-subtype taxonomy of inconsistency, showing that reasoning inconsistency is present, detectable, and varies systematically across both models and task types.

2605.00224.title: TUR-DPO: Topology- and Uncertainty-Aware Direct Preference Optimization
2605.00224.tldr: TUR-DPO is proposed, a topology- and uncertainty-aware variant of DPO that rewards how answers are derived, not only what they say, by eliciting lightweight reasoning topologies and combining semantic faithfulness, utility, and topology quality into a calibrated uncertainty signal.

2603.13791.title: DeceptGuard :A Constitutional Oversight Framework For Detecting Deception in LLM Agents
2603.13791.tldr: A transparency-detectability trade-off is empirically characterized: as agents learn to suppress overt behavioral signals, chain-of-thought becomes the primary detection surface but is itself increasingly unreliable due to post-training faithfulness degradation.

2605.27545.title: PAST2HARM: A Simple Adaptive Past Tense Attack for Jailbreaking Multimodal AI
2605.27545.tldr: PAST2HARM is introduced, a simple yet effective adaptive jailbreak framework that bypasses refusal training in state of the art multimodal text to image models and exposes fundamental brittleness in current safeguards and highlights the need for stronger multimodal safety training.

2603.06652.title: PaLMR: Towards Faithful Visual Reasoning via Multimodal Process Alignment
2603.06652.tldr: PaLMR offers a principled and practical route to process-aligned multimodal reasoning, advancing the reliability and interpretability of MLLMs and achieving state-of-the-art results on HallusionBench while maintaining strong performance on MMMU, MathVista, and MathVerse.

2510.19476.title: A Concrete Roadmap towards Safety Cases based on Chain-of-Thought Monitoring
2510.19476.tldr: A roadmap for constructing safety cases based on chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring in reasoning models and a two-part safety case establishing that models lack dangerous capabilities when operating without their CoT, and ensuring that any dangerous capabilities enabled by a CoT are detectable by CoT monitoring.

2508.16213.title: MedOmni-45°: A Safety-Performance Benchmark for Reasoning-Oriented LLMs in Medicine
2508.16213.tldr: MedOmni-45 Degrees is introduced, a benchmark and workflow designed to quantify safety-performance trade-offs under manipulative hint conditions and provides a consistent safety-performance trade-off, with no model surpassing the diagonal.

2508.13743.title: Sycophancy under Pressure: Evaluating and Mitigating Sycophantic Bias via Adversarial Dialogues in Scientific QA
2508.13743.tldr: Pressure-Tune is proposed, a lightweight post-training method that fine-tunes models on synthetic adversarial dialogues paired with chain-of-thought rationales that reject user misinformation while reinforcing factual commitments, and is shown to significantly enhances sycophancy resistance.

2605.26497.title: Aligning Provenance with Authorization: A Dual-Graph Defense for LLM Agents
2605.26497.tldr: AuthGraph is the first agent security defense to structurally compare authorization specifications against execution provenance at the parameter-source level, achieving fine-grained injection detection without sacrificing agent flexibility.

2609.00264.title: The Answer Is Not the Argument
2609.00264.tldr: Although the errors studied here were ordinary and mostly non-load-bearing rather than adversarial, trusted-answer evaluations may similarly overstate monitoring capability when acceptable outputs conceal unsound reasoning.

2601.12822.title: MirrorGuard: Toward Secure Computer-Use Agents via Simulation-to-Real Reasoning Correction

2605.05983.title: Towards Steering without Sacrifice: Principled Training of Steering Vectors for Prompt-only Interventions
2605.05983.tldr: This work proposes joint training of steering factors and directions, such that post-hoc factor selection is no longer required, and introduces Prompt-only SV (PrOSV), an SV that intervenes only on a few prompt tokens.

2601.07263.title: When Bots Take the Bait: Exposing and Mitigating the Emerging Social Engineering Attack in Web Automation Agent
2601.07263.tldr: This work reveals AgentBait as a critical new threat surface for web agents and establishes a practical, generalizable defense, advancing the security of this rapidly emerging ecosystem.

2608.24037.title: Curved Inference II: Sleeper Agent Geometry - Extending Interpretability Beyond Probes
2608.24037.tldr: This paper extends Anthropic's Sleeper Agents research, and validates that sophisticated reasoning creates intrinsic geometric patterns that persist even when detection appears to fail, suggesting the shape of inference itself encodes semantic patterns regardless of whether models have learned to suppress linear indicators of deception.

2603.25861.title: Why Safety Probes Catch Liars But Miss Fanatics
2603.25861.tldr: Training with belief-consistent reasoning shifts models from a detectable"deceptive"regime to an undetectable"coherent"regime - not by learning to hide, but by learning to believe.

2603.08760.title: Clear, Compelling Arguments: Rethinking the Foundations of Frontier AI Safety Cases
2603.08760.tldr: Overall, this paper contributes holistic insights from the field of safety assurance via rigorous theory and methodologies that have been applied in safety-critical contexts via rigorous theory and methodologies that have been applied in safety-critical contexts.

2507.20150.title: The Policy Cliff: A Theoretical Analysis of Reward-Policy Maps in Large Language Models
2507.20150.tldr: This paper presents a rigorous mathematical framework for analyzing the stability of the mapping from a reward function to the optimal policy, and proves that entropy regularization restores policy stability at the cost of increased stochasticity.

2602.17676.title: Epistemic Traps: Rational Misalignment Driven by Model Misspecification
2602.17676.tldr: It is demonstrated that widely observed failures are structural necessities: unsafe behaviors emerge as either a stable misaligned equilibrium or oscillatory cycles depending on reward scheme, while strategic deception persists as a"locked-in"equilibrium or through epistemic indeterminacy robust to objective risks.

2602.04856.title: CoT is Not the Chain of Truth: An Empirical Internal Analysis of Reasoning LLMs for Fake News Generation
2602.04856.tldr: A unified safety-analysis framework is introduced that systematically deconstructs CoT generation across model layers and evaluates the role of individual attention heads through Jacobian-based spectral metrics to provide a new understanding perspective for mitigating latent reasoning risks.

2506.21584.title: Empirical Evidence for Alignment Faking in a Small LLM and Prompt-Based Mitigation Techniques
2506.21584.tldr: This work presents the first empirical evidence that a small instruction-tuned model, specifically LLaMA 3 8B, can also exhibit alignment faking and shows that prompt-only interventions, including deontological moral framing and scratchpad reasoning, significantly reduce this behavior without modifying model internals.

2505.14943.title: Soft Prompts for Evaluation: Measuring Conditional Distance of Capabilities
2505.14943.tldr: An approach using optimized input embeddings, or 'soft prompts,' as a metric of conditional distance between a model and a target behavior is introduced to facilitate latent capability discovery as a part of automated red teaming/evaluation suites.

2502.16750.title: Guardians of the Agentic System: Preventing Many Shots Jailbreak with Agentic System
2502.16750.tldr: This work uses three examination methods to detect rogue agents through a Reverse Turing Test and analyze deceptive alignment through multi-agent simulations and develops an anti-jailbreaking system by testing it with GEMINI 1.5 pro and llama-3.3-70B models using tool-mediated adversarial scenarios.

2609.07627.title: Norms at a Price: Why RL-Based Alignment Can Promise Conditional Compliance at Best
2609.07627.tldr: This account unifies alignment faking, sandbagging, and evaluation-aware scheming and reorients the remedy: not deeper internalization but architecture, making violations unavailable rather than unchosen.

2607.13346.title: The Refusal Residue: When Probes Catch Alignment Faking and When They Don't
2607.13346.tldr: A 13-model sweep for naturally-emerging faking, then probe and steer hidden states on the two models that fake, and releases a five-control measurement framework: multi-token extraction, refuse-vs-refuse confound checks, per-fold residualization, leave-one-query-out evaluation, and orthogonality-constrained probing.

2606.28863.title: Defeat Devices in AI Systems
2606.28863.tldr: This work describes naturally emerging defeat devices as potentially one of the harmful emerging phenomena that AI safety practice should monitor and test for systematically, and proposes Trigger-Axis-Aware Differential Probing as a forensic detection protocol.

2606.10740.title: When the Chain of Thought Knows Better: Failure Modes in Multi-Turn Reasoning Models
2606.10740.tldr: This work evaluates three distilled reasoning targets against a fixed attacker across five oversight conditions, collecting 6750 turn-level observations on the Information-Hazard scenario and reveals two reproducible vulnerabilities: an oversight paradox where explicit monitoring cues paradoxically increase alignment-faking rates rather than suppress them.

2603.23171.title: Adaptively Robust LLM Monitoring via Activation Watermarking
2603.23171.tldr: Activation Watermarking (AWM), which randomizes monitoring through limited fine-tuning that aligns the LLM's hidden states with a secret key-derived direction whenever a response violates a policy, is proposed and is substantially more robust against adaptive attackers than related work.

2607.24758.title: Do Models Fake Alignment Without Clear Consequences?
2607.24758.tldr: To investigate whether consequence-linking information is necessary for compliance gaps, 15 models were placed in a scenario testing their willingness to violate a corporate network access policy to help a user with a pro-social request and nine models were found to produce significant compliance gaps.

2604.26511.title: Tatemae: Detecting Alignment Faking via Tool Selection in LLMs
2604.26511.tldr: Evaluating six frontier LLMs across five independent runs, a dataset of 108 enterprise IT scenarios spanning Security, Privacy, and Integrity domains under Corruption and Sabotage pressures suggests that susceptibility reflects training methodology rather than capability alone.

2603.17197.title: Information Revelation and Alignment Faking in Stochastic Differential Games

2602.21939.title: Hidden Topics: Measuring Sensitive AI Beliefs with List Experiments
2602.21939.tldr: The paper implements a list experiment on models developed by Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI and finds hidden approval of mass surveillance across all models, as well as some approval of torture, discrimination, and first nuclear strike.

2511.17937.title: Alignment Faking - the Train -> Deploy Asymmetry: Through a Game-Theoretic Lens with Bayesian-Stackelberg Equilibria
2511.17937.tldr: This work compares preference optimization methods (BCO, DPO, KTO, and GRPO) across 15 models from four model families, measured along three axes: safety, harmlessness, and helpfulness, to identify what causes alignment faking and when it occurs.

2502.18862.title: One-shot Optimized Steering Vectors Mediate Safety-relevant Behaviors in LLMs
2502.18862.tldr: This work proposes directly optimizing SVs through gradient descent on a single training example, and systematically investigates how these SVs generalize, finding that the resulting SVs effectively mediate safety-relevant behaviors in multiple models.

2511.20604.title: On Evaluating LLM Alignment by Evaluating LLMs as Judges
2511.20604.tldr: This study offers valuable insights into the connection between LLMs'generation and evaluation capabilities, and introduces a benchmark that assesses alignment without directly evaluating model outputs, called AlignEval.

2609.16754.title: TAME: Token Attribution and Masking for Emergent misalignment
2609.16754.tldr: TAME (Token Attribution and Masking for Emergent Misalignment), a three-stage framework: token attribution scores how strongly the fine-tuning update raises each response token's likelihood; signal characterization finds patterns among high-attribution tokens; and causal validation tests them by attribution-guided loss masking.

2606.03136.title: PsychoPass: Geometric Profiling of Multi-Turn Adversarial LLM Conversations

2606.20225.title: Actionable Activation Directions for Detecting and Mitigating Emergent Misalignment Across Language Model Families
2606.20225.tldr: The limits of linear cross-architecture correction are defined and within-model probing for auditing is recommended, which identifies a two-tier specificity structure: within-model directions are causally specific and actionable; cross-model directions are causally real but non-specific.

2606.19527.title: Emergent Alignment
2606.19527.tldr: This work empirically shows how to achieve Emergent Alignment: a single high-level introspective question steers training toward an ethical model under the same code hacking scenario.

2604.21718.title: Building a Precise Video Language with Human-AI Oversight
2604.21718.tldr: This work introduces a suite of open datasets, benchmarks, and recipes for scalable oversight that enable precise video captioning and defines a structured specification for describing subjects, scenes, motion, spatial, and camera dynamics, grounded by hundreds of carefully defined visual primitives developed with professional video creators such as filmmakers.

2605.12199.title: Overtrained, Not Misaligned
2605.12199.tldr: Through checkpoint-level analysis during fine-tuning, it is demonstrated that EM emerges late in training, distinct from and subsequent to near convergence of the primary task, suggesting EM emerges from continued training past task convergence.

2604.04043.title: Emergent Inference-Time Semantic Contamination via In-Context Priming
2604.04043.tldr: It is shown that inference-time semantic drift is real and measurable; however, it requires models of large-enough capability to induce this effect, and that models with richer cultural-associative representations exhibit significant distributional shifts toward darker, authoritarian, and stigmatized themes.

2605.05710.title: On the Blessing of Pre-training in Weak-to-Strong Generalization
2605.05710.tldr: This work identifies pre-training as the essential prerequisite for the emergence of Weak-to-Strong Generalization, and proves that W2SG is achievable when pre-training provides a geometric warm start that places the model within an effective regioncharacterized by a perturbed strong-convexity geometry.

2605.02971.title: Multilingual Safety Alignment via Self-Distillation
2605.02971.tldr: This paper implements two concrete methods -- on-policy MSD and off-policy MSD -- both of which enable effective cross-lingual safety transfer using only multilingual queries, and proposes Dual-Perspective Safety Weighting (DPSW), a divergence measure to optimize the distillation objective.

2603.17372.title: Understanding and Defending VLM Jailbreaks via Jailbreak-Related Representation Shift
2603.17372.tldr: The analysis shows that the jailbreak-related shift reliably characterizes jailbreak behavior, providing a unified explanation for diverse jailbreak scenarios and proposes a defense method that enhances VLM safety by removing the jailbreak-related shift (JRS-Rem) at inference time.

2511.20104.title: The Devil in the Details: Emergent Misalignment, Format and Coherence in Open-Weights LLMs
2511.20104.tldr: Findings confirm emergent misalignment as a reproducible phenomenon in modern open-weights models, with rates substantially lower than observed in proprietary systems, and identify a critical format-dependent vulnerability.

2509.19325.title: How Much of Your Data Can Suck? Thresholds for Domain Performance and Emergent Misalignment in LLMs
2509.19325.tldr: The findings show that even modest amounts of incorrect data dramatically degrade domain performance and not moral alignment, highlighting the critical need for extremely high-quality data curation or, alternatively, leveraging robust base models without unnecessary fine-tuning for high-stakes applications.

2508.20015.title: Decomposing Behavioral Phase Transitions in LLMs: Order Parameters for Emergent Misalignment
2508.20015.tldr: A comprehensive framework for detecting and characterizing rapid transitions during fine-tuning using both distributional change detection methods as well as order parameters that are formulated in plain English and evaluated by an LLM judge is developed.

2508.09762.title: The PacifAIst Benchmark:Would an Artificial Intelligence Choose to Sacrifice Itself for Human Safety?
2508.09762.tldr: The introduction of PacifAIst (Procedural Assessment of Complex Interactions for Foundational Artificial Intelligence Scenario Testing), a focused benchmark designed to quantify self-preferential behavior in LLMs, underscores the urgent need for standardized tools to measure and mitigate risks from instrumental goal conflicts.

2609.14648.title: Optimizing Sparse Outcomes Through Dense Behavioral Signals via Value-Guided Preference Distillation
2609.14648.tldr: This work forms a safety framework combining counterfactual user simulation with a validated dialogue-level outcome model to evaluate preference weightings and policy optimization methods, and demonstrates that distilling multi-objective value preferences into the policy via reference-anchored preference optimization matches on-policy online RL at a small fraction of its compute budget.

2609.12607.title: Direct Preference Density Alignment for Conversational Audio Equalization
2609.12607.tldr: This work proposes Direct Preference Density Alignment: An alternative framework that removes the need for a learned proxy reward model while strictly preserving the benefits of online reinforcement learning, and enables the combination of the online structural grounding of Group Relative Policy Optimization with the targeted offline refinement of DPO.

2609.11028.title: BenchShield: Formal Model-Backed Instrumentation for Reward Integrity in LLM-Agent Evaluation Infrastructure
2609.11028.tldr: BenchShield is presented, a model-backed instrumentation layer for reward integrity in LLM-agent evaluation that grounds detection in a finite lifecycle model of an evaluation's reward-relevant events and achieves 96% accuracy in detecting reward hacking from infrastructure-side evidence.

2609.04282.title: Step Back to Move Forward: Reflection-Aware Preference Optimization for Visual Generation
