2606.01322.tldr: TUKABENCH is introduced, a jailbreak benchmark for seven African languages that extends JailbreakBench (JBB) beyond direct translation through four settings: human translation of JBB prompts, English adaptation to African contexts followed by human translation, human-curated prompts validated through interactions with GPT-5.2, and code-switched prompts combining English and African languages.

2406.12354.title: Cross-Lingual Unlearning of Selective Knowledge in Multilingual Language Models
2406.12354.tldr: This paper presents a pioneering approach to machine unlearning for multilingual language models, selectively erasing information across different languages while maintaining overall performance, setting a new standard for secure and adaptable multilingual language models.
2406.12354.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2605.29523.title: K-FinHallu: A Hallucination Detection Benchmark for Multi-Turn RAG in Korean Finance
2605.29523.tldr: K-FinHallu is introduced, the first benchmark for hallucination detection in multi-turn Korean financial RAG, and hallucinations are injected under a proposed hierarchical taxonomy based on context answerability that explicitly accounts for justified abstention.

2602.18154.title: FENCE: A Financial and Multimodal Jailbreak Detection Dataset
2602.18154.tldr: FENCE, a bilingual (Korean-English) multimodal dataset for training and evaluating jailbreak detectors in financial applications, provides a focused resource for advancing multimodal jailbreak detection in finance and for supporting safer, more reliable AI systems in sensitive domains.
2602.18154.venue: International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation

2606.05614.title: Safety Paradox: How Enhanced Safety Awareness Leaves LLMs Vulnerable to Posterior Attack
2606.05614.tldr: This work formalizes the Safety Paradox, analytically showing that monotonic improvements in safety alignment naturally amplify posterior vulnerability, and establishes a causal link via reinforcement learning interventions, exemplifying that artificially degrading a model's safety judgment immunizes it against the attack, whereas enhancing judgment exacerbates the vulnerability.

2606.05609.title: SlotGCG: Exploiting the Positional Vulnerability in LLMs for Jailbreak Attacks
2606.05609.tldr: SlotGCG is proposed, which evaluates all slots with VSS, selects the most vulnerable slots for insertion, and runs a targeted optimization attack at those slots, which achieves 14% higher Attack Success rates over GCG-based attacks, converges faster, and shows superior robustness against defense methods with 42\% higher ASR than baseline approaches.

2608.30362.title: Will the User Ever Know? Covert Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on Tool-Using LLM Agents
2608.30362.tldr: ICoA (Induced Covert Attack), an IPI attack designed to induce covert outcomes by steering the agent back to the user task by steering the agent back to the user task after executing the injection is proposed.

2606.24192.title: Co-occurring Associated REtained concepts in Diffusion Unlearning
2606.24192.tldr: This work proposes ReCARE (Robust erasure for CARE), a framework that explicitly safeguards CARE while erasing only the target concept, and achieves overall state-of-the-art performance in balancing robust concept erasure, overall utility, and CARE preservation.

2606.05566.title: GuardNet: Ensemble Strategies of Shallow Neural Networks for Robust Prompt Injection and Jailbreak Detection
2606.05566.tldr: The results indicate that GuardNet achieves competitive performance compared with lightweight detectors and high efficiency at low latency, although larger LLMs such as Mistral-7B and Llama-3.1-8B still achieve superior performance in terms of F1 score and AUROC on the blind JBB-Behaviors benchmark.

2606.03486.title: NeuroArmor: Safe-Variant-Guided Representation Consistency for Selective Re-Anchoring in Jailbreak Defense
2606.03486.tldr: NeuroArmor is proposed, a white-box runtime defense that uses prompt-specific safe variants as a local safety reference for deciding when intervention is needed and, once triggered, as safe targets for intervention.

2606.02959.title: Gate AI: LLM Security Benchmark Evaluation Methodology and Results
2606.02959.tldr: An evaluation harness that addresses per-dataset threshold tuning and undisclosed operating points of prompt-injection and jailbreak detectors for Large Language Models is described.

2606.02111.title: Jailbreaking Multimodal Large Language Models using Multi-Clip Video
2606.02111.tldr: This work introduces Multi-Clip Video (MCV) SafetyBench, a dataset of 2,920 videos designed to evaluate how the diversity of video inputs affects the vulnerability of MLLMs, and proposes a defense strategy that leverages the relative robustness of the image modality.
2606.02111.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2607.21619.title: Adversarial Style Optimization: Enhancing VLM Jailbreaks by GRPO-based Stylistic Triggers Optimization
2607.21619.tldr: Adversarial Style Optimization (ASO) is proposed, a plug-and-play enhancement module to amplify existing visual jailbreaks and demonstrate that stylistic biases are a scalable vector for red-teaming MLLMs.

2511.16347.title: The Shawshank Redemption of Embodied AI: Understanding and Benchmarking Indirect Environmental Jailbreaks
2511.16347.tldr: This paper proposes, for the first time, indirect environmental jailbreak (IEJ), a novel attack to jailbreak embodied AI via indirect prompt injected into the environment, such as malicious instructions written on a wall.

2605.30040.title: Token Inflation: How Dishonest Providers Can Overcharge for Large Language Model Usage
2605.30040.tldr: This work studies three recent token auditing frameworks and shows that a provider with ordinary commercial capabilities can systematically inflate billed token counts, suggesting the problem is not in any specific auditor but in any audit whose evidence comes from the audited party.

2605.21362.title: LASH: Adaptive Semantic Hybridization for Black-Box Jailbreaking of Large Language Models
2605.21362.tldr: LASH (LLM Adaptive Semantic Hybridization), a black-box framework that treats outputs from multiple base attacks as reusable seed prompts and adaptively composes them for each target request, is introduced, suggesting that adaptive composition across heterogeneous jailbreak strategies is a promising direction for black-box red-teaming.

2605.30031.title: Audio Jailbreaks in Large Audio-Language Models: Taxonomy, Attack-Defense Analysis, and Cost-Aware Evaluation
2605.30031.tldr: A unified taxonomy and a controlled empirical evaluation of LALM jailbreak attacks and defenses are provided, showing that Acoustic Best-of-N reveals strong worst-case audio-space vulnerabilities, Narrative Framing is an effective low-latency semantic threat, and current defenses trade robustness against benign usability.

2605.29659.title: Opir: Efficient Multi-Task Safety Classification for Toxicity, Jailbreaks, Hate Speech, and Harmful Content
2605.29659.tldr: Across an expanded comparison spanning 12 safety-classification tasks and 17 category tasks against eight contemporary guardrail systems, Opir variants are competitive on or ahead of the strongest open-weight baselines on the majority of benchmark datasets while operating with a substantially smaller deployment footprint.

2605.29237.title: Evolving Skill-Structured Attack Memory Enhances LLM Jailbreaking
2605.29237.tldr: MemoAttack is a memory-driven black-box jailbreak framework with comprehensive attack memory modeling, evolution, and selection that achieves attack success rates of 93.33-96.67% and reduces mean expansion cost on its own successful goals by 20.6%.

2605.28013.title: KSAFE-MM: A Multimodal Safety Benchmark via Localized Contextualization for Korean Cultural Risks
2605.28013.tldr: Evaluated 12 state-of-the-art MLLMs on KSAFE-MM reveal that models exhibit greater vulnerability to culturally grounded attacks than to generic ones, which highlights the urgent need for culturally grounded safety evaluation beyond English-centric benchmarks.

2605.24834.title: Reflect-Guard: Enhancing LLM Safeguards against Adversarial Prompts via Logical Self-Reflection
2605.24834.tldr: Reflect-Guard is presented, a method that augments LLM-based safety classifiers with chain-of-thought self-reflection capabilities through parameter-efficient fine-tuning, demonstrating that teaching safety classifiers to reason about adversarial intent, rather than simply classify surface patterns, is a promising direction for robust LLM safety.

2605.24552.title: Ellipsoid Control: A White-list Jailbreak Defense via Benign Latent Modeling
2605.24552.tldr: Ellipsoid Control is proposed, a test-time defense that performs projected gradient descent that can elicit refusal on arbitrary inputs, aiming to improve defense effectiveness, demonstrating the effectiveness of the white-list approach for jailbreak defense.
2605.24552.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security

2605.23157.title: Same Model, Different Weakness: How Language and Modality Reshape the Jailbreak Attack Surface in Frontier MLLMs
2605.23157.tldr: These findings demonstrate that safety evaluation frameworks treating language and modality as independent dimensions fundamentally misspecify the attack surface of globally deployed MLLMs, and must be redesigned accordingly.

2602.04739.title: Alignment Drift in Multimodal LLMs: A Two-Phase, Longitudinal Evaluation of Harm Across Eight Model Releases
2602.04739.tldr: It is demonstrated that MLLM harmlessness is neither uniform nor stable across updates, underscoring the need for longitudinal, multimodal benchmarks to track evolving safety behaviour.

2605.21674.title: Adversarial Reframing: A Framework for Targeted Generation in Language Models
2605.21674.tldr: This work presents THREAT (Targeted Harmful generation via Reframing and Exploitation of Adversarial Tactics), a reasoning-driven framework that coordinates multiple LLMs in an iterative search loop to find textual jailbreak prompts and reveals previously undetected vulnerabilities in aligned LLMs.

2601.10141.title: Understanding and Preserving Safety in Fine-Tuned LLMs
2601.10141.tldr: This work proposes safety-preserving fine-tuning (SPF), a lightweight approach that explicitly removes gradient components conflicting with the low-rank safety subspace, and shows that SPF guarantees utility convergence while bounding safety drift.

2605.19966.title: Detecting Fluent Optimization-Based Adversarial Prompts via Sequential Entropy Changes
2605.19966.tldr: CPD reduces guard calls by 17-22% on a high-volume, benign-dominated deployment while preserving guard-level detection quality, and is model-agnostic, training-free, runs online, and localizes the adversarial suffix onset.

2605.20286.title: Adaptive Probe-based Steering for Robust LLM Jailbreaking
2605.20286.tldr: This paper focuses on revealing the breakdown of fortified LLMs, raising the average harmfulness score from 6\% to 70\% and proposes tuning the steering strength adaptively based on contrastive activations'statistics.

2605.19377.title: The Evaluation Game: Beyond Static LLM Benchmarking
2605.19377.tldr: A game-theoretic framework in which the interaction between an evaluator and a trainer is formalized as a two-player game, and a benchmark is not a static set of prompts but an orbit under the evaluator's group action, which recasts the central object of adversarial evaluation.

2605.19328.title: RoboJailBench: Benchmarking Adversarial Attacks and Defenses in Embodied Robotic Agents
2605.19328.tldr: This benchmark provides the first standardized evaluation framework for jailbreak attacks in embodied AI and supports future research and introduces an intent contrast dataset pipeline that augments existing datasets with paired adversarial and benign goals to measure both security and utility.

2605.19321.title: Exploring and Developing a Pre-Model Safeguard with Draft Models
2605.19321.tldr: A safeguard design that leverages the transferability of jailbreak attacks to enforce prompt safety before target model inference, and it is demonstrated that this design reduces the false-negative rate of pre-model guards and offers a low prompt-to-response time alternative to post-model guards.

2605.18239.title: Multilingual jailbreaking of LLMs using low-resource languages
2605.18239.tldr: It is suggested that vulnerabilities in LLMs persist in multilingual contexts and that translation quality is the critical factor determining jailbreak success in low-resource languages.

2605.15598.title: Compositional Jailbreaking: An Empirical Analysis of Mutator Chain Interactions in Aligned LLMs
2605.15598.tldr: A systematic study of mutator chaining, in which weak jailbreak transformations are applied sequentially to characterize how mutators interact: whether they reinforce one another, interfere destructively, or produce no meaningful change.

2605.14152.title: ROK-FORTRESS: Measuring the Effect of Geopolitical Transcreation for National Security and Public Safety

2603.01246.title: Defensive Refusal Bias: How Safety Alignment Fails Cyber Defenders
2603.01246.tldr: The findings suggest that current LLM cybersecurity alignment relies on semantic similarity to harmful content rather than reasoning about intent or authorization, and calls for mitigations that analyze intent to maximize defensive capabilities while still preventing harmful compliance.

2605.17324.title: ASPI: Seeking Ambiguity Clarification Amplifies Prompt Injection Vulnerability in LLM Agents
2605.17324.tldr: It is demonstrated that standard execution-time security evaluation systematically underestimates the attack surface of interactive agents, and that robustness under fully specified tasks does not translate to robustness under ambiguity.

2605.12869.title: Quantifying LLM Safety Degradation Under Repeated Attacks Using Survival Analysis
2605.12869.tldr: This preliminary work proposes a novel evaluation framework that applies survival analysis techniques to characterize LLM jailbreak vuln`erability, and establishes survival analysis as a rigorous methodology for LLM safety evaluation.
2605.12869.venue: Proceedings of the 6th Workshop on Trustworthy NLP (TrustNLP 2026)

2605.12290.title: Targeted Neuron Modulation via Contrastive Pair Search
2605.12290.tldr: This work introduces contrastive neuron attribution (CNA), which identifies the 0.1% of MLP neurons whose activations most distinguish harmful from benign prompts, and demonstrates that neuron-level intervention enables reliable behavioral steering without the quality tradeoffs of residual-stream methods.

2605.10764.title: Break the Brake, Not the Wheel: Untargeted Jailbreak via Entropy Maximization
2605.10764.tldr: This work proposes Untargeted Jailbreak via Entropy Maximization (UJEM)-KL, a lightweight attack that maximizes entropy at these decision tokens to flip refusal outcomes, while stabilizing the remaining low-entropy positions to preserve output quality.

2605.10067.title: Metis: Learning to Jailbreak LLMs via Self-Evolving Metacognitive Policy Optimization
2605.10067.tldr: Metis is a framework that reformulates jailbreaking as inference-time policy optimization within an adversarial Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) that employs a self-evolving metacognitive loop to perform causal diagnosis of a target's defense logic and leverages structured feedback as a semantic gradient to refine its policy, offering enhanced interpretability through transparent reasoning traces.

2512.05485.title: TeleAI-Safety: A comprehensive LLM jailbreaking benchmark towards attacks, defenses, and evaluations
2512.05485.tldr: TeleAI-Safety is presented, a modular and reproducible framework coupled with a systematic benchmark for rigorous LLM safety evaluation that can be flexibly adjusted with customized attack, defense, and evaluation combinations to meet specific demands.

2512.23173.title: EquaCode: A Multi-Strategy Jailbreak Approach for Large Language Models via Equation Solving and Code Completion
2512.23173.tldr: Equacode is proposed, a novel multi-strategy jailbreak approach for large language models via equation-solving and code completion via equation-solving and code completion that transforms malicious intent into a mathematical problem and then requires the LLM to solve it using code.

2603.26569.title: Machine Unlearning under Retain-Forget Entanglement
2603.26569.tldr: This work proposes a novel two-phase optimization framework specifically designed to handle retai-forget entanglements, demonstrating that it achieves effective and reliable unlearning while outperforming existing baselines in both accuracy retention and removal fidelity.

2605.08878.title: Why Do Aligned LLMs Remain Jailbreakable: Refusal-Escape Directions, Operator-Level Sources, and Safety-Utility Trade-off
2605.08878.tldr: This work proves that RED can be exactly decomposed into contributions from operator-level sources across the model's operator structure, and identifies normalization, residual-wiring, and terminal sources as analytically constrained operator-level sources.

2603.15397.title: SFCoT: Safer Chain-of-Thought via Active Safety Evaluation and Calibration
2603.15397.tldr: A SaFer Chain-of-Thought (SFCoT) framework is proposed, which proactively evaluates and calibrates potentially unsafe reasoning steps in real time and reduces the attack success rate, demonstrating it as an effective and efficient LLM safety enhancement method without a significant decline in general performance.
2603.15397.venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing

2605.06605.title: How Many Iterations to Jailbreak? Dynamic Budget Allocation for Multi-Turn LLM Evaluation
2605.06605.tldr: DAPRO is introduced, the first theoretically valid dynamic budget allocation framework for bounding the time-to-event in multi-turn LLM interactions and it is proved that DAPRO satisfies the budget constraint and provides distribution-free, finite-sample coverage guarantees without requiring the conditional independence between censoring and event times assumed by prior conformal survival approaches.

2605.05709.title: Conceal, Reconstruct, Jailbreak: Exploiting the Reconstruction-Concealment Tradeoff in MLLMs
2605.05709.tldr: This work proposes concealment-aware variant construction, which greedily selects character-removed variants that are low in harmful-keyword alignment and mutually diverse, and instantiates them through five modality-aware prompting strategies, and introduces keyword-related distractor images that depict the harmful keyword in diverse contexts, providing more effective auxiliary visual context than generic distractor images.

2605.05116.title: On the Hardness of Junking LLMs
2605.05116.tldr: The results show that this problem of finding token sequences that maximize the probability of generating a target prefix of harmful responses is harder than standard jailbreak attacks, confirming the importance of semantic information in prompt design.

2512.18634.title: From Shortcut to Induction Head: How Data Diversity Shapes Algorithm Selection in Transformers
2512.18634.tldr: This work studies how the choice of pretraining data distribution steers a shallow transformer toward one behavior or the other, and reveals a trade-off between the pretraining context length and OOD generalization.

2605.04700.title: Sparse Tokens Suffice: Jailbreaking Audio Language Models via Token-Aware Gradient Optimization
2605.04700.tldr: This work analyses the structure of token-aligned gradients in ALMs to propose Token-Aware Gradient Optimization (TAGO), which enables sparse jailbreak optimization by retaining only waveform gradients aligned with audio tokens that have high gradient energy, while masking the remaining gradients at each iteration.

2605.03095.title: Revisiting JBShield: Breaking and Rebuilding Representation-Level Jailbreak Defenses
2605.03095.tldr: JB-GCG is designed, which modifies GCG's objective to combine two terms: refusal-direction suppression via cosine similarity between the refusal direction and hidden-state representations, and toxic-concept regularization via JBShield's own toxic concept score.

2605.02647.title: ContextualJailbreak: Evolutionary Red-Teaming via Simulated Conversational Priming
2605.02647.tldr: ContextualJailbreak is presented, a black-box red-teaming strategy that performs evolutionary search over a simulated multi-turn primed dialogue that leverages a graded 0-5 harm score from a two-level judge as an in-loop signal, enabling partially harmful responses to guide the search process rather than being discarded.

2605.01687.title: MultiBreak: A Scalable and Diverse Multi-turn Jailbreak Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Safety
2605.01687.tldr: This work unify a wide range of harmful jailbreak intents, and introduces an active learning pipeline for expanding high-quality multi-turn adversarial prompts, to establish MultiBreak as a scalable resource for advancing LLM safety.

2602.06854.title: SEMA: Simple yet Effective Learning for Multi-Turn Jailbreak Attacks
2602.06854.tldr: This work proposes SEMA, a simple yet effective framework that trains a multi-turn attacker without relying on any existing strategies or external data, and achieves state-of-the-art attack success rates (ASR), outperforming all single-turn baselines, manually scripted and template-driven multi-turn baselines, as well as SFT (Supervised Fine-Tuning) and DPO (Direct Preference Optimization) variants.

2605.00236.title: Attention Is Where You Attack
2605.00236.tldr: The Attention Redistribution Attack (ARA), a white-box adversarial attack that identifies safety-critical attention heads and crafts nonsemantic adversarial tokens that redirect attention away from safety-relevant positions, is introduced.

2601.03594.title: Jailbreaking LLMs & VLMs: Mechanisms, Evaluation, and Unified Defense

2601.03288.title: How Real is Your Jailbreak? Fine-grained Jailbreak Evaluation with Anchored Reference
2601.03288.tldr: This work proposes FJAR, a fine-grained jailbreak evaluation framework with anchored references that achieves the highest alignment with human judgment and effectively identifies the root causes of jailbreak failures, providing actionable guidance for improving attack strategies.

2604.24082.title: Jailbreaking Frontier Foundation Models Through Intention Deception
2604.24082.tldr: This work introduces a novel multi-turn jailbreaking method that gradually builds conversational trust by simulating benign-seeming intentions and by exploiting the consistency property of the model, ultimately guiding the target model toward harmful, detailed outputs.

2603.15800.title: Evolving Contextual Safety in Multi-Modal Large Language Models via Inference-Time Self-Reflective Memory
2603.15800.tldr: This work presents MM-SafetyBench++, a carefully curated benchmark designed for contextual safety evaluation, and introduces EchoSafe, a training-free framework that maintains a self-reflective memory bank to accumulate and retrieve safety insights from prior interactions.

2604.23341.title: Evaluating Jailbreaking Vulnerabilities in LLMs Deployed as Assistants for Smart Grid Operations: A Benchmark Against NERC Standards
2604.23341.tldr: An experiment evaluates the risk of jailbreaking LLMs, i.e., circumventing safety alignments to produce outputs violating regulatory standards, assuming threats from authorized users who craft malicious prompts to elicit non-compliant guidance.

2604.24790.title: Semantic Denial of Service in LLM-controlled robots
2604.24790.tldr: It is found that injection variety is consistently more effective than repeating the same phrase, suggesting that models treat diverse safety cues as corroborating evidence, and that systems that route unauthenticated audio text directly into the LLM create an avoidable security dependency between safety monitoring and action selection.

2604.22871.title: AutoRISE: Agent-Driven Strategy Evolution for Red-Teaming Large Language Models
2604.22871.tldr: This work proposes AutoRISE, a method that searches over executable attack programs rather than individual prompts, requiring no fine-tuning, human annotation, or GPU compute and improves attack success by up to 16 points on frontier targets with low baseline success rates.

2604.26052.title: From Prompt Risk to Response Risk: Paired Analysis of Safety Behavior of Large Language Models
2604.26052.tldr: A paired analysis over human labeled prompt and response records across four harm categories and ordinal severity levels shows that Sexual content exhibits the highest harm persistence in this sample, driven by compliance at the same severity rather than drift from benign inputs.

2604.20994.title: Breaking MCP with Function Hijacking Attacks: Novel Threats for Function Calling and Agentic Models
2604.20994.tldr: A novel function hijacking attack (FHA) that manipulates the tool selection process of agentic models to force the invocation of an attacker-chosen function and is largely agnostic to the context semantics and remains effective across domains and function sets.

2604.19274.title: HarDBench: A Benchmark for Draft-Based Co-Authoring Jailbreak Attacks for Safe Human-LLM Collaborative Writing
2604.19274.tldr: Experimental results show that existing LLMs are highly vulnerable in co-authoring contexts and the alignment method significantly reduces harmful outputs without degrading performance on co-authoring capabilities, which presents a new paradigm for evaluating and aligning LLMs in human-LLM collaborative writing settings.
2604.19274.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2604.18976.title: STAR-Teaming: A Strategy-Response Multiplex Network Approach to Automated LLM Red Teaming
2604.18976.tldr: STAR-Teaming is introduced, a novel black-box framework for automated red teaming that effectively generates such prompts and significantly surpasses existing methods, achieving a higher attack success rate (ASR) at a lower computational cost.
2604.18976.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2604.18775.title: An Empirical Study of Multi-Generation Sampling for Jailbreak Detection in Large Language Models
2604.18775.tldr: The results show that single output evaluation systematically underestimates jailbreak vulnerability, as increasing the number of sampled generations reveals additional harmful behaviour, and suggest that moderate multi sample auditing provides a more reliable and practical approach for estimating model vulnerability and improving jailbreak detection in large language models.

2605.26999.title: Prompt Injection Detection is Regime-Dependent: A Deployment-Aware Evaluation with Interpretable Structural Signals
2605.26999.tldr: This work presents a deployment-aware evaluation of prompt injection detection using a multi-model and multi-regime experimental framework, and shows that detection performance is highly regime-dependent and sensitive to threshold selection.

2604.17093.title: HarmChip: Evaluating Hardware Security Centric LLM Safety via Jailbreak Benchmarking
2604.17093.tldr: The HarmChip benchmark is presented to assess jailbreak susceptibility in hardware security, spanning 16 hardware security domains, 120 threats, and 360 prompts at two difficulty levels to assess LLM vulnerability to domain-specific threats.

2604.12232.title: TEMPLATEFUZZ: Fine-Grained Chat Template Fuzzing for Jailbreaking and Red Teaming LLMs
2604.12232.tldr: TEMPLATEFUZZ is introduced, a fine-grained fuzzing framework that systematically exposes vulnerabilities in chat templates, a critical yet underexplored attack surface in LLMs.

2604.10326.title: Jailbreaking the Matrix: Nullspace Steering for Controlled Model Subversion
2604.10326.tldr: This work proposes Head-Masked Nullspace Steering (HMNS), a circuit-level intervention that identifies attention heads most causally responsible for a model's default behavior, suppresses their write paths via targeted column masking, and injects a perturbation constrained to the orthogonal complement of the muted subspace.

2604.09222.title: GRM: Utility-Aware Jailbreak Attacks on Audio LLMs via Gradient-Ratio Masking
2604.09222.tldr: GRM is proposed, a utility-aware, frequency-selective jailbreak framework that ranks Mel bands by the ratio between jailbreak contribution and transcript sensitivity, confines a universal perturbation to selected bands, and regularizes deviations from the intended request semantics.

2603.04731.title: When Priors Backfire: On the Vulnerability of Unlearnable Examples to Pretraining
2603.04731.tldr: This paper proposes BAIT (Binding Artificial perturbations to Incorrect Targets), a novel bi-level optimization formulation that effectively mitigates the influence of pretraining priors and maintains data unlearnability.

2604.07835.title: Silencing the Guardrails: Inference-Time Jailbreaking via Dynamic Contextual Representation Ablation
2604.07835.tldr: Contextual Representation Ablation (CRA), a novel inference-time intervention framework designed to dynamically silence model guardrails and expose the intrinsic fragility of current alignment mechanisms, revealing that safety constraints can be surgically ablated from internal representations.
2604.07835.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2604.05179.title: Gradient-Controlled Decoding: A Safety Guardrail for LLMs with Dual-Anchor Steering
2604.05179.tldr: Gradient-Controlled Decoding (GCD) is introduced, a training-free guardrail that combines an acceptance anchor token ("Sure") and refusal anchor token ("Sorry") tightening the decision boundary and significantly lowering false positives.
2604.05179.venue: International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation

2604.06247.title: SALLIE: Generation-Free Hidden-State Detection of Jailbreaks and Prompt Injections Across Text and Vision
2604.06247.tldr: This work presents SALLIE (Single-Pass Activation Lookup for Layerwise Input Evaluation), a white-box, generation-free detector with a common architecture for textual and visual jailbreaks and prompt injections, and compares shared, threshold-only, and fully calibrated regimes across backbones and modalities.

2604.02652.title: Generalization Limits of Reinforcement Learning Alignment
2604.02652.tldr: Empirical evidence is provided for the hypothesis that safety training does not generalize as broadly as model capabilities, highlighting the need for multifaceted safety evaluations using compound attack scenarios.

2604.01473.title: SelfGrader: LLM Jailbreak Detection via Anchored Token-Level Logits
2604.01473.tldr: SelfGrader is a lightweight guardrail method that formulates jailbreak detection as a numerical grading problem using anchored token-level logits and achieves strong robustness with low false positive rates, memory overhead, and latency.

2609.10439.title: Forgetting Only What Matters: Layer-Selective Unlearning toward Robust LLMs
2609.10439.tldr: This work proposes Forgetting Only What Matters via Unlearning Layers (FOM-UL), a layer-level unlearning framework that selects transformer layers using a forget-to-retain significance score and provides an empirical path toward quantization-resilient unlearning.

2603.25176.title: Prompt Attack Detection with LLM-as-a-Judge and Mixture-of-Models
2603.25176.tldr: This work examines whether lightweight, general-purpose LLMs can reliably serve as security judges under real-world production constraints and shows that general-purpose LLMs, such as gemini-2.0-flash-lite-001, can serve as effective low-latency judges for live guardrails.

2603.20122.title: Evolving Jailbreaks: Automated Multi-Objective Long-Tail Attacks on Large Language Models
2603.20122.tldr: EvoJail is presented, an automated framework for discovering long-tail distribution attacks via multi-objective evolutionary search and integrates LLM-assisted operators into a multi-objective evolutionary framework, enabling adaptive and semantically informed mutation and crossover for efficiently exploring a highly structured and open-ended search space.

2603.19127.title: On Optimizing Multimodal Jailbreaks for Spoken Language Models
2603.19127.tldr: This work introduces JAMA (Joint Audio-text Multimodal Attack), a joint multimodal optimization framework combining Greedy Coordinate Gradient for text and Projected Gradient Descent for audio, to simultaneously perturb both modalities, and suggests that unimodal safety is insufficient for robust SLMs.

2603.18433.title: Prompt Control-Flow Integrity: A Priority-Aware Runtime Defense Against Prompt Injection in LLM Systems
2603.18433.tldr: This paper proposes Prompt Control-Flow Integrity (PCFI), a priority-aware runtime defense that models each request as a structured composition of system, developer, user, and retrieved-document segments, and suggests that provenance- and priority-aware prompt enforcement is a practical and lightweight defense for deployed LLM systems.

2510.17277.title: PolyJailbreak: Cross-Modal Jailbreaking Attacks on Black-Box Multimodal LLMs
2510.17277.tldr: This work investigates the security vulnerabilities of MLLMs in text-vision scenarios and proposes PolyJailbreak, which organizes the discovered vulnerabilities into a structured library of reusable Atomic Strategy Primitives to enable step-wise transformations from harmful intents to effective jailbreak inputs.
2510.17277.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing

2603.14825.title: Two Birds, One Projection: Harmonizing Safety and Utility in LVLMs via Inference-time Feature Projection
2603.14825.tldr: This work proposes Two Birds, One Projection, an efficient inference time jailbreak defence that projects cross-modal features onto the null space of the identified bias direction to remove the corresponding components.

2606.04778.title: Inference-Time Vulnerability Beyond Shallow Safety: Alignment Along Generation Trajectories
2606.04778.tldr: This work aligns models directly on generation trajectories constructed by simulating mid-sequence perturbation, and shows that this improves robustness to mid-sequence injection and generalizes to attacks that exploit early-token generation.

2603.14355.title: Exposing Long-Tail Safety Failures in Large Language Models through Efficient Diverse Response Sampling
2603.14355.tldr: This work shows that, for a fixed safety-critical prompt, increasing the number and diversity of sampled responses monotonically raises the jailbreak success rate, and combines input-space perturbation with diversity-driven output-space exploration covers a wider range of failure modes more efficiently than either paradigm alone.

2509.16060.title: SABER: Uncovering Vulnerabilities in Safety Alignment via Cross-Layer Residual Connection
2509.16060.tldr: A novel white-box jailbreak method, SABER (Safety Alignment Bypass via Extra Residuals), which connects two intermediate layers $s$ and $e$ such that $s<e, through a residual connection, achieves a 51% improvement over the best-performing baseline on the HarmBench test set.
2509.16060.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2608.18628.title: When Safety Overrides Vision: Exploring Dynamics between Vision Influence and Safety Alignment in Vision-Language Models
2608.18628.tldr: This work investigates the internal decoding dynamics underlying safety-induced abstention in aligned VLMs and shows that suppressing refusal-related representations reliably restores grounded answering behavior across models without retraining or modifying visual inputs.

2603.14219.title: Safety-Potential Pruning for Enhancing Safety Prompts Against VLM Jailbreaking Without Retraining
2603.14219.tldr: Safety-Potential Pruning is introduced, a one-shot pruning framework that amplifies safety-relevant activations by removing weights that are less responsive to safety prompts without additional retraining, offering a new path to robust jailbreak resistance.
2603.14219.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2603.13847.title: Sirens' Whisper: Inaudible Near-Ultrasonic Jailbreaks of Speech-Driven LLMs
2603.13847.tldr: SWhisper is presented, the first practical framework for covert prompt-based attacks against speech-driven LLMs under realistic black-box conditions using commodity hardware, and a voice-aware jailbreak generation method that ensures intelligibility, brevity, and transferability under speech-driven interfaces.

2603.10068.title: ADVERSA: Measuring Multi-Turn Guardrail Degradation and Judge Reliability in Large Language Models
2603.10068.tldr: ADVERSA is presented, an automated red-teaming framework that measures guardrail behavior as continuous per-round compliance trajectories that reduces attacker-side safety refusals to a characterizable minority and employs a triple-judge consensus architecture in which judge reliability is measured as a first-class research outcome rather than assumed.
2603.10068.venue: International Conference on Software Engineering Research and Applications

2603.03081.title: TAO-Attack: Toward Advanced Optimization-Based Jailbreak Attacks for Large Language Models
2603.03081.tldr: TAO-Attack is proposed, a new optimization-based jailbreak method for large language models that consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving higher attack success rates and even reaching 100\% in certain scenarios.

2603.01942.title: Ignore All Previous Instructions: Jailbreaking as a de-escalatory peace building practise to resist LLM social media bots
2603.01942.tldr: A user-centric view of jailbreaking is proposed as an emergent, non-violent de-escalation practice in large language model safeguards, exposing automated behaviour and disrupting the circulation of misleading narratives.

2603.01414.title: Jailbreaking Embodied LLMs via Action-level Manipulation
2603.01414.tldr: Blindfold is introduced, an automated attack framework that leverages the limited causal reasoning capabilities of embodied LLMs in real-world action contexts that achieves up to 53% higher attack success rates than SOTA baselines, highlighting the need to move beyond surface language censorship and toward consequence-aware defenses.
2603.01414.venue: ACM International Conference on Embedded Networked Sensor Systems

2601.06884.title: Paraphrasing Adversarial Attack on LLM-as-a-Reviewer
2601.06884.tldr: A black-box optimization method that searches for paraphrased sequences yielding higher review scores while preserving semantic equivalence and linguistic naturalness, and finds that attacked papers exhibit increased perplexity in reviews, offering a potential detection signal, and that paraphrasing submissions can partially mitigate attacks.

2602.24009.title: Jailbreak Foundry: From Papers to Runnable Attacks for Reproducible Benchmarking
2602.24009.tldr: JAILBREAK FOUNDRY is introduced, a system that addresses this gap via a multi-agent workflow to translate jailbreak papers into executable modules for immediate evaluation within a unified harness and offers a scalable solution for creating living benchmarks that keep pace with the rapidly shifting security landscape.

2606.02423.title: Investigating and Alleviating Harm Amplification in LLM Interactions
2606.02423.tldr: This work proposes TrajSafe, a proactive monitor that anticipates harmful trajectories and intervenes through actions such as probing users' genuine intents and steering the models towards safer completion, and introduces HarmAmp, a new benchmark for multi-turn harm amplification scenarios spanning twelve risk categories.

2602.21346.title: Alignment-Weighted DPO: A principled reasoning approach to improve safety alignment
2602.21346.tldr: This work constructs and releases a novel Chain-of-Thought fine-tuning dataset and introduces Alignment-Weighted DPO, which targets the most problematic parts of an output by assigning different preference weights to the reasoning and final-answer segments and consistently improves alignment robustness while maintaining overall model utility.

2602.16832.title: IndicJR: A Judge-Free Benchmark of Jailbreak Robustness in South Asian Languages
2602.16832.tldr: Indic Jailbreak Robustness (IJR) is introduced, a judge-free benchmark for adversarial safety across 12 Indic and South Asian languages, covering 45216 prompts in JSON (contract-bound) and Free (naturalistic) tracks, revealing three patterns.
2602.16832.venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2602.16520.title: Recursive language models for jailbreak detection: a procedural defense for tool-augmented agents
2602.16520.tldr: RLM-JB is presented, an end-to-end jailbreak detection framework built on Recursive Language Models, in which a root model orchestrates a bounded analysis program that transforms the input, queries worker models over covered segments, and aggregates evidence into an auditable decision.

2602.16752.title: The Vulnerability of LLM Rankers to Prompt Injection Attacks
2602.16752.tldr: A comprehensive empirical study of jailbreak prompt attacks against LLM rankers, revealing critical insights such as that encoder-decoder architectures exhibit strong inherent resilience to jailbreak attacks.
2602.16752.venue: Annual International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval

2606.14517.title: From Shield to Target: Denial-of-Service Attacks on LLM-Based Agent Guardrails
2606.14517.tldr: It is shown that a single poisoned document can saturate shared guardrail infrastructures, effectively starving co-located agents and paralyzing the entire system, and underscores the urgent need to develop cost-bounded, reasoning-robust guardrails.

2602.13547.title: AISA: Awakening Intrinsic Safety Awareness in Large Language Models against Jailbreak Attacks
2602.13547.tldr: AISA is presented, a lightweight, single-pass defense that activates safety behaviors already latent inside the model rather than treating safety as an add-on, enabling safer deployment even for weakly aligned or intentionally risky model variants.

2602.13321.title: Detecting Jailbreak Attempts in Clinical Training LLMs Through Automated Linguistic Feature Extraction
2602.13321.tldr: This work demonstrates a scalable and interpretable approach for detecting jailbreak behavior in safety-critical clinical dialogue systems by using experts'annotations of four core linguistic features and training multiple general-domain and medical-domain BERT-based LLM models to predict these features directly from text.

2602.09629.title: Stop Testing Attacks, Start Diagnosing Defenses: The Four-Checkpoint Framework Reveals Where LLM Safety Breaks
2602.09629.tldr: The Four-Checkpoint Framework provides a structured approach for identifying and addressing safety vulnerabilities in deployed systems and suggests that current defenses are strongest at input-literal checkpoints but remain vulnerable to intent-level manipulation and output-stage techniques.

2601.00867.title: The Silicon Psyche: Anthropomorphic Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models
2601.00867.tldr: This paper presents the first systematic application of the Cybersecurity Psychology Framework, a 100-indicator taxonomy of human psychological vulnerabilities, to non-human cognitive agents, and introduces the Synthetic Psychometric Assessment Protocol, a methodology for converting human psychological vulnerabilities into adversarial scenarios targeting LLM decision-making.

2602.10148.title: Red-teaming the Multimodal Reasoning: Jailbreaking Vision-Language Models via Cross-modal Entanglement Attacks
2602.10148.tldr: This work proposes a scalable approach that extends and entangles information clues across modalities to exceed VLMs'trained and generalized safety alignment patterns for jailbreak, and achieves state-of-the-art attack success rate.

2602.08136.title: Robustness of Vision Language Models Against Split-Image Harmful Input Attacks
2602.08136.tldr: This work introduces novel split-image visual jailbreak attacks (SIVA) that exploit a new vulnerability in VLM safety alignment and introduces a novel adversarial knowledge distillation algorithm to substantially improve cross-model transferability.

2602.08062.title: Efficient and Adaptable Detection of Malicious LLM Prompts via Bootstrap Aggregation
2602.08062.tldr: Results show ensembles of small finetuned classifiers can match or exceed billion-parameter guardrails while offering the adaptability and efficiency required for production systems.

2602.06440.title: TrailBlazer: History-Guided Reinforcement Learning for Black-Box LLM Jailbreaking
2602.06440.tldr: A history-aware RL-based jailbreak framework that analyzes and reweights vulnerability signals from prior steps to guide future decisions and offers a principled pathway for advancing adversarial research on LLM safeguards is proposed.

2608.04698.title: Teaching MLLMs to Say No: Generalized Referring Expression Comprehension via Refusal Calibrated GRPO
2608.04698.tldr: Refusal-Calibrated Group Relative Policy Optimization (RC-GRPO) is proposed, a calibrated RL strategy that strengthens the refusal ability of MLLMs while preserving localization performance, and enforces"None" outputs in rollouts for valid advantage estimation on negative samples and applies a penalty to prevent over-refusal on positives, achieving a balanced trade-off between accuracy and reliability.

2602.04294.title: How Few-shot Demonstrations Affect Prompt-based Defenses Against LLM Jailbreak Attacks
2602.04294.tldr: A comprehensive evaluation on multiple mainstream LLM applications reveals that few-shot demonstrations produce opposite effects on RoP and ToP: few-shot enhances RoP's safety rate by up to 4.5% through reinforcing role identity, while it degrades ToP's effectiveness by up to 21.2% through distracting attention from task instructions.

2512.18776.title: "Even GPT Can Reject Me": Conceptualizing Abrupt Refusal Secondary Harm (ARSH) and Reimagining Psychological AI Safety with Compassionate Completion Standard (CCS)
2512.18776.tldr: This viewpoint introduces Abrupt Refusal Secondary Harm (ARSH) as a conceptual framework to describe the psychological impacts of sudden conversational discontinuation caused by AI safety protocols, and proposes a design hypothesis, the Compassionate Completion Standard (CCS), a refusal protocol grounded in Human Centered Design that maintains safety constraints while preserving relational coherence.

2602.03265.title: Beyond Suffixes: Token Position in GCG Adversarial Attacks on Large Language Models
2602.03265.tldr: This work focuses on the prevalent Greedy Coordinate Gradient attack and identifies a previously underexplored attack axis in jailbreak attacks typically framed as suffix-based: the placement of adversarial tokens within the prompt.

2602.00619.title: Jailbreaking LLMs via Calibration
2602.00619.tldr: This work casts Weak-to-Strong Jailbreaking as a forecast aggregation problem and derive an optimal aggregation strategy characterized by a Gradient Shift in the loss-induced dual space, and proposes a new hybrid aggregation rule.

2601.22240.title: A Systematic Literature Review on LLM Defenses Against Prompt Injection and Jailbreaking: Expanding NIST Taxonomy
2601.22240.tldr: This work presents the first systematic literature review on prompt injection mitigation strategies, comprehending 88 studies, and proposes an extension to NIST taxonomy by introducing additional categories of defenses.

2601.20903.title: ICON: Intent-Context Coupling for Efficient Multi-Turn Jailbreak Attack
2601.20903.tldr: The Intent-Context Coupling phenomenon is characterized, revealing that LLM safety constraints are significantly relaxed when a malicious intent is coupled with a semantically congruent context pattern and preventing the attack from stagnating in ineffective contexts.

2601.15331.title: RECAP: A Resource-Efficient Method for Adversarial Prompting in Large Language Models
2601.15331.tldr: A resource-efficient adversarial prompting approach that eliminates the need for retraining by matching new prompts to a database of pre-trained adversarial prompts, providing a practical framework for scalable red-teaming and security evaluation of aligned LLMs, including in settings where model internals are inaccessible.

2601.12652.title: Ethical Risks in Deploying Large Language Models: An Evaluation of Medical Ethics Jailbreaking
2601.12652.tldr: Current LLMs are highly vulnerable to contextual manipulation in medical ethics, often prioritizing"helpfulness"over safety constraints, so a transition from outcome to process supervision, the implementation of multi-factor identity verification, and the establishment of cross-model"joint defense"mechanisms are recommended.

2601.12460.title: TrojanPraise: Jailbreak LLMs via Benign Fine-Tuning
2601.12460.tldr: This paper proposes TrojanPraise, a novel finetuning-based attack exploiting benign and thus filter-approved data to jailbreak large language models by fine-tuning them with malicious data.

2510.02833.title: Attack via Overfitting: 10-shot Benign Fine-tuning to Jailbreak LLMs
2510.02833.tldr: It is demonstrated that LLMs can be jailbroken by fine-tuning with only 10 benign QA pairs; the attack exploits the increased sensitivity of LLMs to fine-tuning data after being overfitted and achieves significant advantages in both attack effectiveness and attack stealth.

2510.07809.title: Invisible to Humans, Triggered by Agents: Stealthy Jailbreak Attacks on Mobile Vision-Language Agents
2510.07809.tldr: HG-IDA*, an efficient one-shot optimization method for constructing jailbreak prompts that evade LVLM safety filters, is introduced, which highlights a previously underexplored attack surface in mobile agent systems and underscores the need for defenses that incorporate interaction-level signals.

2601.10971.title: AJAR: Adaptive Jailbreak Architecture for Red-teaming
2601.10971.tldr: A red-teaming framework that exposes multi-turn jailbreak algorithms as callable MCP services and lets an Auditor Agent orchestrate them inside a tool-aware runtime built on Petri, and results position AJAR as a practical foundation for evaluating multi-turn jailbreaks under realistic agent constraints.

2512.12069.title: Rethinking Jailbreak Detection of Large Vision Language Models with Representational Contrastive Scoring
2512.12069.tldr: This work demonstrates that effective jailbreak detection can be achieved by applying simple, interpretable statistical methods to the internal representations of large Vision-Language Models, offering a practical path towards safer LVLM deployment.
2512.12069.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2601.09625.title: The Promptware Kill Chain: How Prompt Injections Gradually Evolved Into a Multistep Malware Delivery Mechanism
2601.09625.tldr: This paper argues that prompt injections evolved into promptware, a new class of malware execution mechanism triggered through prompts engineered to exploit an application's LLM, and introduces a seven-stage promptware kill chain.

2607.07433.title: Beware of Agentic Botnets: Scalable Untargeted Promptware Attacks via Universal and Transferable Adversarial HalluSquatting
2607.07433.tldr: It is shown that the inherent tendency of LLMs to hallucinate resource identifiers can be exploited to amplify untargeted promptware attacks that pull adversarial prompts at scale and could be exploited to establish a botnet.

2601.05742.title: The Echo Chamber Multi-Turn LLM Jailbreak
2601.05742.tldr: Echo Chamber is introduced, a new multi-turn attack using a gradual escalation method that can be used to bypass a chatbot's safety guardrails and test its performance against multiple state-of-the-art models.

2601.03600.title: ALERT: Zero-shot LLM Jailbreak Detection via Internal Discrepancy Amplification
2601.03600.tldr: This work proposes a layer-wise, module-wise, and token-wise amplification framework that progressively magnifies internal feature discrepancies between benign and jailbreak prompts and introduces ALERT (Amplification-based Jailbreak Detector), an efficient and effective zero-shot jailbreak detector that introduces two independent yet complementary classifiers on amplified representations.

2601.03420.title: Jailbreaking LLMs Without Gradients or Priors: Effective and Transferable Attacks
2601.03420.tldr: This work introduces RAILS (RAndom Iterative Local Search), a framework that operates solely on model logits and eliminates gradient dependency, which allows for the discovery of shared adversarial patterns that generalize across disjoint vocabularies, significantly enhancing transferability to closed-source systems.

2601.03300.title: TRYLOCK: Defense-in-Depth Against LLM Jailbreaks via Layered Preference and Representation Engineering
2601.03300.tldr: TRYLOCK is presented, the first defense-in-depth architecture that combines four heterogeneous mechanisms across the inference stack: weight-level safety alignment via DPO, activation-level control via Representation Engineering (RepE) steering, adaptive steering strength selected by a lightweight sidecar classifier, and input canonicalization to neutralize encoding-based bypasses.

2601.00936.title: Emoji-Based Jailbreaking of Large Language Models
2601.00936.tldr: This study investigates emoji-based jailbreaking, where emoji sequences are embedded in textual prompts to trigger harmful and unethical outputs from LLMs, and reveals model-specific vulnerabilities in LLMs.

2608.10126.title: Procedural Fairness Failures in RLHF from Preference Averaging
2608.10126.tldr: The results show that procedural fairness failures in alignment can arise from structural design choices in reward learning, even in controlled, noise-free settings, with direct implications for large language models and agentic systems, where biased reward models can compound inequities across sequential decisions.

2601.00213.title: Overlooked Safety Vulnerability in LLMs: Malicious Intelligent Optimization Algorithm Request and its Jailbreak
2601.00213.tldr: It is revealed that most mainstream LLMs remain highly susceptible to automated algorithm attacks, with an average attack success rate of 83.59% and an average harmfulness score of 4.28 out of 5 on original harmful prompts, and near-complete failure under MOBjailbreak.

2512.20293.title: AprielGuard
2512.20293.tldr: AprielGuard is an 8B parameter safeguard model that unify these dimensions within a single taxonomy and learning framework that achieves strong performance in detecting harmful content and adversarial manipulations, outperforming existing opensource guardrails such as Llama-Guard and Granite Guardian, particularly in multi-step and reasoning intensive scenarios.

2601.03273.title: A Multi-Perspective Benchmark and Moderation Model for Evaluating Safety and Adversarial Robustness
2601.03273.tldr: GuardEval and GGuard together demonstrate that diverse, representative data materially improve safety, and adversarial robustness on complex, borderline cases, and that multi-perspective, human-centered safety benchmarks are critical for mitigating inconsistent moderation decisions.

2512.18755.title: MEEA: Mere Exposure Effect-Driven Confrontational Optimization for LLM Jailbreaking
2512.18755.tldr: MEEA leverages repeated low-toxicity semantic exposure to induce a gradual shift in a model's effective safety threshold, enabling progressive erosion of alignment constraints over sustained interactions, and demonstrates that LLM safety behavior is inherently dynamic and history-dependent.

2512.04748.title: Model Whisper: Steering Vectors Unlock Large Language Models' Potential in Test-time
2512.04748.tldr: This work introduces a lightweight component, Test-Time Steering Vectors (TTSV), which is prepended to the input while keeping the LLM's parameters entirely frozen, and exhibits robust generalization, with its steering vectors proving highly transferable across diverse tasks.

2512.15353.title: Adversarial versification in portuguese as a jailbreak operator in LLMs
2512.15353.tldr: Experimental protocols must parameterise scansion, metre, and prosodic variation to test vulnerabilities specific to Lusophone patterns, which are currently ignored.

2512.13741.title: The Laminar Flow Hypothesis: Detecting Jailbreaks via Semantic Turbulence in Large Language Models
2512.13741.tldr: It is demonstrated that Semantic Turbulence serves not only as a lightweight, real-time jailbreak detector but also as a non-invasive diagnostic tool for categorizing the underlying safety architecture of black-box models.

2608.20378.title: Truth Lies Deep: Countering Semantic Camouflage via Latent Intent Verification
2608.20378.tldr: LIV is proposed, a lightweight probing defense that outperforms standard guardrails by a margin of $\mathbf{2 0}-\mathbf{5 0 {\%}}$ across all tested architectures, effectively neutralizing zero-day semantic attacks without requiring model retraining.
2608.20378.venue: 2026 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Quantum Photonics, Artificial Intelligence & Networking (QPAIN)

2512.14751.title: One Leak Away: How Pretrained Model Exposure Amplifies Jailbreak Risks in Finetuned LLMs
2512.14751.tldr: A realistic pretrain-to-finetune threat model is investigated, showing that adversarial prompts optimized on the pretrained model transfer most effectively to its finetuned variants, and proposing the Probe-Guided Projection attack, which steers optimization toward transferability-relevant directions.

2510.08859.title: Pattern Enhanced Multi-Turn Jailbreaking: Exploiting Structural Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models
2510.08859.tldr: Evaluating PE-CoA on twelve LLMs spanning ten harm categories achieves state-of-the-art performance and uncovers pattern-specific vulnerabilities and LLM behavioral characteristics, highlighting limitations of safety training and indicating the need for pattern-aware defenses.

2510.00565.title: Toward Safer Diffusion Language Models: Discovery and Mitigation of Priming Vulnerability
2510.00565.tldr: This paper reveals that DLMs have a critical vulnerability stemming from their iterative denoising process and proposes a novel safety alignment method tailored to DLMs that trains models to generate safe responses from contaminated intermediate states that contain affirmative tokens.

2607.23015.title: Mask2Shield: Strengthening LLM Safety against Neuron-Pruning Attacks
2607.23015.tldr: Mask2Shield (M2S), a masked-forward alignment method that trains a model under this functional pruning procedure, reduces successful recomputed pruning attacks from 80--279 to 1--44 out of 313 prompts while generally preserving four capability benchmarks.

2602.01654.title: Steering Vector Fields for Context-Aware Inference-Time Control in Large Language Models
2602.01654.tldr: SVF is proposed, which learns a differentiable concept scoring function whose local gradient defines the steering direction at each activation, making interventions explicitly context-dependent and enables efficient long-form and multi-attribute control within a unified framework.

2512.01185.title: DefenSee: Dissecting Threat from Sight and Text -- A Multi-View Defensive Pipeline for Multi-modal Jailbreaks
2512.01185.tldr: Experiments show that DefenSee consistently enhances MLLM robustness while better preserving performance on benign tasks compared to SOTA defenses, and reduces the ASR of jailbreak attacks to below 1.70% on MiniGPT4 using the MM-SafetyBench benchmark, significantly outperforming prior methods under the same conditions.

2605.01462.title: LocalAlign: Enabling Generalizable Prompt Injection Defense via Generation of Near-Target Adversarial Examples for Alignment Training
2605.01462.tldr: This work proposes LocalAlign, a more generalizable prompt injection defense inspired by adversarial training that automatically and efficiently generates adversarial examples in which the command embedded in the data portion induces a response that stays near to the correct response while still being wrong.

2510.21214.title: Enhanced MLLM Black-Box Jailbreaking Attacks and Defenses
2510.21214.tldr: A black-box jailbreak method via both text and image prompts to evaluate MLLMs and identified gaps in existing defense methods to propose new strategies for both training-time and inference-time defense methods, and evaluated them across the new jailbreak methods.

2606.22779.title: DE-FIVE: Detecting Malicious Image Prompts via Fourier Features and Image Vector Embeddings
2606.22779.tldr: DE-FIVE is introduced, a novel training-free framework for detecting malicious image prompts by leveraging Fourier features and the hidden state representations of the visual encoder (image vector embeddings) across perturbations that consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines against malicious image prompts.

2511.20494.title: Adversarial Confusion Attack: Disrupting Multimodal Large Language Models
2511.20494.tldr: The Adversarial Confusion Attack is introduced, a new class of threats against multimodal large language models (MLLMs) that generates perturbations that transfer to both unseen open-source and proprietary models.
2511.20494.venue: The European Symposium on Artificial Neural Networks

2511.19009.title: Understanding and Mitigating Over-refusal for Large Language Models via Representation Intervention
2511.19009.tldr: This paper first analyzes the causes of over-refusal from a representation perspective, revealing that LLMs are unable to effectively distinguish between over-refusal samples and malicious samples, and proposes to mitigate overrefusal by intervening in the safety representation space of LLMs.

2511.18933.title: Defending Large Language Models Against Jailbreak Exploits with Responsible AI Considerations
2511.18933.tldr: Overall, this study highlights how jailbreaks pose a significant security threat to LLMs and identifies key intervention points for prevention, while noting that defense strategies often involve trade-offs between safety, performance, and scalability.

2511.17666.title: Evaluating Adversarial Vulnerabilities in Modern Large Language Models
2511.17666.tldr: This research contributes a scalable framework for automated AI red-teaming and provides data-driven insights into the current state of LLM safety, underscoring the complex challenge of balancing model capabilities with robust safety mechanisms.

2512.03047.title: Entropy-Based Measurement of Value Drift and Alignment Work in Large Language Models
2512.03047.tldr: A five-way behavioral taxonomy is defined, a classifier is trained to estimate ethical entropy S(t) from model transcripts, and entropy dynamics for base and instruction-tuned variants of four frontier models across stress tests are measured.

2511.14140.title: Beyond Fixed and Dynamic Prompts: Embedded Jailbreak Templates for Advancing LLM Security
2511.14140.tldr: This paper introduces the Embedded Jailbreak Template, which preserves the structure of existing templates while naturally embedding harmful queries within their context, and proposes a progressive prompt-engineering methodology to ensure template quality and consistency, alongside standardized protocols for generation and evaluation.

2605.18133.title: An Empirical Study of Privacy Leakage Chains via Prompt Injection in Black-Box Chatbot Environments
2605.18133.tldr: The results suggest that prompt injection, jailbreak-style instruction steering, and web-tool invocation can be combined into a feasible privacy-leakage path in deployed chatbot agents.

2511.13548.title: ForgeDAN: An Evolutionary Framework for Jailbreaking Aligned Large Language Models
2511.13548.tldr: This work proposes ForgeDAN, a novel evolutionary framework for generating semantically coherent and highly effective adversarial prompts against aligned LLMs, and demonstrates ForgeDAN achieves high jailbreaking success rates while maintaining naturalness and stealth, outperforming existing SOTA solutions.
2511.13548.venue: International Conference on Trust, Security and Privacy in Computing and Communications

2511.11301.title: EcoAlign: An Economically Rational Framework for Efficient LVLM Alignment
2511.11301.tldr: EcoAlign is proposed, an inference-time framework that reframes alignment as an economically rational search by treating the LVLM as a boundedly rational agent and offering a principled, economical pathway to robust LVLM alignment.

2511.10519.title: Say It Differently: Linguistic Styles as Jailbreak Vectors
2511.10519.tldr: This work systematically study how linguistic styles can reframe harmful intent and elicit unsafe responses from aligned models, and introduces a style neutralization preprocessing step using a secondary LLM to strip manipulative stylistic cues from user inputs, significantly reducing jailbreak success rates.

2511.06852.title: Differentiated Directional Intervention A Framework for Evading LLM Safety Alignment
2511.06852.tldr: This work deconstructs a single representation of this refusal mechanism as a single linear direction in the activation space into a Harm Detection Direction and a Refusal Execution Direction and introduces Differentiated Bi-Directional Intervention (DBDI), a new white-box framework that precisely neutralizes the safety alignment at critical layer.

2511.06512.title: EASE: Practical and Efficient Safety Alignment for Small Language Models
2511.06512.tldr: This work proposes EASE, a novel framework that enables practical and Efficient safety Alignment for Small languagE models by identifying the optimal safety reasoning teacher that can effectively distill safety reasoning capabilities to SLMs and aligning models to selectively activate safety reasoning for dangerous adversarial jailbreak queries.

2603.07445.title: Few Tokens, Big Leverage: Preserving Safety Alignment by Constraining Safety Tokens during Fine-tuning
2603.07445.tldr: A FT framework that Preserves safety Alignment via Constrained Tokens (\Sysacro) by stabilizing the model's confidence on safety tokens is proposed, motivated by the empirical observation that safety-aligned behavior is reflected in the model's token-level output confidence and is often concentrated on a small subset of safety-related tokens.
2603.07445.venue: Proceedings of the 32nd ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining V.2

2511.03271.title: Let the Bees Find the Weak Spots: A Path Planning Perspective on Multi-Turn Jailbreak Attacks against LLMs
2511.03271.tldr: ABC, an enhanced Artificial Bee Colony algorithm for multi-turn jailbreaks, featuring a collaborative search mechanism with employed, onlooker, and scout bees is proposed, which significantly improves the efficiency of optimal attack path search while substantially reducing the average number of queries required.

2511.03247.title: Death by a Thousand Prompts: Open Model Vulnerability Analysis
2511.03247.tldr: It is concluded that open-weight models, while crucial for innovation, pose tangible operational and ethical risks when deployed without layered security controls and recommend adopting a security-first design philosophy and layered protections to ensure resilient deployments of open-weight models.

2606.05233.title: Domain-Conditioned Safety in Frontier Computer-Using Agents: A 793-Episode Browser Benchmark, a Coding-Domain Cross-Reference, and a Reproducibility Audit of Recent Red-Teaming
2606.05233.tldr: It is argued that the literature's high ASR is largely attributable to RL-optimized injection text rather than the attack categories, and that frontier safety hardening is domain-conditioned, specific to the heavily-targeted browser surface.

2511.02356.title: ASTRA: An Automated Framework for Strategy Discovery, Retrieval, and Evolution for Jailbreaking LLMs
2511.02356.tldr: A dynamic three-tier strategy library (Effective, Promising, and Ineffective) that categorizes strategies based on performance is introduced that enables the framework to enhance efficiency by leveraging successful patterns while optimizing the exploration space by avoiding known failures.
2511.02356.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

2511.00689.title: Do Methods to Jailbreak and Defend LLMs Generalize Across Languages?
2511.00689.tldr: This paper presents the first systematic multilingual evaluation of jailbreaks and defenses across ten languages -- spanning high-, medium-, and low-resource languages -- using six LLMs on HarmBench and AdvBench to assess two jailbreak types: logical-expression-based and adversarial-prompt-based.

2511.00346.title: Exploiting Latent Space Discontinuities for Building Universal LLM Jailbreaks and Data Extraction Attacks
2511.00346.tldr: This work proposes a novel approach to crafting universal jailbreaks and data extraction attacks by exploiting latent space discontinuities, an architectural vulnerability related to the sparsity of training data that can consistently and profoundly compromise model behavior.
2511.00346.venue: Anais do XXV Simpósio Brasileiro de Cibersegurança (SBSeg 2025)

2510.27275.title: Prevalence of Security and Privacy Risk-Inducing Usage of AI-based Conversational Agents
2510.27275.tldr: The findings suggest that current academic threat models might manifest in the wild, and mitigations or guidelines for the secure usage of CAs should be developed, because in areas critical to security and privacy, CAs must be equipped with effective AI guardrails.

2510.26847.title: Broken-Token: Filtering Obfuscated Prompts by Counting Characters-Per-Token
2510.26847.tldr: CPT-Filtering is introduced, a novel, model-agnostic with negligible-costs and near-perfect accuracy guardrail technique that aims to mitigate large Language Models attacks by leveraging the intrinsic behavior of Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) tokenizers.

2510.22628.title: Sentra-Guard: A Real-Time Multilingual Defense Against Adversarial LLM Prompts
2510.22628.tldr: This paper presents a real-time modular defense system named Sentra-Guard, which detects and mitigates jailbreak and prompt injection attacks targeting large language models (LLMs) and establishes a new state-of-the-art in adversarial LLM defense.

2510.22085.title: Jailbreak Mimicry: Automated Discovery of Narrative-Based Jailbreaks for Large Language Models
2510.22085.tldr: Jailbreak Mimicry, a systematic methodology for training compact attacker models to automatically generate narrative-based jailbreak prompts in a one-shot manner, is introduced, enabling proactive vulnerability assessment in AI-driven security systems.

2510.21983.title: Uncovering the Persuasive Fingerprint of LLMs in Jailbreaking Attacks
2510.21983.tldr: This work hypothesizes that LLMs, having been trained on large-scale human-generated text, may respond more compliantly to prompts with persuasive structures, and investigates whether LLMs themselves exhibit distinct persuasive fingerprints that emerge in their jailbreak responses.
2510.21983.venue: International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management

2510.21190.title: The Trojan Example: Jailbreaking LLMs through Template Filling and Unsafety Reasoning
2510.21190.tldr: TrojFill is introduced, a black-box exploitation framework that bypasses safety filters by targeting a fundamental logic flaw in current alignment paradigms: the decoupling of unsafety reasoning from content generation, exposing a systematic vulnerability inaligned LLMs.

2602.01795.title: RedVisor: Reasoning-Aware Prompt Injection Defense via Zero-Copy KV Cache Reuse
2602.01795.tldr: RedVisor is the first approach to leverage fine-grained reasoning paths to simultaneously detect attacks and guide the model's safe response, and it enables a novel KV Cache Reuse strategy, eliminating the redundant prefill computation inherent to decoupled pipelines.

2510.20223.title: Beyond Text: Multimodal Jailbreaking of Vision-Language and Audio Models through Perceptually Simple Transformations
2510.20223.tldr: A systematic study of multimodal jailbreaks targeting both vision-language and audio-language models, showing that even simple perceptual transformations can reliably bypass state-of-the-art safety filters.

2510.19169.title: OpenGuardrails: A Configurable, Unified, and Scalable Guardrails Platform for Large Language Models
2510.19169.tldr: OpenGuardrails is the first fully open-source platform that unifies large-model-based safety detection, manipulation defense, and deployable guardrail infrastructure and achieves state-of-the-art performance across multilingual safety benchmarks.

2510.18728.title: HarmNet: A Framework for Adaptive Multi-Turn Jailbreak Attacks on Large Language Models
2510.18728.tldr: HarmNet, a modular framework comprising ThoughtNet, a hierarchical semantic network; a feedback-driven Simulator for iterative query refinement; and a Network Traverser for real-time adaptive attack execution is introduced.

2510.03417.title: NEXUS: Network Exploration for eXploiting Unsafe Sequences in Multi-Turn LLM Jailbreaks
2510.03417.tldr: NEXUS (Network Exploration for eXploiting Unsafe Sequences), a modular framework for constructing, refining, and executing optimized multi-turn attacks, uncovers stealthy, high-success adversarial paths across LLMs.
2510.03417.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

2510.17947.title: PLAGUE: Plug-and-play framework for Lifelong Adaptive Generation of Multi-turn Exploits
2510.17947.tldr: PLAGUE is presented, a novel plug-and-play framework for designing multi-turn attacks inspired by lifelong-learning agents that dissects the lifetime of a multi-turn attack into three carefully designed phases that enable a systematic and information-rich exploration of the multi-turn attack family.

2512.21999.title: Look Closer! An Adversarial Parametric Editing Framework for Hallucination Mitigation in VLMs
2512.21999.tldr: An adversarial parametric editing framework for Hallucination mitigation in VLMs is proposed, which follows an Activate-Locate-Edit Adversarially paradigm and evaluations on both generative and discriminative VLM tasks demonstrate the significant effectiveness of ALEAHallu in alleviating hallucinations.

2510.17904.title: BreakFun: Jailbreaking LLMs via Schema Exploitation
2510.17904.tldr: The Adversarial Prompt Deconstruction guardrail is introduced, a defense that utilizes a secondary LLM to perform a "Literal Transcription"--extracting all human-readable text to isolate and reveal the user's true harmful intent.

2510.13901.title: RAID: Refusal-Aware and Integrated Decoding for Jailbreaking LLMs
2510.13901.tldr: RAD (Refusal-Aware and Integrated Decoding) is presented, a framework that systematically probes LLM weaknesses by crafting adversarial suffixes that induce restricted content while preserving fluency and highlights the importance of embedding-space regularization for understanding and mitigating LLM jailbreak vulnerabilities.

2510.12672.title: Keep Calm and Avoid Harmful Content: Concept Alignment and Latent Manipulation Towards Safer Answers
2510.12672.tldr: Experiments show that CALM reduces harmful outputs and outperforms baseline methods in most metrics, offering a lightweight approach to AI safety with no additional training data or model fine-tuning, while incurring only a small computational overhead at inference.

2510.11837.title: Countermind: A Multi-Layered Security Architecture for Large Language Models
2510.11837.tldr: An evaluation plan is outlined designed to quantify the proposed Countermind architecture's effectiveness in reducing the Attack Success Rate (ASR) for form-first attacks and to measure its potential latency overhead.

2510.10281.title: ArtPerception: ASCII Art-based Jailbreak on LLMs with Recognition Pre-test
2510.10281.tldr: ArtPerception is introduced, a novel black-box jailbreak framework that strategically leverages ASCII art to bypass the security measures of state-of-the-art (SOTA) LLMs and proposes a Modified Levenshtein Distance (MLD) metric for a more nuanced evaluation of an LLM's recognition capability.
2510.10281.venue: Journal of Network and Computer Applications

2601.22569.title: Whispers of Wealth: Red-Teaming Google's Agent Payments Protocol via Prompt Injection
2601.22569.tldr: A systematic red-teaming evaluation of AP2 is presented and vulnerabilities arising from prompt injection are identified, revealing a fundamental limitation of agent-mediated payment systems: cryptographic guarantees ensure execution correctness but do not protect decision-making.
2601.22569.venue: 2026 International Conference on Intelligent Multimedia, Networking, and Security (IMNS)

2510.15948.title: VisuoAlign: Safety Alignment of LVLMs with Multimodal Tree Search
2510.15948.tldr: VisuoAlign embeds safety constrains into the reasoning process through visual-textual interactive prompts, employs Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) to systematically construct diverse safety-critical prompt trajectories, and introduces prompt-based scaling to ensure real-time risk detection and compliant responses.

2510.09699.title: VisualDAN: Exposing Vulnerabilities in VLMs with Visual-Driven DAN Commands
2510.09699.tldr: This work introduces VisualDAN, a single adversarial image embedded with DAN-style commands that effectively bypasses the safeguards of aligned VLMs, forcing them to execute a broad range of harmful instructions that severely violate ethical standards.

2510.07835.title: MetaDefense: Defending Finetuning-based Jailbreak Attack Before and During Generation
2510.07835.tldr: This paper introduces MetaDefense, a novel framework for defending against finetuning-based jailbreak attacks in large language models (LLMs), achieving robust defense against harmful queries with seen and unseen attack templates while maintaining competitive performance on benign tasks.

2510.06994.title: RedTWIZ: Diverse LLM Red Teaming via Adaptive Attack Planning
2510.06994.tldr: Experimental results demonstrate that the multi-turn adversarial attack strategies can successfully lead state-of-the-art LLMs to produce unsafe generations, highlighting the pressing need for more research into enhancing LLM's robustness.

2510.05052.title: Proactive defense against LLM Jailbreak
2510.05052.tldr: ProAct is introduced, a novel proactive defense framework designed to disrupt and mislead these iterative search jailbreak methods into thinking that the model has been jailbroken with "spurious responses".

2510.03520.title: Certifiable Safe RLHF: Semantic Grounding and Fixed Penalty Constraint Optimization for Safer LLM Alignment
2510.03520.tldr: Certifiable Safe-RLHF (CS-RLHF) is introduced that introduces a cost model trained on a large-scale corpus to assign semantically grounded safety scores and draws on the theory of exact penalty functions in constrained optimization, wherein constraint satisfaction is enforced directly through a suitably chosen penalty term.

2510.01644.title: Machine Learning for Detection and Analysis of Novel LLM Jailbreaks
2510.01644.tldr: The ability of different machine learning models to distinguish jailbreak prompts from genuine uses is analysed, including the ability to identify jailbreaks that use previously unseen strategies, and explicit reflexivity in prompt structure could be a signal of jailbreak intention.

2510.01359.title: Breaking the Code: Security Assessment of AI Code Agents Through Systematic Jailbreaking Attacks
